column9: Liked these better as a kid..
column10: Taste-wise, these are pretty decent.  I found that I got tired of the orange flavor that is added.  I remember liking them a bit more when I was younger.
I did a rush order on this item and was to get it before christmas, I received it 3 weeks late!

I bought this product because it was recommended by Dr. Oz. It suppose to help with bad breath. Since I'm on a diet, I thought I would try this. It does taste a little salty to me but I'm not a big parsley fan. You can drink it without gagging. The taste is just okay. I got it because it seemed healthy. Once a day is enough for me.

I am a huge fan of coconut and chocolate is my weakness.  The manufacturer mixes both to create a pretty good product with Cacao Bliss.When I first received this jar, I was not too impressed.  The appearance of the product was that of stale/old chocolate. It was crumbly when I tried to dip my spoon in it.  I had anticipated a creamy substance.  This product is not creamy out of the jar.  Unless the entire jar has been left in the sun or in a hot spot, don't expect to dip your knife or spoon in and spread it around on a piece of toast.In terms of eating options, I do recommend heating the product.  While I now enjoy eating it in its solid form out of the jar, heating some of the product creates a substance that can be spread easily on toast.  I also like taking shavings of this product and sprinkling it on cupcakes.  The coconut and chocolate flavor is a subtle addition to any sweet treat.I will note that the flavor took some getting used to.  It probably took three to four samplings before I started to really want to eat spoonfuls of the product.  I think with any new product that has a slightly different consistency and flavor there is an adjustment period.  I'm glad I didn't give up on it and took some time to experiment with how it could be used.  I will be incorporating this product into gift baskets for both my vegan and non-vegan friends and family.It is recommended that this product not be refrigerated.A snapshot of the product's nutrition facts can be found in the product image gallery.As a vegan product, there is no milk, eggs, honey or other animal-based substances that go into the formulation of this product.  According to the product packaging, this product is "made in a facility that processes tree nuts and soy, but does not process peanuts, gluten, dairy, cholesterol or GMO's."  This product is also sugar cane free.Considering that Amazon typically packages products in sets of 2 or 6, it is nice to be able to purchase one jar without committing 40 or 50 dollars on a bulk set of 6.  I do wish the jars were a bit larger.I give this product 4.5 stars.Cacao Bliss is made in the United States.

I give it a 5 star for taste, but a 3 star for price. It really costs too much for what it is. I recently purchased a mini food processor so I can make this myself using shredded coconut and cocoa. (Can also make coconut butter this way and save yourself big bucks!)

Very healthy and very tasty -- sort of like a better Nutella (which seems much too sweet, once you have tried this). Artisana products are clearly best of breed. Amazon prices are extremely reasonable (some of the Amazon marketplace sellers were twice the price).

Holy moly this stuff is delicious!  I am a total sucker for anything with chocolate and coconut, so I admit bias, but this is just....so.... GOOD.  Good for you, too.  It is crumbly when not heated, and it is definitely not oversweet, so you get the full experience of the deliciously dank cacao and the natural sweetness of the coconut.  Seriously, I eat this stuff right out of the jar with a spoon, it's that kind of good.  I also put a tablespoon or so into banana smoothies (yum!) or put a dollop on fresh fruit -- strawberries go great with this stuff.Caveat: if you are one of those folks who is a sugar addict or who can't do flavor without some major sweetness added then this product may not be for you, because it is "natural" sweet, not "industrial" sweet.  For those of you who find fruit to be plenty sweet then by all means this stuff is a complete five star.

column4: Rachel @ My Naturally Frugal Family "Rachel J"
column10: I didn't think that Artisana could improve on their coconut butter (as it is just a pure delicious treat in a jar).  However with the addition of cacao to the butter I think they definitely took it up a notch.  I love to use this on a slice of toast in the morning and it provides such a wealth of nutrients as well as being very filling.I am sure there are more applications for it, but right now I can't move past it slightly melting on a slice of warm toast !

column9: Shipped 6 different boxes but WOW so good!
column10: Not sure why Amazon split my order into six different boxes - kind of irritating and not very "sustainable".BUT this is a great way to get coconut into your diet in a very delicious way!  I love to spread this on Ritz crackers and have it with coffee.  I plan to make my own homemade crackers to make it a healthier snack.This is not very sweet but it definitely does cure a sweet tooth.HIGHLY recommend!  Price right now is great - stocked up.

column9: So Good, I eat it straight from the Jar!
column10: I have ordered several jars of Cacao Bliss. I have yet to try an Arisana product that i did not like. If you like coconut and chocolate, you must try it for yourself!

This is my first time trying the Artisana brand (comes highly recommended); I normally use Nutiva Certified Organic Extra Virgin Coconut Oil -- 54 fl oz or the Trader Joe's brand (which is virgin, not extra virgin coconut oil). I am a regular user of coconut oil but had never tried it mixed with sugar cane free, vegan cacao. It's definitely healthy. Taste-wise, it's a LOT less sweet than Nutella Hazelnut Chocolate Spread 13 Oz. - which I sadly love! - so this will take some getting used to. But, in trying to cut back on processed foods and refined sugar, this is a good trade off. Just like regular coconut oil, this treat stays in solid form in cooler temperatures (under 70F/21C) and will melt at higher temps, even turning liquid when it's warm (above 80F/26C). In its solid form, it breaks up like chocolate shavings; in its softer form, it has the consistency of Nutella or smooth peanut butter. It can be enjoyed on bread or salt-free crackers - or eaten alone, straight out of the jar - for a mildly sweet treat. However, be prepared that this product is not that sweet; it has more of an earthy, cacao flavor and the coconut flavor is not as strong as in plain coconut oil. Otherwise, it's a healthy way to add the benefits of organic coconut oil and the sweetness that comes from nature (cacao) to one's diet.**Note: Be be mindful that some may experience a mild-to-moderate allergic reaction (i.e., itching, hives, headache, throat swelling etc.) to this product, most likely in response to the cacao. Unfortunately, I was one of those people - I found out the hard way - but Amazon's excellent customer service was very helpful in issuing me a refund. Too bad, as I otherwise liked this product.

I love opening up a medjool date and lathering in some cacao bliss... DELICIOUS! Dabbing it on strawberries also makes a great dessert. It definitely has a thick consistency that's rich, maybe a little too rich for some people (after all there is a lot of coconut oil in it).

I ordered this product by mistake and tried to cancel order to no avail.  I wouldn't order it again because I don't eat that much chocolate, however, it is a wonderful product if you are a chocoholic! I still have most of the jar, and imagine I'll have it for a long time... good news is that it keeps well!!

column9: pretty good, but just don't eat too much
column10: i have to say when i first ate this product, i was excited - it tasted delicious and reminded me of a chocolate macaroon. i recommend it heated - i ate it at room temp. and it was a solid, crumbly mess. still good, but not as appetizing. this product should come with a WARNING: if you take it by the spoonfuls because of its wholesomeness and great taste, you WILL get a nasty stomach ache later on and then diarrhea or some variation of that. IT'S a LAXATIVE, no doubt. Right now, I can't even think about eating it for another few days, as my stomach is trying to recover. lol. My other issue is that this has AGAVE SYRUP, which I try to avoid when possible. As Dr. Mercola has made clear, agave SYRUP isn't so natural and wonderful as it is a PROCESSED product with unnatural, unhealthy (high) levels of fructose, not unlike high fructose corn syrup. But don't expect to hear that from the natural health community anytime soon - once a healthy food darling takes off, it's hard for it to come back down, as ppl get so fanatical about it. So, anyway, all in all, I would recommend this Cacao Bliss can do as an OCCASIONAL indulgence.

If you like extremely sweet things, like fudge, you might be disappointed by this.  But if you're looking for a comparatively healthy way to enjoy intense dark-chocolate flavor, give it a try.  The flavor is amazingly rich and chocolatey, and I love that it is not too sweet.  I also like that it is sweetened with Stevia instead of with sugar or high fructose corn syrup or something like that.  It might take a little getting used to (especially if you were expecting something like fudge or cake frosting), but I think the level of sweetness is just right.As for the texture, the product at room temperature is solid and crumbly, not really the right consistency for spreading on toast, cupcakes, etc.  Just put it in the microwave briefly and it will become easily spreadable (or spoonable).  In my opinion it tastes delicious either way!
I love Cacao Bliss.  It is a sweet treat right out of the jar by the spoonful.  Wouldn't want to eat too much at one seating, however, as it is quite rich.  I will order again!!!
Very grainy and solid, which I had not anticipated. I thought it would be smoother. Tastes good but the grainy product is a slight turnoff for me.

After reading all of the positive reviews, I was anxious to try out this product.  I was so disappointed when I got it.  The texture is chalky and the taste to me is unpleasant.  It was really quite solid so I warmed it up so that I could mix it up better.  It became more of a spreadable consistency, but the grainy texture and the taste did not improve.  I'm going to try using some of it in my smoothies, but if it still doesn't taste good to me, it's going into the garbage.I also ordered the Artisana coconut butter and Artisana macadamia butter.  I had the same same bad experience with the coconut butter in that the texture was grainy and the taste was unpleasant to me.  I did, however, really like the macadamia butter a lot.
Cacao Bliss is excellent.  I also put a little extra coconut oil into the jar to keep it nice and moist.

This coconut butter tastes awesome. Way too expensive for such a small jar. I am going to try what another person posted on the coconut butter review and make my own with coconut flakes, a food processor and some cacao powder. I just can't justify spending 11$ on a jar this small.

Great taste. I eat it with a spoon when I need a chocolate fix. Very healthy and great tasting. My fav chocolate is bars made with 90% cocoa, this is sweeter tasting to me. I didn't do 5 stars because I wish it was cheaper and I feel like there should be other flavor variations, maybe add cinnamon or something, i'm not sure.

column9: TASTES LIKE AN OLD SHOE DIPPED IN COCONUT OIL
column10: GROSS!!!  I really tried to like this..so did my hubby and my son.  We all said YUCK!!!!!!!!The men dumped half a pound of sugar in it and still hate it.They both said.. just eat coconut oil with cocoa powder and no sugar - same thing!

I fell in love with Stash chocolate mint tea two years ago.  I am thrilled to be able to buy it now in an economical and environmentally friendly way.  This is used for my private use and I've felt uncomfortable with all the many boxes I've gone through in order to have my six bag a day tea fix.  If you are a tea junkie and care about our landfill situation then go for broke and purchase this way and save yourself a couple of hundred bucks.

I have tried many OOlong teas and this is by far the best.  It has a wonderfully light coconut, mango flavor.  The two flavors blend well together, neither one overpowering the other.  I will definitely buy again.
really nice tea, and smells wonderful. I enjoy it with a teaspoon of "sugar in the raw."  Stores well as is wrapped in foil. I usually buy the box of 100 teabags since it is an excellent value

column9: A ginormous box of 1,000 tea bags
column10: Stash Chamomile Herbal Tea is tea bags with dried, crushed chamomile flowers.Honestly, as far as I'm concerned, chamomile is chamomile. I suppose that when you use loose flowers you get sediment in the cup and I have seen this happen with some brands of chamomile tea bags, these don't do that.I have also had organic chamomile (this isn't) but I can't taste the difference.Each bag is individually packaged and that is either good or bad depending on how and where you use it and if you are concerned about excessive packaging.If you really, truly like chamomile tea, or own a restaurant, this ginormous box of 1,000 single-serving tea bags is a good choice.
Fast shipping. Smells good when you open the tea bag - tastes like watered down coffee with a faint mint aftertaste. Not recommended.

Dried pears are my absolute favorite dried fruit but they aren't easy to find. Trader Joe's used to sell them for $4 a pound but discontinued them several years ago, to my dismay.While these cost more, they are very good and still a decent deal if you have Amazon Prime. I didn't think they tasted any different from the ones I've had in the past.

I've been looking for good dried pears since I ate some in a dried fruit mix and loved them.  These are just as good as those first ones I ate.  Tender, moist, and sweet, these are about as close to candy as dried fruit gets while being relatively low in sugar and high in fiber.
These dried pear were packaged well and tastes better than Mariani dried pear in the combo package.  The resealable tab is well designed.  I don't taste the sulfur dioxide that much.

They come in packages that are folded, not sealed shut, and the quality was uneven.  Perhaps 20% of the pears are truly soft and moist, the rest are varying shades of dried out.  Will not be buying these again.I received some dried pears as a present years ago and those pears were uniformly big, moist and juicy!  I wish I remembered the brand, cause good dried pears are wonderful!

purchased the Bergin Nut Company PEARS AS A GIFT FOR MY BROTHER TWICE...EXTREMELY TASTY AND FRESH..THEY COME IN A THREE PACK AND STAY FRESH FOR A LONG TIME...WILL DEFINITELY ORDER MORE IN THE FUTURE...THANKS FOR MAKING A GREAT PRODUCT AVAILABLE...LOVE AMAZON...YOU ARE THE BEST
Okay but not the best dried pears I have ever had.  Not real big and juicy - acceptable in taste.
I used these in my blender to make "pearsauce".  Great in cereal or oatmeal.  No chemical taste.  Good price on a hard to find item.

column9: Do not buy this.  It has strong sulfur dioxide taste. Yuck!
column10: The dry pears have a strong sulfur dioxide tastes.  It tastes yuck.  I do not recommend this product at all.  I'll contact the company and try to return mine.

I like the taste of dried fruit, but usually I feel as if I'm giving my jaws a workout whenever I eat some. These pears are soft, almost creamy in consistency, and sweet beyond belief. I had intended to chop the pears and use them in baked goods, but I guess I have to wait for the next batch to do that!

I must admit, these taste very good and info on the box says "Indulgence you can feel good about". Don't believe that for one minute.The second ingredient in this product is sugar. It's a tiny, thin 2.5 inch square (approx 17g or slightly over half an ounce). Look how this product compares to a fun size snickers bar (15g)  Granola Thin  /  Fun Size SnickersCalories:  80 /  72Cal from fat: 35  /  33Total Fat  4g  /  3.7gSaturated fat  1.5g  /  1.3gCholesterol  0  /  2mgSodium  75mg  /  39.9mgTotal Carb  11gm  /  8.9gmSugars  6gm  /  7.4gmProtein  1gm  1.2gmThese actually compare somewhat UN-favorably with the candy bar, at least in terms of fat, sodium and carbs. Granted, the difference is not huge. What bugs me is it's essentially candy masquerading as "healthy". Also, with both the fiber is fairly negligible. I'm not saying they come right out and say it's "healthy" but they certainly do imply it.Lets talk about cost. There are 10 packages in a box. Each package is .6oz. I paid about 3.40 for my box. I paid that for about 6-7 ounces of product. So if I were buying them by the pound, I guess that would be over 8.00 for 1 pound. For that price, I can buy myself a nice steak.As I said before, these do taste good but I find the cost is prohibitive and they aren't really any better for you than candy and are very small. I doubt I'll be buying them again and for sure they are not an "indulgence" I would feel good about giving to kids.

column9: Product is wonderful but this package is way overpriced!!!
column10: These granola thins are a great product.  Absolutely delicious and still healthy.  It's so hard to find something that tastes really good with low calories and carbs.  This particular package of three 10-pk boxes is outrageously overpriced as I picked up a 10-pk box at Kroger the other day for $3.39.  I'm thinking $19.99 for 3 boxes is a huge profit for somebody.  I love buying snacks on Amazon but I'll stick to the grocery for these until a better deal comes along.

This product tastes good, but like the other person posted.....this is WAY OVERPRICED!  >$8/box???!!!!  I love the taste; the sugar content is not too terrible; and the calories aren't too bad, for me anyway, but the thins ARE very crumbly; I eat them over a plate.  This is NOT a snack-in-the-car treat, unless of course you don't mind getting crumbs and possibly chocolate all over yourself and your vehicle.

column9: Get Nature Valley Oats N' Dark Chocolate Instead
column10: That tastes much better and more filling, and I think they're healthier.  I have been buying these Oats N' Dark Chocolate for a while until I saw a big package of these granola thins at Costco... it was interesting at first, but I realize it tastes more like milk chocolate than dark. Plus, pay attention to the interesting comparison to the Snickers Fun Size by another commenter.

Good concept, poor execution.  Individually packaged pressed granola with chocolate holding it together.  They are crumbly, messy, and not very tasty.  Don't even think about giving them to your children for a snack... What a mess!  Not to mention, over-priced.  I bought them because I enjoy other Nature Valley products, and had a coupon for a new product.  Will not purchase again, would not recommend.

These are delicious and i don't buy healthy foods so i don't care about the candy bar comparison. I bought the chocolate ones and always want to eat two. but as other reviewers have stated, they are ridiculously messy. crumbs every where. you have to look in the mirror when your done eating to make sure you don't have chocolate on your face. you must also wash your hands. this is not a granola bar for on-the-go, which is why i buy granola bars in the first place. i have never eaten a granola bar sitting down at a table with a plate and napkin. they are yummy but i think i'd rather have a chewy bar.

While these taste good, they are far too messy.  I am consistently challenged by them in attempting to avoid both (1) getting crumbling granola all over my desk and floor and (2) having the chocolate melt all over my fingers.  I have had granola bars my whole life and I am well aware of the crumbs they can generate--but these bars will send granola flying just by opening the wrapper and the chocolate on these bars melts instantly upon any bodily contact (like fingers).  I bought these as a snack of convenience, which they most definitely are not.

I love Nature Valley Crunchy Granola Bars and I love chocolate. But these new granola thins are disappointing and not up to the same standards of other Nature Valley products, imo. They're simply granola wafers with chocolate on top and the granola wafers taste old (something that I've never experienced with other Nature Valley products.) To top it off, they're actually expensive in comparison to Nature Valley's other, much better, products. If you want a good granola and chocolate product, try Nature Valley's Crunchy Dark Chocolate bars, which offer a mixture of cocoa and oats, with chunks of dark chocolate. Unlike these, they're delicious!

Between the crumble factor and the extremely messy "chocolate" (which tasted more like MOCK-olate) coating, these snacks are a ridiculous waste of calories, effort and money. The chocolate sticks to the cardboard tray and melts immediately upon contact with your fingers. The bar itself disintegrates all over the place when you bite into it. A terribly executed idea.

I have been waiting for Amazon to carry this item. My son LOVES them, and Costco was carrying them in bulk. Now they are not, but they can be purchased at Target for $2.97 a box!! This vendor is ripping people off!!! I love the convenience of shopping with Amazon, but I refuse to pay this ridiculous price!!

column9: Taste good but amount of packaging is ridiculous for a 'nature' conscious company!
column10: I have to say these taste really good but if you have any kind of environmental conscience then you can't help but feel guilty about the unnecessary individual packaging! Each thin is in it's own plastic wrapper and has a thin piece of paper attached. I just feel it's a bit rich when the companies website says 'Enjoy Nature' and they so obviously play on the nature conscious theme. They are tasty but there are other nice things out there so for this reason I won't buy them again.

These snacks are very good for portion control, half the size of a playing card, so they are small. I could definitely eat more then one, but they do curve the sweet tooth so instead of a piece of candy or soda, opt for this instead. Wish the amount was more then 10 in a box would buy them again, well for on the go.

column9: the one and only box I will ever buy of these
column10: They are super small, super crumbly, and more chocolate sticks to the little tray than to the granola.  Not worth the 80 calories I have to put into my calorie tracker to eat one of these.  I won't be buying another box.

If you are thinking of buying this product, make sure to glance at the nutrition facts! These are a tasty snack, but they are absolutely an indulgence.  With little protein (1g), and less than a gram of dietary fiber, all that you're getting here is a snack to satiate a craving for something sweet.  I'd rather have an Oreo...

column9: Could they possibly waste more packaging?
column10: I didn't realize each would be individually wrapped or I wouldn't have bought it, too much waste and too much mess spills when you open. I also don't taste dark chocolate, and it says milk right on the ingredients, so I think they're full of it. I have to eat over the garbage can because everything spills, then wash my hands because the incredibly thin layer of milk chocolate melts immediately. Refrigerated, it's not nearly as bad, but that's silly for a simple snack.As a single, it's entirely unsatisfying. It's so small that it's almost inert, it does nothing to stave off hunger or bring back alertness. They should have packed two to a pack, that would at least put a dent in it, while still being at comparable to all of their other bars; buy one of them instead. Just assume you'll need two at a time. Hey, there's such a thing as too few calories.What amazes me is that the label contains four different sugars: One sucrose, and three different ways of saying maltodextrin. Obviously NV believes consumers are stupid and will gladly try to hide the actual level of sugars (it would be the first ingredient if all four were added together).Note that they've just started selling boxes of 48 instead of 36 in stores, so Amazon might get them soon.

column9: Not even close to dark chocolate
column10: The "chocolate" is definitely not dark chocolate or even milk chocolate. It's some kind of chocolate cream that just tastes like sugar. I was very disappointed by this fake chocolate. I'm unsure as to the quality of the granola as it's not very filling. Also you get just one thin per pack.I will stick to their Oats 'n Dark Chocolate bars in the future.

I agree with the other reviewers regarding the price. I just bought a box of 36 at Sam's for $8.98 including tax. I eat two each day, Monday-Friday, so these should last me at least 3 weeks.As for the comments about them being messy, I am convinced that these reviewers are either parents or just plain incompetent snackers. There's nothing difficult about eating them. All you have to do is rip the package down the middle, break off a piece using the package itself if you choose to, pick it up and eat it.If you stick one squarely on your face, you will get chocolate on your face.If you open the package and flip it upside down, you will get crumbs. It's granola pressed together, and it will make crumbs; if you want cardboard, go buy Kashi.

column9: Great Product, Bad Price on Here
column10: I am not big on granola so I didn't know if I would like these or not,these things are great! My husband and I bought them from the grocery store and they were 2.98 for a box. So the price of a 3 pack is a horrible price, I would tell everyone to buy from a store instead. The chocolate does melt kind of fast, and it can be messy with crumbs but well worth it to me.
Found these at Costco once then never again.....was happy to be able to buy them on Amazon...They are wonderful!!! The perfect quick pick me up snack.....

i have to say i really enjoy reading the diversity of reviews for this product.  tasty/not tasty, overpriced, not heathy, etc.  bottom line for me is the taste and i'm on the tasty side.  the dark chocolate with the whole grain cracker is a great combination.  my complaint is how the chocolate is stuck on the cardboard liner the square comes in.  is it "healthy"?  eh.  who cares.  how much stuff in the breakfast bar isle is healthy.  most are over-priced candy bars.  it is what it is and i likes it!

column9: Mistake in the pricing for sure!!!!!!
column10: This product is not worth more than $2.50 per box. The grocery stores are selling it for around $4 per box (pack of 10). This vendor is surely ripping off customers with this price. Amazon...........please do something about this vendor.

column9: So yummy it's almost a cookie
column10: This product is so good. Because of the layer of chocolate(or peanut butter) it tastes more like a cookie than a granola bar. The problem with this is that I just want to eat another one. It's so very nice to find something that is healthy that can satisfy my sweet tooth.Thank you Nature's Valley.

So right off the bat i should let you know that i have IBS. my symptoms have gradually gotten worse over the years and my doctor(s) have no idea what is wrong with me. My bowels are so irregular that i have been afraid that i'm developing a dependency on my medicines.  When i was in the UK for new years this year i had an episode...a bad one.  Pharmacies in Scotland are a tricky place but very cool since they are more concerned with preventative care then we are.  the dude (chemist) said i should try CaliFig, it's an all natural fig syrup that helps keep you regular.  i bought some and it was like a miracle! Both types of irregularity as well as many of my other symptoms literally disappeared. if i had known that finding it and getting it shipped to the US was so difficult i would have bought a case but alas i foolishly thought it was easy to find i just had never seen it before.When i ran out of the syrup after arriving back home i decided to try this Baar version.  it works but i wont lie to you; not as well. I'll keep using it till i can find a CaliFig source that is not overpriced in shipping. If you have digestion issues of any kind i'd recommend giving this a try: 2 TBL every night!

column9: Oh so Yummy!!! Plain Fig Syrup with No Additives
column10: This is the stuff to buy!I looked up "Califig"...and that has all sorts of other stuff added: SORBITOL (a sugar), artificial colors, and Sodium Benzoate (which is related to Benzine)If you have digestive issues, I would not put things in my body that will irritate the issue.Ooooo.....Try a ginger, peppermint tea sweetened with fig syrup. That would probably do you really well, if you like the CaliFig.Fig syrup is great for coughs, sore throats, asthma, anemia, catarrh, colitis, gout, and digestive ulcers.I drizzle it over cereal or oatmeal, mix it in with juice....Mix it with milk and it tastes almost like chocolate.yum yum YUM!It is very high in vitamins and minerals..Goolge it!I bought 6 bottles.My kids love it!

The Pacific Brand "Cream of" soups are a great replacement for those to have to go gluten free.  The taste is as good or better than the traditional condensed soups.  The only reason it's four stars is that most often, you must add some GF flour or other GF thickener as it can be a tish on the thin side (compared to traditional soups).  Will buy this again and again and so thankful to have found a GF version that is high quality and tastes just as good, if not BETTER!

My husband is allergic to wheat, therefore a Gluten Free diet is a must.  I have hoped to see one day a gluten free version of "Cream of" type of soups.  Well!  Kudos to Pacific Natural Foods for coming out with Cream Celery, Cream of Chicken and Cream of Mushrooms and they all are Gluten Free!  Oh we love this stuff, I ordered a case of each - they are a must in my pantry.  This stuff is great for quick meals - including rice and chicken dish using Cream of Mushroom (like Campbell's soup recipe).Hope to see more companies pay attention to the need of more gluten free stuff!  I am a HUGE fan of Pacific Natural Foods for good!

I really wanted to love this product since I use a lot of cream of celery soup as sauce and casserole base. Celery is one of the "dirty Dozen" foods that should only be eaten in their organic forms. If I did a blindfold test on this soup, I would have called it a very salty cream of mushrom, with a slightly unpleasant after taste. My original order was a "subscribe and Save, and I neglected to cancel before the second shipment arrived. Ouch! A real disappointment.

I've been looking for this soup organically and not in an aluminum can.  Trying to stay away from BPA when possible.  I use this soup in a recipes and it has been a great replacement to the stuff in a can.  I don't eat this soup plain, but it's been working out well in my recipes!
It is great having cream soups for recipes again since I cannot eat gluten! Tastes better than Campbell's. I feel better serving it because it is not full of chemicals as well.

I tried this boxed cream of celery soup in 2 dishes recently and BOTH turned out fabulous.  Although I must admit it is not a very strong flavor of celery, it works just great if you add in one Rapunzel Sea Salt/Herb bouillion cube and some water to 1/2 of the package. Then I just stir it in to my rice or quinoa dish and put a little poultry seasoning in.  BOTH TIMES everyone was WOWED!! (Of course, I added in sautéed onions and garlic in one dish and onions, garlic, red peppers and celery in the other dish.)Regardless, I just signed up for the Subscribe and Save for this new Pacific Condensed Cream of Celery Soup, because my husband is not onlyGF but is allergic to tomatoes (Arrgh...).YAY FOR COOKING WITH SAUCES AGAIN!  THANK YOU AND BLESS YOU, PACIFIC FOODS!  You are on my "A-List" forever!!!

We were glad to finally find some Gluten Free soups to use. There are many times that when I go to make something that it calls for soups and when cooking gluten free it's hard sometimes to find the right thing to substitute. Now we've found it!
When my boyfriend found out he was to be GF, he thought he had to give up his favorite dishes, especially those with cream soups.  I have found this cream of celery soup does the job.

Yeah I agree, I've been using this for years and when the local stores quit carrying it (for whatever reason they do stuff like that), I was glad to see it here, and loaded up.  By the time you cook your rice this will be more than ready, and it's a great sauce base to start from if you want to use half at a time.  Somehow they lucked out and managed to get the flavors just right, and they haven't mucked it up since.

column9: Wonderful Taste and Easy to Make
column10: I love this Taste of Thai Peanut Sauce Mix.  It is spicy and flavorful, but not too spicy that I can't tolerate it.  The sauce comes in two packets and all you have to do is mix it with some coconut milk and warm it up.  It is delicious over white rice and chicken or tofu. Add a little cilantro and scallions on top and you have a wonderful meal.
very good. Made for a quicker meal, family really liked it. Good strong peanut flavor comes thru.

column9: The Best Taste and Easiest Prep
column10: I have been using this product for years and it is marvelous.  Take a (boneless) chicken breast and dredge in the peanut bake mix.  Place any extra mix in the botton of the dish.I place foil over the dish, and then take it off ten minutes prior to the chicken breast being done.  This will condense down the juices that have gathered and make a marvelous sauce to put over mashed/baked potatoes. Watch closely the last five minutes so that it doesn't burn in the bottom of the pan due to sugar in the mix.  This is an easy, easy dish to prep, and it is "company worthy".  It does have a mild to medium spicy (depending on your palette) kick to it.

I bought this based on the rave reviews given here, but my experience was quite different. The sauce had an overpowering plastic or artificial flavor. Imagine a 99-cent frozen dinner of noodles and peanut sauce, and you'll be pretty close. I actually threw them all away.
I'm a fan of the Thai Peanut Sauce, Very much so.  I find it to be a delectable treat which I enjoy with my family.  Quick, easy you know.
Just what we were looking for. Makes for a quick and easy meal with noodles and fresh veggies. Great taste.

I love peanut sauce.  I hadn't tried a dried-sauce mix before.  This one has potential; the flavors are not bad underneath.  But the "underneath" is far underneath a lot of sugar.  I finished the original meal I made with the sauce but threw out the second packet in the box.Tastes differ, and clearly, this mix has fans.  I rarely post negative food reviews because many people interpret the criticism personally.  If you know that you like it, then Amazon's price is a bit lower than my local grocery store's where it is sold 2/pack. I'm posting this review to suggest that if you're thinking about buying the box of 12 on the basis of reviews alone--don't.  Try it first.  I've tried many new, locally unobtainable food items on the basis of reviews here, and usually, the reviews are reasonably accurate.  Not in this case.  But this mix is available in my out-in-the-sticks grocery store, so it might be in yours, too.  The sauce mix seems to be more widely available than the peanut bake mix.

We have used "A Taste of Thai Peanut Sauce" mix for about 5 years now. Mixing the packet with one can of coconut milk makes it is so easy to use. The taste is pretty good with a bit of spice. Of the prepackaged peanut sauce we like this one the best (our favorite was discontinued 5 years ago) and we have tried LOTS. It is great to pour over vegetables, meat, and rice. Even my kids all like it.

I am really pleased with this product because it is very tasty & both gluten and dairy free.  It is very difficult to find sauces that are both gluten & dairy free.  It's pretty pricey in the store, but much more reasonable when bought in bulk as I found here on Amazon.
We have come to rely on this product for making Phad Thai. Add it to rice noodles with a some chopped turnip or radishes. Add some shrimp or scallops, and a dash of chilli pepper. Great!

I ordered this popcorn specifically because it was GMO Free. Wonderful taste and big kernels. We liked it so much we ordered another to stock up.  When our 2nd shipment arrived it came as small cardboard box with no interior packaging (I mean nothing just a box) and popcorn spilling out of the seems. Gross! That's why I had to give it a 3 stars. Had shipping been primo I would have given this product a 5. This is my 1st ever review, hope it's helpful.

column9: Our Search For the Best Popcorn
column10: Having a bowl of popcorn in the evening is a real treat at our house.  We've tried several methods of popping to perfect that just-right, melt in your mouth tenderness.  Seems that letting the steam escape while it pops is a key factor (as in the making of "kettle corn"). And then for a great cooking oil, we like coconut, which doesn't burn, and also imparts a wonderful flavor.  In addition, it is a healthful alternative. But one of the most important ingredients to the perfect batch of popcorn is the raw product itself.  We are delighted with our recent purchase at Amazon of Great Northern Bulk Popcorn, which has to be the most tender we have tried.  This is also an Organic product, and, with free shipping included, made it a real bargain!  SVM

I read all the reviews online for popcorn and decided on this product.  It arrived very quickly and was packaged sufficiently.  The popcorn itself was fabulous!!  Double the popped kernel size of the grocery store variety.  Tastes wonderful!!  I would highly recommend this popcorn and wouldn't hesitate to order from this company again!

This is my 2nd 50# bag of Great Northern popcorn that I've purchased.  Most importantly, it's organic!!  The kernels ALL pop nice and big and don't have a lot of the "kernel" left on.  It's very tasty and has become addictive!  It's my favorite popcorn ever.

We love popcorn and eat it just about every week.  We've used everything from microwave packages to Redenbacher loose popcorn, but I was looking for a cheaper way to get popcorn in bulk.  At the time I bought this popcorn, I got free shipping with Amazon's SuperSaver shipping.  My cost was .73 cents per pound.  As of today there's a shipping fee, which makes it quite a bit more expensive per pound.The popcorn arrived in a large "feed bag" without any outer box to protect it.  The bag was quite dirty from the UPS man's truck, but I poured it all into a food-grade 5 gallon bucket (available at Lowe's with a gasketed lid) and into a kitchen canister. The popcorn itself was clean and bug-free.I popped some for our weekly movie night, and everyone liked it.  The kernels pop up nice and fluffy, and there weren't many duds in the pan.  50 lbs. should last us a year or more, but we like to stock up on foods we enjoy anyway.Depending on whether or not you can get it with free shipping, this is a good deal on good quality popcorn.  I'll buy it again when this is gone - if they're offering free shipping.

As a popcorn fan I ordered Amazon's 50 lb bag,  popcorn is a good whole food that is easy to fix and easy to eat but besides that I grind it to make a breakfast dish of cornmeal mush cereal, Which is delicious with a little honey and canned milk on it.  From the ground pop corn we also make nourishing corn bread,  An all around good item for your food storage program is popcorn from Amazon. have a good one while I munch my popcorn sprinkled with olive oil and sea salt from Amazon.

Hello , Well in the house we eat a lot of popcorn ...while doing cookouts to movie watching.. so we bought a big popcorn machine ..we have tried a lot of different kinds of popcorn  and find that Great Northern Popcorn is the best..It pops up light and fluffy with a great taste even without topping it with salt or butter and stays fresh for days in a zip lock bag .. so we give it a 5 star rating...Thanks for makinggreat products.. The Sobliros Family

I am very VERY pleased with this purchase.  I purchased 100 lbs last week, and went and purchased another 100 lbs last night because of how happy I am with the purchase.  The kernels are top quality, and being non-GMO to boot!  I have a large popcorn machine that we use a lot, and I couldn't get over the difference in using this corn to the regular kind I usually buy.  The popcorn was fluffier, and really tasty!I am very pleased!

column9: It Doesn't Appear to Be Organic...
column10: This popcorn is non-GMO, which means it isn't genetically modified. Nowhere on the bag does it claim to be organic.  While all organic corn needs to be non-GMO, not all non-GMO corn is organic.  Corn is genetically modified to make it resistant to pests and disease.  Non-GMO corn not grown organically is frequently sprayed with pesticides.  So Great Northern Popcorn needs to make it clear whether or not it is claiming this is an organic product, because the bag doesn't back up what is stated in the Amazon description.  If you search "organic" on the Great Northern Popcorn website, "no results" comes back.  Great Northern...is this corn truly organic, or simply non-GMO?

column4: Leah M. Brown "Leah Marie Brown, Author"
column9: Lawd!  A great taste of Nawlins!
column10: On a sultry July morning, a few years before Katrina blew into town, a friend and I wandered into the frenetic, powder-sugar dusted Cafe du Monde for an early cup of coffee and the pastries we had heard so much about.  We were hot, sweaty, and more than a little worn out from having hoofed all over the historic district.  It would take more than a few Dunkin Donuts to revive our exausted, jaded spirits and a whole lot more than a Krispee Kream to skewer our skepticism.The pastries needed to be fresh, hot, and Paris-pretty to impress us.What we had that morning (several plates of steaming, sinfully-sweet, perfectly-powdered beignets) were tiny pillows of pastry perfection.  The beignets were so good, we made several more early morning trips to Cafe du Monde during our stay in New Orleans.Once home, I experienced a serious post-perfect-beignet let-down.  Krispee Kream no longer cut it.I was thrilled when I discovered I could buy Cafe du Monde's beignet mix online.  I ordered several boxes, stocked up on a truck-load of powdered sugar, and anxiously waited by my mailbox.  When the much-coveted beignet mix was finally delivered, I wasted no time in firing up the oil and brewing a pot of coffee.I was very pleased with the beignet mix.  The directions were easy to follow (just add water) and the amount of mix in the box was generous for the price.  Once properlly prepared, the beignets were just as delicious as those served at Cafe du Monde (of course, you do have that tiresome clean-up when you make them at home that you don't have when you go to the cafe in New Orleans, but all truly great things come with a price).Note:  Be sure to follow the directions precisely.  If you do not roll your dough out to the suggested thickness, the beignets will not puff properlly.  Too thin and they will be crispy and flat.  Too thick and they will not puff but will be cakey.  Also, make sure you heat your oil to 370 degrees.  Correct oil temperature is crucial to making golden, ambrosial beignets!  ****  For more information on making good beignets, you might want to visit the Cafe du Monde website.

Always look forward to the down home treats. Could have picked up elsewhere at other locations I was told about for cheaper, but didn't have time. It arrived on time as scheduled and was enjoyed by family, and the kids. Looking forward to making some for coworkers soon. Good stuff you don't have to wait to get your hands on while on the road.

column9: Simplify Making Beignets at Home with this Mix
column10: This easy to use mix for beignets using the Cafe du Monde recipe produces delicious beignets without a lot of fuss.  It is a simple matter of adding water to right amount of mix from the box and a minor amount of rolling before frying in a shallow pan to create tasty beignets at home.  There is plenty of mix in the box for several small batches.

I love this stuff.Beignets are little puffs of golden fried dough, smothered in powdered sugar. It is difficult to eat a beignet from Cafe Du Monde without getting powdered sugar down your front. They are delicate, melt in your mouth morsels of yummy-ness.If you can get to New Orleans and have the real thing then lucky you. If you are like me and live far away from New Orleans; and if you are craving a good beignet, you can buy this box and whip up your own.You get this box, you follow the directions on the back exactly, don't skimp on the powdered sugar and you will have your own little pockets of yummy goodness in your mouth. Two Notes: First: This is not a calorie free, low calorie, low fat snack. This is something you do for fun with the grandkids, to impress guests, or because you simply don't count calories. Second: Be sure you follow the directions exactly. Cafe Du Monde knows what they are doing and they do it well. Do not try to improve perfection.Worth the money.Enjoy.

Got this as a Christmas gift as I put it on my wish list. Looked pretty good. Within the price range of family.However, I am used to buying premium tea from other sources. And now I know why and why I will continue to do so.I was first shocked to find that the tea was in shards, crumbled pieces. This takes it down a notch for experienced, premium tea drinkers. It makes one think we're getting the leftovers of the higher grade harvests. When infused, the leaves maintain a flat, crumbled shape, they don't unfold into beautiful leaf structures. I believe this hinders the flavor of the infusion.The flavor? The madarin is very nice. A pleasant, citrus flavor, subtle, delicate. However, it's difficult to detect a very noticable white tea flavor. Contrary to popular opinion, white tea does indeed carry a sweet soft tea flavor. In some ways the citrus notes overpower the tea flavor. Perhaps this is to cover up a lower grade white tea harvest.It's not horrible, just disappointing. But, you get what you pay for and three tins at the price offered, you'll get a lot of cups of tea, just not the best quality. BTW, you can infuse this tea more than once, but if you want to save it in another container in the refrigerator for the next infusion, be prepared to have to scrape it out of the tea strainer because it infuses flat against the screen.

Coconut water, unfortunately, does not match these expectations.When I first tried it, I couldn't quite place the taste.  It wasn't until a student of mine tried it and cringed, made a face, and commented that it tasted like glue that I recognized the flavor..no, I've never tasted glue, but if you taste the Vita Coco you'll understand what I mean. I froze a half dozen of these and took them to the ball field with me, and after a half hour of baseball, these did a fantastic job of quenching everyone's thirst, with minimal wrinkling of noses.So to sum up, the product, if you are purchasing it primarily for the high potassium content and as an all natural sports drink, does its job admirably.  It rehydrates you and definitely helps in preventing any muscle cramps.  However, if you're thinking about purchasing this merely because it sounds as if it'd taste good, I'd suggest you think twice, or try a single box first to make sure you actually enjoy the taste(I believe they are sold at many supermarkets, I know I've seen them at Whole Foods before).

column9: From someone who grew up on coconut milk/water!!!!!
column10: I ordered two to try out from Amazon but while waiting on the delivery, I was out shopping when I observed a lot of companies were suddenly cashing out on coconut milk/water! I bought one brand-name from Lucky's Super Market and another brand from Walgreen's next door. Being of Polynesian heritage and homegrown from the islands but living on the mainland, I thought, "Hmmm..all these centuries coconuts been around, suddenly its being pitched as nutritional & interesting. Let's see what the catch is". Finally, VitaCoCo came. I tasted it and spit it right out. It didnt taste like coconut water to our family 'at all', not even from an over-ripe coconut. Then I looked to see where it was produced. Before I go further let me explain something to those who may not know. Agriculture for fruits are always better on tropical islands, or from the Caribbean islands. You won't find any fruits more richer in juice or sweeter anywhere else in the world. Vita CoCo says it is produced by a company in Latin America, Brazil. Produced for All Markets Inc. New York, NY.My sister then poured some into a glass and screamed, "OMG They're ripping people off! It's watered down!" She said that because pure coconut milk has a milky color to it. Some less, some more but never crystal clear. The younger the fruit, the richer, more nutritional, and milky the coconut milk. The more mature the fruit, the sweeter & thinner the milk. As the fruit ripens the coconut water gets converted into the solid meat of the fruit. The meat then becomes more nutritional then the milk. So I told her that they weren't ripping consumers off because it says, 100% pure coconut WATER. It's either a little coconut milk diluted with a lot of pure water, or this is what Brazilian coconuts taste like. And it seems like they're using 'over-riped' coconuts. Which makes sense. Then they could also market the meat of the coconut.As for those who have to have potassium every night like my aunt, DO NOT rely on Vita Coco's ad. My aunt finished off the 17 fl oz of Vita CoCo and still woke up with painful side effects from taking prednisone. This is also how we know Vita CoCo is using over-ripe less nutritional coconuts, or watering it down. I ended up having to prepare her daily one banana she's suppose to have before bedtime. Drink mango or guava juice all! The most nutritional of all island fruits ;)

I use this to replicate a Vietnamese curry I grew up with:To a large pot add the following:1 can of Karee Curry Paste with 1 can (14 oz) of coconut milk, 2-3 cups water, 3lbs of chicken, 2 large or 3 medium potatoes (cut to bite-sized cubes) and 2-3 carrots (same as potatoes), 1 large onion (cut into quarters), and a few whole jalepenos (remove the stem).  You can also add a stick of lemongrass.  You can also substitute coconut milk with regular milk, and eggplant for the chicken (veggie option).Bring to boil then simmer for 20-30 minutes.  Add corn starch to bring the soup to its desired consistency. I like it thicker and stew-like.  Salt+MSG to taste.  You will need MSG to bring the flavor out - I use 1 part MSG per 1 part salt.Server over rice or with french bread.  You can spritz in some lime (my parents always do) but I like it without the lime.I'm lazy so this does end up over cooking the chicken a bit, but it ensures the potatoes and carrots are soft and mushy the way I like them - plus no extra steps.  Make sure the water covers the chicken.  Chicken breast seems to dry out, leg quarters stay tender.  If you use eggplant I like to use larger chunks (1.5" or so) since they tend to mush up  a bit.Anyways I love this curry paste.  I would get "curry pangs" and have to make this every couple weeks while I was in college.  So easy to do and it would feed me for a few days.
