As I have mentioned, I'm not a big fan of these pre=prepared meals, but somethine we just need something in a hurry, and this sort of thing fills the bill very nicely.  Keep a couple on hand.

I was actually pretty hesitant to review this, because I was not the one that actually cooked it. However, it looked pretty easy to cook. The good thing is that it tasted better than I thought it would. I normally don't buy Velveeta dinners, because I'm not really impressed with how the cheese taste. However, since I was able to add meat to it, it was better than expected.

column9: Not for kids who are stuck on the classic kraft mac n cheese
column10: My kids LOVE the classic kraft mac and cheese, so i thought i'd see if they liked this. Of course, they didn't because it's different from their norm. Why break something that isn't broken? However, my dad LOVED it. This mac n cheese has more seasonings which my dad loved and thought was a pleasant surprise. He loves hearty meals so the classic mac doesn't do it for him. It was very easy to make. just like any other hamburger helper or kraft boxed meal.

column9: A quick and easy dinner for when you are pressed for time
column10: I was never a fan of Hamburger Helper, but I must admit that I like the new Kraft Velveeta Skillets Dinner Kits. When you whip this kit up, you get elbow macaroni pasta and ground beef, all in the creamy Velveeta cheese sauce. As with all similar Kraft dishes you must be a big fan of that cheese, as it does tend to dominate the taste of the dish.Everyone in my house seems to love it, and some days, when I am pressed for time, it is nice to have a dinner that I can throw together quickly and easily. Is it great food? Of course not, I definitely wouldn't recommend that you make it often. But, sometimes it really works!(Review of Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheesburger Skillets Dinner Kit)

column9: Another of these good Velveta Dinners!
column10: It sounds like this is good and it is.  I would rate it slightly higher than the cheeseburger mac that hamburger helper does.  However, it should not go unnoticed that on sale at the grocery, HH is often a dollar or less per box. The price on this item on the Zon here is pretty far out there, so from that perspective add a star if you find this in the grocery or a good online sale.  Subtract one if you are going to buy it on some of the high prices it's offered for here.I'll give Kraft credit here for saving their brand name for me and doing a set of quality items in the package. The taste combined with my drained washed and reseasoned ground beef was very good.  I like to add a little red wine, some mushrooms and some half and half to the sauce on these to give them a classier taste.  The cheese held up well. I took exception to those eazy mac things they did up a few years ago.  I can't imagine anyone liking them unless they were starving!  The question I have on this product is why...  Yes there's improvement over HH, but not that much, they don't do much different, if they sent it with a can of pre-cooked ground beef, and you could just heat it up that would be something. I don't get how this can compete, especially at the price.

My family hates hamburger helper so I expected this to be the same.  However they did eat this. It isn't gourmet food, or even great food.  but it is edible for a quick no hassle meal. Clean up is a breeze as it all cooks in the skillet.  Would I make it all the time? No.  But I will keep a box in the pantry for emergency meals.

This is very yummy and a step above your regular Hamburger Helper types. I honestly felt like I was eating a cheeseburger we all loved this one and will continue to use it. This was great with salad and bread and most importantly very quick and yummy.

column9: Good taste, cheese goes a long way
column10: I really like this product. It has good flavor and is not too salty, although I do find that you actually only need to use half the cheese sauce to get plenty of flavor. The seasoning packet was a really good too. We use this with ground turkey, but we found its really excellent with mushrooms too. The elbow macaroni is larger than the usual variety, making it a friendly size for kids to pick up. Its very similar to hamburger helper, and I think its really good.

This was a life saver while watching my nephews. I wasn't sure what to make for dinner while keeping track of an 18 month old so the one skillet made it a breeze to cook and clean up.  This is better than running out for food and surprisingly tasty.  I would say keep this in the house because on those days you don't want to cook or ran out of ideas this is a great saver!  I did add a few spices to the meat and added garlic which I removed when feeding the kiddos but over all they enjoyed it and I thought it was great!

This is a SUPER quick and easy dinner. I recently had to go GF due to a bad Wheat allergy I just developed, but I LOVED this when I could eat it!!! Its easy, quick and tasty.All you need is water and ground meat to make a super easy main dish for dinner.  We used ground turkey to lower calories and be healthier. No one could tell the difference between it and ground beef.  The sauce is a good flavor and doesn't taste "fake" like some other one skillet dinner mixes (HH). Velveeta doesn't have a stong taste when eaten in a slice, but this sauce tasted really cheesy, as if it were cheddar based.  Its GREAT for those nights when you are just too tired from work to sit upright, let alone make dinner.I sadly can't eat this anymore, but if they come out with a Gluten Free version I'll be back.

The kit comes with everything you need, except for one pound of hamburger.As it has only makes 5 - 1-cup servings, we decided to make if for lunch, as it wouldn't be enough for 4 adults and 1 4 yr old who adores cheesy mac!For a change, we had no small packs of hamburger, or cooked hamburger left in the freezer, so I opted instead for a one pound pack of sausage that we had in the freezer instead. It was very simple to fry up the pork, and since it was so lean, it did not need to be drained, and then add all the pasta, seasoning packet and water to the pan. After a quick covered boil, all that was left was to add the Velveeta sauce! All in all it took less than a half hour and made up a pretty tasty lunch!My only quibble is that you need to keep an eye on when it is boiling. Ours was done in 9 minutes, not 11, as per the box. So don't leave it, or it might get too dry and burn!We ate it without any side serving, but for dinner I would serve a side salad and rolls with it. It was quite tasty and I would definitely make it again

This was a surprise, even though it had a great aroma while it was simmering, I did not expect the great tangy cheesy taste that was highly pleasing to my taste buds! It was as easy to cook as any of the skillet helpers out there but it creams them all with it's taste! The box has three packages inside the dry mac, a seasoning and the cheese sauce (yes it's a sauce not powder) and with the easy to follow instructions I had this ready to serve in aobut 30 minutes!By the way, I added half a can of corn and served it with  Broccoli Cheese Rice and it was perfect!
Easy preparation, nice to have on shelf when you need a quick meal. Nice and chessy. Can either be a side dish or the main course.  Velveeta is always to be relied upon as one the great comfort food.

column9: Delicious alternative to the 'other' brand Cheeseburger meal-in-a-box!
column10: I enjoyed this Kraft Velveeta Cheeseburger meal-in-a-box kit: simply cook up one pound of ground beef, drain, add the contents of the packets along with water, and you'll have a delicious dinner in about 15-20 minutes!  The taste here is quite nice: it's different than the 'other' brand (come on, you know, Hamburger Helper, which is a very similar product), but it's a quick and easy dinner, and quite good.  This makes up a huge helping, so cook for others or eat leftovers: I enjoyed this Velveeta 'mix' and think you will too: recommended!

I grew up on hamburger helper.  It was in my mom's arsenal for quick tasty meals.  I'm sure you could use ground turkey or ground chicken if you don't eat ground beef as a replacement for this.  My boys love when I use velveeta for our nachos, so as a pasta dish it was enjoyed!  Thanks Velveeta for coming up with a quick dish!

This is basically the Velveeta Deluxe box set, but with a 2nd set of seasoning for the meat.  Honestly this style of liquid cheese is too salty for me and then they add a salty substance for your meat as well.  I think you could easily make a healthier version with a simple box of the regular Kraft Mac & Cheese.  And if you like the liquid cheese and want to save money - just buy the Velveeta Deluxe and add your hamburger or turkeyburger (whatever) to your liking.  The difference is minimal.  I tried the Broccoli version at the same time I bought this - I had the same feeling.  So in other words, you may like it - BUT you've been warned on what you actually get for your money.

column4: Reading It All "Reading It All - Robyn"
column10: I am not going to get into the "health" factor in the Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheesburger Skillets Dinner Kit, 12.86-Ounce (Pack of 6)...I am sure that it has too much salt - most boxed meals do...I wouldn't serve this often.But for a quick dinner that is filling, creamy and cheesy for a construction worker's appetite - it works!The liquid cheese packet definitely adds to the creamy texture...something my boyfriend who likes a hearty meal noticed!

Velveeta cheese really is not my cup of tea..and the seasoning packet added a another flavor that seemed artificial and chemically to me. I am not that fussy either, I love Kraft Mac n'Cheese and the occasional Hamburger Helper so I am not a food snob. This was just not very appealing in flavor.

I hate Hamburger Helper.  Well, hate is a strong word.  It's boring.  This product, however, is not.I wanted to try this out just for curiosity's sake.  I'm a big fan of Velveeta's Shells and cheese and wondered what it would be like as a meal.  I cooked my hamburger meat-more than the recipe called for-and began the process of doing the rest of the meal.  Oops!  I forgot the spice pack.  I added it later than when the recipe said I had to add it.  Nonetheless the meal was delicious.  I plan on keeping this last minute meal in my cabinet as an emergency back-up or just to have as a planned meal.

column9: Better choices out there than this Salty Quickie.
column10: Velveeta box pastas are pretty good. Not high culinary art but solid, easy to make and tasty. That is why this was a disappointment.  First this is no easier to make than melting Velveeta and mixing in pasta and beef. Cheeseburger flavor not really. Lastly it was salty. Really salty. Not usually a problem in a house where salty snacks are adored but every person mentioned it was too much salt. I knew by the flavor and reaction that if I ever made it again I would have to only ad part of the flavor pack. Why bother though when there is hamburger helper, other Velveeta box meals or you can just make put together the ingredients yourself.  This got two stars because it's easy to make, stores for a long time, great to take on a camping trip or college dorm. It is ok, just add the flavor pack to taste instead of by directions. Better yet buy something else.

column9: Hamburger Helper Should Have No Fear
column10: This is Kraft Foods' entry into the "Hamburger Helper" market.  I prepared the meal according to the directions on the box and it delivered a perfect product in terms of consistency; it was neither runny nor too dry.  Preparation time was as described and it was easy to prepare.The most subjective part of this review is the product's taste.  While it was OK, it was just OK.  There was a slightly sour taste to the sauce (some may find this pleasing) and it was slightly gritty -- as if not all of the granules in the seasoning package had dissolved, although I feel I had stirred it thoroughly.Overall, not a bad meal but not one that I would seek out again.  I prefer the taste of the original Hamburger Helper product more.

I made this for my family last night hoping that because they love velveeta shells and cheese that they would love this Cheeseburger Mac.  Unfortunately, once you add the seasoning and it's all made, it just tastes like Hamburger Helper, which we're not fans of.  You couldn't really even tell that it was a Velveeta product.  The cheese packet in it is the signature Velveeta gooey cheese in the foil.  I think the problem for me was the seasoning mix they ask you to add when you add the water and pasta.  If I would have left that out then it might have tasted like the cheesy taste I was looking for.If your family likes Hamburger Helper and one skillet meals like that, then you will probably love this as it was a little bit better than those meals... but I won't be buying this again.

column9: Makes me want to try the other "flavors"
column10: As always, anything with Velveeta is _really_ good and after trying this dinner kit I really want to try some of the other kits they displayed on the box like the Nacho one and the BBQ chicken.  Yum!

I loved this quick meal so much (my family and kids too) that i purchased more of them at my local grocery store. Creamy Velveeta cheese, bright flavors, and perfect noodle texture melt in your mouth and will leave the kids wanting more. Even my picky eater likes this one. With the ability to cook the whole thing in 20 minutes, it's perfect for busy moms and dads.

My kids love Hamburger Helper so I figured this would be a great new product to try since anything with Velveta is good!  It was easy to make and only took a few minutes to complete.  The kids absolutely loved it and I thought it tasted great too.  My only complaint was that, visually, it was unappetizing.  It didn't look like the picture on the box.  It was kind of a grayish brown color and actually worried me a bit before I tried it.  Luckily, my kids and I don't really care how it looks so we all enjoyed it, but Kraft would benefit by working on presentation.

My wife and I have recently been turned onto Velveeta, and have begun to prefer their macaroni and cheese mix over the regular Kraft Mac & Cheese that we've bought in the past. Our kids seem to have enjoyed it too. When we saw these new skillet meals, we figured we'd give them a try. The cheeseburger meal we tried definitely wasn't something to be too excited about, but it did taste good. Throughout the whole meal, it reminded me personally of Hamburger Helper. I didn't feel like there was much of a difference other than the signature Velveeta cheese. The huge plus to all of it is that our picky kids who hardly eat anything ate up everything on their plates. To them it was another mac & cheese meal (even though there was other things thrown in), and that is all that mattered. From that perspective, the dinner was a huge success, and would definitely be something we'd want to purchase again.  It's hard to find meals where our kids will actually eat everything, and enjoy doing so. Too often than not they don't even try the meal, and yet says, "I don't like this."To sum it up, for adults, nothing too special. For kids, especially those that love mac & cheese, this was a winner for us.

When my wife and I first got together we had a pantry full of Hamburger Helpers. We both worked late hours and it was great for a quick dinner. Back then, of course, they had a whole line of different flavors and varieties, rather then the stagnant line of 'meat and cheese' they have today.Fifteen years later we still keep a few Hamburger Helpers stocked at home, but we only have them about once a month. When Velveeta came out with their version, we gave it a try. I'm not a fan of other Velveeta products, but my wife is. This product, however, has won me over. It's better then Hamburger Helper in just about every way. First, it cooks much easier... Hamburger Helper has a powdered cheese mix that gets 'clumpy' and has to be rigorously stirred in order to mixed properly. I found the easiest way is to heat the cheese, water and milk in a separate pot, then add it as a mixture when it's time. This not only reduces heating time, but makes it easier to mix. Velveeta's Cheesy Skillets doesn't have that problem... the cheese is not powdered, so it mixes in without any trouble. There's an additional seasoning packet that is powder, but takes no effort to mix it in. So cooking-wise, Velveeta wins easily.As far as taste, Velveeta is FAR better. The seasoning adds a lot more flavor, and when we went back to Hamburger Helper to finish off the last box, we found it almost bland in comparison. Velveeta is a bit more expensive, but the price is well worth it... we haven't bought Hamburger Helper since. Of course, this is not exactly the healthiest meal, but when your time is limited and you need a bailout for dinner, I'd recommend Velveeta.

column9: Not bad, but definitely tastes like a boxed meal...
column10: This is the second Velveeta skillet meal I received through the amazon Vine program. The first was Kraft Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets Dinner Kit, 14.64-Ounce (Pack of 6), and I have written a review of that product, as well, in case you'd like to compare the two.This product is clearly aimed at the same market of people who buy Hamburger Helper or Tuna Helper boxed dinners.  These meals are easy and quick to prepare - generally requiring nothing more than adding water and some pre-cooked meat to the ingredients of the box. As one might expect from the product title, this product is "cheesier" than most hamburger helper-type meals, but I also found it to be more flavorful, as well, and that was a good thing. It smelled good while cooking, looked appetizing, and my family of five enjoyed the meal. They didn't think it was anything spectacular, but no one turned up their noses at it, either.One thing that I should mention is this: My family of five downed this meal very quickly and had nothing left over for second helpings. I wouldn't really consider one box enough food for a family of five unless your family members are very light eaters. I don't even have any kids out of grade school, yet, and this wasn't enough food for us - even with all the other food set out on the table, which included bread, vegetables, and a dessert. If you have a large family or even a middle-sized family you may want to consider cooking up two portions of this meal if you're planning on satisfying everyone's appetites.

Brown up some hamburger, add the noodles, water, and the seasoning packet.  Cook it up til the water is gone, stir in the cheesy glop and its ready to eat!!Flavor:  amazingly, the seasoning packet adds the flavor of hamburger additives (pickle, mustard, onions, very weird). The cheese packet adds the usual sort of cheese like flavor of velveeta. Overall, pretty bland and very salty.Texture:  noodle mushiness is controlled by how much water you add and how long you let it cook.  Feels like you would expect.Ease of use: A+ .Overall value:  its fairly inexpensive and I suppose wouldn't be a terrible thing to have in the cupboard for those desperate nights when the kids are starving.In reality, since you have to brown the hamburger, the time factor is a little more than I'd like for something that tastes this mediocre.  In the same amount of time or less there are many tastier healthier options for your family.  But compared to other meals of this type, this one is a middle of the roader. If your kids have a thing for the taste/feel of melty Velveeta, this might be the quickie meal for you.

column4: Glenda Boozer "Live, live, live! Life is a ba...
column9: It really does taste like a cheeseburger
column10: The Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheeseburger Skillets Dinner Kit was surprisingly cheesy-tasting. I wish they had whole-grain pasta, but this is a shortcut for an easy meal. I also added a package of seasoning vegetables, which really improved it, but I bet most people, especially kids, will like it just the way it's designed to be prepared.

made this the other night and doctored it with a can of diced tomatoes and green peppers.  It was really tasty and my husband gobbled it down.  Real time saver too.  It says to cook on the stove, but you can cook it and then put it in a casserole dish in a warm oven.  I would definitely buy this again.

Draft Veleeta Utimate Cheesburger Skillets dinner is a quick way to serve dinner when time and energy is in short supply. Granted, it is far from gourmet, but the kids will probably eat it up.It's simple to prepare and all that you will need to provide is a pound of ground beef that you have already fried up in a pan. Then, add water and noodles. Once those are cooked, it is a as simple as adding the package of velveeta. Along with a vegtable, or salad, it's a decent meal whipped up quickly.The good news about the taste is that it's pretty good. However, I prefer a bit more seasoning and the cheese is rather bland. Perhaps sprinkling some sharp cheddar on top would brighten up the taste a bit. Overall, though, it's much better than its closest competitor, Hamburger Helper.

This is a comparable product to Hamburger Helper.  The quality was very good.  Ease of cooking was high.  The sauce did have a good flavor to it.  The ingridents were of good quality.  If you want a quick easy dinner that taste good, this is a good alternative.

"Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheeseburger Skillets Dinner Kit, 12.86-Ounce (Pack of 6)" is ok for what it is. It's easy and quick enough to make; except for the meat, everything you need comes in the box; and the flavor is tangy (if a bit too salty for my tastes). In all, while it wasn't my favorite mac n' cheese dish, "Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheeseburger Skillets Dinner Kit" was ok enough that I can give this a slight recommendation.

column9: Great Product!  But too much for a meal
column10: I really liked this product.  It tastes great and is easy to prepare.  The reason I gave it 4 stars rather than 5 is because it is too much for a meal.  I liked it as a side dish with a large garden salad and some homemade whole grain bread.  This is the same opinion I had about the Velveeta Shells and Broccoli dinner.  Both are great but not as a meal unto themselves.  I enjoy Velveeta, but it is too much for an entire meal.  All in all though I would recommend this product to everyone who isn't lactose intolerant.  And I have to say that my nieces and nephews LOVED it!!

For out-of-the-boxed, processed-food quick skillet dinners, this one was pretty good! I don't know how they artificially simulated things like the taste of pickles, mustard, and onions, but this definitely tastes like cheeseburger. Sure, it's not healthy, but it's not terrible either (use lean beef). These boxed one-skillet dinners are designed for convenience, but often they're either overly salty or just bland. This strikes a good flavor balance.I fed this to my kids, and they both ate their servings and asked for seconds. And considering that one of them is a picky eater, and the other is 3 1/2 and so rarely finishes a serving of ANYTHING, that's a glowing endorsement.
This was a very tasty disk for the amount of time it took to prepare.The directions are simple.  The only drawback was the sauce seemed salty.

I never liked cooking and honestly, I never cooked good food. However, things have changed with Velveeta CHeesy Skillets. It tastes very very good and requires only a few minutes to prepare. When I served it to my girlfriend, she couldn't believe that I cooked it myself. If you don't have a lot of time for cooking but still want a good meal, go for this one. You won't be disappointed.(Personally, it's a little salty, so you should not use the whole seasonal powder.)

This is very similar to Hamburger Helper, and looking at the box I was sure that it would be about as good.  Easy to make, one pan meal.  I have to say however that I was pleasantly surprised with how good it was!  Usually I doctor up boxed meals with various seasonings, but really this didn't even need it.  I have bought some of the other flavors, and been just as impressed.  Great product!

column9: Tastes good but similar to Hamburger Helper
column10: This product is very similar to the Hamburger Helper version.  It comes with noodles, a spice packet and the Velveeta cheese.  You brown the meat, add water, spices and noodles and simmer then add the Velveeta cheese sauce.  It's a very quick meal (~20 minutes, give or take) and tastes pretty good.  One thing I will say is that I'd recommend adding your own spices to the meat while browning it.  The included spice packet adds flavor to the noodles, but it didn't seem to stick with the hamburger.  So the hamburger can taste pretty flavorless once finished.Overall, it tastes good and is quick.  While it reminds me of Hamburger Helper, the Velveeta Cheese does add something.

column9: Is what it seems like it
column10: If you like velveta or mac n cheese you'll love this product, I think. It comes with the seasoning, noodles, and cheese--you provide the meat. I cooked the ground beef with onions. Probably all told, it took 15 minutes. It was fast and for a family who has kids who want there mac and cheese I suspect perfect. I have in the past added carrots and peas or blended caulieflower and broccoli to these products to make em a full meal. I personally think there is plenty of cheese sauce to go around. And I always add a little fresh ground pepper to balance out the salt.All that being said if you dont like cheese sauce or velveeta this wont change your opinion. Also I didnt think the seasoning added too much flavor wise, seemed mostly salt with maybe some onion or garlic powder. Also it doesnt really save time over anything else that requires ground beef, ie hamburgers or tacos, except on the prep side.If you or more likely your kids enjoy mac n' cheese though, give this a shot, its a nice change up and adds some protein to the normal mac dish.

Undoubtedly this will be compared to Hamburger Helper right off the bat and I suppose it's fair because they both try to do the same thing. Create an easy to prepare meal with nothing but ingredients in the box and some hamburger.Does this taste like a Cheeseburger? Not to me. The cheese is almost overpowering and once you get paste the cheese there isn't to much flavor there.It's easy to prepare and it's quick. But if you are looking for a culinary experience that will rock your taste buds... well this isn't the way to go.On a side note - if you or anyone you know is on a low sodium diet, or are keeping track of your sodium intake read this label. The sodium content for one serving is off the charts. I was legitimately shocked at how high it was.While I may eat it again down the line it's not something I am going to run to the store to specifically get and bring back to share.

I had the ultimate "Taste-testers" test this product......my grandkids.  They gave it a thumbs-up all the way.  It is super creamy & taste like a cheeseburger.  The 4 stars came from me......it gets a 5 star for taste.  I felt that it could have used more macaroni.  I almost cooked some more to add to it.  But, I guess less macaroni maybe helped to make it creamier.  We will definitely buy this again...it could be a meal all by itself.

I can't say this is my favorite food in the world - but it is excellent as an emergency back up meal for a busy family.  You quickly brown and drain the ground meat, adding a seasoning packet - then add water, the noodles, and cheese into the pot.  20 minutes from start to finish - more or less.  Velveeta is a guilty pleasure of mine...so this was an easy sell to me.  I must admit that the flavor seemed to me to be more like a sour cream - than what I would normally expect from Velveeta - but I still enjoyed the meal.

You know, for a convenience meal, this is quite tasty.  I was quite pleased with the flavor and ease of preparation.For the record, the box contains a packet of seasonings, elbow macaroni, and a package of cheese sauce.  You add one pound of ground beef, although I believe you can cut down on that a bit if you want.  I found the seasonings well balanced, enough for adults but not too much for kids, so something the whole family could eat and enjoy.  I did not detect any strange chemical undertones as are sometimes found in packaged meals.It was very simple to make.  When I come across a meat sale, I divvy it up so I always have some one-pound portions of beef in the freezer.  So I took one out, defrosted it a bit in the microwave, and browned it in a skillet while I was doing other things.  Then add two cups of water and the package of spices, let it boil up, then cover and simmer 11 to 13 minutes.  I timed mine at 12 minutes and that was a bit too long for the noodles.  I would recommend sampling the noodles at 10 minutes and judge from there.  Then turn off the heat and add the cheese sauce -- yes, thankfully, it's a sauce, not dried powder.The box says it makes five one-cup servings.  That makes at least four adult-sized servings, maybe five depending on side dishes.  The leftovers went to the office for lunch and were good microwaved, although I first added a few drops of water to keep it from getting too dry.Would I pick up another box to have on the shelf for one of those nights when I need a quick meal?  Absolutely!

I tried both the Kraft Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets Dinner Kit, 14.64-Ounce (Pack of 6)and this one, and I have to say this one is a winner.The instructions were easy enough to follow and you just simply need to add your own meat. I used ground turkey instead of red meat. The seasoning was good, and didn't taste too salty. It helped balance out the taste of Velveeta, which I always find a bit too sweet.I'd buy these for a quick and easy meal on days I'm tired from a full day of work.

column4: Therabbitssing "on the rock that spews lava.."
column10: It's like Hamburger Helper, easy to prepare, fast, heck a child could make it.  And honestly, as far as taste goes...I'm sure children will like it. It really tastes like a cheeseburger.  In a bowl.  With pasta.  Maybe I'm just not used to it but, as a cheese lover I thought I'd love it.  It's only okay.  You get the feeling it tastes like a cheeseburger but, somehow that doesn't translate as well when it's in a skillet scooped into a bowl.  It's a worthy alternative to the instant meals since the Velveeta cheese is indeed...cheesy.  Somehow I just couldn't get into it.

column9: Easy to make, great flavor and you only add ground beef and water
column10: I'll admit it - Hamburger Helper is a guilty pleasure of mine. I don't have it every week or even every month, but sometimes I just crave it. It is tasty, but I think it is also a comfort food that reminds me of my childhood and simpler times. Since I was a kid, my favorite flavors have been Beefy Pasta and Cheeseburger Macaroni. When we visited my Dad and money was tight, he would just make a box of Kraft Macaroni and Cheese and throw a little browned hamburger meat in it as a cheaper version of Hamburger Helper.I was intrigued to see that Kraft came out with their own version of the trusty old Hamburger Helper meals. As far as I can remember, I don't recall any competition for them in the past.So I ordered a box of the Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheeseburger Skillets Dinner Kit. The first difference I noticed right off the bat is that unlike the Hamburger Helper, you don't need to add milk. In fact, the only things you need to add are water and ground beef.Included in the box are the macaroni noodles, a seasoning mix in powder form, and a packet of Velveeta cheese sauce. I call it cheese sauce for lack of a better word, but it is more like a really soft Velveeta than a sauce as it isn't runny.The Kraft Skillets Dinner is a one-pot meal, as with the Hamburger Helper, making cleanup easy. You will need a measuring cup for the water, but using it only for water merely requires drying for the measuring cup, not washing.You begin by browning the ground beef, then you add the water, seasoning mix and macaroni, which is then cooked on a low heat for about 11-13 minutes. Once that stage has completed, you simply squeeze the cheese packet into the pot and stire it until it has melted and mixed into the seasoned sauce. Voila!As for the flavor, it is just as good as the Hamburger Helper. I think I would honestly find it hard to choose between the two products based on flavor. The one deciding factor for me is probably that you don't need to add milk. I don't drink milk, so I don't usually buy it unless I need it for a recipe and most of the carton usually goes bad before I've used it all.I will definitely be buying more of this to keep a box on hand in the pantry.

column9: Not for Macaroni and Cheese Purists
column10: We are pretty big macaroni & cheese lovers in my house, and we enjoy frying up some hamburger to throw in from time to time, so I jumped on the chance to review this product.It's quick and easy, fry up the burger, throw in the water, seasoning mix and macaroni. When the water is absorbed, mix in the accompanying Velveeta cheese sauce, and serve.I found that it was a little on the watery side for me, I like my mac n cheese kind of dry, but it wasn't over the top. The taste is mac n cheese mixed with stroganoff flavor. Not bad, but not wonderful either. It's almost like they're trying to appeal both the mac n cheese lovers AND the hamburger helper crowd.Would I buy it again? Sure, if it's on sale, but I wouldn't go out of my way to buy it.

This is your typical "add hamburger," pasta & seasoning boxed meal.  The difference it that it comes with a packet of creamy Velveeta cheese.  If you are a fan of Velveeta, then you will like this!The cheeseburger flavor is excellent.  In addition to the ground hamburger, I added a can of diced tomatoes, a chopped onion, and some sliced mushrooms to mine for a more 'complete' burger taste.  It also suggest on the back of the box that you can sprinkle some shredded lettuce on top just before serving, and I imagine, if you wanted, you could add some sliced pickle too!The box weighs 12.8oz (364g), making "about 5 1-cup servings."  Inside you will find three packets: powdered cheeseburger flavor packet, foil packet of real Velveeta cheese, and a bag of dry macaroni.  Unfortunately, despite the large size of the box, there is only 12oz of macaroni (1.5 cups dry), which is about enough to feed two adults when made.  Of course, you can add more macaroni of your own to stretch it a bit further, but doing this cuts down a little on the cheeseburger flavor.  If you have your meat already browned, it takes less than 15 mins to prepare (extra if you need to brown your meat).Overall, we liked the flavor, and with the additions I mentioned above, it was like eating a cheeseburger in a bowl!  Recommend for two people, for a quick but filling meal.

column9: Meh...you'd do better making your own
column10: I don't regularly eat Hamburger Helper but I did eat quite a bit in college.  When I saw this new offering from Velveeta I thought "oh cool, I should try that."  Instead of a creamy Velveeta-ey version of classic HH it was gritty, dull flavored, and all around pretty week.  I would recommend avoiding this product.  If you're inclined toward trying it I would say go with Hamburger Helper, or better yet make it homemade.  Ground beef, Velveeta, pasta, and milk will do you much better.

I loved this stuff, but others in my house didn't care for it as much as me.  They didn't think it was bad, just not spectacular.One thing is for sure, no matter what, anything that requires you add hamburger is going to vary in quality based on the quality of hamburger you put in it.This one ends up being somewhere around 50/50 in amounts of burger and noodles.Inside you get a bag of noodles, a packet of the creamy velveeta cheese and a packet of seasoning.The seasoning is what others in the house were not so sure on.  This seasoning doesn't blend with the cheese or anything like that, its made to season the hamburger.  When the meal is done cooking you will add the cheese.One thing I can say is that I feel like it could have used more cheese but I am like that with everything.  Extra cheese, extra sauce and all that.In the end, I would probably buy this again as I prefer the melty cheese over powder and I think it tasted great, but I will likely not get to eat it that often as others in our house would rather have something else.

column9: Looks thick and cheesy on box
column10: You know when you see Velveeta that your getting a thick and cheesy flavor.  Velveeta appears to be branching out from the mac & cheese business for a stab at, well, Hamburger Helper.  The price point is great.  The preparation is easy and quick, but the final product falls short of expectations.  The hamburger flavoring dominated the meal.  The thick gooey Velveeta cheese gets quickly eaten up by any excess water in the pan making it thin and runny.  The taste was good, but not the thick, cheesy goodness that I expected.

column4: Baivab Mitra "Save a tree, one at a time"
column10: My family like the taste of this product. This is a great for dinner as a side dish and my kids love to eat it and tell us to bring the same product over again

column9: Not for those watching their salt intake
column10: On the positive side, this Velveeta Cheesy Skillets - Ultimate Cheeseburger Mac is easy to make - the directions were clear and easy to understand and yes, it does only take 20 minutes. You can prepare everything in one pan which makes clean up a breeze. However, I wouldn't make this dish again - while I love cheesy food (the more cheese the better) I found this dish tasted very salty (and I don't mind salt - love it on my chips and fries). The salt/seasonings seemed to overwhelm this dish.The serving size is 2.5 ounces (approximately 1 cup) and there are approximately 5 servings in a box.Here is the nutritional Information - as prepared (percentages based on a 2000 calorie diet):Calories: 350Calories from Fat: 140Total Fat: 9g 25% (Saturated Fat: 3g 25%; Trans Fat: 0.5)Cholesterol: 15mg 22%Sodium 850mg 38%Total Carbohydrates 27g 9% (Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Sugars 6g)Protein 8gVitamin A: 2%Vitamin C: 20%Calcium: 15%Iron: 15%There is a note which says that 1 cup prepared as directed with 90% lean ground beef contains 16g total fat (5g saturated fat, 1g trans fat), 65g cholesterol, 900 mg sodium, 27g total carbohydrate (1g fiber, 6g sugars), 24g protein.

column9: It's better than average for a Velveeta/HH type meal, though it seems pricey
column10: I used to have Hamburger Helper (HH) as a kid.  But when I became an adult, I bypassed the HH for something cheaper, making cheese sauce myself.  So I usually make a roux and then add pasta to it.  This meal is better tasting then I thought it would be.  It comes with a spice pack, cheese sauce pack and pasta.  You supply the meat.  I personally wouldn't buy the product for $2.50 a box when I can buy a bag of pasta on sale at my local supermarket for $1, then add spices already in my cupboard and then make a roux, which yes, takes 30-40 minutes instead of the 20 here.  I have no kids and my boyfriend and I have time to cook, so time isn't too tight for us.  Even with a a dollar or two of real cheese added to my recipe, I'd rather know what I am eating for $3 (which really would make twice as much pasta as the pasta that came in the box) then eat something loaded with odd ingredients I don't know.Despite this, the skillet meal is easy to prepare, even an older kid could probably do this and it would save time for busy adults.  It tastes ok. The spice gives it a Mexican sort of appeal and I ate it as shown on the back of the box, with shredded lettuce and onion.  I do think that most of the money you pay for this item goes into packaging and the design of the box.  Since I am not eating the box, I'll stick to my own cheese sauces, thanks!Note:  I did use very lean beef for this meal and it came out rather cheesy, which was a good thing.

This was certainly a simple meal to prepare, but keep in mind that it makes five servings that are 350 calories each.  It seems like it only makes about three servings, so I was surprised at how small the servings actually were.  The noodles were kind of big and cooked up a little mushy for me, but I didn't quite follow the directions to the letter because I misread them--but it still worked.  The cheese sauce had a strange artificial aftertaste to it, which I didn't like.  For that reason alone, I'd stick to Hamburger Helper if I were to buy this sort of thing for a quick meal.  I'm also a vegetarian, so I'll mention that this doesn't contain chicken fat or beef stock or anything that would be non-vegetarian.  I used some Boca crumbles to make this into a meal, and I'll say it wasn't bad--but that aftertaste hung around with every bite.

We found this product to be suitable for someone in a hurry with not much time to cook, but still wanting a nutritious meal. After cooking it was not watery and had a very good consistency. In addition, it had an excellent aroma with an excellent cheese taste. This is not your mother's hamburger helper but seems to be a step above that. Just add some good quality low fat hamburger to it and follow the easy instructions and you will produce a fairly well balanced meal, just add some orange juice and/or vegetable or fruit, and bread, on the side, to more completely balance it, and enjoy. Best when freshly made, the left-overs were just okay after microwaving.

column9: How'd they get the cheeseburger taste in there?
column10: Our family doesn't eat "skillet dinner mixes" very often, but they sure are handy to have around for busy school nights when there's little time between homework and sports practice. Plus, now that my son is getting old enough to start taking on some meal-preparation responsibilities, I've been keeping an eye out for meals he can make on his own. This one is certainly in his skill level!The instructions are easy enough to follow: brown some ground beef (not mentioned on the package: rinse it in a colander under hot water to reduce your meal's fat content then return to the pan); add 2 cups of water and the noodles from the box; bring to boil then cover and simmer until most of the liquid is gone; finally, stir in the cheese goop... er, sauce... and serve. Definitely something a pre-teen can handle!Our first impression: we were all surprised how Kraft managed to get the cheeseburger taste in there... straight down to the pickle flavor. Seriously, where did that pickle flavor come from? The box mentions 'natural spices' but nothing about dehydrated pickle or pickle juice, but WOW it certainly had that taste! Second impression: we couldn't decide if that was a good thing, or a bad one.Nutritionally, there's not a lot to feel good about with this meal. It's high in fat, low in fiber, heavy on the salt and chock full of additives. But, sometimes when you're trying to feed a hungry family in a hurry those things don't matter as much as getting their bellies full. For our family, we've decided that if we have this in the future we'll be sure to pair it with generous servings of fresh veggies and fruit.To sum:PROS:1. Easy enough for a tweenager to make.2. One-skillet main dish.3. Calories can be slightly reduced by using very lean ground beef or even ground turkey, and rinsing the meat after it's browned.4. Very, very filling.5. Definite 'cheesburger-y' flavor.CONS:1. Low fiber.2. High sodium.3. High fat.4. Where DOES that pickle flavor come from???

column9: Easy to Prep One Pan Meal
column10: This product is a bit of a change for me. I live in a home with, other than me who'll eat anything, an organic vegan wife and an organic vegetarian daughter. So let's say I got a bit of razz when I started to prepare this product for me and me alone to eat. I figured it'd make a great sort of food to make a work lunch since we have a microwave there to re-heat casseroles.There are four simple steps to prepare this meal if you call 'cover the pot' a step. The instructions say to use one skillet for the entire preparation but I transferred the browned meat (first step) into a saucepan for the remaining time. It made no difference, I"m sure. Total preparation time is about a half hour, but it's not an unattended half hour. Step one is to brown the ground beef which, of course, requires monitoring and turning. Step three which starts cover the pot says one needs to monitor and stir the pot regularly for the roughly quarter of an hour this step requires. While hardly onerous or demanding, this isn't something you can just throw together in a pot, turn up the heat and come back to a finished product in a few minutes.The result is some rather loose cheese sauce which coats soft elbow macaroni and the browned crumbled ground beef (or other meat, I suppose). As with most casseroles, this tasted substantially better after having stood for an hour and much better after 24 hour refrigeration and a reheat. Overall I found this to be generally good tasting and perfect for my intention of taking some to work for reheating in the microwave. It'd also make a quick family dinner especially if you have the time to prep it an hour ahead of dinner time to allow it to stand for a bit.There are two downsides which, to me, detract from the enjoyment in this dish. The first is probably exclusive to me. I find this food to be rather salty. Then again, I never salt my food and often find restaurant food to be too salty as prepared so I would anticipate that this would not be an issue for most folks trying this product. For example, I work with one woman who heavily salts her pizza. I'm sure she'd complain this product needs salt.The second issue I have is presentation. This dish looks terrible. There is no suitable description, metaphor or simile I can use to describe how this looks on a plate which would be suitable for a food product. If presentation is important to you, then proceed with caution. I don't doubt that the experts at Kraft can prep this dish to look like the box picture but my try fell woefully short. Then again, if this one is for children, that's not an issue, I'd guess. I think kids will eagerly lap this food up.I'm glad I got this and ate the entire amount up, but due to the saltiness, I think this may be my last shot at this product. Those who are comfortable with the saltiness of a typical sit down restaurant won't, I think, feel likewise.

column9: Good for a quick and easy meal.
column10: We did not like this as much as we liked the chicken and broccoli flavor, however it still is the same simple to make, 20 minute meal.  Good flavor, though a bit too cheesy for me.  Defintiely follow the serving suggestion and add some chopped lettuce and tomatoes when you serve it.  Definitely makes it taste like a cheeseburger.

Velveeta Skillets Dinner Kits make for a quick and easy meal.  Prepartion time is aroung 20 minutes with most of time spent browning the ground beef and simmering the pasta.  Taste was better than average with creamy velveeta cheese sauce.  Sodium is high at 850mg per cup serving and fat is at 9g.  With that in mind, this is not something to cook every night but is worth having on hand for those quick dinners.

Our family has started to dig into various Cheesy Skillet meals by Velveeta, and this one has become our favorite.The preparation for this meal couldn't have been any simpler...just follow the instructions on the box and you're good to go. Within 15 minutes, your senses will be on cheese overload.I've uploaded some pictures into the "Customer Images" section - not an easy task, because I wanted to dive right into this meal instead of taking pictures of it!The cheese was delicious, there were noodles aplenty, and it provided a very hearty meal. I could only finish 2 servings before I was stuffed.If you serve this with a side dish of vegetables, you'll have yourself one smiling family.Highly recommended!

column9: Velveeta Ultimate Cheeseburger Skillet Helps Create a Simple Meal
column10: A simple meal is often welcome when your working life takes up a good portion of your day and Velveeta Cheesy Skillet Ultimate Cheeseburger offers exactly that. It contains the basic ingredients in a box, ready to prep and serve with minimal effort or culinary skill. All you need is ground beef and water to create this food product and it can be served as a main dish or a side dish with other foods.Velveeta is the most popular processed cheese food in America and while I am not too fond of the taste of the actual cheese product, I have found the Velveeta meals a decent tasting food that makes for a reasonably easy meal. And this particular product is no exception. The cheese is fairly smooth and there is a decent amount of balance from the seasoning mix. I found it compatible to my palate, even though I readily admit it is nothing incredible.Nutritionally, Velveeta Cheesy Skillet Ultimate Cheeseburger is fairly good. The base product, without meat, has a good amount of calcium and iron. But on the negative side, there is a good deal of sodium in this product and it definitely comes through in the taste, which is a little saltier than I prefer. Calories are not too bad, provided you can consume in moderation. A single box is intended to serve five people and if you can keep your portion down at that level, your waistline and heart shouldn't suffer.I like meals that are easy to prepare and Velveeta Cheesy Skillet Ultimate Cheeseburger certainly fits in this category. There is little to do other than brown the ground beef, add water, stir, and wait. Taste- wise, the product is good, but not great and it doesn't come even close to the taste of a freshly made meat, pasta, and cheese casserole. However, it will do in a pinch and it has enough to offer to award it with a slight recommendation.

We don't use 'skillet meals' very often but wanted to try this because it's new.The only other version of this we had eaten was from Hamburger Helper. The Velveeta product was just this side of homemade tasting, and beats HH hands down. The only odd thing was having to add a packet of cheesy powder to the dish when making it; reminiscent of Kraft Mac N Cheese. I had fully expected all of the cheesy sauce to come from Velveeta cheese.This dinner was creamy and yes it was salty, but in a good way. I would buy this and keep it handy for the teen to make a quick dinner. Both my son and husband loved it and said they would definitely eat it again.If I make this again I might add a little finely diced onion and a can of diced tomatoes to make it stretch since my family gobbled this down and didn't leave much for me!

Just finished dinner and figured I'd review it.  The Velveeta ultimate cheeseburger mix was relatively easy to prepare and I liked it.  I thought the cheese was just a bit sharper than typical velveeta, but I liked it.  My wife thought that it is cheesier than hamburger helper and likes this better.  I'm up for trying a couple of the other flavor mixes.  Good meal.  If you buy it I hope you enjoy and thanks for reading my review.

column9: Good enough to be better than its competition
column10: Velveeta decided to expand its business I guess.  Well it did a pretty good job here.  This is like a super-cheesy hamburger helper that I really enjoyed.  It's not like a steak at a five-star restaurant, but it's definitely satisfying and I think it will find a lot of happy buyers.

column9: NOT Hamburger Helper, but Quite Good Just the Same
column10: My box showed up today around noon, which solved the question of "What's for dinner?"  I've been looking forward to trying this ever since I heard about it -- I'm a big Hamburger Helper fan (have been ever since I moved out on my own some 20 years ago).  I figured this would be Hamburger Helper with real cheese rather than cheese powder.Preparation is easy; brown the ground beef, drain, add 2 cups of water with the seasonings packet and the macaroni.  This is the first place you know this isn't HH; you have to make sure you cook the water (or "most of it" as the instructions say) off before you add the Velveeta.  Another difference is that the seasonings smell a little .... strong, and a little unusual, to put it mildly.  I wasn't too fond of the odor emanating from the skillet, and at this point I started to hope that I wasn't going to have to make something different for dinner.This also tastes different from HH.  Not bad -- in spite of my initial worry, the Velveeta Cheeseburger Skillets tastes quite good.  But it is rather different from HH, and if you're expecting HH you will probably be disappointed.  I can't quite put my finger on what the spice is, but there is a definite spice that makes this taste completely different from any cheeseburger macaroni that you've ever had before.I'm not sure if this will completely replace Hamburger Helper for me; I'll have to wait and see what other varieties they come out with before I make that decision.  But I do know that this is a good alternative, and for people who want something different, it will be a good choice.

Velveeta Cheesy Skillets look like your typical 'boxed dinner'. You add a pound of ground beef to macaroni and seasoning, for a quick, tasty meal, but the similarities end there. Velveeta Cheesy skllets dinner kits have a package of creamy Velveeta cheese sauce right in the box, so the meal is much more creamier and cheesier. It comes in four varities, but I tried the Ultimate Cheeseburger Mac. Very easy to make and really tasty.  The box makes the directions very clear and concise and all you need to add is water and ground beef. I really think having the package of Velveeta cheese sauce makes a huge difference from other brands because it didnt turn out watered-down like some of this type of meal so. It was very rich and creamy.The seasoning pack gives it a little "zing", so it is more than just mac and cheese with meat. The box also suggests "cutomizing: it with chopped tomatoes and lettuce. Although this sounds good, I prepared it the regular way.  I love to cook, but sometimes I come home from work and dont feel like preparing a big meal. Those are the days I like to have something easy to prepare. This was perfect and  because a package makes about 5 servings, so there was plenty left over. Very filling and satisfying, I would definitely buy it again. I could preapare it and divide into servings for several lunches during the week. I think it's also great for kids who like mac and cheese. While, it certainly is not a "gourmet" meal , it is quite excellent quality.

I just made this today for dinner- the boys loved it.This is a regular, one dish meal- perfect for a casual meal at home. I made it for my man and younger brother. Super easy to fix and the flavoring was great. I cooked it exactly as the directions state. Clean up is simple as it is all cooked in the same pan. Love that.I had a side salad and bread as well with this meal, which worked well with it. The box comes with spices that dress the meal up a bit. Totally recommend this if you love Velveeta or the similar meal by Hamburger Helper- The Velveeta Skillet meal is MUCH more delicious.

column9: Tasty, and easy to add to
column10: To get it out of the way, let me mention the obvious downside. At a minimum of 350 calories for one cup - and you will eat more than one cup - it's better to treat it as a very occasional treat than a mainstay. It's beef, velveeta and starch; and it's slightly higher in calories than some equivalent products. But if you're dieting, you're already avoiding meals like this one.As an occasional treat, though, it's nice. It's simple to prepare, and it went flawlessly. It cooks in one pan, is tolerant of varying heat (I cooked it over a woodgas stove), and doesn't take long. The taste is a little on the bland side as is, but adding spices and other additions is easy. It's creamy and rich. I added some tomato and some minced, dried onion, and spiced with a splash of hot sauce and lemon pepper. It doesn't need salt. It was good. And if you actually measure out a cup of the stuff and sit it next to a decent quantity of vegetables, it's not as much of a dietary train-wreck as you'd think, and you aren't hungry again soon afterwards.I think packaging could be improved; the packaging isn't very suitable for burning or recycling.

The New Cheesy Skillet by Velveeta is a simple and quick meal that will feed your entire family. I enjoyed how easy this dish was to prepare and you didn't need to add much to the dish to create a full yet satisfying meal. I loved the fact that Velveeta didn't put in a powdered cheese product but instead used creamy Velveeta that created the perfect dish.The Hamburger helpers are a bit too salty for my taste but this product didn't over salt the product and this made it that much better. I will definitely purchase this product in the future as an easy dish for my family on those hectic days.
I am not one for boxed meals, but I thought I would try this.  It was really delicious and would be good for a speedy meal.

My children love Velveeta Mac and Cheese, so I was happy to see a Velveeta version of "hamburger helper."  Usually, when I have made "HH" I "doctor it up" with add-ins, like mushrooms, sour cream, french fried onions, etc.  I wanted an accurate review of this product, so I prepared it exactly as directed on the box, with no additions.  My family was very pleased with the results.  The cheese sauce is rich and creamy, and does not require "waiting time" for it to thicken, as with other box meals.  The noodles cooked up well, and I didn't have any that were undercooked, as happens sometimes with other meals.  I will say that one box prepared would not have been enough for my family (three adults and two teenagers) if I had not also prepared two side dishes to go with the meal.  I usually prepare two boxes of HH (or this Velveeta in the future) so that everyone can have all they want, plus there will be leftovers for lunch the next day.  I have also tried the Velveeta BBQ Chicken Ultimate skillet, and I must say, it is even better than the cheeseburger meal.  I am very pleased with this product, and I hope that Kraft will expand the line to include more choices.

Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheesburger Skillets Dinner looks scrumptious -- on the cover.  It is easy to make, doesn't take a lot of time, and I am sure tons of children would love it.  Just not me.  I found it to be a lot like Hamburger Helper's Cheesburger dinner not only in taste, but rather, in its lack of good taste.One lb. of hamburger meat is all that is needed -- the rest of the ingredients are included.  Once the meat is cooked you add two cups of water, the macaroni, and the spice packets.  That cooks down and then once most of the water is gone, you add the cheese packet.I wasn't keen on it, my husband ate it because he was hungry.  LOLNatalie S. for Amazon Vine
This is a tough review to write, because this product is average in every way. You follow the instructions, and you end up with macaroni and cheese. Not bad, but nothing special.

column9: Quick and yummy, but very salty
column10: This evening we had Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheesburger Skillets Dinner Kit, 12.86-Ounce (Pack of 6) for dinner.  We were excited about trying this because my husband loves Hamburger Helper Cheeseburger Macaroni and wanted to see if this was better. Twenty minutes is the total prep time, and all you need to prepare this dinner is two cups of water.My family had mixed reactions to the prepared meal:Dad: Wasn't what he expected - He thought that it would have a thick, Velveeta-type sauce.  The sauce tasted very cheesy, but was thin and kind of watery. Still it tastes better than the previous favorite.  We have a new winner!  Oh yes, there is no way that this is five servings.  It is one Dad-at-home-alone dinner, or all three family members having a meal with a salad on the side.Mom: It really is more like three servings than five, maybe even two servings if Dad is hungry.  It doesn't matter though, because of the over 1,400 mg of sodium per our family sized portion (850 mg per serving as the box calls a serving x 5 servings = 4,250 mg/3 people in our family = 1,417 mg. per serving)  Due to health issues, I can't eat that much salt, and I'd prefer that the rest of the family limit their salt as well.  I might be outvoted though.Kid: (with teeny appetite)  I tasted mustard, so I won't eat this.As it turns out, the dinner does contain a minute amount of mustard, so if you have mustard-hating kids, beware.Thanks for reading, and hope this gives you the info you need to decide if Kraft Velveeta Dinner is for you.

When Hurricane Irene hit New York, we lost power but still had a stove that worked. This kit provided a quick and easy and quite cheesy meal.  Essentially all you add is browned meat and water.  The macaronis are simmered in a seasoned water for a little over ten minutes, then mixed in the browned, drained meat.  A packet of velveeta is stirred in the meat and macaroni mixture.Everyone loved it except me.  No I wasn't expecting haute cuisine but I though it could have been less salty and more flavorful. It does taste like a cheeseburger.It is designed to please as opposed to challenge. In fairness, everyone else thought it was absolutely delicious--to the extent that they went out and bought ten boxes.  It definitely benefits from serving with a nice crisp salad or jazzing up with some hot peppers, tomatoes and/or salsa.This is ideal for the busy family, college students or any one looking for a filling, flavorful, easy to prepare meal.

I've always preferred the boxed Velveeta with shells over Kraft Macaroni and Cheese (or is it cheese and macaroni?).  It's cheesier and more flavorful.  To now compete with Hamburger Helper, Velveeta came out with their new "Cheesy Skillets" meal-in-a-box.  I tried the "Ultimate Cheeseburger Mac" version.  Unfortunately, I didn't have any hamburger on hand, so I used what I did have: kielbasa.  I also added some roasted peppers.The pasta in Velveeta Cheesy Skillets is a much larger version of elbow macaroni.  It really holds and absorbs the sauce well.  In addition to the tradition soft cheese sauce like the Velveeta shells boxes come with, there's a seasoning packet to add to the meat, pasta, and water.  It really added a lot of flavor to the already rich, creamy cheese sauce.  It feels a step above Hamburger Helper, much like their boxed shells is a step above traditional boxed macaroni and cheese.My only disappointment?  There was literally only a handful of pasta included in the big box.  And the package says that it contains five servings.  Five?  Seriously?  Who are they kidding?  If I split the box up into five servings, everyone would literally get half a cupful.  These are supposed to be entire meals-in-one, not side dishes.  Let's be realistic here.My suggestion?  Buy the box and an additional box of pasta, add additional water when cooking, and you'll make a real dinner for five.  There's plenty of seasoning and sauce to cover and flavor any added pasta.

column4: Chris Swanson "I'm just this guy, you know?"
column9: It's like some sort of wonderful "helper" for your "hamburger".
column10: So here we have Kraft's answer to a certain popular food product. How does it compare?If you're familiar with the cheeseburger macaroni version of that other boxed hamburger thing, you're on the right track, except that this version comes with actual liquidish sauce that you stir into the finished product. What you end up with is kind of like mac and cheese with undrained hamburger. It's quite greasy, but tastes decent, though frankly I couldn't actually really taste the cheese. That might be a bonus for some.Really this is quite similar to the other thing, so if you're looking and can't decide which to buy, go with whatever is cheapest and you'll do just fine.

This is a fairly easy dish to prepare. I picked up a pound or so of lean ground sirloin and browned it well to achieve some flavor. Next I followed the directions on the box and made some improvisations to add some pizzaz. Without a personal touch with spices and other goodies, especially some well sauteed onions etc, this would be a fairly blase cheesy glob of meat. A green veggie and a piece of fruit for dessert help to soothe your conscience a little bit for the enormous calorie count in the meat and cheese. Bon appetit.

I love velveeta's macaroni and cheese and this is pretty much that with added seasonings and adding your own hamburger. It fed two adults and we even had some leftover for lunch. Took 20-30 minutes to cook, but was very easy. It's rich and very filling. I would get again and will certainly be trying the other skillet dinners they are offering.

The Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheeseburger Skillets Dinner Kit is a Hamburger Helper like dish.  I'm sure they hate that comparison but there it is.  You brown a pound of beef (or whatever ground meat you like) in a skillet, add noodles, water and sauce mix and cook - so very similar.  At the end of the cooking process though you squeeze in a bag of liquid Velveeta and stir in.So how does it taste?  Not bad, but not great.  Honestly the cheeseburger flavoring was not the best and seemed bland overall.  The cheese and noodles were good but the whole I did not find overall satisfying.  I felt it was an average dish and have rated it accordingly.
WE were a bit underwhelmed. The noodles were typical of macaroni-type food, but the seasoning and the cheese was a bit strong.

This dinner was some cheesy, yummy goodness. My only complaint was that it didn't make very much. We have a family of seven and I would have had to fix 3 boxes to feed all of us. I would say that with the average serving size, it would have fed 2 adults and 1 child. It really was delicious, though - and super easy to fix.

Working moms and running moms are going to appreciate this box  mix.  The other brand is convenient but there is nothing smoother than Velveta made into a sauce.  The product was very easy to use and made a fast meal with a vegetable side a quick and filling meal.  I fully intend to try the other flavor"s" asap.  Kids sports practices can make meals a real adventure.

column9: Surprised my Brother with this one
column10: I sent this to my brother, a 37 year old consumate bachelor.  His comment was, "I don't know why they call this Hamburger Helper....I think it does just fine by itself!"  In all seriousness he liked it a lot and said kids would really like it because it's so cheesy.  He would know...

column9: I Prefer This To Hamburger Helper...
column10: I love food, so when I saw these available on the Vine, I jumped on them. I was afraid they were going to be disgustingly gooey and cheesy, much like Velveeta's Shells and Cheese are, but this was actually really good!I like the big noodles (they're about twice the since of regular macaroni noodles), and the cheese ratio was perfect. Definitely not to much, but not lacking either. While I don't normally make Hamburger Helper, I usually have a box or two in my cabinet in case I just do NOT feel like putting anything together. I will now be replacing those with these. I noticed in the grocery store that there's a bunch of different flavors that looked pretty good. I won't be eating these often, but they're absolutely more substantial than HH!

Having a busy schedule, I can appreciate an easy boxed meal to cook every now and then. I'd have to say I prefer this brand to Hamburger Helper because of the taste and the quality of the product. Instructions were easy to follow, the food was tasty and it's a nice back up to have in the pantry when you don't feel like making a meal from scratch.

I believe I love these dinners even more than the Hamburger Helper brand meals. I tried the broccoli and cheese skillet first and it was very good. This one tastes good as well. I'm not really sure about the sodium, perservatives etc. It's a fast meal so of course you will have those issues. I just need something quick to fix and this is it. I think I will try it without the sauce packet next time, I think it will taste better without it. (just the cheese packet)

This meal-in-a-box courtesy of Kraft is quite tasty and very easy to make. Miles better than just macaroni and cheese, you add in your own ground beef and some spices and cheese that comes in the box. While I can't quite place the spices, the net result was something that tasted exactly like one of my mother's home-cooked meals. The amount of cheese sauce was "just right"- the meal wasn't overly cheesy but I could still get hints that something rich and creamy was lying underneath.  I threw some frozen peas and carrots into the mix to round out the meal, and was able to get 6 filling meals out of it. Move over, Hamburger Helper, I am totally going to buy these again.

I didn't bother using the seasoning packet and opted to use my own instead. Tastes really good. Basically an updated version of macaroni & cheese. Not my fave meal, but good if I need to whip something up in a jiffy.

Ok, first let me say, this is not the healthiest of meals so if you are on a health kick, this one isn't for you.I personally love this kind of stuff so I was very excited to try it.it's easy enough to make, brown the ground beef, drain, add water and pasta and the flavor pack and then add the cheese.Surprisingly, I wasn't too happy with this one.  it lacked taste.  I don't think there was enough cheese or the normal Velveeta cheese that you can buy in the store.  It seemed to lack the cheese taste when the meal was said and done.  The cheese seemed a bit watery and really not enough.  So we ate 1/2 of it in one meal and the next day, I added a bag of frozen veggies to it and I also added salsa and more cheese and it tasted good.I don't think the cheese that comes with the meal is the same one that you buy in the store.  I really did water down and lacked taste.  If you want to try it, get some Velveeta and add it on your own.

column9: Easy to make and very tasty
column10: Much like the old Hamburger Helper dinners but the creamy Velveeta cheese makes a huge difference. Extremely tasty and very easy to make!

column9: Pretty Good for an Easy Meal
column10: This Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheesburger Skillets Dinner is your basic "Hamburger Helper" type skillet dinner. The spice mix is very mild and the cheese sauce is standard Velveeta. The finished serving size might seem a bit small for many people. The dinner is easy to make and quick. If you are into this kind of product, this one is probably on the lower end of the spice scale and should be good for younger kids.

My experience with this cheesy skillet wasn't a good one. I followed the directions but it came out kind of runny at the end and wasn't very cheesy. It may have been something I did, but the end product just wasn't very good. I'm not a big "cheeseburger" person anyway. I did try the chicken & broccoli skillet and it turned out amazing. I would definitely recommend that one over this skillet. I just prefer the chicken and the noodles over the hamburger and noodles in this skillet.

I don't know if Velveeta was trying to step ahead of Hamburger Helper.  It calls for less added ingredients than HH so it's easier in the long run.  It's good, not great.  I can't figure out how to get the "boxed" dinner taste out of it without overloading it with salt or other seasonings.My daughter loved it but then she loves anything with mac and cheese.

My sodium radar told me to not even try this product, but it sounded good so I did. Ew! A whopping 900mg of sodium in a one cup serving, to go with the 370 calories. It is worth it to take the extra effort to boil whole grain pasta, make a cheese rue myself, then add hamburger. Time-consuming, sure, but way better tasting and better for me. Even my husband gave it a thumbs-down and he is like Mikey from Life cereal commercials!

We tried out Cheesy Skillets last week with some fresh ground beef.  The flavor was fairly unassuming.  Typical boxed meal fare.  The cheese was creamy, not gritty.  The spices were light, not overpowering or even noticeable.  Thirty minutes later, we were both running for the restroom through...Might be good for choosey children, but nothing to break the cookie-cutter boxed meal mold here...

Just like Hamburger Helper & related products, the Velveeta Cheesy Skillets meals are fast and easy to prepare. Yes, Velveeta cheese is actually not healthy for you and all, but despite that I do think these taste better than Hamburger Helper. Even the most novice cook can prepare one of these without issue in under 20 minutes; all it takes is some water and meat (I prefer ground round or other less fatty alternatives to ground beef).  My son made this without a problem and we combined it with some vegetables to complete the meal. Everything else aside, better pricing could probably be found at your local store.
just nasty.hamburger helper gone bland.noodles are ok;sauce mix is throw-away. too much fake cheese flavor.you'd have to dump a lot of veggies&spices to overpower that gross cheese,haha!

column4: Desired FX "Call me Don. It's shorter than Is...
column10: (I'm not sure why it isn't marked as such, but this is a Customer review from the Amazon Vine(tm) Program.)On the plus side, it's easy to make: you only dirty a skillet and spoon.On the minus, it doesn't taste like much of anything. For all the seasoning and cheese, it still seems like it needs salt. It doesn't taste like any cheeseburger I've had...or even like one of those beefy mac dishes. It's just bulky stuff that lays in your stomach.I really can't recommend this to anyone.

column9: Yummy and Easy to Make. I Use it When In a Hurry...
column10: I don't like to use instant foods. In fact I am kind of a health nut who grows wheat grass to juice and takes ginger shots to combat being sick when everyone else is. But sometimes you don't have time to cook a complete meal for your family in todays fast paced world. Velveeta Cheesy Skillets work. Tastes good out of the box and even better it you add a little parmesan cheese or spice it up your own sprinkling of seasonings. Works for me.
My husband loves velveeta shells and cheese so we HAD to try these!! Very quick and easy. Don't need anything but the meat. But you may want to add a salad or some veggies for a round dinner! :)

Nice Qucik Meal ; Tastey Macaroni & hamburger(so how bad could it be?) .Better taste if you use lean hamburger & of course drain the excess grease before mixing.Affordable fast meal after a hard day of work.

column9: It's no Julia Child.....but it's very tasty, easy to fix!
column10: I fixed this dish with lean ground beef.  Browned the meat, added two cups of water, stirred in the seasoning and macaroni.  When that was done few minutes later, I added the Velveeta Cheese, minus a few tablespoons, and VIOLA!!  It was tasty for a quick dish.Don't overcook the macaroni, use the exact minutes stated on the box.  The Velveeta Cheese is tasty.  And, you can't expect this to be lacking calories, as anything with cheese can be a killer!  But I like it.Upon reheating, I used the remaining cheese.  It works great.With a lb of ground beef, you have plenty of macaroni, seasonings, and cheese.  This will serve a small family, providing you have a vegetable side dish too.But, here's the key.  Eat at while fresh, because when you reheat, the macaroni can get mushy.  Or, make sure you do not overcook the macaroni the first round.Kraft Velveeta..... tasty, easy to make, great for kids too. ...Rizzo

Velveeta just one up Kraft with their version of a ground hamburger meal with cheese. I love the fact that the cheese is not powder, not that Hamburger Helper wasn't good, i just prefer this type. Good job Velveeta.

This dinner in a box is basically a Hamburger Helper-style cheesy macaroni.  It comes with pasta, spices, and cheese- you add the hamburger.  It can all be cooked in one pan, which is a definite plus, and it is definitely a quick and easy meal.  Those are the positives.  I wasn't nearly as pleased with the results as I was with the process.  The resulting concoction was was very greasy, and didn't have much flavor.  I used extra lean beef, so I don't think the meat was the issue.  I had previously tried the chicken and broccoli Cheesy Skillet, and that one was good, and didn't have a grease problem.  I'd buy that one again, but I'm steering clear of this variety.

column9: Not bad for one pan dinner
column10: This one-pan dinner isn't bad, it's basically another version of Hamburger Helper (which I happen to like as far as this type of thing goes), so there aren't a lot of surprises here.  It's simple to make and fairly cheesy, but I was left wishing there were a bit more cheese.  I think adding some parmesan cheese would help as well, I may give this product another go round and see how that works.  I can't say this is any better or worse than any other one-pan dinner, so I suppose if you're in the market for that sort of thing, this is as good as it gets.

This is basically just another version of hamburger helper, for some reason I didn't like the taste of this, not sure if it was the cheese sauce or just the spices.  I think we'll stick with hamburger helper.
Tasty, filling and easy! I would recommend Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheesburger Skillets Dinner to any body that wants to have on hand a fast tasty meal.
I did not use beef, but added more pasta and vegetables. Everyone loved it! It was a bit salty. But the salt added to the taste. Very convenient. Will buy again.
Nothing outstanding, it tastes a lot like hamburger helper which I really don't care for.But at the same time my kids really liked it!

I took this box of Cheesy Skillets to a cabin getaway and had it for dinner one night while we were there. That was not a good move. The nearest restaurant was 25 miles away. And guess where we went for dinner that night? The skillet smelled up the whole cabin. We had to leave the doors open and let all the bugs in to get the stench out. So we had a smelly cabin and tons of mosquitos because we cooked something we couldn't even eat. That's right, we threw it out.That was my experience with this product. I also had the Chicken and Broccoli flavor which I liked, so it's not a blanket statement for the whole product line - just this flavor.

Good:This is the best boxed mac n' cheese that I've ever had. The texture and flavor are the closest thing to real macaroni and cheese. It is definitely better than the powdered cheese form. It tastes pretty decent. With some hot sauce, either the rooster asian sauce or tabasco, it's even better.Fast and easy to make.Good value for the money.Bad:Presentation is nothing like the box. It is less cheesy orange and more white-ish. It does not look very appetizing, until you put a reddish hot sauce on it. On the bright side, I'd rather Kraft put less food coloring in their food and not more, so this is a good thing.Not surprisingly, it's not as good as real mac n cheese, but it's the closest thing to it coming out of a heavily processed box.Verdict:If you're a poor university student, or you can't cook, this is the thing to get. I could have seriously used this a few years back. A good change from endless boxes of pizza or chicken wings.
