The Kraft Velveeta skillets dinner is saved by the cheese, barely. The seasoning packet added no real taste to the meal but made everything yellow. The Velveeta pouch was big and added plenty of cheesy taste to the pasta. If you are a fan of box pastas and cheese then you will like this; if you are like me and prefer fresh, then go ahead and skip. It tastes way too processed.

This is your typical 'pasta-in-a-box' meal. Prep is easy, all you add is meat. The flavor was good with minimal cardboard taste. But...it's way too salty. Now I realize that some will love the saltiness, but I don't. Salt messes with my blood pressure and leaves that fresh, too much salt taste in my mouth.
This is just like hamburger helper.  Very good stuff.  A little more expensive in the end but still very good stuff.

This is basically a Velveeta version of Hamburger Helper Cheeseburger Mac, which if you add extra seasonings, is pretty good along with being a cheap meal. I have to say Hamburger Helper has just met its match.You cook up the hamburger the same way, add in water, a seasoning package, and then the noodles. Then, when the water is absorbed, you add in a package of Velveeta cheese. YUMMY!! It really made the meal pop with a great cheesy flavor without being too cheesy, a problem that I commonly have when cooking with Velveeta.I also like the fact that the macaroni noodles were a larger noodle. Typically you get little elbow macaroni noodles in the Hamburger Helper. That just added to the filling meal.I recommend this. It comes out to be about $2.50 a box when ordered off Amazon, which is cheaper than buying Hamburger Helping in the store. It is a good, hearty meal good for any family.Shawn KovacichCreator of numerous books and DVDs.

*DISCLAIMER: I did NOT use the seasoning packet as I knew the meat would have more than enough spice*My husband LOVES Hamburger Helper, so I was curious what he'd think of this. I didn't tell him that it was from Velveeta and simply browned up some Venison sausage and cooked the noodles and cheese sauce as the instructions state. I didn't add the seasoning because the venison sausage has tons of spice to it.We all dug in. We all loved it. When I told him that it was from Velveeta, his response was "I thought the cheese tasted different." I LOVE that the cheese isn't some processed powered stuff, but is rather thick, creamy cheese that folds into the meal perfectly. I can't wait to purchase more of these once they hit our local store!
This would be great for someone who has kids who like macaroni and cheese and want something different for dinner.  It's easy to make and has a good flavor.
This was simple to cook. Nice and cheesy.  Kids enjoyed the change from plain old macaroni and cheese. But I like to add veggies to it.
Everyone knows and loves MAC and CHEESE, well news flash  MAC and cheese just got better and more filling. With just 1lbs. Of ground beef macaroni became  a new family favorite.

column9: Too rich, but easy to make
column10: I love the Hamburger Helper of this flavor, so I was hoping the Velveeta version would be even better.  I have to say I'm disappointed.  It was just too rich to eat.  I wanted creamy, and I normally do like rich, but this is *so* rich.  Neither my husband or I could finish our portion.  On the bright side, this was extremely easy to make, and the directions were very clear.  I would not buy this product.

I wouldn't feed this to my dog!This is nothing more than Hamburger Helper, just in a prettier box.By the time that it takes you to grill the beef, boil the noodles, & add the sauce and seasonings, you could of just made a healthy and nutritious meal for your family.  I could of made eggplant Parmesan in less time (with a salad)...Yuck!
If you like a lot of cheese flavor is this for you!  I used ground turkey instead of beef and really enjoyed it.  I'll buy more.

My family couldn't wait to try this out when it came in the mail, but after just one bite, I could tell that no one would have it. This dinner kit is very easy to make but that's the only positive thing to say. It's too salty, doesn't taste like anything pictured on the box, and it has trans fats. There's no way I'll ever have this in my home again.

See that photo on the cover of the cheesy skillet? Your dish will turn out nothing like it. I had feared that this product would be too cheesy, and in actuality it was not cheesy at all. In fact, it lacked taste and was incredibly bland. I was shocked at how awful it tasted, and even my very hungry family did not like it.The Velveeta package is what confuses me here, because as soon as you add it to the noodles it seems to disappear and you're left with plain noodles and hamburger. Besides the cheese sort of disappearing, there is no taste with this product.The traditional powdery cheesy Mac n' Cheese you get out of a box (which I actually can't stand) is better than this.

column9: Tasty and good for a quick meal
column10: If you're pressed for time and want something that's easy to prepare, filling, and that the kids will eat, this should suit just fine. I wouldn't eat just this for a meal, though, due to the high fat content.We (two adults and three kids) had this for dinner a few days ago, and my wife said it was very easy to prepare. She mentioned that a few times, actually. This makes a good amount of food when prepared according to the package directions. The package indicates enough for about five people, and that's about right. There was more than enough to go around, plus leftovers, although we didn't eat this exclusively for the meal.Most of the family liked it. The flavor was good, and it went down very easy. There was a surprising amount of cheese, enough so that I think in addition to the ground beef you could add additional things like chopped onion, bell pepper, or whatever, and make quite a nice dish out of it. I ate some cold leftovers with lunch the next day, and it tasted just fine.My only gripe is the same thing I have with other cheese-type products: it's very high in fat, and therefore felt rather greasy, and sat a little heavy in my stomach. According to the box, one serving as prepared gives you 25% of the recommended daily fat intake. Because of this, given a choice this isn't a food product I'd eat on its own. Rather, I'd have this along with a small salad, fruit, etc. I'd really like it if instead of having the cheese sauce pre-made in a pouch, they provided a powder (similar to mac-and-cheese) so I can prepare the cheese sauce how I like it.

column9: a crowd-pleaser; even (most) adults liked it
column10: We had six kids and four adults to feed when two families got together one evening this weekend, so we made two packages of the Cheesy Skillets Ultimate Cheesburger Skillets Dinner. In one skillet we added chopped tomatoes, which the adults preferred more than the kids. But everyone liked it and definitely wanted to make it again. We polled the kids and got a thumbs up from all of them! Most of the kids liked that it had "big macaroni" instead of the classic Kraft Dinner small elbow noodles. Both sets of parents usually add sliced cheese when we make the Kraft Dinner to boost the cheese flavor, and all of the kids felt this was cheesier even than that. (No surprise...an actual cheese sauce vs. dried cheese powder is going to win out.) One of the girls said it was "just yummy!" One of my boys said he wanted to add ketchup (well, it IS a cheeseburger meal) and another, hot sauce. I personally did not care for it and thought the flavor was weird. It really depends on you more than anything.

The preparation of this hamburger helper-type meal was very easy. Brown some ground beef, add water, pasta and the seasoning packet. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for about 13 minutes. Uncover and add the enclosed packet of cheese sauce. Stir and serve.My family liked this meal as it was like eating mac & cheese with browned hamburger. It was a bit bland for me so I zipped it up by adding a good sprinkling of white pepper on my serving.Easy to fix and relatively tasty.Recommend.

I normally only make these meals when I am in a pinch for dinner.  I have had a couple of favorite flavors of Hamburger Helper over the years.  I must say that I found this boxed dinner to be quite good.  It simply takes one pound of ground beef, and 2 cups of water, and in about 20 minutes you have dinner.  There is a liquid cheese sauce that is not normally in most boxed dinners.  It was rich and creamy.  I really liked that this reheated well too.  These Cheesy Skillets would be a great item to have in your pantry when you need to make dinner that is fast and simple, and tasty to boot.

I can't tell you how many times I've had Hamburger Helper. And even though I like Hamburger Helper (hey, it's easy!) I always felt like there was room for improvement. Well, that improvement is here!Kraft Velveeta's Cheesy Skillets is basically the same concept as Hamburger Helper. You brown the meat, drain it, cook the noodles, add seasoning packet... and voila! But the best part is the cheesy packet you add at the end. Wow! It really kicked it up a notch! Everyone in my house thought it was absolutely delicious! If you love Velveeta, you can't go wrong!All I know is... I'll never buy Hamburger Helper ever again!

I found this product to be a step above Hamburger Helper. The sauce seemed smoother and had a more flavorful taste. The taste was very good, but maybe a tad on the salty side, but not so much so that was a deal breaker. This is a product I would gladly use again.

column9: Satisfying The Kid In All Of Us
column10: My mom always made the greatest Mac and Cheese, she would add, at times, different things like hamburger, tomatoes etc.  I suppose it helped clean out the fridge, but it was always good.  I still enjoy Mac and Cheese and we love using different cheeses etc. but stick to the basics.  Is it fair to compare Cheesy Skillets to what mom made?---of course not.  No one cooks like our moms did!  I will say that after trying  this I was surprised to find that it was better than I anticipated.  I suppose an aversion to prepared food is one of my faults. We did not add a full lb. of hamburger as it calls for, rather about 3/4 lb., which for us was about the right amount.  It was tasty, slightly salty, but enjoyable.  For those times when you get home and just do not feel like preparing a meal and don't want to go out, it would be great to have this in the pantry.  Easy to fix, quick and really quite good tasting.

My husband, my 9-year-old daughter and myself really enjoyed this meal but we all three made the comment that it needed more macaroni.  The recipe calls for 1 pound of beef and that's what we used but it seemed so much more beefier than it should've been.Preparing this meal was very quick and easy and I didn't think the calories were bad at all.  The box says that it makes 5 1-cup servings and I don't know who could be satisfied with just 1 cup but for the 3 of us (with me being on a diet) it seemed just right when we had some rolls with it.I would recommend this meal.  It's pretty tasty.

column9: Fabulous product - Improvement over Hamburger Helper!
column10: In our house, I've been barred from EVER buying Hamburger Helper.  I suppose that's what happens when you cook from scratch for a bunch of boys nightly!  So, when I mentioned that we were going to try this, the number of moans and groans almost outweighed the sound of the hamburger cooking in the skillet.  But, were we ever in for a surprise.  This stuff is awesome!  It actually includes a large packet of smooth Velveeta cheese to mix in with the entree and just that one element really makes it go over the top in taste.  Mind you, if you'd like to save the calories from the cheese packet, the entree tastes great without it.My only complaints are: 1), it's a bit salty.  This is particularly heightened after adding that packet of cheese.  It's not over the top like some soups can be, but it's definitely a negative.  If you're on a salt-controlled diet, this might be an issue. 2). The actual serving size of the package is small.  And I mean, VERY small.  If you have a family of 3, then each individual would get one serving.  Any larger than that, then you're in trouble unless you have VERY young children.  If you have a hungry husband and sons, you'll wind up buying 3 boxes to actually make enough to fill them up.  My suggestion: add a salad with meat, along with a vegetable and some healthy bread and that helps considerably.  In addition, add something like a can of diced tomatoes to this dish and use ground turkey or chicken to make it healthier.  Milk to drink always helps too.  There is enough sauce to add an additional 1/2 pound of meat to the dish, along with the tomatoes, and the cheese sauce can cook a bit longer in the pan to make it more "runny" to infuse with the additional ingredients.So, this is definitely a "keeper" in this house.  I about fell off my chair when I heard a "Yum!"  But, Velveeta has been creating "Yums" for years and I am not surprised that this dish is in keeping with their history. Highly recommend!

The dinner kit was fast and easy to prepare and it was tasty.  I am a Velveeta fan, so that probably helps.  But I'm giving it 4 stars since I think the added flavor packet took away from the cheesy experience.  Next time, I will try it without the packet to confirm this.

column9: Comfort Food for your inner child
column10: When they say cheesy - they mean cheesy.  This is the type of one pot meal mom made when my brothers and I were kids.  When this arrived it was one of those off days when I didn't quite know what to toss together for supper & thought now's a good time to give this product the once over.It was on the table in 20 minutes, as promised.  I used turkey but imagine the ground beef choice would be just as easy.  Brown the meat, toss in the flavor pack & pasta, 2 cups of water & let simmer for 11 minutes.  Then add the Velveeta Cheese pouch & kick it up a notch.  True comfort food in the blink of an eye.  Serve with some green beans & salad & you have a meal the family will enjoy (and ask for again).The nutrition values are a little on the high side and I don't like that little trace of trans fats at all but for a quick and easy meal with no fuss it's still a good option & better than a lot of "fast food" choices you may haul home.I say give it a try & judge for yourselves.  If you don't agree leave a comment below but I'll bet you're happy with your purchase.

The latest spin on semi-homemade dinners is Kraft's Velveeta Cheesy Skillets. The kit includes pasta, a seasoning packet, and the gooey Velvetta cheese. All you need to add is 1 lb. of ground beef (or turkey) and 2 cups of water. The product claims to be ready in about 20 minutes, and that is correct. It took me about 19 minutes from start to finish. In terms of overall flavor, my kids, husband, and I all loved this meal.  In terms of the nutritional value, it's approximately 350 calories prepared and 25% of the daily recommended fat value. The real kicker is in the sodium content... 850mg. Let's be honest, it's not a gourmet meal; however, for a quick fix on a school night, you can't beat it. Serve it with a side salad and some fresh steamed broccoli, this meal is a winner.

For what is, a variation on Hamburger Helper but more expensive, this is OK.  There was something about the flavor, possibly the spices, that I just didn't enjoy.  Moreover, it really didn't taste like Velveeta cheese, which I really enjoy cooking with.  This is not something I would actually buy and eat on a regular basis. If I really want a boxed meal I'll go with Hamburger Helper

The new Velveeta Cheesy Skillets Ultimate Cheeseburger kit is fantastic! A one skillet meal that uses creamy Velveeta instead of powdered "cheese flavoring"? Awesome! I found this to be far superior to the similar Hamburger Helper flavor. While it IS rich, it makes a great, quick meal with a side salad.

column9: Similar to Hamburger Helper with a Velveeta taste
column10: We had two boxes of this product for 7 of us and had plenty.  Taste is good if you like Velveeta Cheese flavor rather than American Cheese.  There seems to be plenty of cheese and good pasta.  Good flavor.

This was very disappointing.  While it's easy to make, it has a very strange taste to it.  The first thing that jumps to find is a McDonald's cheese burger.  It tasted very artificial and cheap.  Not something I'll ever make again.

column9: An old stand-by hits the spot!
column10: I've always had a soft-spot for pasta and cheese because when I was raising my six children it was an easy, economical solution for a quick meal that they all liked. For some reason unknown to adults, kids do tend to like pasta and cheese in all its variations much better than adults do. I used to prepare the macaroni and cheese (no hamburger) for them with a salad and a half sandwich or a plain burger. Simple and easy...Ease of preparation is one of the reasons I got this product. The other reason is that when I saw the burger bits on the package it reminded me of good ol' juicy cheeseburgers that I loved in my younger days. Even though I don't eat them now, there was a time when I scarfed those cheeseburgers down...with big slices of raw onion. Yummy! Anyway, this dish blends together in a taste reminiscent of a cheeseburger and is very tasty. A bit too salty, but since I won't be eating it often, it won't harm me.In summation, Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheesburger Skillets Dinner Kit, 12.86-Ounce (Pack of 6) passes the taste test, the ease-of-preparation test and since one box is enough for five people, it also passes the economical test. What more could anyone ask for in a hurried meal?It hits the spot!Reviewed by Betty Dravis, September 26, 2011Author of "Dream Reachers" series of books (with Chase Von)

column9: Not just a Hamburger Helper wannabe!
column10: I thought this would be a lot like Hamburger Helper.  Boy was I wrong!  Because the cheese sauce isn't added until the very last step (just before eating), this is creamier and smoother than any variety of Hamburger Helper I've ever had (and I've tries most of them).  I suppose some people would think that the extra step (waiting until the seasonings and pasta have already finished cooking before adding the cheese sauce) make this more complicated.  I don't think so, and it is SO worth that little extra step!

column9: Tasty Way to a Simple Meal
column10: The Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheeseburger Skillets Dinner Kit brings to mind hamburger helper.  Start with ground meat (I used goat), cook, drain the fat, add the spice mix, macaroni, water, cook until ready, add in the Velveeta.  To add more flavor and make a little healthier, i also mixed in sauteed onions, pistachios and hearts of palm.  A good dose of vegetables (really, anything on hand will fit the bill), greatly improves the dish, and takes little extra work.

That title about sums it up. Total prep time is about 20 minutes, and in addition to the package's contents all you need is a pound of ground beef and two cups of water. In the last step you may look at the amount of cheese sauce they want you to add and hesitate, but that block of Velveeta is only that intimidating when it is in one solid chunk; once you mix it in it looks like the front of the package. Each box gets you roughly four normal-sized servings.This may just be me hearkening back to my old college dorm days, but I tried it cold (having refrigerated about 2/3 of it, as I was cooking for one that night) and actually enjoyed it just as much as I did right after taking it off the skillet.In short, this is one easy box dinner I will be returning to several times.

Like the box says, you get a pound of lean hamburger, cook it up, drain it, add two cups of water, seasoning, pasta, bring to a boil, and then cook it until most of the water is gone.  Then you add the Velveeta and you get- Surprise -Velveeta Cheese Hamburger HelperActually, the stuff is fairly good.  I've got kids and the family liked this.  The little one ate it right up.  It's a little high in calories at 350 per serving.  But all in all it's a good meal and fairly inexpensive for the family.It's not bad and I give it four stars.

This is a great tasting and easy to prepare "mac n cheese" meal.  I would consider this the deluxe variety and not the basic type that we find in stores.  I prepared this vegan style and am sure it would be that much easier to prepare it with "meat".Tastes great, highly recommended.

column4: Sir Charles Panther "Life is hard.  It's hard...
column9: Not Bad, Not Great...Another Meat `N Noodles Product
column10: In the box you get yer dried elbow macaroni, an envelope of "seasoning," and an envelope of squishy Velveeta "cheese sauce."The box is a bit of a deception, as the contents easily would fit in a smaller box.  A bigger box conveys the expectation of a bigger end-product, right?  And of course a bigger box stands out better on the store shelf and offers a lot more copy space for that crucial moment when you have to engage and convince the consumer.  Mmmmm, pretty golden-yellow colors, and red cursive-y lettering, with a photo of noodles as big as my fingers...I followed the on-box instructions explicitly.  Well, okay, I admit it, I used 1.37 pounds of hamburger instead of the stated 1 pound.  All glory and praise to Odin that there were no adverse effects!  It all turned out just fine, basically just like the photo on the front of the box, neither watery/runny nor dry; everything glommed together just right.  The stated "makes about 5 one-cup servings" is about right.  Now, Kraft came out with the "family size" macaroni n' cheez kit way back when, and I'd argue that Velveeta (a Kraft brand) would want to do the same thing, and it might even help actually fill up this oversized/underutilized box.I didn't add anything to the recipe, as this was the first time with the product, and I was cooking with this review in mind.  As for taste, it was just fine.  Nothing special, but not bad.  Now, did this taste like "ultimate cheeseburger?"  No, not at all.  That's because there was no bun, mayonnaise, pickles, mustard, or grill-charred meat with a slick slab of melted cheez atop, all of the things I put on a cheezburger.  I did go with the "customize it!" advice on the back of the box and had some chopped onions, diced tomatoes and chopped lettuce on hand, which was a nice addition to the product, more than anything lending it some crunch, and a nicer range of flavor.  One could really go nuts and drop some salsa into the mix, or even saute' some fresh broccoli or carrots with the hamburger.  Now we're talking a meat n' cheez dinner creation that's a lot more interesting and certainly more tasty.If I were to use this product again--and this might be a good thing to put in the copy on the package--I'd cook some diced onions with the hamburger, and/or some chopped mushrooms.  This would bulk up the servings somewhat, and definitely yield more depth of flavor.  I added no spices to the product, and it was accordingly bland.  If I were to cook this again, I'd add salt, pepper, some caraway seeds, maybe a bit of rosemary and most definitely some garlic and a little bit of red pepper.Yes, it was ready in about twenty minutes, as the box copy promised.Yes, I'd use this product again, but I can't say I'm going to go out of my way at the store to find it and buy it.I do like the TV ads for this product, though, funny and original.  Let the smiting continue!Bottom Line: this is another offering in the great American Hamburger Helper tradition.  It's a one-pan dinner that's really easy to make and takes little time.  Following the instructions yields a passable main dish that while not bad, isn't really that interesting and offers some nutritional value.  The kit does offer, however, a foundation upon which one can experiment and improvise to create more varied mealtime indulgences.

I have to admit, I am NOT a fan of processed foods. I cringe at the thought of Hamburger Helper and products like that. However, I have a soft spot in my heart for Velveeta Shells & Cheese, which I loved as a kid and would spice up in college with veg or meat to make it into a full meal. So when I was given the opportunity to review the new Velveeta Cheesy Skillet, I decided to take the plunge into childhood nostalgia.The long story short is that we really enjoyed this. The dish was exceptionally cheesy, which my household loved and the flavor of the meat blended wonderfully with this dish. My girlfriend was actually disappointed that we only recieved one package instead of the full six pack you get here at Amazon. So the fact you have two people who prefer to cook everything from scratch loving this dish tells you the flavor quality here.My only qualm is that this is exceptionally high in sodium and fat even before you add the hamburger. To offset that we went with 93/7 extra lean ground beef.For those that are curious, you're getting 15 ounces per package here compared to the 12 ounces you would get in a 2% milk Shells and Cheese package, so although the Cheesy Skillets cost a bit more, you're actually getting more foodstuff to balance it out.I definitely recommend this for those that don't like to cook or that need a quick meal on a small budget.

My hubby and I really enjoyed this dish.  Very similar to Hamburger Helper Cheeseburger Macaroni.  It's great if you have kids or just as a meal by yourself. If you want, you can substitute ground beef for the Boca ground Crumble and it still tastes good.  It's real easy to prepare in a single skillet.  I like that it is the creamy cheese, instead of the powder.The second time I made it - I add bacon bits, so it had a more Bacon Cheese Burger taste.

column4: C. Ball "An idea that is not dangerous is unw...
column10: Being a house with two big sons, having some meals be easy to prepare and inexpensive is essential.  But it also has to taste good!  This fits both bills and as an added bonus, it doesn't contain the mysterious sulfites that sometimes leave me feeling like my inside are wringing themselves with some other products.  My sons took to this immediately and cooked it up and devoured it.  This is definitely an upgrade to the other "helper meals".  This one is much cheesier and tastier.

column9: Quick and easy, much better than powdered cheese mixes
column10: This is very similar to Hamburger Helper in terms of ease of preparation, but it uses a Velveeta-based liquid (or semi-liquid) cheese sauce in a foil packet rather than powdered cheese that you reconstitute with milk and butter.  That bumps it up quite a bit in terms of flavor, although it's still just cheeseburger macaroni, so it's not going to change your life.(Except perhaps by shortening it slightly...in the interest of full disclosure, for any health nuts out there that may somehow be unaware, cheeseburger macaroni isn't the healthiest meal you can choose.)

A definite step above the traditional helper for hamburger that is widely avaiable. My family enjoyed this meal very much. We had a lot of home grown tomatoes that I chopped up with some lettuce and the tomatoes mixed in with the finished product added a lot of extra flavor that I really liked. My only complaint is that I find it a bit of a problem to squeeze out the velveeta from the package. It can get rather messy trying to get out every bit of the cheese sauce (waste not, want not) lol The flavor is good, and I think anyone who wants a good quick, easy meal, this one is worth getting.

column9: Like Hamburger Helper with a Bit More Cheese and Flavour
column10: I've enjoyed many a meal of Mac & Cheese Hamburger Helper through the years, and Kraft's Velveeta foray into the skillet, quick meal world is very much in this vein...but cheesier and tastier. Our family liked it.The cooking process is pretty straight-forward - cook the ground beef, add the noodles, water, and seasonings, boil, and add the cheese. It's probably a 20 minute process, but the chief need not be standing over the stove that whole time.It was enough food for a couple of adults and a couple of little kids.

I was really surprised  at how good this product tasted. I was expecting something bland like hamburger helper. The cheese was thick and creamy, and the overall dish was not super salty like I expected. I would definitely try all the varieties of this product.

column9: Creamy Cheeseburger Macaroni in a box
column10: This is an upgrade to your traditional Hamburger Helper brand.  If you like Velveeta with its creamy smooth cheese, then you will like this product.  I don't purchase a lot of easy quick meals but I always have it on hand for emergencies.  This fits the bill perfectly.  It has taste, texture, and provides a great casual meal for the family, especially my children.  Water + ground beef + this box = quick easy dinner.

its not much different than its competitors when it comes to the ease of preparation. in this, they are all pretty much interchangeable. hence, all that really matters is in the taste. it's quite good actually, cheesy and savory. i just wish that it was a tad cheesier and creamier. i admit i improvise a lot when cooking - my style is loose and dynamic i guess. so, trying to be 'healthy' - yes, box preparations ain't exactly the healthiest, but i never say i wasn't lazy - i tossed in some fresh cauliflower and broccoli with the pasta. the flavorings comes next, and that's when i tasted it to make sure it wasn't too bland. that's when i noticed that it WAS bland, and added a bit of salt to taste. what i didn't realize is that how salty the cheese sauce was! that really threw me off. thankfully i didn't add a lot of salt, so the dish was palatable and quite nice really. however, looking back, i think that if someone prepares the meal strictly according to the directions without additions, the end product may be a tad salty.all in all however, a decent and quick meal.

Some days you just want something fast and easy for dinner. Luckily, Velveeta Cheesy Skillets kits are fast, easy, and pretty tasty.I made this one using ground turkey, and it turned out to be a pretty big hit for my family. In about 20 minutes, we were chowing down. The sauce did taste a little artificial, but then it's to be expected with this kind of boxed dish. The cheese sauce, though, was immensely better than powdered sauces in other skillet meal kits.The price is a little on the high side, but having the cheese sauce makes up for it.

I was reluctant to try the Velveeta skillets dinner kit because I cannot stand hamburger helper and this product reminded me of it. However I was really surprised by how much I liked it. This meal has so much flavor it's unbelievable. You can really taste all of the flavors of this meal and it doesn't taste like cardboard as other box meals do. The cheeseburger box meal makes a lot of food as well. In comparison to other box meals this Velveeta box meal has them beat hands down with taste and quality. If you are looking for a great meal at a reasonable price look no further than this meal. This is so simple to make as well...cook hamburger, cook noodles, add the cheese, and the sauce packet and it's complete. I liked this cheeseburger skillets dinner so well that I purchased another one recently. This is also a hit with the family. Highly recommended to all family who likes Velveeta cheese or box meals.

One of the greatest "joys" of being a college student is being poor and the culinary innovation that is invoked in order to make the most out of your dollar.  I found myself as being the Hamburger Helper Connoisseur among my friends.  Little did I know that they were as healthy as Cup O Noodles and with each bite, I met my daily allowance of sodium. So it was with a bit of nostalgia that I approached my trial with the Velveeta version.  I would say that when it comes to helping make a quick meal, the relative ease of preparation is a big plus.  But the basic recipe is somewhat lacking, although cheesy.  I found that adding some extra garlic, chopped onions, and some fresh diced tomatoes, it became a lot better.  But I don't really see how it is much easier than making a similar dish by adding dry pasta noodles, velveeta cheese and some milk.

column9: Really cheesy, really easy and really good!
column10: This meal was incredibly easy to prepare, following the instructions on the box.  Essentially brown some ground beef, and add everything else in one skillet.  A few minutes later you have a really delicious cheesy treat.let's be honest, this is a meal in a box.  If you are seeking a true epicurean, go buy your fresh ingredients and make a fresh meal.  This cannot compete with that, and it isn't trying to.  If however, you are a busy parent, who gets home at 5:30 and is trying to have a good warm dinner everyone will eat by 6:00, this is a good choice.Again, this is not the healthiest thing you will eat all day, probably.  However, it's great comfort food, it's warm, cheesy and tasty!We highly recommend this for an easy quick meal.

"Kraft Velveeta Cheeseburger Dinner"; is really good in flavor but you have to make sure to do not add salt. It has a lot of salt pre-added.  It does feed three to four people if you add a salad or vegetable with it. It is easy and quick.  I have bought another dinner from Kraft Velveet and it was good too. It beats eating a boxed macaroni and cheese.  This is good, fast and tasty and I recommend it for any one who needs to eat on the run.  Thanks to Kraft, again.

I love Kraft Velveeta Cheesy Skillets. This is a great Box Meal. Just add Ground Beef and water. No other ingridents needed. This could not be easier. Everything needed to make this a great meal is in the box. The cheese is very creamy. This comes with creamy cheese and not the dry cheese found in most Boxed Meal Kits. The price is also great. Great for your family and your family will enjoy.

This dinner kit should be in everyone's pantry.  If you have this and a pound of hamburger, you'll never be caught short for a quick dinner.  Just brown your hamburger, pour in the mix and some water and you're all set.  And...did I say...it tastes really good.  The color could be more appetizing but it probably won't last on your table long enough for that to be noticed, much less a problem.

column9: Family approved, Mom not so much...
column10: I do think that the creamy cheese mix that Velveeta includes is a better option than the Hamburger Helper offerings of a powdered cheese.  However, it did not increase the taste factor enough for me to contemplate five stars. I try to limit the processed food that I feed to my family so if time constraints have me picking a meal to fix along these lines taste tends to win out for me and I found it to be just ok.  My husband found it to be to his liking and my kids also seemed satisfied with the meal which is why I gave it four stars.  I personally did not find the cheese to be as tasty as it could have been.

I am a cheesy mac person, so this was right up my alley! I love the super cheesy of this product! I love the big fat noodles and it wasn't as salty as other prepackaged meals. This is always super easy and doesn't take a lot of effort if you have had a long day or it is too hot out and you want something yummy for dinner. You can always add lots of things to make it extra yummy but it does help when the cheese is perfect and aplenty in my opinion!I would love to find other prepared meals they have out, Velveeta knows cheese!!

If you're looking for something fast, easy and tasty for dinner than you need look no further - it's as simple as boiling water for pasta and cooking up some hamburg.  The creamy Velveeta sauce is really what makes this good, much more satisfying than other powder cheese sauces.  The seasoning that is included may not be to everyone's liking - I only used about 3/4 of the seasoning provided and I found it perfect for my taste - plenty of flavor.  Other people may prefer using all of the seasoning, or even less.Round your meal out with a salad and you can't go wrong - for a busy weeknight dinner this is perfect!

column9: For a "Hamburger Helper" type of meal, this IS perfection
column10: I remember as a kid just LOVING any "Hamburger Helper" product.  Over time, my taste buds have become more refined, but I'm still willing to try a new "just add meat and water" meal.This one knocks it out of the ballpark on flavor and quality.  VERY cheesy, huge noodles, and great overall flavor make this THE best of the boxed dinners that I have had to-date.  A separate cheese packet is included (not the dry powdered stuff, but the squeeze-out cheese), which definitely enhances the flavor and texture while making preparation easy (no "pockets" of dry powder to deal with when blending in the cheese).The only downside is that it goes quickly; one box is just enough to feed my wife and I (no kids).Folks, if you like the boxed dinners, then I can almost guarantee this one will be a winner with you - my new favorite - enjoy!

column9: Simple to prepare, but a little salty
column10: My guess is that this product will forever be compared to Hamburger Helper, and it should. It tasted much the same as the HH offering. The thing that distinguishes this product though, is the use of Velveeta Cheese in the ingredients. I love Velveeta Cheese and have since I was a kid (many moons ago). There is also a spice packet that is part of the ingredients. The product contains 900 mg of sodium, which amounts to 38% of daily values. One serving also contains 350 calories, but if this is your main dish, chances are you will eat more than one cup of this. I did like the taste however, but as I try to be more health conscious, I will not eat this very often. For a quick fix it works well.

This is pretty tasty if you eat this sort of thing, and I'll admit it's a rare guilty pleasure for me.  As compared to the brand that is no doubt its main competitor, I thought this one tasted better, probably because of the already mixed almost-cheese sauce that is included (which also replaces the milk that's usually added).It's pretty much a toss-up in terms of nutrition, given that we aren't looking at a nutritional champ to begin with here.  As prepared, this one has 350 calories per serving, the other 310.  This has 140 calories from fat, the other 110.  This one has 850 mg of sodium, the other one has 810.  The Kraft Velveeta Cheesy Skillet comes out slightly ahead overall, with protein of 8 g compared to the other's 3 g and dietary fiber of 1 g compared to less than a gram for the competitor.  These differences are probably attributable to the "cheese" sauce.  The sauce also pushes this one over the edge for total fat, with 9 g for this one and 0.5 for the other.  After the ground beef is added, the difference is 25% of the recommended daily amount vs. 19% (virtually none of it "good" fat in either one).It is significant that although both brands claim zero transfat, both also list partially hydrogenated oil as one of their ingredients, meaning they certainly do contain transfat, just less than the half-gram per serving that would require full disclosure.  If you eat the whole package - about 5 cups, so realistically with a dinner and a leftover lunch or two, you easily might - you could get whacked with as much as 2.4 g of transfat, not to mention the saturated fat in the ground beef you add to both.  At 800+ grams of sodium, you probably need to skip another meal that day to avoid going over the recommended daily value for sodium, too.  You might consider fasting that day if you plan to eat more than one serving!But, as I said, it's a guilty pleasure; by definition, that's not the most nutritionally sound choice that can be made.  In any case, all other things (price, availability) being equal, I will probably choose this one if I choose it again.

Wow! This actually tastes like a cheeseburger! I've prepared it two ways, one is by the box directions which was FANTASTIC. The second time I left out the pasta and made it into a "sloppy joe" type meal. The boys loved it and it tastes great! I can't praise this enough.

column9: Fast, Flavorful, and Easy To Fix!
column10: I'm very familiar with Hamburger Helper, and, frankly, this beats HH hands down.  Both meals call for a pound of hamburger, to which is added a quantity of macaroni, and a sauce for flavoring.  The big difference with the Velveeta skillet dinner is that the flavoring sauce doesn't come in a powdered form.  Nope, the folks at Kraft put a nice foil packet of Velveeta cheese in with their macaroni, and that makes all the difference.  The Velveeta Ultimate Cheeseburger Skillet Dinner is much richer and creamier, cooks up quickly, and paired with a nice salad, makes for a great fast dinner.  My brother and I both enjoyed it so much, we bought another box to have later on.  I let my cats lick the bowl and they loved it too!  Two paws up!

I thought this Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheeseburger Skillets Dinner was very tasty. I like to keep quick meals like this or hamburger helper when my kids have Dance or Gymnastics and you need a quick meal. My daughter loves hamburger helper cheeseburger macaroni but she says she loves this more. I have to agree with my daughter, I don't know how they did it but it tastes like a McDonalds cheeseburger. It's weird but it's almost like you can taste a hint of ketchup, mustard, onion & pickle in it. It's quick and easy to make and it comes with a seasoning packet that you add in with the macaroni after cooking your ground beef. When it's done cooking you add the liquid cheese packet. Another thing I like about it, is you don't have to add milk, you just add 2 cups of water. It is really yummy.

column9: People who like this sort of thing will find this the sort of thing they like.
column10: I don't know what Abraham Lincoln was speaking of when he said that, but it fits this Velveeta product pretty well.  If you like this sort of boxed meal, then you'll probably enjoy this, though I have to say that I think Hamburger Helper does it better.  Heck, I think you can do way better from scratch if you're so inclined, and it wouldn't be that much more difficult.For all the cheese product in this thing (The "seasoning" bag was filled with cheese powder, and there was a whole pouch of Velveeta to add to the finished product) the resulting meal wasn't all that cheesy-tasting.  And really, the point of this sort of meal isn't just relative cheapness or convenience, but also big flavor.  Stuff like this is as much about satisfying some kind of itch for something that tastes like it's bad for you.  That's a big part of the appeal of fast food after all.  And on that point, this product doesn't deliver what I think it ought.On the plus side, though, it is relatively cheap.  You'll get four to five decent-size servings out of it at between about 350 to 400 calories a serving.  Made with veggies instead of meat and both price and calorie count go down.  And you can certainly add seasonings of your own to make it more appealing.  Just don't expect big flavor as it comes out of the box.  It's just not there.  One note though: Cooking for the recommended amount of time makes the pasta really soft.  If you like yours al dente, start testing well before the 11 minute mark.So honestly?  I doubt I'll ever buy a box of this again.  It tasted fine; it just didn't excite me.  Meh.

I've tried to write this review three times now, and every time I get a power blip or something happens to the browser and I lose it.  One more time.I made this carefully, and it is not tasty.  It has a big packet of spices that has a lot of whey, onion, and cheese and spices like black pepper are lower than an ingredient that is listed as "not more than 2%.I've eaten tasty mac and cheese, and I've even eaten decent hamburger helper, like Hamburger Helper, Cheesy Nacho, 7.9-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6).  That stuff is cheaper and tastes better.This stuff is easy to make.  You brown one pound of beef (I weighed it to be sure I was following directions) and then drain it (pouring out the tasty juices, I won't do that again), then add the misnamed seasoning packet and the pasta, along with two cups of water.Bring it to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and cook for 11-13 minutes.Then remove from the heat and mix in the velveeta packet.They suggest that you add lettuce?  Or chopped tomatoes, so I added Ro-Tel to part of it - the other part I kept pristine so that I could taste it as made.  I used hot Ro-Tel, and, other than the flavor of the Ro-Tel it was bland.  I have to think that the pasta is sort of bland and the spicing in the packet is lacking.  It could have some more onion flavor, or more than 0.5% garlic or something.The value in this is what I believe to be parboiled pasta that can be cooked in this fashion.The net weight of this stuff is 12.8 ounces - with a pound of beef, it makes 5 one cup servings.  My wife guesses that it serves three adults, or six-eight toddlers (if you were making lunch for a day care, say).Now, this is my suggestion:Suppose you buy a piece of velveeta in the store, some cream, some beef, and a little garlic powder, some onion powder, and some pasta.Cook a quarter pound of pasta in one pan, boiling and draining normally, and then brown a pound or two of beef with a bunch of onion and garlic powder, to taste.  In a third pan (or in the one you boiled the pasta in), grate or cube about a pound of Velveeta and heat it gently with a 2 tbsp of butter, stirring frequently until melted, then add about 1/4 to 1/2 cup cream a little at a time while stirring. Add a little white pepper and 1/8 tsp nutmeg, if you like it. Or use sour cream instead of whole cream, or put a little beef broth into the beef after it has browned.Now combine the cheese sauce, the pasta (use more or less to taste, the beef (please don't drain it unless you are on a low fat diet, and then do so carefully - if you have one of those old fat brushes, use that, try to save the juices).  Then add a whole can of Ro-Tel, to your family's taste, hot, mild, lime-chili, whatever.  Taste it - and if it is bland, fix it.Dust the top with paprika before serving it.This dish will taste good, and it won't take you much longer to make it than it would to start with this mix.  And if it is bland, you have only yourself to blame.  You can put more or less salt, pepper, herbs, and whatever - you don't need to use a mix to make a cheese/macaroni/beef dish.  This stuff really isn't that hard.Now, there is nothing wrong with Velveeta.  It melts nicely, it makes a great cheese sauce.  It usually has some flavor.  And there is nothing wrong with this stuff except that it is just tasteless, and almost anyone can do better.  Seriously, YOU can do better than this bland product.  If you like Velveeta, use it. If you don't like Velveeta, well, making it yourself allows you to make your cheese sauce from a different type of cheese.  Mexican melting cheese is good.  Heck, Sargento six cheese is great.If you don't want to do it yourself, save money and buy Hamburger Helper.I can't rate this less than 3 stars, far as I can tell, it is wholesome and it doesn't actively taste bad. It doesn't actively taste of much at all.  So it gets three stars, and a suggestion that you can do so much better by doing it yourself that you should try.If I had some of this stuff I had to use, I'd:Add a half tsp of white pepper, a half tsp of paprika, garlic powder to taste and onion powder to taste.  I might consider a knorr garlic cube.  Or Chipotle.  I would always add the Ro-Tel, this is the biggest fix you can make to this stuff. Paprika to dust the top before serving.  And, well, beef broth instead of water - that "seasoning" is really, really bland. A dollop of sour cream when you put the cheese sauce in, and a tablespoon of butter.Because as shipped, it is horribly bland.

Overall, I like this new velveeta Cheesy Skillets meal. It was very fast - less than 20 minutes including browning the meat) and unlike Hamburger Helper, the Velveeta doesn't require milk. So quite simple to make in a pinch if you haven't been to the store or whatever. And the noodles are larger than the ones in the Hamburger Helper version. The only negative thing was a slight after taste for the first few bites. It was sort of a chemical tinged flavor. I was the only one of the three of us that had this for dinner that experienced that after taste sensation. It's entirely possible that it's just me, so I am only taking one star from the overall rating.

I do love a nice boxed dinner! Velveeta Cheesy Skillets Dinner is a breeze to prepare; just brown the ground beef and drain, add water and seasoning packet, simmer eleven minutes or so, stir in creamy cheese sauce and finally add any optional embellishments desired.The taste of the finished product alone is very good - I guess it would be fair to say I like it quite a bit better than the Hamburger Helper Cheesy Mac, which leaves a high-sodium aftertaste. I added a tomato embellishment (though using tough-skinned, yet seeded garden fresh tomatoes) and wished that I had just left it alone, although if the tomatoes were a bit better it would have been really nice, but I'll stick with the base recipe in the future. There is nothing I don't like about this product.Each box makes five satisfying one cup servings. I'm always good for a couple of servings and there's plenty left to share or to save for a later time. So, with the creamy, smooth texture and the velvety, rich cheesy flavor, I will most assuredly continue to buy Velveeta Cheesy Skillets Dinner. It's delicious and I look forward to having more.

I eat Kraft Mac & Cheese dinners a few times a month, sometimes the deluxe and sometimes the regular type.  I never serve them as the main entree but as a side dish & I stick to the recommended serving size.  I thought that I would really like the Cheesy Skillets as a change-up from the usual but I found the onion flavor/aroma overpowering.  Now, I'm not a big fan of onions so someone who likes Kraft's other Mac & Cheese offerings and loves onions might love this one.  It is what it is:  a quick-fix dish for those who aren't watching fat, sodium, and/or cholesterol in their diets.

My college age daughter was babysitting a bunch of kids and made this the other day, it was a hit. Everyone loved it and she liked the easiness of it all. The kids were not used to Velveeta and thought it was very creamy. Not for everyday, but convenient when you need something easy and handy to fix that tastes good!

I'm a fan of Velveeta shells and cheese, so of course, this is no exception.  It is very easy to make, simply brown your meat, then add the water, noodles, and spices. Cook until the noodles are tender, then mix in the cheese sauce.  The spices that came with have a distinct chargrilled burger taste.  The cheese was very creamy and much thicker than what you would get with the mix from similar meals in a box.  I did find it to be a little salty, but I am somewhat sensitive to salt as it is.I would recommend this over similar boxed meals because of the superior flavor and quality.

column9: Not Bad for What It Is
column10: I didn't expect too much from this dinner-in-a-box meal and it didn't disappoint.I cooked the dish using ground turkey and once browned, added the water, elbow pasta, and powdered seasoning pack as instructed. Once that got thoroughly mixed and simmered for a while I added the Velveeta creamy cheese sauce, stirred, and the dinner entree was done.The result was something like a box of Kraft Macaroni and Cheese but with larger pasta, meat, and a creamier texture.  The Velveeta flavor was not as chemically cheesy/sharp as Kraft and the subtle differences in the seasoning made it more interesting than the one-note Kraft.If I was to do this again I would add kielbasa or sausage to add more interest.Overall, not bad for an "instant" dinner.

column9: You Can Adjust Everything To Meet Your Dietary Needs
column10: This new Velveeta Cheesy Skillets boxed dinner was a nice surprise from the usual powdered cheesy boxed dinners. In our household, we have to watch sodium and cholesterol levels and this dinner can be tweaked to your dietary needs. For a one cup serving, there are 350 calories, 140 calories are from fat. The cholesterol has 15 mg- mostly from the cheese and some from the gound beef. The sodium is pretty high at 850 mg, but this is mainly from the spice packet and some from the cheese preservatives. The best part, is we used only a tablespoon of the spices and we lowered the cholesterol to 300 mg- a huge difference for your diet. You can use any type of gound beef, they say to use a pound, but that is way too much meat- we used 2/3 of a pound and it was perfect.We browned less beef- 2/3 of a pound- drained it, added the water, a tablespoon of spices and the elbow macaroni. Bring it to a boil, then simmer on a high simmer covered, stirring every couple of minutes. In about 13 minutes, when the water is gone, it's ready for the creamy Velveeta cheese packet to be mixed in and it's ready to eat. Because we used less ground beef, we also used a little less cheese. We added some sliced tomatoes and olives on the side and it was really good for a boxed dinner. It would be good with any kind of salad. The creamy Velveeta cheese made this dinner really so much better tasting than dinners with powdered cheese, and being able to control the sodium with just a little of the spices is a huge plus. Even with hardly any spices, the taste was delicious, the sodium and cholesterol low, it's quick and easy to prepare, so this will be a dinner we will definitely have again.

Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheesburger Skillets Dinnereasy, quick, delicious, one pan to clean up.  Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheesburger Skillets Dinner is a lot of fun to prepare, and the end product is so delicious -- everyone wants seconds. I kid you not! Even Dad loves Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheesburger Skillets Dinner! :)add a little vegie salad, a few jumbo pitted black olives and a few warmed taco shells on the side, and you've got a really nice casual dinner.*off to order another case of Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheesburger Skillets Dinner from Amazon*  Highly Recommended! --Katharena Eiermann, 2011

First, I'll say that I made this without any meat. I'm a meat-a-holic so I wanted to get the full taste of this product without being biased by the beef. My initial observation is that the amount of noodles that comes with the kit seems rather insufficient. The kit also included the silver pouch of creamy cheese that comes with other Velveeta noodle products and a small packet of seasoning (an orange-ish powder).The way I made this was that instead of water, I used heavy whipping cream with the cheese sauce. I only used a little of the seasoning because it seemed disproportionate to the amount the noodles in the box. I can't imagine how season-y this would taste if someone used the whole pouch.The taste was okay. It has a leg up on Hamburger Helper because the cheese sauce is creamy as opposed to a powder. It also seems like the noodles are larger in size than the noodles that come with Hamburger Helper. However, it's hard for me to recommend one over the other because the difference isn't that big. I can see ardent lovers of Hamburger Helper liking this just as much.

I had low expectations for this meal but was pleasantly surprised by how tasty it is. Total cooking time was about a half hour. I added a large can of diced tomatoes and a chopped onion once the dish was cooked and then added shredded lettuce to the top once it was plated. It would have been good without these additions but adding those ingredients definitely made it better. I would buy this product again.

We're used some Velveeta products in our house from time to time ranging from the boxed cheeselike form to the newer pasta mixes.  This is another of the pasta mixes they currently offer and clearly these are designed to compete with the Hamburger Helper brand that you add meat, water and sometimes butter to as well.  Since this is a competitor, it makes sense to compare them.Frankly this Velveeta version of the Cheeseburger variety falls far short of the Hamburger Helper version.  The steps are almost identical except for the added foil packet of Velveeta sauce that you add at the end.  I'm not sure what caused the sour taste that no one in the family liked, but since we have liked the plain boxed pastas versions before, I'm thinking it must be the seasonings packet.  Not only did this not stand up to the level of Hamburger Helper but it also fell short of the store brand of this particular variety which we've also had several times, thus the 2 instead of 3 stars I would have given it had it pleased my family as much as s the store brand.The final result is that the product is OK but certainly not as good a taste as other brands of this exact same variety. Since these box mixes tend to cost more than either Hamburger Helper or store brands, the value is even less.  You'd do better just adding your own ingredients to pasta and cheese you had around the house.

Something you have to know about me is that I almost never cook or bake exactly according to directions.  I didn't with this either.  With five kids, I do my best to make meals stretch... and I do a lot of cooking from scratch.Some days, though, it is really, really nice to have a solid base to build on.  And that is how I used this Cheesy Skillets meal.I started with browning the hamburger, as per the directions, but to that I had added an onion and some chopped celery.  When it came time to add the pasta and seasonings, I added an extra handful of macaroni, and additional water.  I would have added additional water anyway because of our altitude.The best part was adding the cheese packet.  Not dried cheese, this was creamy and smooth.Because this was something I was asked to review, that is the extent of the changes I made.  Served with bread and a vegetable, this made a great meal.The result?  My kids loved it.  I liked it.  They requested that I definitely do this again.If I wasn't reviewing the product, I would have considered other additions.  Tomatoes added near the end would be great, as would a handful of fresh spinach.  If I had less ground beef around, I think a half pound of meat plus some great northern beans would be yummy.  I could see adding lots of different vegetables -- corn, peas, green beans, cauliflower, broccoli... I am quite certain those would all work.The best part?  This is something my teen and tween boys could easily prepare without assistance.

column9: Okay, If You Like This Kind of Thing
column10: Okay, let's get one thing out of the way first. Velveeta is to American Cheese, what American Cheese is to Mild Cheddar. We're talking about a substitute for a substitute here.But if you're used to powdered cheese, this isn't too bad. It's not as good as a can of spray cheese, so we're certainly not talking gourmet here.Consider this meal to be a Hamburger Helper alternative. You don't need a bunch of stuff in your pantry. You don't need to think about gathering ingredients. You just need a pound (or so) of lean ground beef, and a skillet. The big advantage this has over Hamburger Helper is that the "cheese" (using the term loosely) is already a sauce. You don't need a quarter or half cup of milk, which is a big plus for someone like me who doesn't drink milk.Make sure you use very lean ground beef - 90/10 or leaner. Anything less lean, and between the oil in the "cheese", and what you aren't able to completely drain-off will make a mess of your meal. It won't look anything like the picture on the package if you do that!So if priced the same as Hamburger Helper, I'd pick this. But if I wasn't going to buy a Hamburger Helper-style meal to begin with, there's no reason to get this. It's just something to eat. It's not a culinary feast. (It's sure nothing you'd want to serve guests, unless you're trying to show how poor you are.)

This isn't marketed as a "health food", so I'm not going to consider nutrition, organic eating, and such issues.  Just taste . . . and I loved this stuff.I suppose this Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheeseburger Skillet begs comparison with Cheeseburger Hamburger Helper (which I really like) -- so compare I must.  This product derives the cheese aspect from Velveeta rather than the powdered form found in Hamburger Helper.  Although not Wisconsin cheddar, the Velveeta definitely brings more to the party than does the powdered counterpart from the HH box.I like a few shakes of hot sauce in my HH, but the Velveeta Skillet comes with additional seasoning which adds much flavor (I still like a little hot sauce, but less).Quick and easy, of course.Anyway, if you've got low rent tastes like me, and you've been a fan of Cheeseburger Hamburger Helper . . . try this one out.  Good chance that you'll love it.

The first thing I noticed about this Velveeta Cheesy Skillets Dinner Kit was that the box was heavy. That was surprising, because I'm used to the less-expensive just-add-ground-meat dinner mixes. But this was the cheese sauce pouch making it so heavy. And man, is that stuff good. I could've just eaten the cheese sauce -- forget the beef and everything else!The kit was very easy to make, following the steps that are typical of these kinds of dinner mixes. The main difference was the addition of that cheese pouch at the very end. There's a suggestion on the box to customize it with chopped tomatoes and shredded lettuce, and I imagine chopped onions and all kinds of other stuff would be good, but I just prepared this kit straight-up, since it was for a Vine review.The taste was great, the macaroni noodles were nice and plump as befitting a heartier mix, it was indeed ready in about 20 minutes, and it all worked fab as not only dinner but leftovers. I was surprised that a one-cup serving has 350 calories -- yowza. But overall, very good.

The new Cheesy Skillets dinner mix from Velveta is very easy to make and is good when you're pressed for time. The flavor I sampled was the Cheeseburger dinner which does indeed taste like a cheesburger. Prep. was very easy, just fry up some hamburg, add the mix and that's about it. If you're a family on the run or a single guy it's a great quick dinner.

column9: Tasted like Hamburger Helper to me...
column10: Meh, not impressed. I am a huge fan of Velveeta Shells and Cheese so I thought I would really enjoy this as well. However, it didn't taste any different than your basic Hamburger Helper to me. It took about the same amount of time and simply had a packet of noodles, packet of "seasoning" (which, unfortunately, mine got punctured so it was chunky, but it dissolved during simmering) and packet of Velveeta cheese sauce. I wasn't impressed at all. I'd probably purchase whichever was cheaper if I was choosing at the grocery store.

An alternative to hamburger helper, my family really enjoyed the cheeseburger skillet meal.  For me, easy clean up and low preparation time.  It was nice having a meal with velveeta versus the powdered cheese.  It was rich and creamy, and had a really good taste to it.  I would definitely buy this for my family.

I've eaten these boxed meals for years; in fact ever since I was a kid, and I must say this one is better than average.  It's easy to prepare and has a real home made taste unlike it's competitors.  If you're looking for something tasty to do with ground beef that's quick and easy you should give this a try.

I will admit that I was a bit skeptical that this product would be any good. People I know always made fun of Velveeta.Not only was the product great, but I think it is better than Hamburger Helper. It is probably the cheese that makes the difference too.The only thing that I found that could be better was the level of seasoning. That is, I would have rathered it be a little spicier. Of course, maybe I could have fixed that when cooking the meat. In any case, this product is way better in this regard than Hamburger Helper.Even if a bit more expensive than Hambuger Helper, I'd buy the Velveeta product.Give it a try.

Adults only. Do NOT try this on kids. PG13 (pretty gross for those under age 13) when using our "customized" skillet meal. We live by nutrition labels since my second heart attack. Packaged food kits, are customized to heart-healthy. In this case, it ended with a fantastic delightful dinner. Velveeta has always been known to be tops in taste, so the concern was calories, fat, sodium, and fiber.It took a bit more time-but it was worth it. We replaced ground beef with 5 cups of veggies (zucchini, onion, water chestnuts, mushrooms, & Broccoli; a cup of each). They were sautéed in place of the meat, then the Velveeta Cheesy Skillets Dinner Kit-Ultimate Cheeseburger Mac was completed as box directed. The 2 cups of water was actually the liquid drained off the water chestnuts and mushrooms, with a cup of canned tomatoes (Hunt's Diced Heart Healthy No Salt Added; Basil, Garlic & Oregano).The result was more than hoped for. A delicious cheesy veggie-mac meal, plenty of superb Velveeta cheese taste, crunch from the water chestnuts, and chew factor from the mushrooms. The only problem was stopping with one cup for a single serving meal, since our "customized" recipe actually ends up with 10, not 5 cups. Will power can't be boxed. That's still okay, because of the huge difference in nutrition numbers for this customized formula. We found nutrition info for the fresh veggies, and used can labels for the rest. It's not scientifically perfect, but close. We did the math.Nutrition facts first "as prepared on box with beef" and (customized facts), one cup serving comparisoncalories 350  (141);total fat 16g  (4.7 g);cholesterol 65mg  (7.5mg);sodium 900mg  (432mg);carbohydrate 27g  (19.5g);fiber 1g  (2.4g);Protein 24g  (5.7g).Per serving calories CUT 60%; fat CUT 70%; cholesterol CUT 88%; salt CUT 52%; & fiber increases 140%. That's a win/win/win/win/win and still comes with that voluptuous Velveeta taste.Just a customizing (as suggested on the back of the product box) for those concerned about their weight and health. Flavor and texture were not compromised. Next: Nacho Supreme with meat replacement. This is actually fun as well as delicious. Like doctoring a cake mix. There's a whole book on that. Bon appetit (enjoy YOUR meal)!.

I'm Mike and I really love hamburger helper.I have tried other "look alike" products, but few measured up to the original. But Kraft may have exceeded it with their Velveeta Ultimate skillets line.There are several things I like better with this product.One, it uses larger macaroni and they hold more cheese sauce on the inside.Two is the cheese sauce itself. Not a powdered mix, but a foil-packed Velveeta cheese that you add at the end of the preparation. This also means you don't have to worry about the cheese burning during cooking, which in turn means easier clean up.As to cons, could use more macaroni for my taste, but that is easily added in.Overall, an excellent product and I will definitely be trying some other flavors as well.

column9: Better than plain mac and cheese
column10: This product is a quick meal and is delicious. If you like mac and cheese then you will absolutely love the added Velveeta.  Add some 90% ground round that you have browned with some onions and you have one incredible meal!  I have some left over for this evening and I was thinking about adding some tomatoes.  Would very much like to purchase this product again.  Yum!

I'm generally not one to use this type of product, since I make most of our meals from scratch, using fresh ingredients. Still, this boxed dinner kit is a quick and easy way to get dinner on the table, for anyone who is pressed for time.Directions are simple: you brown 1 lb. of ground beef, add 2 cups water, the seasoning packet and pasta, cover, and cook for 11-13 minutes. Then you stir in the Velveeta cheese, and dinner's ready.I had a few problems with the meal.First problem, the recommended cooking time for the pasta, made for a too-soft consistency. Better to reduce your time by a few minutes, I think, for a more "al dente" consistency.Second problem, the saltiness!  Even with the addition of the very creamy Velveeta cheese, the flavor of salt was overwhelming. I don't know if I can recommend using less of the packet of "seasoning" since I don't know how that would affect consistency or flavor of the dish.Now, the box says this contains 850 mg of sodium. Yep, that's salty alright! In any case, for a quick, once in awhile dish, this might be okay, but not unless you enjoy really salty dishes.

column9: Generally OK for a box meal
column10: I didn't have high expectations for this, but it was decent for a box meal. The seasoning was good, albeit very much on the salty side. The cheese was plentiful and creamy. All in all, an OK one-skillet quick meal that takes about 20 minutes to prepare. Nowhere near as good as even the most basic scratch-made casserole, but decent if you set the benchmark as a mass-market box meal.The nutritional, caloric and fat components make this something you would not want to have as part of your regular diet. It's not horrible when it comes to nutrition, but there's not any bright spots either.The sodium content is very high -- you'll want to give this a pass if you are on a sodium restricted diet.I found that adding broccoli florets made the texture and flavor more interesting, and also cut down on how salty it was.

The new Velveeta Cheesy Skillets Ultimate Cheeseburger kit is a bit different from what I'm used to--no powder or any of that sorta annoying stuff--it comes with real burger. I tried it two nights ago and yes, it was good, but without the pain of having to boil powder.  Excellent!

The Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheeseburger Skillets Dinner is quite good. I actually like this better than Hamburger Helper. It's even easier to prepare in my opinion. It's rich, creamy and of course very cheesy. In other words, it's delicious. :)The only downside is I found it to be a bit salty. Maybe I'm hypersensitive because I don't normally eat foods that are high in sodium content. Everyone's palate is different and perhaps you may not find this to be the case at all. However, those who are  sensitive to the amount of sodium in their food, you might agree.Even so, I'd still recommend this product if you're looking for a quick, easy and tasty meal. The kids will probably like it. I know the adults I had taste test this thought it was good as well.

column9: Loved the rich creamy cheesy flavor
column10: My 13 year old daughter and I prepared this for dinner tonight and we loved it. It was super easy to prepare and she will be able to make it for future quick dinner nights and the whole family loved the Velveeta cheese flavor.I did add a bit of green onion to flavor my ground beef and pepper to add spice. I wish there was more pasta as the ground beef ratio was a bit overpowering but the flavor is something to be reckoned with and my family will be asking for more.I can't wait to try the broccoli cheese variety with chicken! Yum!

column9: I liked it, didn't love it....
column10: I am a big fan of easy to make skillet dinners like this one. Sometimes when you have to work, and are coming home late and don't have time to cook, you want something easy to prepare that you can serve with a side salad. The cheeseburger skilled fits the bill. It was easy to prepare, quick, and was in general a crowd pleaser. My father and mother both liked the taste very much. My sister said it was a bit salty... And I felt it tasted a bit pickly for my taste. I don't much care for pickles on burgers, and there is a sweet, salty pickle taste that really made it taste like cheeseburger, but I felt kind of ruined the flavor. I prefer my pickles not on my burgers.Still, this is bound to please those who like the taste of a McDonald's cheeseburger with all the toppings. That is exactly what it tastes like. I just can't rate it that high, because for me the taste was ok, but nothing I would find myself craving.

When I prepared this I was hoping for the anti-hamburger helper and unfortunately got more of the same.  The seasonings did nothing to make this stand out.  It was a nice box-meal but there was nothing distinct about it.  The amount of noodles provided were inadequate as well.  The ultimate cheeseburger mac tasted like every other cheesy-mac that I have tasted. The use of Velveeta cheese made the cheese taste smoother to the palate but other than that it is the same.  If you have a particular affinity for Velveeta cheese and like mac and hamburger then this would be the purchase for you.  The directions were easy to follow, the only ingredients you need to add are water and ground hamburger.  It is a simple easy meal to prepare.

column9: One of the best crackers ever
column10: We had a sample of these crackers in a store and loved them.  They're tasty, crunchy, filled with various seeds, and incredibly high in fiber while low in calories.  They're also gluten-free.  We love them with cheese or by themselves as a healthy snack.  We're so glad we found these on amazon.com so we can have them any time!

I have only found a few gluten free crackers I like, this IS NOT one of them. I purchased these at Sam's Club, much cheaper. These crackers were hard, not crunchy, almost seemed stale. The first bite didn't taste too bad but they left an awful, odd after-taste, similar to burned grain. The texture wasn't too bad, not the usual prepackaged gluten-free grainy texture. My husband went Gluten-Free when I had to, he almost almost anything and he doesn't like them either. We tried them plain, with cream cheese, with cream cheese/olives, in salad, with cheddar cheese, nacho cheese but nothing would conceal the after-taste, in my opinion they were Horrible! I would say it is just my taste buds but...I not 1 of my 5 kids, 4 of which will eat pretty much anything, liked these. We offered them to friends, family, and neighbors but after trying them no one would take them. It could be possible that we purchased a bad batch, there were 2 packages in the box, but I don't think we want to chance buying and wasting another box. After reading some of the other reviews it appears many people love them, I guess you never know unless you try them. We hated to toss them in the trash so we occasionally used them as dog treats, the dogs did like them.

With Tahitian vanilla and a great name (Beanilla), I had high expectations for this product. Alas, it doesn't taste like vanilla and barely even smells like vanilla.  It smells like cheap candy:  a sickening starchy sweetness, almost like Play-Doh mixed with confectioner's sugar, with a hint of McDonald's vanilla shake.  The product melts in your mouth (good), but tastes like sweet powdered clay.I keep the Beanilla in my cupboard and retry it periodically, hoping that my taste buds were off in the past.  But, whether sprinkled on coffee (the main reason I purchased the product) or mixed into icecream, the product is gross.Perhaps I'm not using it as intended or am not thinking of it the correct way.  If you think of it as a powdered creamer like Coffee-Mate (and you like Coffee-Mate), you might like it in coffee.  It might also be better in baked goods (on the label it recommends using the product for "frosting, sauces, puddings, and other recipes as a substitute for vanilla extract").  Liquid vanilla extract contains alcohol and slightly thins what you're making -- I see an advantage in using a powdered vanilla if you want to avoid these characteristics.I'm giving the product a chance and want to like it, but it's the most artificial tasting real vanilla I've had.  I purchased the 12oz. version.  If you think you'd like to try it, I'd advise trying the 4 oz version first.Ingredients on the Label:  "Dextrose, Silicon Dioxide, Vanilla Bean Extractives"I recommended "Authentic Foods Vanilla Powder," also sold here on Amazon for a more genuine vanilla taste.  It's made with:  "Natural Vanilla Bean Extractives, Evaporated Cane Juice, Silica, Cellulose."  I like this for icecream and for coffee drinks.You might also use Raw Vanilla Bean Powder, which is expensive at triple to quadruple the price, but it contains only vanilla.

I don't know why Vanilla powder is so hard to find, except at Starbucks.  I wanted it for my coffee.  This product had very little taste.  I don't know how they managed that.  There has to be a better one around.
After looking everywhere local, at last I found vanilla powder.  It's wonderful in cookies and breads.  A little expensive but well worth it.

I bought this based on some of the reviews at Amazon indicating this product was more organic/authentic and the other products were not "true" vanilla as they weren't "brown" in color and were dextrose based. My idea was to replicate the vanilla used at Starbucks, however I couldn't find this brand (now I know that it is made by cooks). I use this powder in coffee, however because the method of manufacturer is by spraying liquid vanilla on silica oxide (basically inert sand) then ground up and sold as a powder you never really get the sand out of the food. In my coffee, the last couple of inches of liquid in my cup are usually a gritty taste (basically sand) so I never get to fully drink all my coffee. For that reason I am giving it a low rating. I would suggest getting of the other brands which maybe are less organic but will taste just the same and won't have this gritty feeling.

The vanilla powder didn't do what I wanted (was hoping to use it to enhance the vanilla taste in my coffee) but that's hardly the fault of the manufacturer.  It  has a pleasant odor and now plan to use it in cakes and other recipes that call for vanilla extract.  Can't say that I would (personally) recommend it but that's only because it didn't work for my intended purpose.
The vanilla powder is great in our coffee. It really adds great flavor. Thanks for a great product.

I love teas with mint, so I decided to give this one a try. Its really good and refreshing but the mint flavor isn't as strong as I would like to be. Not saying that it should be overbearing, but I had to question whether or not mint was even in the tea. All in all, its a good tea.

I love this tea. It has a wonderful mint flavor that is in perfect balance with the green tea.  I drink this daily and could not do without it. I feel better as opposed to when I used to drink coffee.

column9: tastes pretty good for a cheap tea
column10: This is not the world's best tea.  The taste is much different from the green tea served in Japanese restaurants and tea houses.  But for only 10 cents/bag, the taste is decent and it is not really weak like some other cheap teas.

This tea is awesome! I even got my "macho" husband to drink it every night before bed! Unfortunately, our local grocery stores aren't carrying the mint flavor anymore, so going to order it here - well worth the price! Thanks amazon!
GOOD FLAVOR ... GOOD PRICE ... JUST WISH IT WAS OFFERED IN DECAF!

I wasn't a tea drinker until I developed ulcers and wasn't able to drink coffee for a few months. I bought this tea on Amazon and am so happy that I did. This is my favorite tea in my cupboard (and I have tons since I wanted to learn really quick what I liked). The mint flavor is mild and doesn't hide the flavor of the green tea.
