In my opinion, if you're going to have a convenience food, it ought to be all-inclusive.  I actually used some Costco canned chicken in mine and it was by far the best tasting thing on the plate.  Also the nutrition information is based on there being 5 servings per box.  Perhaps if you are a bird!  I'd say 2-3 is closer to the truth if this is being served as your entree.  So in reality, your portion might be as much as 975 calories with 250 of those being fat.  If you're going to eat something that unhealthy it ought to taste a lot better than this stuff.  I won't be buying it again.

column9: Good for Vitamin C(heese) but lacking in Vitamin B(roccoli)
column10: Since I have been known to burn water, my spouse took the reigns on preparing this dinner for our family. She advised me this was very to make...It only took her 3 minutes to do the food preparation and 15 minutes for the actual cooking/seasoning/serving.I'm the family taster, so I got first dip - and this tasted very cheesy, very creamy...that was because of the Velveeta cheese packet and not the powdered stuff. I did enjoy the additional seasonings, and I was prepared for a hearty meal. However, once the dehydrated broccoli package was added to the mix, I could barely see any of the broccoli in the completed meal. I've uploaded a picture in "Customer Images" to illustrate this.The preparation was quick, it was delicious, and it was a very quick 1-skillet cleanup. Each family member enjoyed this meal (since we're partial to cheese), but I was expecting to see and taste a bit more broccoli.This piqued our interest and we will probably look for other flavors/variations of the Cheesy Skillet meals, but I'd suggest adding your own broccoli if that's what you crave.

For me , broccoli sitting by itself on a plate could not possibly be more unappealing. Put it in soup with cheddar , or mix it in Kraft Velveeta skillets , and I'm all in.So easy to prepare , and so delicious. The dinner for the wife and I was ready in a couple of minutes , and satisfying. The box provided enough for two , and enough palette satisfaction that I can see this fast becoming a dinner fave

As a quick, convenient dinner, this can't be beat.  I had the box in my pantry and one night, after running kids from place to place and walking in when everyone was hungry and I had no plans for dinner, it was nice to be able to grab the box and serve a meal within 20 minutes.  So I have to give it a high rating for that.Taste: it was okay.  I really wouldn't say it was great.  I prefer whole grain fresh pasta to dried white pasta, real cheese to Velveeta, fresh broccoli to dried and rehydrated green stuff.  This is NOT gourmet food, folks.  But for what it is - a meal you can put on the table 20 minutes after walking in the door - it is edible.

column9: The boxed dinner that is quick, easy, yummy & cheesy
column10: I have had a special place in my heart for these "meals in a box" or dinner kits.  Mainly because I can recall as a child my mother being able to really doctor these box dinners.  She would add cheese, veggies and various spices making it so much more that a "pre-packaged meal".  I have adopted many of her techniques in my cooking today.As for these dinner kits by Velveeta, it seems that the Cheese Masters are a little late to the party since Hamburger Helper and even Rice/Pasta Roni have had a corner on this market for years.  Nevertheless, this "dinner in a box" calls for chicken rather than beef. The promoted flavor is broccoli and cheese.Inside the box there is a bag of orzo (rice shaped pasta), a seasoning packet, and a packet of dried broccoli florets and a standard foil package of Velveeta.  The only thing missing is a pound of chicken.  The preparation is about 15 to 20 minutes and the result is pretty good.  I did however make two minor adjustments in my preparation of this meal. I lightly dusted my chicken with low sodium seasoning as I cooked it and added fresh broccoli to the completed dish.  I feel these additions really made the flavor pop (I am sure onions and peppers would be good too).Overall this is a pretty good meal and easy to make.  I was somewhat turned off by a boxed meal "starring" Velveeta. I like Velveeta but it is a very processed food and I find a little of it goes a long way.  In other words has a very strong flavor and I try to avoid too much sodium.  However this meal doesn't taste too salty and isn't too cheesy. I am eager to try one of the other box meals Velveeta has.  For the novice cook this is a good meal for the "seasoned chef" this could be a nice foundation for a more epic dining experience.

Velveeta Cheesy Skillets was pretty okay. It wasn't really that cheesy actually, but it decent enough. The other thing was that it took way longer than the 20 minute time it claimed. I'm sure it was supposed to be around 20 minute cook time, it took a while.I might buy this on sale, and use it when I'm in the mood, it's still 'dinner in a box' per se, but it's not wonderful and simple.

column9: Dinner Kit Plus Chicken Chunks Makes Tasty Family Casserole
column10: When combined with cooked chicken chunks, this Kraft Cheesy Skillets Dinner Kit makes a great-tasting one-dish family dinner.  The box instructions call for one-inch pieces of boneless, skinless white meat chicken that you cook quickly in a large skillet on your stovetop.  However, because I've never quite mastered the art of cooking chicken in a skillet, I poached my chicken instead, using an Oster Electronic Food Steamer.  This added about 20 minutes to my total preparation time.After the chicken was cooked, the rest of the preparation only took about 15 minutes!  First, you add 2.5 cups water, a seasonings packet, and a pasta packet to the skillet.  The pasta in this kit is orzo (pasta shaped like grains of rice).  After bringing the mixture to a boil, you reduce the heat, cover the pan, and simmer (stirring often) for about 7 minutes.  Then you add a packet of dehydrated broccoli flakes, and cook another 3-4 minutes until the water is mostly absorbed.  Finally, you take the skillet off the stove, and stir in the package of soft Velveeta cheese.My family liked this casserole, with its smooth cheese sauce, quite well.  Because it uses broccoli flakes, it doesn't taste strongly of broccoli, and broccoli-haters probably won't know that the broccoli is even there.  The flakes do produce very tiny, but visible, broccoli florets.  I supplemented the finished casserole with a side dish of another vegetable, because my household likes vegetables and eats a lot of them.  The casserole was filling, but I think that four servings, rather than five (as indicated on the package), is what you should expect from the kit, at least if you are serving hungry people.  This product gets good marks for not being overly salty.  Although there is 620mg of sodium in a single serving, it doesn't taste salty, and a person on a low-salt diet can have it from time to time.I rate this product at 4 stars ("I like it").  Although the key ingredient (boneless, skinless chicken) has to be purchased separately, the kit produces a tasty, interesting chicken casserole that is very fast and easy to prepare.

This was a nice treat!  The box contains pasta in the shape of rice granules, similar to couscous.  It also has dried broccoli and a packet of Velveeta.  As you would expect from a boxed meal kit, the preparation is very simple and fast.  If you are concerned about messing it up, don't be.  The flavor is yummy and cheesy, but of course has that artificial twang.  If that doesn't bother you, I recommend it.  It's the best food of this type that I've had in a while.

column9: EXACTLY what you think it will be
column10: Whatever your reaction to the phrase Velveeta Cheesy Skillets dinner might be, you are right. For those who have visions of faux-cheesy guilty pleasure indulgence - you are right. For those who have visions of a queasy stomach and otherworldly aftertaste - you are right. For those who imagine weird little packets of freeze-dried green somethings passed off as "broccoli" - you are right. For those who imagine smooth, pliable bright yellow "cheese-food" sauce - you are right. For those who think this sort of thing is a once-in-a-blue-moon treat - you are right. I cannot imagine ever going to the store looking for this. I can imagine picking it up on a big sale, with a coupon, and thinking what the hell and putting in my cart. Maybe once-in-a-blue-moon...

In the time it took to make this product, I could have made a much healthier and better tasting dinner from scratch. I was never a big fan of Velveeta cheese, but decided to give this a try. I had to laugh when I read from another reviewer that this product contained broccoli dust, because that is honestly the best description I would be able to think of. The instructions are pretty lame, because it says to brown the chicken, but it doesn't say to add any fat so the chicken doesn't stick to the pan. I added a tiny bit of oil, so it wouldn't stick. The taste was nothing in comparison to a homemade meal. I think it had a kind of chemical taste to it, with a gross after taste. My 18 yr. old son wouldn't finish what I put on his plate, and that surprised me, because he eats just about anything, but he is also used to homemade food, and didn't expect to get served this kind of meal. Even if I browned some cut up chicken, and then added some water, real cheddar cheese, heavy cream, pasta and some frozen broccoli and let it cook for the same amount of time that this product calls for, it would have been better tasting and a lot healthier, so I would pass on this one... for sure.

This is the kind of food a person puts in their pantry and uses when they can't think of anything else, are out of everything else, and don't have time to fix a decent meal. It will do in a pinch, but don't expect it to supply you with a vegetable. I could almost count the broccoli flakes in the tiny package included inside. With all that being said, Cheesy Skillets is relatively easy to cook, alleviates the need to think of something to fix when you're in a hurry and don't know what to cook, and, with the right seasonings, tastes fine.I cooked mine according to the package directions, crumbled crackers over it and popped it in the oven until all the moisture was absorbed. This also allowed the flavors to coalesce.If I use this product again, I'll add some steamed broccoli just before I pop it in the oven to alleviate the guilt of not having a balanced meal.Finally, this product is high in sodium. By the time my appetite was satisfied, I had  consumed twice the daily requirement of salt. Actually, since I have high blood pressure, three times, but who's counting?

First of all, to call this a "Chicken and Broccoli Skillet" is two-thirds wrong.  There is no chicken - you have to add it - and the broccoli is akin to fine print in a cell phone contract.  Maybe it should have been called "Chicken Tasting Skillet with Broccoli Coloring."Packaging, preparation, and cooking are all simple enough to satisfy the lazy parent, the overzealous latch-key kid, and the agoraphobic nerd on a 72-hour World of Warcraft bender.  Those interested in nutrition, the love of cooking, or anything with a semblance of non-processed would be best to steer clear.  Lucky for me I steamed some broccoli and sautéed some chicken to "complete" the meal.What the Velveeta skillet does have going for it is Velveeta and portion size.  There is no mistaking the quintessential Velveeta texture that could make billy-goat puke tolerable.  The supplementary benefit of this particular blend is that it can be used to spackle walls and caulk bathrooms...if you're into that neon-orange, Tennessee Volunteers, garbage-man convention sort of color scheme.  Regarding portion size, I ate for three consecutive days, and was "blocked" for the day following.Overall, this is probably not a product I'd buy.  The taste wasn't appealing enough to overcome the shortfalls.  Big fans of Velveeta will probably love it, but I'd rather have Hamburger Helper mixed with Mac'n Cheese.

column9: Quick & easy meal that hides the broccoli!
column10: You have to add your own chicken to this meal which is much like mac & cheese, although the macaroni is more like a large rice than macaroni. Good to keep around for a quick, easy meal (you can leave out the chicken out, or use canned or pouch chicken.)Something to keep in mind for those emergency kits & tastes FAR better than those emergency meals/rations!If you are expecting broccoli flowerettes, they aren't there, yet a great way to hide veggies from kids that don't want to eat them! That way they can eat their veggies without realizing it!The box says portions are 3 oz! Sodium level is high (650mg per very small serving!) If using as a main course, I'd say realistically there are about 2 servings per box, so if sodium sensitive, you may want to avoid.Taste pretty darn good for something that comes from a box!I'd LOVE to see a similar meal made from wild rice that is wheat/gluten-free!Nutritional info is as follows..Calories 270Calories from Fat 72% Daily Value*Total Fat 8.0g12%Saturated Fat 2.5g12%Trans Fat 0.0gCholesterol 15mg5%Sodium 620mg26%Total Carbohydrates 39.0g13%Dietary Fiber 2.0g8%Sugars 5.0gProtein 10.0gVitamin A 2% * Vitamin C 40%Calcium 15% * Iron 10%*NOTE: I wish food & supplement companies would post their nutritional info on Amazon.com (w/ a note that it is subject to change IF it is! Also, they CAN change it if it does change!)All-in-all a good-tasting meal & nutritionally not too bad for something out of a box!

When I looked at the box that's on Amazon I originally thought that it was pasta, to be honest I didn't bother reading the description. Upon receiving and actually opening the box we found out that it was actually a rice dinner with little pieces of broccoli that can barely been seen. After making our boneless chicken breast and putting everything together I must say that it did turn out pretty well and actually does taste good. I personally wouldn't spend the money getting this box since I'm quite capable of making my own rice and broccoli dinner from scratch but if you want something quick to do when you're running short on time then this would be a good way to prepare something simple for dinner.

column9: Okay, but a little more work than I like
column10: I consider this in the category of what should be quick, easy, edible food. However, the instructions are a bit more complicated than I like for food in this category. If I open this box, it is because I am short on time and need something quick and easy. However, here are the instructions:1. Brown 1 pound of chicken (cut into 1 inch pieces) in a large skillet2. Add 2 1/2 cps of water, seasoning and pasta. Bring to a boil3. Cover and stir often for 7 minutes. Add broccoli; cover and cook until most of the water is gone, about 2 - 4 minutes. Remove from heat.4. Add cheese with Velveeta cheese sauce pouch. Stir in cheese sauceSince some of those steps actually have multiple steps embedded inside them, this goes from and easy dump and heat meal to a more complicated recipe. For the same amount of work I can this same meal - just with fresh broccoli and ingredients I can actually pronounce.Now, I am no food snob - I actually enjoy the microwave version of the Velveeta broccoli and cheese pasta. Its just that the instructions for that meal is simply open the cup, dump in the broccoli dust, fill to line with water, microwave and stir in cheese sauce. For this amount of effort, the pretty much a similar product - I will pass in the future.Now, if you just really like the taste of Velveeta over other brands of "cheese sauce" and want a meal where all you have to do is add chicken - this is for you. However, this doesn't fit the bill for "quick and easy" and the flavor doesn't compare to fixing the same meal, in the same amount of time - with fresh or frozen broccoli and your own spices. Don't get me wrong, it isn't terrible; just not the ease I would be looking for in a box.

How much you like this product is going to depend on how much you like Velveeta. Despite the fact that there are a variety of elements in the finished dish (chicken, broccoli, pasta), pretty much all you can taste is the Velveeta. Half of my family loved it and the other half (myself included) thought it was a just-okay bit of comfort food. For a skillet meal it was a bit more involved and time consuming to prepare than one of those frozen skillet meals. Personally I'd rate this three stars, but since my family was equally split I'll average it out to four stars.

column9: Decent enough spin on a mac n' cheese dish
column10: "Kraft Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets Dinner Kit, 14.64-Ounce (Pack of 6)" is decent for what it is, and I did like it a bit more than the other Kraft Velveeta cheese dinner kit that I tried (i.e. Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheeseburger). The dish is easy enough to prepare. The taste is less salty than the usual processed dinner kits that I've tried, and the orzo which is used in place of macaroni works well with the cheese and chicken combo. However, the dehydrated broccoli crumbs that comes with the package is rather sad, adding no texture and only a slight, vague flavor to the dish.In all, this dinner kit is just ok. In spite of the fact that I'm actually a big mac 'n cheese fan, I've tried enough Velveeta dinner kits to realize that they just aren't my cup of tea. However, for those in the market, I will give this a slight recommendation.

column9: Flavor, ease of preparation just okay
column10: Usually, I find these boxed dinners a fair trade-off considering the time they save; however, this one doesn't save that much time over preparing a similar dish from scratch.  The cook needs to cut up the chicken and saute it until done, then add the orzo, "broccoli" (more on this later), and water, simmer until the orzo is cooked, and then finish with cheese.  The slight time savings comes mostly from not having to clean and cut up broccoli, but you might want to think twice about whether that 5 minutes or so is worth it.The chicken is, of course, whatever quality you choose to buy.  The orzo is typical plain white orzo, which was a nice change from the rice most of these products use (wouldn't it be nice if one of them would include a whole-grain option sometime, though?) The cheese, as you might suspect from the name, is Velveeta.  All fine, if you like them.The broccoli, though, is pretty odd.  It's minced (I use that term generously -- the pieces are really tiny) and apparently freeze-dried.  In the prepared dish, it looks more like a bit of parsley was added for color.  Surprisingly, it does add some broccoli flavor.The flavor, overall, wasn't bad, but this is the first one of these kinds of meals I've had that truly made me think the effort to make it from scratch would be very similar to the effort to make it from the box, and scratch would have been significantly better.Nutrition-wise, it's about average for this type of meal: 5 servings, 390 calories per serving, 8 grams of fat, 620 mg of sodium, 39 grams of carbs with 2 grams of fiber, and 10 grams of protein.

column9: Very good, but make sure you follow the directions
column10: Like the other Velveeta dinner kits, this one requires only the box and a pound of meat (in this case, chicken) to make an affordable and delicious meal.Do not make the mistake my girlfriend did the first time we made this. If you have to grease your skillet, use a Pam spray or something similar. Using oil really will mess you up later on, as it doesn't boil off, and ends up messing up the texture to the point where it's almost a mush. Follow the directions, and you are good to go.

This product sounds so good, but I was very disappointed in the finished product.  It definitely has a fake cheese taste that I cannot stand.  The tiny little packet of dehydrated broccoli is a joke, even after it is cooked it looks more like seasoning than a vegetable. This dish would be so easy to make from scratch with frozen chicken, instant rice, frozen or fresh broccoli and the cheeses of your choice, I can't imagine why anyone would buy this.

column4: Lettetia "As Long As I Am Able To Read, I Sha...
column10: Kraft Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillet Dinner Kit is a tasty item to add to your dinner menu.  It is fast and easy to make, smooth and creamy and has a fresh, homemade flavor.  I am certain your family will love it.

column9: Very nice but the broccoli is hard to see
column10: I made mine with 2 packages of Perdue Roasted Turkey and it taste great.  The sauce is rich which makes this quite filling.  The broccoli florets are nearly invisible, too bad as I like broccoli.  Otherwise very enjoyable and recommended.

column9: Easy and tasty but not much broccoli
column10: Very easy to make and the creamy Velveeta cheese tastes great. The only problem is the lack of broccoli; I didn't expect big florets or anything but there was hardly any broccoli at all. I ended up cooking some frozen broccoli I had and mixing it in the mix; very tasty.

Kraft Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillet Dinner Kit is delicious! My family was very happy with this meal. You can't go wrong with chicken and cheese for kids, and as a mom, I was happy with the broccoli! It tasted like a homemade casserole that my mom used to make, just don't tell her that! This was a wonderful weekday dinner when paired with a nice salad and fresh bread. I will definitely be trying the other varieties.

I was actually skeptical of this product because I am not a fan of Velveeta mac and cheese, but this was pretty tasty.  The broccoli is on the pitiful side, though.  As my husband put it, it is the equivalent of broccoli "dust" in the mix, but the taste of broccoli is still there.  I liked the consistency of the pasta, it was more akin to pilaf/rice than regular pasta, a nice change of pace.  I would definitely buy this again, my 10 year old loved it, too.

We frequently purchase Velveeta Shells and Cheese which our family loves a lot. We had the opportunity to try Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets and we were happy with the experience. The item was very easy to prepare with clear directions. We used browned white meat chicken but you could prepare this without the chicken as a simple side dish. There is not much else to add about this solid product.

...but overall, not a bad Chicken Helper knock-off. The cheese is very creamy and blends well, and the broccoli taste is a nice contrast, but so far, none of these Velveeta meals can hold a candle to Hamburger and Chicken Helper. Good enough that I'd buy it again, but nothing to rave over.

For those times when you're short of time and the family is hungry, this Cheesy Skillet is just the ticket. All you need is a pound of chicken breast and this dinner kit to make a satisfying meal in about 20 minutes. We've got a hungry teenager in our house, so I used two pounds of chicken breast and it worked fine. Many times these dinners in a box don't have a lot of flavor, but this one is an exception. The flavor was very good.A great dinner in a box to keep on hand!

My wife and I were pleased and I might add surprised at just how good it was. We're not fans of boxed dinners so it was a nice surprise.We did not use quite a full pound of chicken and found that to be plenty. The Velveeta taste was not overwhelming but the broccoli, chicken and cheese flavors blended well.Sorry to say we didn't have Ritz crackers for the topping but think that would have been a nice addition and a bit of crunchiness.

The new Kraft Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets Dinner Kit is DELICIOUS! A one skillet meal that uses creamy Velveeta instead of powdered "cheese flavoring"? I found this to be far superior to the Hamburger Helper flavor. It is rich and yummy and it makes a great, quick meal with a side salad.

I found this particular Velveeta Cheesy Skillets to be ok - neither great or horrible, just ok.  By the time the pasta (it is pasta, even though it looks like rice) is fully cooked it becomes a little bit mushy.  And I didn't care for the seasoning packet they include with this - it's not extremely strong, I just didn't care for the taste.  If I were to ever make it again I would omit the seasoning, or use very little of it.  The 'broccoli' they include in the kit is a joke, it's like a tiny packet of dried herbs, you can hardly tell it's there and it doesn't contribute to the meal at all.  If you really want to improve the quality of the meal cook some fresh broccoli and stir it in just before you serve it.It was very easy to make, and it was nice to be able to cook it all in one pan, but aside from that this wasn't something I'd want to cook again when I have other choices.

We ate this for dinner tonight and it was delicious. On an evening when I was running (quite) behind schedule, this took me about 30 minutes from start to finish to make, and that included defrosting the chicken which I had forgotten to do earlier. I was a little worried that the velveeta sauce would be overpowering as I'm not usually a fan of too much cheese, but it was the perfect creamy texture. My only complaint, if it is one, is that the dehydrated broccoli is less than appetizing as it comes out of the box, and I truly think there could be more in the meal to give it a little added veggie punch ... or I'll try and remember to add my own next time. Overall, though, the flavoring was good and it rated thumbs up from my husband, myself, and our 4 and 5 year old daughters.

column9: Amazingly Good Dinner from a Box
column10: What a pleasant surprise Kraft Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets Dinner Kit provided! I was a little leery, having tried a number of boxed dinner kits that were bland and disappointing. I wondered if I should spice it up a little, but decided against it because I wanted to review the product without tinkering.Kraft supplies everything but the chicken, and there is a spice packet, but I still wasn't convinced this was going to be much more than mac & cheese with a few pieces of broccoli and chicken. WRONG!On a night when dinner was left to the last minute, I prepared the Chicken & Broccoli skillet and served it with fresh picked tomatoes and basil. Not expecting much, we were amazed how good it was, certainly as good (if not better) than a meal from a family restaurant. It is superior to the frozen skillet and microwave steamer dinners we've tried (and we've tried a wide variety). As for spicing it up--that's totally unnecessary. We both thought the meal was delicious. In fact, we couldn't wait to have the leftovers (which were still good).

As promised, this pasta was very easy and fast to make.  The whole meal can be made in one pan, which is also a plus.  This pasta is reasonably tasty.  I wasn't expecting gourmet from this, but it was fast and filling- good for a busy night.  The pasta is orzo-like, and the cheese sauce is the sort of fake stuff one expects from velveeta.  My main complaint was that there's hardly any broccoli in the broccoli pouch.  There's a few freeze-dried sprigs, and that's pretty much it.  If I buy this again I will definitely cook some fresh broccoli and add it to the pasta.

column9: Not bad for a one pan meal in a box.
column10: For a meal in a box this one wasn't too bad. The only part that I wasn't very crazy about was the pasta. It was kinda hard to keep from thinking that it looked like a pan full of maggots in a cheese sauce. I didn't particularly like the flavor or the gooey texture of the pasta and what's with the dried Broccoli? There wasn't enough of it to even taste it and what came with this looked like it had been ground up into a powder and had some dried sticks in it that looked like dark green tooth picks that had been chewed on. Using the real cheese in the foil pouch instead of that powdered gunk they usually use in the box meals was the best part. Even though I probably won't be trying this one again I will be trying the other ones with the real cheese in it. And for me that's saying a lot since I haven't bought any of the box meals like HB Helper, Chicken Helper, Tuna Helper and other similar stuff in a very long time because of that awful powdered cheese stuff they use in them.

I enjoyed this product.  I mean, what's not to love - velveeta mac & cheese, broccoli and chicken???  It was easy to prepare, very filling - great comfort food.  I served this as a side dish with chicken salad sandwiches and all my guests truly enjoyed it.  I gave it 4 stars because as a meal, I think it would be too much, but as a side dish, it was terrific.

I assumed this would be very similar to Chicken Helper, which I enjoy, but the Chicken Helper definitely tastes like processed food.  The Velveeta Cheesy Skillets tastes like I made it from scratch, and I will definitely buy this again.  I was so impressed by this flavor that I am excited to try the other varieties of Velveeta Cheesy Skillets.

I was reluctant to try the Velveeta skillets dinner kit because I cannot stand hamburger helper and this product reminded me of it. However I was really surprised by how much I liked it. This box meal is just bursting with flavor unlike other box meals. You can really taste all the ingredients of the cheese, broccoli, and chicken. The Velveeta brand box meals are the best that I have tried thus far. They are really simple to make and make a good size dinner portion. For the price you cannot go wrong with Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets Dinner Kit. These are a hit with the family as well. So what are you waiting for? Go out and buy one today and you will not be disappointed.

column9: Family gave it a thumbs up...
column10: During the summer we do a lot of outdoor activities so this leaves little time for kitchen prep.  I cut chicken into chunks the night before we went to the zoo and upon returning home just threw them into the pan along with the included ingredients. My family felt that I had whipped up a tasty dish.  I gave it four stars keeping in mind what type of box dinner I had selected.  Yes, there are more healthy options for dinner out there but in this category Kraft has created one of the better chicken dinner kits.  I would also recommend throwing a box of frozen broccoli florets into your cart as the included broccoli is really just a tease.  This kit will feed your family with little prep so keeping a box on hand is not a bad idea for those extra busy days.

column9: Tasty - I'd keep this in the cupboard to have on hand
column10: This Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli is one of those dinner kits that I like to have on hand "just in case". It's easy to make - the directions were clear and easy to understand and yes, it does only take 20 minutes. I love cheesy food (the more cheese the better) and found it to be very tasty. As others have mentioned, the broccoli included here is a joke - it looks pretty unappetizing when you open the packet and by the time you serve the dish, the broccoli looks like dark green dust in the meal. Adding your own broccoli florets would make this dish a real chicken "and broccoli" dish.The serving size is 3 ounces (approximately 1 cup) and there are approximately 5 servings in a box. I found that that was a fair approximation (unlike the serving sizes for some products which aren't even close to reality).Here is the nutritional Information - as prepared (percentages based on a 2000 calorie diet):Calories: 390Calories from Fat: 100Total Fat: 8g 17% (Saturated Fat: 2.5g 15%; Trans Fat: 0)Cholesterol: 15mg 25%Sodium 620mg 28%Total Carbohydrates 39g 13% (Dietary Fiber 2g 8%; Sugars 5g)Protein 10gVitamin A: 2%Vitamin C: 20%Calcium: 15%Iron: 15%There is a note (in very small print) which says that 1 cup prepared as directed with boneless, skinless chicken breast contains 11g total fat (3g saturated fat, 0g trans fat), 75g cholesterol, 670 mg sodium, 39g total carbohydrate (2g fiber, 5g sugars), 33g protein.If you like cheesy food (and aren't watching your sodium too closely), I think you'll like this meal.

column9: I did like it..but a couple of problems.
column10: This box dinner was very easy to make and had a very good flavor. I had some leftover chicken which made it much easier and faster to prepare. The only problem I had with it was the broccoli. Tiny little pieces which I probably would not use the next time. I will use fresh or frozen broccoli.The cheese sauce was very good, but I am glad I didn't put all of it in the dish. I really liked the orzo pasta. It was very different than any of the other Kraft Velveeta products I have tried. I wish it didn't have so much sodium in it.I felt it deserved a 4 score because of the above problems. Will try some of the other Skillet Dinner Kits though.

Excuse the title quote from the SciFi series LEXX, but I thought it appropriate.  This stuff was very good, someone who helped sample it made a key statement, that the broccoli actually tasted fresh.  I guess in the little sealed packet it hydrates better than the completely dried out mix they have in some other packaged dinners.  I do recommend something for novice cooks that worked well here. Despite all the flavors here, the chicken should be the star of this dish.  I learned something many years ago in Vancouver about how chicken should be prepared, and it's true.  Now you can't do this too far in advance, but as your searing the chicken you should season it too, and make a nice brown grill when completed.  The seasoning is seared in, along with the moisture and the flavor.In Vancouver there was a restaurant, part of a chain also in the US called the Bombay Bicycle Club.  They actually had one in my home town of Fort Wayne many years before, but then I didn't even know it was a restaurant.  I found out this chicken secret eating at the one in Vancouver.  I ordered a salad topped with grilled chicken breast, and when I tasted it I was just blown away.  I'd had these type of salads many times elsewhere, and mostly the chicken was just another run of the mill taste in the salad.  I asked the chef what the secret was, and to my surprise he told me.  People don't season the chicken right before the sear, and once seared it has a difficult time accepting any flavor.  Now I've made Tarragon chicken before, and I know that picks up the flavor of the spice, but not before baking for a few hours.To make a long story short, I seared it just like that, blended the cheese, broccoli, pasta with the chicken, and cooked as ordered.  It was great.  A good meal with nice a flavor contrast, and the chicken stayed the star of the dish.  I'll have to see what they charge for these retail, but if reasonable, I can see myself getting some more real soon.

I make a chicken/broccoli casserole on a regular basis, but it is a time-consuming recipe when you are trying to get dinner in a hurry after work. So I was looking forward to trying this one. It was very easy to make, one dish, simple instructions for even a beginner cook, and looked really appetizing. But the big test was my family. They immediately asked what I had done differently to my casserole. I said, "Just try it and see if you like it." They did, and they DID! My husband loves chicken anyway, and the cheese sauce in this was very creamy. But that's what you'd expect from Velvetta and they didn't disappoint. I'll still make my original from time to time, but in a time-pinch for dinner on the table (which is most nights) I will definitely make this one again, and look forward to trying the other varieties.

column9: too rich and a heavy processed taste
column10: Generally, I like having a box dinner around for times when I don't want to cook much or run out of other foods.  And we have a homemade chicken broccoli and rice casserole we really like, so I thought we'd like this.  For the first few bites we did, but quickly the cheesy taste became extremely rich and unappetizing.The box contains an orzo pasta, a packet of dried seasonings, a packet of dried broccoli, and a large foil packet of Velveeta cheese. To make this, you brown up some chicken breast that has been cut into bite size pieces, then add the orzo and spices and water.  After it simmers a while, add the broccoli and simmer more, then add the cheese sauce.  It's pretty simple, much like any other box dinner on the market.The orzo pasta was very good, I liked it a lot.  The seasonings seemed kind of bland but were adequate.  The broccoli is nonexistent, really.  It's just about 2 tablespoons of dried flakes that don't rehydrate much when cooking.  You can see little tiny green dots throughout the finished dish, but there is no broccoli flavor to speak of.  Frankly, I thought there was too much cheese sauce as well.  About an ounce less of sauce would have been perfect.  It coated everything well and looked good, but the cheese sauce was the main culprit in making the entire dish overly rich in both taste and texture.  We paired this with fresh raw veggies for something to cut the cheesiness and it still was too much.I think this particular skillet would have been better without chicken in it, instead as a side dish with some chicken made separately.  If Velveeta made a boxed side dish that was just orzo, seasoning, and cheese in appropriate proportions, I would definitely buy it.

This is typical of the other Kraft Skillet dinners. My wife and I happen to enjoy them. You could do worse. You provide the chicken and it is easy and quick to make. We will be buying some for quick lunch or dinners

column9: Everyone in my house loves this kit!
column10: Actually, in my house I am in the minority, I am the only one that doesn't absolutely love this kit! When you whip it up, you get orzo pasta, chicken and broccoli, all in the creamy Velveeta cheese sauce. As with all similar Kraft dishes you must be a big fan of that cheese, as it does tend to dominate the taste of the dish.My one complaint with this product is with the choice of the pasta. Instead of orzo, I think that shells would have gone better with the other ingredients, and would bunch less than the orzo. But, nonetheless, that's actually a small complaint. Like I said, everyone else in my house loves it, and that's good enough for me!(Review of Kraft Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets Dinner Kit)

It's easy, cheesy, yummy and ready in about 20 minutes with 4 Steps...1-BROWN chicken pieces2-ADD water, seasoning, pasta3-Cover and simmer for about 7 minutes then add broccoli cook 2-4 minutes4-Remove from heat and stir in cheese sauce.All you need to use this kit is a pound of chicken breast pieces and 2.5 cups of water. This kit has a packet of tasty Velveeta cheese sauce instead of the usual powdered cheese in most "helper" kits. The Seasoning and Broccoli Florets are in separate packets AND the pasta is in a cello bag rather than just being in the cardboard box.The suggested crumbled Ritz Cracker topping pumps up the "yum appeal" AND more salt! Adding a side dish of broccoli, a salad and a fruit dessert makes this a filling, healthy meal.PROS:+Doesn't taste like it came from a box, SECONDS were requested!+Easily modifiable - you can substitute a pound of leftover chicken, ground chicken or even fresh chicken thigh meat pieces+At less than THREE bucks a box, it's worth having on hand to jazz up a quick meal.CONS:I wish microwave instructions were available on the box or from Kraft Customer Service...It's nearly a month of 100 degree days. We're encouraged to use microwave ovens rather than regular stoves and ovens during 2-7 PM electricity usage peak to reduce usage and stress on the "electric grid".

Kraft Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets Dinner is a perfect meal solution for my family.  It is quick, easy, convenient for me.  It is hardy, tasty, filling for them.Sometimes I don't have time to make a totally-from-scratch dinner (even though I would like to be able to do so everyday), but this is the next best thing, and they don't care, anyway.  As long as it is filling and tastes good.All you do is add chicken.  Cook it, and then add the ingredients from the box, and there you have a convenient, hardy, tasty meal for your family.
This reminds me of a hamburger helper,  and it's very good.  A little expensive compared to hamburger helper,  but still very good.

The Kraft Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillet Dinner is one of the most easiest yet filling meals that I've made in a while. The product uses a creamy cheese rather than the powdered cheese found in other products and this makes a big difference in the taste the seasoning was perfect and I only had to add a small amount of my own seasoning to help. I added some grilled chicken breast strips that I use for my salads and this made the preparation that much simpler to prepare.The finished product has a great taste and if you add some steamed broccoli as a side dish and pop some dinner rolls in the oven then you have a perfect meal that is sure to be a hit with the family because my family really enjoyed this. Great Job Kraft!

We normally don't eat this type of food, but it looked interesting. I always liked the Velveeta-style macaroni and cheese products over the powdered. This has an orzo pasta though, not noodles. It was more like a chicken/broccoli/rice casserole dish than an outright pasta dish.I had some already-cooked chicken thigh leftovers in the fridge, so the prep time was very short. The instructions were easy to understand and follow. The little bits of dried out broccoli though, they looked like old parsley. If I were to make this again I might add half a package of frozen chopped broccoli to get some real-veg flavor and texture into it.Overall the flavor was better than most Chicken Helper products, and I assume that's the market Velveeta is going after. The creamy cheesy sauce was a big plus over the straight-powder products offered by Hamburger Helper product.The suggested topping was to grind up Ritz crackers on top; that would have made a nice touch. It was a hit with teen son and husband, and even the teenager could make this for dinner if he had to.

column4: ROBERT W. SAINTJOHN "I am The Pumpkin King"
column10: I wouldn't recommend this as a serious side-dish for a nice dinner. It reminds me of the kind of things I used to eat in college, on a budget. Or late nights after returning from the bars.Anything that's called Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Dinner Kit should not, in theory, make you want to add chicken, real broccoli and real cheese to it to make it edible. It's processed food and it tastes like it.Also, if you do make it, eat it all in one sitting. It is even less appetizing when refrigerated overnight and re-heated the next day.
THIS PRODUCT IS AMAZING! I HAD IT FOR DINNER, AND I HAVE TO ADMIT I HOGGED IT ALL! ALL I CAN SAY IS THAT MY KIDS DIDN'T GET MUCH DINNER THAT NIGHT!

I could eat almost anything Velveeta, and this new item is no exception. Adding chicken really brings out the flavor. It may not be a high-brow entree, but it's a very good one if you're looking for a quick and tasty dinner with the family.
For a fast and easy side dish, this can work but my broccoli loving son didn't like this at all. He said the texture was "weird". I'll stick with regular mac & cheese

column9: Nutritionally Empty & Tastes Kinda Funky. Not a Total Wash, Though
column10: Okay. It's a Velveeta skillet dinner; we're not talking about a four-star prix fixe experience in Paris. My expectations were fairly low: it only had to taste pretty good. The included, freeze-dried broccoli florets were dusty and powdery; they didn't add much to the dish's flavor or appearance. The included seasoning had a kind of unusually sweet flavor to it, which I found initially interesting but was ultimately displeasing. The pasta was more like orzo (large rice, basically).It's a hyper-tasty meal: it has plenty of fat and carbohydrates (and, if you elect to add chicken - protein) per serving. Each serving isn't particularly large, either; I could easily eat two, though at 390 calories, I don't think I'd want to. It's inexpensive - a bonus! - but isn't a good choice as a staple. For an occasional, easily-prepared indulgence, though, it's a good venture and can be a welcome change from spaghetti.

column9: It Made Me Eat My Broccoli
column10: I'm not a broccoli fan, and yet I liked this-- which probably says something about the amount of broccoli in it! My daughter loves both broccoli and mac 'n' cheese, which is why I got this-- turned out she only kinda liked it, whereas I thought it was great.I added the suggested crumbled Ritz crackers to the top and followed the directions, and thought the meal was very tasty. It's really just a sprinkling of broccoli for a bit of flavor, definitely not a full serving. You'd still need to add a vegetable to this meal.

The new Cheesy Skillets dinner mix from Velveta is very easy to make and is good when you're pressed for time. The flavor I sampled was the Choicken and Broccoli. Prep. was very easy, just fry up some chicken, add the mix and that's about it. If you're a family on the run or a single guy it's a great quick dinner. I've had some of the other flavors, but I think I like this one best!

column9: not something i would buy myself
column10: I got this for free from the Amazon Vine Program. Glad I did because I wouldn't spend my own money on the product after tasting it. It is not something I would be willing to buy myself if I was looking for prepackaged meals for my family.It is really easy to make and doesn't take a whole lot of time. You can do it in a skillet or pot. I didn't use chicken since I was in a hurry. I thought it would taste a bit like macaroni and cheese with broccoli but it tastes nothing like mac n cheese. The broccoli itself was dehydrated and olive green colored...was more like broccoli flakes. The pasta is really tiny and looks like rice at first. I barely taste the cheese sauce to be honest since the seasoning overpowers it.Overall, an okay product if you need a quick meal. However, I will not be buying it myself.

column9: Not Bad - Convenient - But, where's the broccoli?
column10: This is a product similar to hamburger helper.  You just add chicken and have a quick and (somewhat) more exciting meal.  The cheese sauce was alright--about what you would expect from Velveeta.  It did not taste like true cheese but did have that Velveeta taste that many people--including me--enjoy.  My main issue with this is the lack of any real broccoli other than minuscule freeze-dried bits of what appears to be broccoli.  It was probably foolish of me given what this is but I was hoping for more.  Overall, if you are looking for a cheesy (or Velveeta-esque) sauce to compliment your chicken with, this is it.  If like me, you were hoping for something a bit more tasty with some broccoli in it, you may be disappointed unless you add the broccoli yourself.

Tried this and was happy with it. It is a product similar to Betty Crocker's Hamburger Helper and Tuna Helper. I am sure it is designed to give them some competition in the 'meal in a box' category. Similarly prepared, you add chicken to this particular one, a breast is great chopped into cubes. The Velveeta cheese sauce mix is excellent with great taste. The only reason I give this 4 stars is I think they could have done a little better on the broccoli. What is in the box, or at least mine, was more like flakes, than pieces. The flavor altogether is a little on the bland side. But may be able to experiment with some added seasoning. Overall, I like it!

First, I have to say that when I got this product, my kids were quite excited.  They love anything with cheese in it so that was a plus from the beginning.  The directions are easy and you can substitute different meats for the chicken breast, which--besides 2 1/2 cups of water--is the only thing not included in the box.  I used ground turkey since I didn't have any chicken breast on-hand.  I'm sure that ground beef, pork or cubed thigh meat would work just as well.  One recommendation:  Stick to the instructions to the tee.  When they say "simmer & stir often", they mean very often.  The pasta sticks to the pan if you do not stir it often enough.  I stirred about every 45 seconds to 1 minute during the first 7-minute cooking time and just barely caught the pasta from sticking too much to the pan.  The reason I placed broccoli in quotations in the title is that the teeny-tiny packet of freeze-dried broccoli once placed in the dish near the end of the cooking time becomes pretty much non-existent.  It is hard to see and it does not have that lovely green look like it does in the picture.  I'd really just call it the Cheesy Chicken Skillet dinner and not even include the broccoli.Flavor was decent, although a little salty if you eat more than a servings-worth.  The kids loved it, of course...it's CHEESY!  It wasn't bad for my taste buds either.  I was thinking that if I make this again, I might just add my own fresh broccoli florets near the end instead of the freeze-dried packet.The Kraft Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets Dinner Kit was a hit with the kids...I'd just leave the word "broccoli" out of it.

I read a lot of the reviews before cooking this product, so I wasn't expecting much as the reviews seemed kind of negative.  However, I was pleasantly surprised.  I needed a main dish in a hurry because I was short on time.  I used a 13 oz. can of chicken instead of cooking up some and it worked out fine.I tossed everything except the cheese into a 2-quart size pot, stirred as directed, added the cheese as directed, stirred it again and served it.  Yes, the broccoli was scant, but since I had steamed fresh broccoli to go with the meal it didn't matter.  Everyone seemed to like it including me and I really thought it was going to be pretty awful because of some the reviews.  Even my kid who is real finicky about cheese in her food liked it and ate all that I put on her plate.  The other kid asked for 2nds of it.I know that it's not the healthiest, most nutritious or even anything really good for you about it, but I realized that this stuff would be a fantastic camp or emergency situation food, assuming you had a camp stove to heat up the water and boil the rice/pasta.  It's got a lot of calories which would be good for camping especially if you do some hiking, and if a winter storm blows through knocking the power off for a couple of days this would be great to cook up on the camp stove.  It would be especially good if you had some canned chicken to add, but even without it I think it would be eaten quite quickly.I'll most likely buy some of this just too store for times that it might be needed and to take it camping with us.  It would really make cooking a meal easier since everything goes into one pot.  And I think this stuff would probably store for several years and still be edible so hey, get a few boxes and save them for 2012 if you believe in that sort of stuff.

column9: GREAT Chicken Dinner -- Move Over, HH!!
column10: I've reviewed other Velveeta Skillets before, and while I like the flavor fine, I stopped short of saying that they were better than Hamburger Helper.  The flavor was different, but not really better.  The preparation was easy, but not easier.  The price is higher, so not better.But I think this chicken and broccoli skillet just might be worth the extra money.  Preparation isn't any easier than HH (but really, how hard is it to fix something like this?!  If you've got a problem fixing it, you may just want to step away from the stove and go to a restaurant!).  The price still isn't really cheaper.  But it tastes MUCH better than any Chicken Helper that I've ever had before.The real strength of the Velveeta Skillet dishes is the cheese.  The Helper boxes use powdered cheese and a milk/water combo to make the cheese.  Velveeta takes advantage of their core product to offer a packet of real, honest to goodness Velveeta cheese.  the result is a much richer, cheesier meal that is really light-years ahead of powder.  Compare Velveeta shells and cheese to any powder-cheese and you'll see what I mean.Preparation is quick, which comes in handy when you're trying to fix something good and quick.  My picky eater didn't like it, though to be honest she barely tried it; in fact, she decided she didn't like it when I told her it was broccoli and cheese.  My son loves broccoli, though, and he cleaned his plate in no time.  Don't tell your kids it's got broccoli in it and they'll be fine -- the broccoli is VERY finely chopped (this is one place that I was disappointed with the Velveeta, to be honest).  You might even experiment with other vegetables, and it's simple to just leave the broccoli out if you don't want it.

column9: amazing my family loved this product
column10: this one box fed a family of five hungry people and we all enjoyed every bite. I used canned chicken and the taste was really good with the rice and cheese.

column4: P. Colin McGraw "AV, Computer & EnviroTech Nut"
column10: My toddlers love mac and cheese and this is an easy way to include some veggies in with it. They call the broccoli "trees". :-)

column4: Kimberly J. Karas "a New England mom"
column9: Convenient fix-up for your chicken.  Not bad!
column10: Liked the pasta and the dish was quick and easy to prepare.  Pleased it wasn't salty tasting, oddly it was a little on the sweet side?  The purpose of this product for me is if I have chicken and I don't have the time, inspiration or other ingredients to make an actual supper.  My main expectation here is the convenience and this definately has that.  I prepared without using a lid on my skillet and just kept it on high with an eye on it.  It was done in minutes.  I think it's a good idea to add your own broccoli because the flakes that it comes with aren't anything too special (as about every person here will agree!  Would be nice with a salad or veggie side dish.  At $0.18/oz I feel your are getting what you pay for here.  My six year old however, said it was too cheesy.  I thought it was fine.  You could either hold back a little on the cheese pouch or feel confident there is enough cheese in there to cover adding your own broccoli or another veggie into the mix.

Please note that I am not evaluating the nutritional value of this, nor am I commenting on the amount of sodium. I did  not read that part of the label and assume that it is within the norm for products of this type. That being said, the entire family REALLY liked this.No one flavor was overpowering (something I feared as I have never been a fan of Velveeta cheese itself). You do have to add the chicken to it ... why I didn't think of that I do not know; it's kind of obvious ... but everything cooks up quickly, and as I said, everyone loves it. We will be buying more of this.

I have a confession. I really like the ready-made meals like hamburger helper. They are comfort food and easy to make when you are too busy to cook something from scratch. Usually the meals from a box are good, but not excellent. This meal was different.  I thought this cheesy skillet with broccoli was so yummy, I went back for a second helping!It takes a few minutes to sauté the chicken bits to get them nice and brown, and we bought some extra broccoli to increase the veg content. And voila! A tasty meal that my entire family praised, including my finicky older father enjoyed. Even my health-conscious older sister commented the meal was very good, and she is usually a bit snobby about premade food.Cooking time can get a bit irksome if you are in a hurry. You do spend time browning chicken, stirring, and getting the meal ready. To cut back on that you could cut the chicken and bake it in the oven at 350 for about 30 minutes, thus saving you the sautéing which sometimes I do not like to do. I really liked it and recommend it.

"Kraft Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets Dinner Kit"; Add chicken with a salad and ; is really good in flavor but you have to make sure to do not add salt. It has a lot of salt pre-added. It does feed three to four people if you add a salad or vegetable with it. It is easy and quick. I have bought another dinner from Kraft Velveet and it was good too. It beats eating a boxed macaroni and cheese. This is good, fast and tasty and I recommend it for any one who needs to eat on the run. Thanks to Kraft, again.

I really wanted to like Velvetta's Cheesy Skillets Chicken and Broccoli but I don't.When the product arrived I looked at the box cover and it looked delicious.I looked at the ingredient label and I began to worry. The ingredients list islong. The product just seems so processed. I thought maybe I could save it by adding real ingredients likefresh broccoli but decided this first round I had to try it just as directed.I was disappointed in the quality of the dehydrated broccoli. I really felt like this was something you feed someonethat you aren't very fond of. I've never been to prison but I imagined that this might be the stuff they are given.Perhaps death row inmates are served this for their last meal so they actually want to go willingly to the execution room so they don't have to eat any more.After I cooked it, it just looked wrong. It smelled wrong. I know I could cook better. I don't think this saves that much time.I'm trying to move away from processed foods. If you are also perhaps you want to avoid this.

I have to admit I was pretty excited to try this, I love Velveeta Shells and Cheese so I was hoping this was a bulked up version of that.  As the other reviews have pointed out, the broccoli leaves something to be desired.  After I opened the packed I thought about leaving it out all together.  The flavor is good overall but it doesn't WOW me and honestly not that much better than Hamburger/Chicken Helper.  I also tried the Cheeseburger Mac version and I liked it better than the Chicken and Broccoli but again, nothing to get excited about.  The flavor is on par with Hamburger/Chicken Helper and the preparation is very similar.  I would probably buy it again because it is a decent, quick meal but it isn't something that I would crave.

As pre-packaged dinners go this offering by Kraft is pretty darn good.  The pasta is rice sized (forgotten the name of such) and the sauce reflects Kraft's mastery of cheeses.  The broccoli is minute but adds a worthy flavor and makes a plain chicken dinner into a filling repast with a creamy cheesy sauce that you really can't turn your nose up at.  I think for working Mom's it's a boon, but use two if you're feeding more than 3.  I don't like Hamburger Helper and I certainly don't like their chicken helper at all, but Kraft has made it palatable with a little extra pizzazz so I may have to go back and try other offerings now that I've discovered that some aren't half bad.
this was a different twist on Broccoli and cheese, but was very easy to prepare.I did think the sauce was salty.  You do not need to add any spice or salt to the dish.
My husband loves velveeta shells and cheese so we HAD to try these!! Very quick and easy. Don't need anything but the meat. But you may want to add a salad or some veggies for a round dinner! :)
This was a nice filling and tasty meal.  I would recommend it. Be sure to cook the pasta long enough.

column9: When you don't know what to cook or want something quick
column10: I ordered Kraft Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets Dinner Kit through Amazon's Vine Program as a sampler.  This is designed to be a quick and easy meal for a person to fix on those nights when things are a little to fast and you don't want to take time to fix a full meal.  The package comes with noddles, velveeta cheese and broccoli; all you have to do is add the chicken.  For preparation I grilled a sliced chicken breast to add to the ingrediants.  Preparation was easy and quick.  Something that left me underwhelmed was the broccoli.  Rather than being heads its only the flower part and a rather small amount; only enough to add color to the meal.  Flavor is a little on the velveeta cheese side of things; not strong but cheesey.  I'll call this one a 3.5 star item with 4 stars on the convience (it's quick but you still need to provide product) but 3 or fewer for flavor.  More broccoli  (heads would have been great) or a different cheese might have added to the meal, how you prepare the chicken could also add more to the flavor.  Call this one 3 stars.

column9: So easy a man age 63 can do it.
column10: Easy to prepare. Good cheesy flavor. Even I can do it.I did realize after trying other Velveeta Cheesy Skillets, that there is plenty of cheese to enlarge upon what is in the skillet. My own adaptation included chicken first cooked on the grill; adding extra broccoli from the garden; some bell, banana, and jalapeno peppers; Roma tomatoes; and mushrooms (fresh or canned). More bulk, less calories per serving, except I could not stop eating with only one serving. I cooked that good. Amazing, these Cheesy Skillet boxes.Also I found that Doritos chips went great with this dish; rather than the customize suggestion of RITZ crackers. That may just be a man's choice. Bottom line...I'll do Velveeta Cheesy Skillets again.Box directions are Brown, Add, Cover, Add Cheese. It's that easy.Hey mom...when it's a no-school day, have the kids cook this up. I'm sure 3rd grader and over can do it. It's that easy. It is possible to leave the broccoli out, if kids complain. Just add their favorite veggie...corn, beans, peas, or carrots. Make lunch fun.

I am a fan of Velveeta cheese so I thought I would like this, and I did. My 2 year old even liked it and he is a very picky eater. I had good chicken to go with it though, and that probably helped it. There was enough to feed my family of 3, but I debate if it could feed four. I liked it enough to keep buying it. Good job, Kraft!

column9: Thank you for a tastey, filling dinner
column10: I cooked this for my wife this evening.  The preparation was easy.  The hardest part was chopping the chicken breast which wasn't any work at all.  The rest of the process was just time.  It took no effort and in the end it was a great tasting and filling meal.  I did add more frozen vegetables because the broccoli flakes that came in the package were not enough vegetables for us.  The cheese has a fantastic taste; better than I had anticipated.  I usually shy away from cheesy dinners and was skeptical when I saw the package of thick cheese to add at the end of cooking this.  I actually think it was the cheese flavor that gave it the flavor that I really enjoyed.  I also enjoyed the thickness of the rice.  It was not the small flimsy rice but a thicker more hearty rice.  This also thickened up really quickly and the meal was ready in about 20 minutes.  My wife and myself had leftovers so I would estimate that this box could feed a family of three.  Overall I enjoyed tonights dinner and will use the coupon that came in the box to buy some more.

column9: Good food. No wait. No kidding.
column10: Kraft Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets Dinner is a food kit that is easy to prepare, tastes great, and can be eaten as an entree or a side dish. Just supply your own boneless chicken breast. Tastes great and worthy of the Kraft Velveeta name.

Kraft Cheesy Skillets are definitely not one of my usual meal choices, but as a departure from the norm, the Chicken and Broccoli is satsifying and tasty. Although it may be a bit too cheesy, you can adjust that. Just don't squeeze the whole cheese pouch into the pan.The nutirition numbers are not great, but unless you're really conscious of that (like I am), they're not that bad either. The calories and fat are in the acceptable range, but keep in mind they change when you add your chicken.This is a good tasting, very quick and very easy dinner solution for busy famlilies. In summary, I'd buy the Broccoli and Chicken dinner for myself, but the other flavors are not nearly as good tasting as this one.

My two youngest daughters (10 and 12 years old) fixed this by themselves the other day and had no problems. They were amazed at the creaminess of the cheese! An easy option for those days when you need a handy quick meal!

Velveeta's version of chicken helper, but obviously cheesier! This was amazing. I am living on a tight budget in my new apartment, so aside from eating pb&j and anything else inexpensive, this was the best meal I've had in awhile. It's easy and quick to fix and tastes awesome. Even the broccoli bits taste fresh and flavorful. I would highly recommend this dinner kit to anyone!

We just made this tonight for dinner.  It says five servings, but that would be as a side dish.  As a stand alone meal there's probably three good servings.  This is basically a cheese risotto in a quick and easy form.  It does lack a little bit of "punch" in flavor, so I'd probably use chicken broth instead of water next time.  The timing of 20 minutes is pretty much right on and it is not difficult to do.  I think if no one came in your kitchen before you served it, they'd be impressed at your good cooking.

I was leery of this product but now I am hooked.  This is really very easy, and only one pot to clean up!  My kids loved it, so I am happy.  I added cut up chicken and more vegetables, broccoli, snap peas and red peppers along with bread and a garden salad, this was a perfect dinner. Very moist and tasty - I normally use my crock pot but liked this even better because no big crock to clean!  This is a quick and easy alternative when you don't have a dinner idea - your kids will love it and eat it because of the cheese sauce.

And easy to make.Though kind of misleading in the title. You'd think there was chicken in it---you add your own, which you can do with ANY box of velveeta mac & cheese. With the broccoli added, it's more *nutritious* than most standard pasta cheese dishes. My only other issue is the high sodium content, but that's pretty much a given with most boxed foods.Great for those nights you dont want to cook

If your looking for a good meal idea this week, Kraft Velveeta chicken and broccoli skillets may be the way to go. I love mac n cheese and broccoli, so it was a no brainer to add chicken to the mix. These skillets remind me of Hamburger Helper in how easy they are to make and how great they taste.

column9: Yum... using leftover cooked roast chicken in the fridge
column10: I like dinner kits - they come with all the ingredients, no thinking involved, just add chicken and you're done.  I like to start with leftover roast chicken, which works great.  Don't use grilled or BBQ, just simple roasted adds the most flavor and doesn't overpower the dish.Flavor was yummy!... better than 'Helper' brand.  Pasta was nice, but the sauce was really flavorful.  Overall, I would recommend.
this product was easy to make and acceptable as a quick dinner solution.  Not unlike other Kraft products, the cheese is good.  Price is reasonable.

This was really, really good. When I was making it, it did not look very appealing. I left the chicken out becasue it looked like it could be awful. I added the pasta (that looks more like dry rice) to the water & the seasoning. The seasoning had a bad smell to it. I cooked it the 7 minutes & then added the dried broccoli to it & simmered it for 3 more minutes. After that I added the cheese & mixed it well. It still looked awful but I dished it up & guess what, it was fantastic. I ate half of it at one time. I don't see where adding your own pound of chicken breasts to it would add any more flavor so I would serve this as a side dish or just eat it as meal. It had a nice flavor of broccoli to it with just the right amount of cheese sauce. GOOD JOB VELVEETA..... I'm sold on it.

Summary:  Preparation a snap, Tastes good, Filling.Kraft Chicken and Broccoli skillets are a box of home style comfort food.  Smooth taste, nice creamy texture.  The cheese sauce is the dominant taste which would be a problem if it wasn't such tasty cheese.It's easy to make but you do have to add your own chicken.  That isn't obvious from the Amazon description.  Kraft suggests a pound of boneless chicken breasts.  I used thighs - I imagine almost any meat would work.A funny thing about the cooking is the dish looks TERRIBLE up until the time you finish.  You might think something has gone wrong - nope.Nutrionally, I see no problems.  For medical reasons I have to stay on a low fat diet and this slips in under my limit.  8g fat, (2.5 saturated) is no biggee - especially for something this cheesy!  Sodium is 620mg - something you might need to watch out for depending on what your daily limit is.It would be easy enough to adjust the recipe so as to lower those numbers.  Add more macaroni, less meat, don't use all the cheese (ANYTHING but that!) and you can make do.Prep time was under half an hour.
The Daughter and I liked it, but the Wife & Sons loathed it.  It couldn't be any easier to make and renders a quick meal, but the cheese taste is unusual.

column4: Sir Charles Panther "Life is hard.  It's hard...
column9: Good Stuff, Easy, but Even Better with Customization
column10: We tried this package's brother first, the Velveeta Cheesy Skillets Ultimate Cheeseburger Mac.  This one was better; my wife and kids agree.  We will definitely look for this one again, but will pump it up to better suit our personal tastes.Although the instructions say one pound of chicken, I went for poultry broke and used a package of 2.47 pounds.  Yes, call me wild, reckless, impetuous, whatever.  Given the fact that the instructions for the amount of water are based on what the orzo and broccoli will soak up, the extra chicken didn't do anything to the recipe, and actually made the finished dish a lot better.  So, I advise that you use at least two pounds of chicken when you cook this kit.Also, the instructions advise to cut the chicken into 1-inch pieces.  I did that, and they came out pretty big, as in pretty big bite-size.  I advise to cut the chicken into ½-inch pieces, and you'll get better distribution throughout the dish.  Smaller pieces also will cut the cooking time.It cooks up just fine, although my cooking time was quite a bit more than indicated on the box.  Total time for me, from the first of the chicken browning until serving was about an hour.  Consider, though, that I used more chicken than advised which likely affected the overall cooking time as indicated on the box's directions.  Yes, it was worth the prep time and wait.The seasoning ingredients are passable, smelling in the pouch an awful lot like canned parmesan cheese, with a hint of celery and parsley.  The orzo plumped up very nicely and filled out the dish well.  The broccoli florets were the only real surprise in the package, coming in a very small envelope and coming out a lot more like ground-up spice bits than the broccoli I thought I'd be getting.  Actually, the box's depiction is about right in terms of broccoli size and distribution.  This package's broccoli will not suffice for your USDA-recommended vegetable intake; it lends color and a small amount of texture to the dish, but to my experience offered no additional taste.  The product's title is "chicken and broccoli," but the ratio is far from equal.The Velveeta cheez pouch was squishy and cheezy and ample; I was surprised by the amount of cheez I was squeezing into the dish.  But hey, it melted down just fine and mixed in with the dish in no time, glomming it all together super-American-style.  As it did this, I was thinking that mixing it with some cream of mushroom soup, dropping the entire thing into a casserole dish, covering it with a top layer of cheez and some fried onions would really make this something cool; I'll have to try this.  Your results may vary.Taste: This stuff was just fine by itself, although my wife noticed immediately that it was pretty bland.  Like, really bland.  Given that I was cooking this for a review, I intentionally did not experiment with the kit (other than my highly irresponsible and psychotically dangerous use of twice the amount of recipe-specified chicken, and a good three tablespoons of extra-virgin olive oil to cook the chicken, and I didn't drain it, leaving the juices and olive oil to join the dish, which  I recommend you do, too).  Yeah, it's pretty bland, but not bad at all, and it's got a lot of potential.  So, I recommend that you up-spice it to fit your own personal needs.  That might mean some salt and pepper.  If and when I make this again, I'll sauté some onions with the chicken, maybe add some fresh sliced mushrooms, and I'll definitely drop in some garlic, black pepper, caraway seeds, and maybe even a dash of powdered cayenne pepper to give this dish some action.Bottom line: in the dinner kit market, this one isn't really that remarkable.  Follow the simple instructions and you'll end up with a suitably tasty and largely unremarkable dinner for 3 or 4.  But, make a few tweaks for your personal tastes, and you'll end up with something much better.

Maybe I'm just easy pleasing, but I enjoyed my Velveeta Cheesy Skillet meal. It's cheesy, hearty, filling, and satisfying. Yes, you have to add your own chicken, but I wouldn't want it any other way. Neither chicken in a can nor dehydrated chicken hold much appeal for me. I do wish there were more of a broccoli presence in this cheese dominated dish, and for a future meal we may add some.For someone watching calories carefully this may not be a meal of choice. The prepared dinner has a stated five serving size, though Mrs. Spudman (she of the canary appetite) and I finished off about four servings together. According to the figures on the side panel, one serving delivers 390 calories (100 from fat) 620 mg of sodium, and 8g of fat.For me this is a good tasting, easily prepared meal that hits the spot. Those eating two servings at a meal don't need to save too much room for dessert.

I think this'll be the last time I try one of these things.  Even for cheap alternatives to help stretch a food budget, they're really just not very good.You already know what to do when you open the box- cook meat, heat water, add rice and flavoring... I mean, seasoning... then top it off with the supplied broccoli...  Wait- broccoli?  What broccoli?  The fact that the packet containing the veggies was no bigger than the one containing the seasoning was a big hint.  Someone else called it 'broccoli dust' and they're quite right!  It looked more like parsley flakes than anything and was hardly noticeable.It wasn't bad, I guess.  Tasted like chicken and cheese with the barest hint of... I dunno, vegetable flavor.  But I can at least say this one was better than the Cheese-n-Mac concoction I tried last time.

column9: Kraft Velvetta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets Dinner Kit
column10: This product is along the lines of Hamburger Helper, but I remember eating Velvetta when I was a kid and wanted to try this product of "liquid gold". The Orzo pasta was a nice treat but the broccoli florets were a joke.  Small little flecks of freeze dried broccoli (disappointing).  The cheese sauce had that strong smell of Velvetta, but once mixed with the rest of the ingredients, it lost the taste that I loved.  Overall, it was okay, nothing special, better off making from scratch.

O.K. I got this for free from the Vine program.  As per the directions we cooked the chicken, added the "fixins", and we had a fair meal for five people.The kids ate it up.  They and my wife liked it.  I'm sure there was some broccoli in it but didn't see too much.  The little kid ate it and he usually turns his nose up at dishes that have too much broccoli; there was no chance of that here.  The sauce is actually more slightly broccoli cheese flavored sauce.  It's more a Velvetta & Chicken dinner with a "drive by" of Broccoli.I give it a C but would not buy it from the store.

column9: It's pretty much exactly what you'd expect: Velveeta!
column10: So, this isn't amazing gourmet food, but you wouldn't be picking this up if you were looking for gourmet.  It's fast, it's easy, it's what you turn to when you're home from work late and you need to cook up something in a hurry without having to think creatively.I'm not going to lie, I love "cheese-product."  I'm a lover of real cheese too, but there's a special place in my heart for processed liquidy cheese-flavored food stuffs. They should really get a category of its own (powdered cheese product, nacho queso, and Velveeta all fall into this delightful category of cheese based non-cheeses.)  Anyway, I love Velveeta piping hot and poured over broccoli, but if you've ever eaten Velveeta and let it cool, you're familiar with the plastic-like texture the Velveta takes on.  It's the same here - you have to eat this meal while it's HOT.  Otherwise, don't bother.  Leftovers are good too - just be sure to nuke it to as hot as you can get it.The instructions call for one breast of chicken.  I feed hungry people, so I added two.  The dehydrated broccoli packet was disappointing, so I also added a fresh head of broccoli to the skillet a little earlier so it could steam in the water.  This was a great move - the fresh broccoli REALLY improves the dinner kit, but it's fine without it.  The pasta to chicken/broccoli ratio was a little low because of my additions, but the pasta is like an orzo anyway, so I didn't mind it.Would I eat this once a week?  Probably not.  Would I buy this again?  Probably - it's like keeping a can of pasta sauce in your pantry.  When you have time, it's the best to just make a simple pasta sauce from scratch, but there are days when there is JUST NO TIME... so... this is another pasta-sauce-from-a-jar-spaghetti-night alternative.

This was a really easy meal to make, but it really wasn't enough for our family of 4. The kids liked it because it was so cheesy. It was a little too cheesy for the adults, but it was good. These would be good to have on hand for nights when you don't have a lot of time to cook.

We love boxed meals because they're so easy to make after a long day and better for you than fast food.  However, we do get tired of the same ole', same ole' meals so decided to give this one a try.First off, they recommend 1 inch pieces of chicken which really cutting them even smaller would have been much better.  Personally I didn't care for the flavor but I love velvetta cheese so I'm guessing that's due to the seperate spice packet that you have to add to the mixture.  What I do love is that there's a completely seperate package with the brocolli so you can add a little of it or a lot depending on your personal tastes.My husband said the dinner was actually very good though he agrees the flavor is a bit dull.

column9: A decent meal in a box
column10: I found that I liked the Velveeta meal better than a complete meal kit. However, I did have to pre-cook the chicken which took away from the box use for me. It wasn't a whole lot less work than cooking a homemade chicken meal. It tasted pretty good and was very cheesy. I have a family of 3 and it fed us with some other sides. Overall it was a decent meal and a fairly quick fix. I would probably get it again in a pinch.

Very tasty , I really like this because its more filling then orignal velveeta macaroni and cheese, so not only are u getting that cheesy treat that everyone knows and loves but with extant nutritional value. Great they thought to add broccoli Yum!

column9: Great quick meal for any occasion
