column10: I was truly impressed with Kraft Velveeta's latest creation. Not only was it absolutely easy to prepare, but it was great tasting as well! From prep to the table it took all of thirty minutes. The instructions were easy to follow and it definitely didn't taste like a meal that came out of a box. It was delicious the night of and was still enjoyable the day after which often is an issue with boxed meals. Highly suggested for quick meal ideas that will satisfy the entire family!

We don't typically do too many processed foods, but every now and then, it's nice to have something fairly "prepped and ready."  I was expecting this to be saltier than it was.  For that, the rating was dramatically improved.  I find most boxed dinners to be far too salty to eat without downing 2 glasses of water, but this didn't have that effect.  What keeps it from being a 5 star deal is that the cheese was a bit overwhelming.  As much as I love whole, fresh foods, I am still a sucker for Velveeta.  Even with my love of the V, I had a hard time tasting any brocolli.  We also added more chicken than it calls for because there are 5 of us and I saw no point in leaving a single chicken breast in the fridge / freezer, and even with the extra chicken, it seemed to be DROWNING in chese.  If you like that, this will definitely hit the spot for you.  Otherwise, stir the cheese mix in as you go, tasting a bit until it's right for you.  If we get this again, we will most definitely have cheese left over.  Next time we buy one or two "quick meals," it's very likely this will wind up in my shopping cart.

One of the things I have always done sith Mac n Cheese is add veggies to it. I love the flavor of the cheese with veggies. One of the biggest complaints I have always had with frozen or boxed foods is the one piece of veggie they will put in a container for 4 and call it a dinner. Buy your own veggies and add it yourself. You will then get a complete serving of veggie.I don't even know what they put in this box. It sure did not look or taste like broccoli. How and why do these companies get away with this?

I followed the instructions to a tee, but in the end I found this bland and kind of gross. Which is weird because from the box and description it seemed very similar to my favorite frozen dinners (Marie Callendar's Chessy Chicken with Rice). But I was sorely disappointed. Skip this, there are far better things to do with a pound of chicken.

Well, I have to admit to being very disappointed in this product.  I doubt that there is enough broccoli in it to constitute even one serving of vegetable in the total amount...  Actually, I am surprised that there is enough broccoli in there, to even allow it to be added to the description on the front of the package.  Yes, as one reviewer put it, there is a small packet of green dust.  sigh.  Bland unremarkable taste.  My skillet dinner looked nothing like the package front.  I will not bother trying any of the other Velveeta Cheesy Skillets, after trying this one!

This was almost unedible.I am a food snob but I can enjoy some good old Kraft Mac 'n cheese.However, this one really was bad. The sauce that comes with it, the dried broccoli, and the flavor combination was just terrible.I would not recommend.

column9: I couldn't taste anything but salt!
column10: I understand it is a box meal so I really did not expect a great deal from it, but this was seriously one of the worst dishes I have ever had the shame of preparing myself.  Based on the box front, I thought that there would be a packet of dehydrated broccoli florets.  Wrong - no florets, just some sort of broccoli flakes.  So I prepare it according to the directions and sit down to eat.  From the first bite I can barely taste anything other than just salt.  I am not salt-adverse though I am not typically one to add a lot of extra salt to my meals, just enough to enhance flavor as needed.  This ended up being so salty I could not finish the dish.  I ate several bites hoping that it would get better, but no such luck.I really don't expect much from a boxed meal, but this kit even managed to disappoint those low expectations. There are much more tasty options out there for quick meals.

What a disaster! What nerve they have! They label this mess "Chicken and Broccoli" but there's no chicken in it. There's almost no broccoli in it, either. You get a teeny tiny pouch with some green dust in it, that they have the nerve to label "broccoli florets".Besides that, the little pasta bits have no taste or texture. Then you drown your meat that you added and everything else in a mass of tasteless cheese sauce that has all the calories and sodium of cheese and none of its good qualities (like flavor).What an expensive way to ruin some perfectly good meat.Step 1 in preparing this is to fry up the chicken. Stop right there, hand me the chicken between two slices of bread, and I'll be a whole lot happier, plus saving the cost of this disaster.

I was looking forward to trying this product as it looks really good on the box. I was not pleased at what was in the box. I did not expect broccoli but what they package as broccoli is some sort of green dust-like substance.I decided to try but replaced the dust with real broccoli. I seasoned the chicken and cooked it separately. Once I had the broccoli and chicken ready I proceeded to use the product as stated in the box instructions.Once finished (and it is not fast) I served it to my family. The consensus was that it would be better to prepare it from scratch.I would not recommend this product unless you are starving and it is the only thing left in your pantry... better yet, go out and get something else.

Preparation for this product is easy. The hardest part of preparing it is cutting the chicken into 1 inch cubes. (I got my husband to do that part.) It's no more difficult to make this that it is to make Hamburger Helper.Unfortunately, that's where the positives end. It doesn't look particularly appetizing until you add the cheese at the end. Though the cheese flavor is pleasant, there is another seasoning packet that you add while it's cooking. I'm not sure what it's for since I couldn't taste it. The chicken had very little flavor at its core. The pasta (orzo?) looks deceptively like bowties on the box but actually more closely resembles rice. The broccoli "florets" may as well be left out. They add nothing. They come dried in a packet. They look like dust as you throw them into your food. My husband described them as unpleasantly textured despite the fact that they are little more than bits. Certainly not what I would consider florets.I'd actually been planning on trying this. The description is great, but the actual flavor falls short. We have leftovers that no one wants. I wouldn't be willing to try this again.
It was so nasty! It has broccoli dust. I was very mushy as well. It also smelled horrible and looked green! I would NOT reccomed it to anyone.
This tastes like something you would find in a prison cafeteria.  Not that I would know what that tastes like, but I don't care for this at all.  Has a funny aftertaste too.  It's also too salty.

column9: Quick and easy...I personally liked it!
column10: I made this for dinner for my wife and three kids.  It was very easy to make and had a very good taste in my opinion.  Although the kids (2, 4, and 7 years old) didn't act like they loved it, they ate every bit  of it.  My wife was very underwhelmed by it and thought it was "bland".  She would have prefered larger brocoli pieces in it as well.It definitely beats mac & cheese with a vegetable (like green beens) for a quick meal.

column9: Good flavor but a bit dry
column10: I like velveeta cheese and thought this combination would be good for our camping trip (practical meal).  Though the flavor is good, the result is not like what it's pictured on the box. The sauce is not as cheesy as the picture shows.  The broccoli gives some flavor and color but don't expect anything bigger than a broccoli flake.  The flavor is good but not what I expected.  A bit dry and more like a cheesy 'orzo' risotto.

column9: But what wine goes with this?
column10: If you like cheese glop on rice with chicken cubes and dried broccoli particulate you might like this.Honestly, this would only be enjoyable after a strenuous twenty mile hike in the mountains.Come to think of it I've had far better freeze dried camping food.Not quite awful...but close

column9: Actually Pretty Good For What It Is!
column10: This is a pretty good product, as long as you know what to expect.  Some of the reviews seem overly critical, considering that the product price and description are right in line with most other comparable items.  It looked fine prepared, and I'll post a couple photos to illustrate.  All of my family members liked it.  They didn't jump up and down for joy and declare that it was pure tastebud-heaven in a box, but they did have seconds.First, some background.  I find that one of the more challenging aspects of preparing meals for a family on a daily basis is often just figuring out what to have.  Some people are really organized and plan their menus for the week in advance.  They buy the exact ingredients they'll need for the next few days and always know what they're going to have.  I'm not that way. There have even been times when I've had something in mind and started to cook it, and then changed what I was making mid-stream, while still using the items I'd already started to prepare as part of the new dish.Maybe it comes from watching too many TV shows like MacGyver over the years, or perhaps I'm just weird, but the bottom line is I'm not that organized when it comes to everyday meals.  Aside from the staples, I usually look for good prices and buy what's on sale.  I also sometimes feel like having something different depending on the weather or people's moods or schedules.  This keeps things interesting and it's a system that works for us, but it's not perfect.The obvious downside of such a method is that there are days when I walk into the kitchen and have no idea what to make.  I look in the fridge and freezer and nothing comes to mind.  The old standby dishes can only be made so often, ordering out would be admitting defeat, and I probably don't have some of the ingredients I'd need to make something new from one of the cookbooks on the shelf.  Those tend to be the days I turn to my third-string emergency backup: boxed dinners.Most boxed dinners tend to consist of some kind of noodles or rice with various flavored sauces, sometimes dehydrated vegetables, and may or may not call for the addition of chicken, tuna, or ground beef.  This one fits the pattern (just add chicken), but adds a bit of a twist by using Orzo (rice-shaped pasta) and including a pouch of Velveeta cheese sauce and a small packet of freeze-dried broccoli bits for variety.I prepared this almost according to package directions but with a small variation.  I cut up some boneless skinless chicken breast into strips, letting them sit in a little oil, lemon juice, garlic, salt & pepper, and herbs for a while, and then fried them.  I only added the extra ingredients to the chicken because I had used more than the box called for.  Portion size looked like it would be a bit small for the family otherwise, but I was concerned that using more chicken would make the dish too bland since the seasoning packet was only intended to be used for about 1lb.  Other than that, it was made as specified, and with a crumb topping as the box suggested.Overall, it was about what I had expected from an inexpensive box dinner, and just a bit different from the typical chicken helper/hamburger helper/tuna helper.  Sometimes that's just what's needed to kickstart dinner on one of those nights when I'm out of ideas.  I'll probably buy more if I notice them on sale.

column9: puts the guilt in "guilty pleasure" without the pleasure
column10: I am a sucker for mac & cheese. It's a guilty pleasure. I sneak a bite at every buffet and Thanksgiving dinner, even though I know it's for "the kids" and it's bad for my health.When I saw this, the marketing seemed to be aimed at grown-ups, and I thought, "maybe my wife will let me get away with this."It tasted like chicken covered in ballpark nacho cheese sauce.Orzo is a terrible choice for mac & cheese. If you follow the instructions, the Orzo becomes overcooked and its texture is so similar to the sauce itself it effectively dissolves. The cheese/starch ratio is too high. It should have been elbow or penne.Green dust came out of the broccoli packet. Once rehydrated, it looked more like broccoli, but there wasn't enough. I could not taste the broccoli at all.There are few things I won't eat, but I will never eat this again.BOTTOM LINE: I have a recipe that's nearly as quick and much healthier. I designed it for convenience and speed. For better flavor, saute the chicken separately and add it last.1. Boil 1 gallon of water.2. Add 1 box of pasta, 2 chopped raw chicken breasts, some chopped broccoli.3. Cook until pasta and chicken are done.4. Drain water from pot.5. Slowly add 1 package of finely shredded cheese while stirring to melt.6. Serve immediately.

While this "dinner kit" resulted in a fairly tasty meal (slather anything in Velveeta cheese sauce, and it's going to be tasty), we were pretty disappointed in this product.  The apparently freeze-dried broccoli was a joke!  It consisted of the teeny-tiniest little pieces of broccoli (think the individual little "nubs" from a floret), such that you couldn't easily detect the dish had any broccoli in it at all.  If you want a meal consisting of chicken & broccoli mac 'n' cheese, you would be far, FAR better off buying some plain mac 'n' cheese (we buy the Kraft Velveeta brand cheese and shells often), than steaming some fresh broccoli to add in with some chicken.  Even adding frozen broccoli florets would be a huge improvement over the "broccoli dust" (to quote another reviewer) included in this packaged meal...

I'm a big fan of the standard Velveeta shells and cheese so I thought this would be great for a fast week-night dinner.  WRONG!  Ended up throwing it down the garbage disposal and ordering pizza instead.  I wish I had read the reviews first, especially Nancy's.  The first problem is that the "broccoli" was virtually non-existent.  I knew it would be dehydrated, but this stuff was dried up beyond recognition.  I immediately regretted adding it to the saucepan and wished I had steamed some real broccoli to toss in.  I pressed on, however, and added the cheese sauce.  It was thinner in consistency than the typical shells and cheese sauce.  I let it set for a few minutes to thicken but was not very excited to dig in.  The taste was bland and the only texture I got was mushy.  The calories and sodium content were also through the roof!  This was definitely not a good purchase and I wouldn't buy it again.

This was just ok, nothing special. Very complicated to prepare and the result did not taste cheesy or broccoli enough. Really not worth the time it takes to prepare and I doubt this would serve a whole family. Two people or one very hungry person.

column9: A marginal meal with misleading packaging
column10: Macaroni and cheese is a number 1 comfort food for me.  I've enjoyed both the Velveeta and Kraft brands before.  However, this cheesy skillet dinner kit falls very short of my expectations for the following reasons:- Chicken is not included in the kit even though the box label says chicken and brocolli.  I figured there would be canned chicken supplied but there wasn't.  So you need to add 1 pound of skinless chicken breast to this recipe as per the instructions on the back of the box.- The pasta looks like Risotto (grains of rice).- The dish is very salty.- There was no broccoli taste to the dish even though there were the dried broccoli florets that were added at the end.- Except for the chicken, the meal has the consistency of porridge so I had to eat it with a spoon.There are two calorie and nutrition counts on the box--as packaged and as prepared.  As packaged it's 270 calories per serving at 5 servings per box with 80 fat calories or 390 calories with 100 fat calories if you add the chicken. There's 620mg of sodium per serving but it tasted much more salty to me.I ate it, it was okay, but I would never purchase this dinner kit because I did not find it satisfying.  The only thing I liked a little was the cheesy flavor.

Type of Pasta: Orzo, it resembles more like rice than pasta, so this dish felt like a chicken,cheesy rice,broccoli type of dish as opposed to straight pasta.Resembles: Hamburger Helper's but much cheesierDifficulty: Very easyTime: 30 minutesA box fills up: About 2 people (maybe more if you eat less)Amount of Broccoli: Very little, wish they had more! but yes, very little, though you can taste it. Basically very Small little flecks of freeze dried broccoli.Amount of Cheese: good amount of cheese for 2 people!Taste: B+Ease to make: ANutrition: C+/B-Overall: B

OK, I'm sorry but when I see a package that is labeled "Chicken and Broccoli" dinner kit, I sort of expect that there will actually be some CHICKEN and some broccoli included in the box! Although the product, as prepared, is tasty enough (though not so nutritious with high calories and sodium), I do prefer the brands of these easy prep dinner kits that do include the meat in an aluminum can or sealed pouch in the kit. I also think there needs to be more evidence of broccoli in the dish.This item would be great for hungry kids and you could definitely skip the additional step of having to cook and prepare the chicken if you're in a hurry. The velveeta and pasta are creamy and appealing to that age group.
We enjoy Velveeta and it's a good item for kids to enjoy too. Kraft makes an excellent product and we all agreed we liked the Chicken and Broccoli Skillets Dinner.

I have only tried the Chicken and Broccoli Cheesy Skillet meal and this meal is amazing!!! It is an easy meal to make and it tastes great. It is called "Cheesy Skillets" for a reason and the meal is covered with cheese and it tastes great. If you want an easy meal to make, I would highly recommend the cheesey skillets. I purchase these meals all the time :)

I like the concept of this: making regular Velveeta shells and cheese a little more substantial by adding in broccoli and chicken, but it just didn't work very well for me. Obviously, taste is very subjective, but this is just my take on this product.I absolutely LOVE Velveeta. It's been one of my favorite boxed Mac n' cheese products since I was a kid, but there was something about this that made me nauseous after about 3 or 4 bites. It also became extremely sticky after a few minutes of sitting on my plate. That never usually happens with regular velveeta shells and cheese. I don't know if perhaps the "formula" is different for this, but it just wasn't very good and the richness became overwhelming fast.Overall, I'm going to stick to regular Velveeta Shells and Cheese.

My thoughts on this product echo what many others here have already stated. The lack of broccoli is a major disappointment. Actually, if there was NO broccoli, that would have been better then the dusty powdery mess that they tried to pass off as broccoli. It's a shame they dropped the ball on this one. I really enjoyed the Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheeseburger Mac Cheesy Skillets Dinner Kit 12.86 oz (Pack of 6)...it was creamy and cheesy, but not too much. This is just false advertising here. If you do decide to buy this, make sure you purchase your own broccoli to mix into it, cause you're not going to get any from this box.

I thought this would be a nice compromise between what I like for dinner, good chicken and pasta with veggies, and what my son likes, anything resembling macaroni and cheese.  The cheese sauce was creamy with a balanced flavor, but I had to add extra chicken pieces (good thing I was using pre-cooked rotisserie) to get a goood cheese to pasta/chicken ratio.  Without the extra chicken this would have been too cheesy for my taste.My biggest disappointment was the "broccoli" that in the end looked like big parsley flakes rather than broccoli. Although the prep was easy and relatively quick, I was reminded why I like my own quick recipes that allow me to have real vegetables of recognizable pieces and real cheese which I personally prefer to Velveeta.Would not buy again.

column9: Umm...it's ok ~ broccoli powder is not my thing...
column10: Velveeta Cheesy Skillets is a fun idea, the chicken and broccoli skillets dinner kit is neat in theory, (you add your own chicken), but the broccoli portion is 'included'...it was a strange kind of broccoli powder, and just wasn't quite what I would want.  Adding fresh broccoli would be a better idea - the taste without the fresh ingredients, is ok but not good...I love Velveeta, but this Kraft Velveeta dinner kit just wasn't my thing.
For what it is (easy dinner) it's ok. I would have liked some actual broccoli in it. The taste was passable. I don't thing I would buy it unless I was desperate.

column9: Tastes better than Hamburger Helper but costs more
column10: My family is a long time lover of Hamburger Helper and other complete meal options.  This is one of the best I have every had.  It is just easy to make and tastes better.  However, my only problem with them is that they are so much  more expensive and not worth the additional cost to me.

This was by far one of the worst prepackaged meals I've had. The broccoli is almost not existant and there is little if any flavor. It just comes out as a pile of mush and no attempts to spice it up prevailed.

column9: It wasn't as awful as I thought it would be....
column10: or as my nine year old said "it tasted a LITTLE better than it looked", which I can tell isn't very good.  So let me preface this review by the fact that the only boxed food my kids ever get is boxed rice like rice pilaf, and prior to trying this I have NEVER fed my family this type of meal, so they certainly aren't used to something like this showing up on their plates.  I mention this only because I spoil my family with food that is easily identifiable and that alone may have put them off from this dish.  We had to force the kids to take a bite of this and they both thought it was just awful.  My 7 year old got up and made himself a ham sandwich and let me tell you he is the type who likes to be waited on, so I can assure you he was motivated to not have to eat any more of this stuff. On a more positive note, the directions were super easy to follow and it was done in 20 minutes.  On a negative note, the supposed brocolli looked more like brown flakes mixed in that in no way resembled brocolli or even the picture on the box.  I was so dissapointed, since we always eat fresh veggies with every meal, that I had to cook some fresh brocolli and add it in so I didnt feel so awful about serving it.  In addition, my husband and I didn't think it was as awful as our kids did, but we didn't think it was good either.  Basically, my husband suggested it was the type of stuff that might be served in a homeless shelter, at which point my nine year old said "I don't think even the homeless would like to have to eat this."  In conclusion, this was a waste of perfectly good chicken (as well as the brocolli I added) and we won't ever be having it again.

We finally got a chance to try this Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets Dinner. It makes a delicious, excellent meal that is quick and easy to prepare and actually tastes like a homemade dish. It is not overly flavory, salty, nor does it taste chemical-ly in the least. It took us about 30-40 minutes to prepare including making the chicken first. The box makes quite a lot of food, it is high in calories, and filling, and very satisfying. The only negatives we found was that we agree that the broccoli florets are almost indescernible, and next time we would make some fresh broccoli to add; and also I got a headache after the meal, perhaps due to some spices or additives in the mix. Can't say for sure. Obviously this is a processed food, so it shouldn't be used every day. But it doesn't taste processed. We liked this very much, and these mixes obviously are a great way to add variety to your regular meal rotation. The pasta in the packet are so huge, I thought I was eating a large variety of wild rice. It really tasted good. I would definitely buy this again.

Our family loves the kraft velveeta cheese noodles so I thought this would be a hit.  Well not so much.  The directions were quite simple & easy to follow.  After seeing that there was no "real" broccoli chunks, I added some I had in the fridge.  Tasting it thru out the cooking I thought it needed some addition seasoning.  Needless to say the skillet dinner was not one of our favorite meals.  Probably won't be buying it anytime soon.

This is a nice product for a quick meal.  It makes up nice and creamy and I liked it very much.  Will probably be keeping a box on my pantry shelf for that time when something quick and tasty is needed.

column9: Try Turkey Breast To Add Tasty Texture To Velveeta Cheesy Skillets
column10: Velveeta Cheesy Skillets Chicken and Broccoli works best with a well prepared kitchen.  First, I recommend using at least a 12" diameter fully covered skillet.  I replaced the portion of chicken with turkey breast cut up into pieces and cook until done.  Next, I add in the 2 ½ cups of water, seasoning, one quarter stick of butter and pasta.  Bring it all to a boil, cover and reduce heat to simmer for the next 7 minutes.  Finally add in the yummy Velveeta cheese sauce pouch and stir in the tasty goodness!Coming from Louisiana, I prefer a little more spice in my meals and found myself adding just one more ingredient to get that unique Cajun flavor!  Sprinkle in 1 tablespoon of Southern Cajun Seasoning Low Sodium to give your meal a real spice kick without all that salt.We enjoyed eating this meal.  Out of a group of just three people who ate this while watching a New Orleans Saints game, there was none left 30 minutes after it was prepared.  The broccoli florets gave the meal a real interesting vegetable taste and the pasta was just right.  Velveeta Cheesy Skillets Dinner Kit really can make everyone at the table smile, if given a little Cajun kick.

I really wanted to like this product but found that it really did not have much flavor.  I had to add some grated Romano cheese to it to make it more palatable.  The picture on the package does not look anything like the end product.The pasta did not cook evenly and ended with some falling apart while other bits were still tough and chewy.I certainly would not purchase it at the regular price.

column9: Got Kids then this is perfect!
column10: I have come to love the Kraft products and no one can find a more wonderful old fashioned comfort food that's better than mac and cheese.  Velveeta has been around for more years than I can count and has not cut down on it's quality of product in these times of financial instability.This is a wonderfully creamy delicious meal in a box that's easy to cook and delicious.  Want the kiddo's to eat broccoli then what better way then with mac and cheese.  Putting chicken in it just makes it a wonderful delight any night of the week but sooooooo wonderful on a cold evening dinner when you hanker for something down home good.Affordable price makes this a must have for stretching the buck to feed the family while giving them something that is just darn good.  Protein, carbs and dairy all in one pack that is easy to make.  It's nice to see a company pride itself on what the public will enjoy without cutting corners on quality and flavor.

This was really good. Being a single guy, the easier the meal the better and this was super simple to make and tasted wonderful. If you like Velveeta and Skillet dinners then you will love this. I also tried the cheeseburger flavor and it's great too. I'm glad I tried this product. It makes dinner easy.

column9: I kind of liked it, but I wouldn't recommend it to you.
column10: "When are you going to make that thing?" my friend exlaimed, seeing the yellow box on top of my fridge for the umpteenth time. "It's been there forever - are you ever going to cook it?""Yah I'll get around to it - I just don't like Velveeta.  It's fake."Well, I did finally get around to making this last night.  If you don't want to read any further, I will say I kind of liked it, but I would never recommend it to anyone.I've uploaded some photos as well if you want to check it out.Let's break it down:1) This thing has a packet of Velveeta "cheese".  I know Velveeta is this great american standard that we all grew up with, but that fake cheese stuff has never sat well with me.2) The seasoning packet and "brocolli florets" are a total joke.  The seasoning did nothing for the dish, and the "brocolli florets" were this dark green and BROWN broccoli-DUST.  No flavor whatsoever.3) It doesn't smell very good when you cook it. You fry up unseasoned chicken then boil it with the pasta and "spices" and "broccoli florets" and it just doesn't smell nice.  You dump in that gross cheese sauce at the end, and maybe only then does it smell remotely edible.4) For ease of cooking, I suppose it's OK - it's a one-pan meal.5) This stuff is filling. But wait till it coagulates: it's disgusting.  It firms up into this scary solid cheese-pasta mash.6) It actually tastes OK - it definitely has that american-macaroni-and-cheese thing going for it.  If you like that, then you will like this.------I can't recommend this to you, however. Let's look at a few things.  COST: This box will run you about $3-$5 depending on where you shop. The pound of chicken you need will cost you another what, $5-6?  There are a number of similar dishes in the frozen food section that are about the same price ($8-10) which already have the chicken in them and have actual whole vegetables (not broccoli dust posing as "brocoli florets").  INGREDIENTS: Gross. Check out the label on this one.  Please, do not be fooled: most stuff like this that you buy in the store has all kinds of crazy fake-flavor enhancers and weird colorings that should make it illegal to call it "food".  You could make your own "cheesy skillet" - try actual cheese and actual garlic and actual broccoli.  Too expensive?  Too difficult?  Take a look at your kid's gut and you tell me if it's worth it. Do a little research into "Natural Flavors" and get back to me.------Overall, yeah, I ate it. I had like a third of it for dinner last night and it was strangely addictive.  But at no time do the spices or broccoli come into play.  It's all about the pasta and crummy cheese sauce here, folks.  Even my chicken is an after-thought, containing no flavor of it's own after only being briefly pan fried then boiled to death in this muck.If you like Velveeta, you'll be ok with this. But I don't recommend this to you, and I'll never buy it myself.** UPDATE **The leftovers were totally gross.  I heated them up the next day for lunch and it's like.... just so sad.  Like eating wallpaper paste.  I actually microwaved some frozen broccoli (broccoli florets - real ones!) and mixed them in - it helped immensely but still I would never buy or make this ever again. 2 stars.

The Kraft Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets Dinner overall wasn't bad. The sodium contained in this was much lower than the previous Skillets Dinner I tried, Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheesburger. However, it had sort of a Rice-A-Roni feel to it. Not that it tasted like it but it reminded me of it. I was never really a fan of Rice-A-Roni. That's maybe part of the reason why I wasn't really into to this product. The directions were straight forward and the preparation was simple. Though the pasta was pretty good, I was a bit put off by the somewhat gooey consistency. I followed the directions to a tee so there is nothing that I did to make it come out this way.All and all, this is not something I would buy on a regular basis. There are other, more appetizing choices than this.
We added our chicken and fixed this for dinner.  It was very good.  We don't do pre=packaged food like this very often, but now and then we just need something quick, and a meal like this works fine.

Surprisingly good.Very easy to make, but it did take more watching and stirring than I would have liked. A nice alternative to Hamburger Helper when you need a "desperation dinner."The kit consists of a packet of risotto (a rice shaped pasta), a flavor pack, a pack of freeze-dried broccoli, and a pouch of Velveeta cheese. You provide and brown your own chicken, boil the rice with the flavor packet, add the chicken, add the broccoli (it looks and smells weird out of the pack), and finish by adding the cheese. The final product looks ok (only vaguely reminiscent of vomit), but it tastes and smells good. It did not taste as salty as I had expected (much less salty tasting than Hamburger Helper), but I did feel thirsty after I ate it.You could also make it without the chicken for a vegetarian version, or if you are feeling particularly lazy.

I don't eat anything with cheese and this is no exception. My husband made it for himself, but not without stinking up the entire kitchen with a vile stench. It didn't look much better in the skillet. He ate a plateful, mentioned it was "alright" and we threw the rest away. My  husband loves cheese but I could clearly see that even he would not be purchasing this in the future....

First, I'm not a huge fan of such "instant" meals.  But. . . Having said that. . . Sometimes you're in the mood for something quick-and-easy.  This item is "okay". To make it a little better, adding additional veggies really helps.  The "broccoli florets" are like tiny dried bits of brown paper.  If you have some fresh veggies, I would leave the packet of "broccoli florets" out completely.

column9: We liked it but didn't love it
column10: I made this for myself and two kids (ages 14 and 5).  While we found it ok, we did not love it.  I would classify it as something we would eat but would not request again.  It was cheesy enough but just didn't seem to have any particular outstanding blend of flavor.  We probably won't buy it again unless it's on sale for a really good price.

Doesn't have a good taste, I was super excited when this came out and I was looking forward to the skillets from velveeta as i love their macroonisadly this overly underwhelmed me, the taste is chemical, and the time it takes to make it is quite long.I prefer to just add plain mac & cheese + broccoli and chicken, tastes much better, and is cheaper.avoid it, not as good as it could be, or even should be,never tried the other flavors, proceed at your own risk

column9: Not as good as other Velveeta Skillet products
column10: Probably one of my least favorite of the Velveeta products.  The cheese is good as usual but the broccoli was definitely lacking.

It's hard to come up with something positive about this product. The pasta is tiny nodules shaped like grains of rice; the broccoli is about two tablespoons of grainy black powder that looked like insect parts; the cheese sauce, while fairly tasty, was only remotely cheese-flavored. About the only part of the dish I liked was the chicken, and that was my contribution.This might be a good product to stock in your emergency kit, since you can be sure it'll still be there when the big one hits. If you want cheese, chicken, pasta, and broccoli, buy your own cheese, chicken, and broccoli, and add them to a box of Pasta Roni or some such.

This is a quick and tasty addition to the family pantry, to be used for impromptu meals.  Exquisite it is not, but I have to admit that Velveeta and it's step-sister Cheezwiz are guilty pleasures of mine.  If you have some chicken and need to throw together a meal in a hurry - this is for you.  It is easy as can be to cut up chicken, saute it, and then ad this package.  I must say that more brocoli and larger peices would have made me give this entree another star.

This was okay in a pinch, if you like Velveeta.  The broccoli in the package was very small, almost like some dried herbs.  You'd be better off throwing in some frozen broccoli while cooking this.I tend to make things from scratch, but if you're rushed for time & need to get something on the table, this was acceptable.
This was pretty good, I had to add abit more broccoli and very well seasoned chicken as well as tad bit more cheese....It was ok I have had better but its fine for the occassional quick meal.

column9: A great-tasting dinner entree you can whip up in a few minutes... what's not to like?
column10: The Kraft Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets Dinner Kit I received as part of the Amazon Vine Program resulted in an easy-to-make, hearty, tasty dinner entree.  All I had to do was cut up a few boneless chicken breasts into little pieces, brown them in a skillet, then add the contents of the kit along with some water (the cheese went in last after everything was basically cooked).  I can't say there were multiple subtle nuances in the final dish, but sometimes you just want something that is fast, tasty, and satisfying, especially during the work week. And this dish was all that.As an added bonus, the pound of chicken breasts the kit called for, in conjunction with the pasta, broccoli, and other contents included in the kit, provided more than enough food for my wife and I, with enough left in the fridge later for our daughter when she got home from work. She really enjoyed the whole cheesy chicken and pasta aspect of the whole thing, but then kids always take to Velveeta, so no big surprise there.After enjoying the sample I received, I'd definitely buy this product again at my own expense.  In fact, I already bought a different flavor in this same line by Kraft and Velveeta, one involving ground beef and a cheeseburger/pasta flavor, but that's another review.  And another positive one too.

Simple to put together. A complete dish just add chicken. Great for cheese lovers. Cook the chicken first, then add the rest of the ingredients. Done in no time.  Great way to squeeze in the green vegetable with the kids.

This is a great product. I don't generally like boxed meals, especially a hamburger helper type product. But this tastes great. It is very cheesy and the spices are right on. I hope they make more varieties in the future.

I really liked this dinner because I love broccoli and cheese but the chicken made it really good.  My husband liked it too, and he usually hates broccoli.  Its easy too, which I love and velveeta tastes great with the chicken.  I only wish the pasta noodles were a bit bigger, but they were still great tasting.  I will buy this again.

We've never been fond of most hamburger helper type products and have only used a couple of tuna helper products that we liked.Most of our meals are prepared entirely and do not use kits.We almost always have boneless, skinless chicken in the freezer and love cheesy meals.Like all boxed or canned kits, I always add ingredients and seasoning, but this turned out decent for a kit dinner.It's easy to add some veggies, onions and black pepper to it and make it better.The broccoli in the product was little more than garnish.Like most box meals, it's a base that you need to personal if you want it to look and taste good.

column4: J. Rose "JR From the Ball so Blue"
column10: I added chunked fresh chicken breast to this item; prepared as directed, and voila - a delectable and easy to create main course. I'd recommend it to folks who want convenience food that tastes great.

column9: "Y'know what this risotto needs? Cheez Whiz."
column10: That's what I found myself thinking as I entered into the last phase of cooking this meal. I'd just spent some time fluffing up some yummy, tiny starchy bits of goodness along with some browned chicken breast, steaming in some dehydrated (and some fresh) broccoli, adding in a little spice pack, creating a lovely looking skilletful of creamy goodness.And in my right hand I held a tube of Velveeta cheese. You know the stuff. A bizarre yellow colour that belongs on the cheeks of a clown, not on food. A peculiar unctuousness that one imagines might be similar to that of natural cholesterol. No flavour, just a fatty presence. Dutifully, thinking of you, dear readers, I spooged the stuff into the skillet.The results were less than fantastic. The meal was satisfying, or at least wasn't directly and immediately awful, and my boys gleefully gobbled the stuff up, but I already have plans to make a more natural follow-up to this meal, with a homemade cheese sauce, and I figure it'll cost about the same as this box, be a whole lot healthier, and take only a few minutes more of my time so long as I'm making the sauce and the meal at the same time.

Using this dinner kit really doesn't save you any time in the kitchen. In the same amount of time or less, you could make a simple, delicious and healthy meal from scratch for less money. But since you're actually considering this, I'll tell you that it doesn't taste half bad. You can't really go wrong with all that cheese (or whatever it is) in there.

Kraft Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets is probably not something you want to eat all the time, but for a two day leftover product was not half bad. If your looking for veggie content you'll need to make a side like we did (green beans) because the broccoli exists in name alone and gets lost in the cheesy yellow sea that is the chicken and cheese sauce. It was perfectly tasty stuff though the cheese sauce tends to overwelm the pasta just a little bit. It's actually better on the second heating when all the ingredients have a chance to fully blend together. It's a perfectly acceptable meal, but nothing i'd want on an every month basis.

A cheesy review for a cheesy product.  I rate it 3 not because it is bad, but it is nothing special either.  It is exactly what it says it is, a pasta dish with cheese and broccoli flavor.  Tastes a bit like macaroni and cheese with broccoli and chicken.  Not much else to say about it.

column9: Great to quickly put something together.
column10: I love cheese and broccoli, so I was looking forward to trying this. The cheese was all right, like similar Velveeta products I had in the past, but the broccoli was so little that I supposed is for the garnish only. The pasta shells are so small that for a moment I thought it was rice. It looks like it. It took less than half an hour to be ready, and it tasted good enough, to be served as a quick dinner in a day one gets home late. I will buy it if I see it on sale.

If you're looking for healthy, typically stay away from Velveeta products.  However, if you're looking for something hearty & filling, Velveeta usually does well.At $15 on Amazon for six packs, the price on this is better than most of the inferior Hamburger/Cheeseburger Helper boxed foods.  The quality of the product is quite good.  Make sure you have a big enough pan/skillet to contain the chicken breasts and all the boxed products.  I have a rather large skillet and that barely kept in all the food.

This is not the type of food I ever buy - I rarely buy packaged, processed, ready to make kits. And, if I make pasta, it's Ezekiel's sprouted grain pasta. But, I saw this available through Vine, and I decided to try it because I travel a lot and figured it may be something my family can make without too much trouble when I am away. I have to say, it was pretty good.Two of my kids were home the night I made dinner and the 10 year old and 17 year old really liked this. I did not use the broccoli included in the package, and instead sprinkled some fresh broccoli on top. The packaged broccoli looked awful; it was dried, crumbly, and small. It barely resembled broccoli and I was afraid it would just taste nasty and ruin the dish. I also added cold grilled chicken breast slices and stirred them in when the dish was hot so the cheese and pasta warmed up the chicken pieces just enough.The cheese is processed, but overall it didn't taste like it. And, the sodium content was not nearly as high as I expected. My 10 year old LOVED the meal and wants it again.  This really surprised me and it's a great thing to have in the cabinet for emergency dinners.

column9: I will get them again, but I would add more of my own broccoli
column10: I really enjoyed this, but I would have preferred more broccoli. The seasonings mixed with the cheese sauce, tiny pasta, and a hint of broccoli is very tasty. My only complaint about it is that there is so little broccoli. I'm assuming this has something to do with them being dried out and put into a little tiny packet. Still the flavor is there and enjoyable. Next time I'll just add my own additional broccoli.Don't confuse this with velveeta shells and cheese. This doesn't taste the same. There is seasoning that is part of the kit that gives it a very different flavor that Velveeta Shells and cheese.

column9: Okay, but tastes synthetic to me. Has partially hydrogenated oil.
column10: Kids liked it, but I thought that this skillet meal tasted rather sythetic.  The cheese was rather overwhelming and broccoli was barely there.  Also, it is rather old school in that it contains partially hydrogentaed oils.  Ok for a quick meal in a pinch, but I can't see eating this too frequently.

We got this and it was delicious.... Even my picky grandson ate it and he hates everything. So easy to make and such a great taste. This is a really tasty meal that you can make when you are short on time :)

My family was not impressed with this dish. I wasn't expecting it to taste like homemade, but I really was expecting it to taste better than it did. With the names Kraft and Velveeta on it I expected it to be somewhat better than generic boxed mac-and-cheese, but that's about what it was like. The box does not come with chicken, so it's not really what I would call a "dinner kit." The broccoli amounted to tiny green flecks that we couldn't really taste. Overall, it was edible, but that's about it. I wanted to like it, but I'm sorry. I won't be buying this for my family.

I love Velveeta shells and cheese, so I fully expected to enjoy this meal.  First of all, it doesn't come with chicken, you need to add your own... which I kind of expected.  So I cooked up my chicken and started tearing open the packages as the box directed.  I actually made this according to the instructions (normally I use instructions as suggestions).First of all, this doesn't really taste like the shells and cheese pasta I was expecting - far more bland.Second - The broccoli was like eating hamster food - it didn't rehydrate and was basically like running across the stray leaf or twig in your meal.B - the pasta was shaped like Orzo - which for some reason was just weird - perhaps if they had been spirals they would have held the cheese better or something.The best part of the meal was the chicken I had made... I wish now that I had blackened it to add flavor to this completely bland boring meal.Final decision - this required more work than many other skillet meals I have made and though I can't say it tasted bad... it certainly isn't something I'll buy again.  I guess if you like eating glue with sticks in it, this is the skillet meal for you.

I received my order of 16 vanilla beans in only 3 days from order placed to placement in my mailbox.  I am hoping to make homemade vanilla extract.  The beans were so soft and pliable to work with.  The aroma was incredible.  Hopefully this will make great extract.
This product was everything I wanted in order to make various dishes such asbread pudding or christmas cake or just an ordinary fruit cake.

I have eaten many brands of soynuts over the years and have come to enjoy the ones that are crunchy (as opposed to hard). I bought this bulk package because my trips to Whole Foods are a bit spread out. Many of the soynuts in this product are extremely hard to eat, and I end up spitting them out. The ones that are good are usually just fine, but it is disappointing to find so many inedible soynuts in a package. I think I will stick to Whole Foods 365 brand.

These soy nuts are very hard - not crunchy in a good way. We ordered these in bulk to save money vs. buying single bags at the grocery store. Not really saving much and they aren't as good. So, we will not be reordering when these are gone.

I love these soy nuts! Nothing but the natural soy roasted into a great nutritious snack! Great for those you are looking for something crunchy like nuts or chips but are allergic to nuts or who want something healthier. Good for those who want a light snack to fuel them during the day!

This stuff is simply crack for cats.All my cats are addicted to it so I use it as treats, and the big bag goes a looooong way if you only give them a few kibbles at a time like candy. I've turned friends on to this stuff and it's always the same thing - their cats go crazy over it.I wouldn't recommend to use it as a regular food because it's very fattening and you'll wind up with lazy jumbokitties that take up all the couch space.

I thought that one of my cats was just going to have a dry coat that wasn't very nice looking. After about 1/2 of a bag of this his coat became shiny and soft. Now he's just gorgeous. While my cats don't act like this is kitty crack, they seem to like it, and eat it just as they should without overeating. The price is great and I'm really happy that I found the right food for my cats.

column9: Must be tasty because he's eating it!
column10: I like Premium Edge Dry Food for Adult Cats - Finicky Cat Chicken, Salmon and Vegetables Formula for three reasons:1. The ingredients are all high quality sources of protein and vitamins.2. The great pricing for a quality formulation.3. Did I mention he likes it!!!
I have 5 cats that enjoy feeding time. They have had several brands of dry cat food and seem to really like this one and Chicken Soup For The Cat Lovers Soul.

column9: Puts Cream of Wheat to Shame
column10: Like a lot of people, I grew up on hot cereals and old-fashioned Cream of Wheat in particular.Graduate to something WAY better:  Cream of the West Roasted Wheat.  This is a whole grain product, not just the starchy farina part of the wheat.  It's better nutrition and digests very well.Easy to stove-top cook, give it a vigorous boil to bring out the flavor.  Microwaves well, too.  Highly recommended.

column9: Like Cream of Wheat but with FIBER!
column10: I love hot cereal for breakfast, and I've always liked Cream of Wheat but it has almost no fiber in it- 1 gram. Cream of the West has 6 grams of fiber per serving however, and tastes even BETTER. It has a nutty, hearty, delicious flavor but a very creamy texture. You can microwave it in 3 minutes and it doesn't get all those nasty lumps like in C of W, it's so easy! I like to add just a little salt and a dash of cream and it's a scumptious, filling, and healthy breakfast for both children and adults. I love it!

This is the best tasting hot cereal around.  It has a nutty flavor and my body craves it.  Don't over cook it or let it get too thick, just bring the water to a boil, stir in the cereal and take it off of the heat and it will thicken up on its own.  A dab of butter and a little bit of sugar or erythritol sprinkled on top and you have a good breakfast side.  I wish I could roast my own wheat and get the same flavor, but I have not had any luck with experimenting recipes.  I can't find it at the grocery store on a regular basis for some reason, so when it is in, I purchase all they get in and store it in the freezer to keep it fresh and weevil free.  I would love to get this from Amazon, but almost $10 in shipping is ridiculous.  If this ever goes on super saver shipping, I am a customer.  Until then, it will be hit and miss when I can find it on the grocery shelf.

The product is excellent.  I have been buying it for several years, first at Whole Foods, and then when they dropped the product, I have been purchasing it online.The price has been going up CONSIDERABLY.  I purchase 36 jars per order to save on shipping.  With each order there is always another price increase.My recent order of September 2012 for 36 jars was apparently packed at the warehouse and sent to the store.  The store did not repack it.  Each box of six was sealed with warehouse tape identifying the item.  It stated the name of the store it was shipped to as well as the flavor.  The following information shocked me, and I quote:RIGONI FRUIT SPRD  8.82 OZ  Pack  6  Retail  5.99Did you note the price?  Retail 5.99!!!!  It did not state wholesale, it said RETAIL PRICE.  No one sells it for 5.99, yet the warehouse stipulates that is the retail price.  Am I missing something here?  I guess it is a matter of what the market will bear.....OUTRAGEOUS!  Perhaps on principal alone I will give up on this product.  The GREED is beyond comprehension.

This product is great for people on who eat plant-based, whole foods.  There is no sugar added.  The product tastes delicious.  The price, however, is quite expensive for the size of the jar.  I found a similar product at a local whole-foods grocery store for half the price.

column4: Phyllis L. Fischer "church of the angels"
column10: i, a mere human, do little more than serve up this product to the queen of cats in the household- her rule over her loyal subjects is fair and just, and she earns her treats by being kind to humans (only certain humans tho- do not ask her about the vet unless you want the air blue with curses)this product is well packaged, and if you wait for amazon sales it can be acquired for less, but please do not tell the queen cat i bought her anything on sale- she pays full price and tips the clerk.

My cats do not like pate style cat food.  Thus, they enjoy Fancy Feast in all varieties except "Classic".  They really enjoy little pieces, be they grilled or shredded, in gravy.This was promoted as:Delicious melding of filet mignon and seafood flavorsDelicious and enchanting shapes made with real seafoodEnchanting shapes made with the delicious taste of real chicken and turkeyHowever, there were no enchanting shapes, just the Classic can shaped pate. So it was disappointing.  No where does it say this is Classic.Also, it comes in three seafood varieties. I don't see where the filet mignon, chicken and turkey flavors come in.

I can't really properly review this stuff from my own personal perspective since I don't eat cat food (well not yet anyway).  But I will say that my cats love it and I guess that's the test, huh?  My cats have always been very partial to Fancy Feast so I give it to them as a treat.  I also have to mix a little into their vet prescribed food (which they DON'T like) to make it palatable for them.  They'll eat pretty much any wet food the vet prescribes as long as I mix in a bit of Fancy Feast - without it they just turn up their noses and won't eat it.I get the food by subscription with free shipping so I always have some on hand.  It's easy and convenient and I love having it delivered right to my door.I rate this food and the subscription service with five Meows.

column9: Not what I expected, but not sure who goofed
column10: I thought I had ordered a chicken and beef mixture but got seafood.  Not sure if the mistake was mine or the distributors.  The cat food did arrive relatively promptly and is as expected.  My cat likes it.

Normally, I have no qualms about ordering from AMAZON ... but, not this time.  I specifically wanted Fancy Feast with the Liver flavored food; because, I'm unable to find it in my area. I also had ordered the brown box of food, which again, was the type that I am unable to buy in my area.  Instead, they sent me what they wanted me to have - WHAT A DISAPPOINTMENT!! What they sent, I could have easily bought at Sam's for a much cheaper price and more cans in the box; i.e., 36 cans for $16.00 ... but, I wanted to try these new flavors for my 3 wonderful children who love their Fancy Feast ... I'll keep what I have but will NOT consider ordering cat food again from AMAZON ...
My cats love this food.I've bought it for years and it does not upset their stomachs.It smells almost good enough to eat!
My cat really likes this one. Likes the extra gravy ones the best. They use meat by-products in their food.  Up to you.

In this economy, I'm glad I found something that tastes good and fills you up for a low price. Maybe when the economy improves I'll be able to afford the diced kind i gravy. I think it would taste even better. It easy open can makes it perfect for snacks on the go, and easy lunch at work. What a great product!OK I was just joking, but seriously though.My cats love this stuff! My older cat who is about 15 years old begs for this every morning like clockwork. He knows my schedule and will meow at the shower knowing it's time for his canned food the minute I get out. I can only assume it must be good since it appears to be the highlight of my cat's day.I'm very careful about what food I give my cats after the issue with the contaminated off-brand food almost killed one of my cats several years ago. I could buy cheaper cat food, but it's not worth the gamble.My cat's like it, and it's reasonably priced here on Amazon.
My 4 Cats lick their platters clean when I serve them Fancy Feast.  Not so with most other brands.  This item definitely gets 5 Happy Cat Stars.  {:^)

Our cats lick the plates clean when fed any kind of Fancy Feast.  Buying it on amazon on the subscription plan is the only way we buy Fancy Feast due to the price.  4 stars instead of 5 just because of the price.  Wish they'd either put it in bigger cans or lower the price per can.  Your cats will love you for it.
The Fancy Feast arrived very quickly, in perfect shape and the cats loved it.  I can't always find this variety where I live in Atlanta!
I can't speak from personal experience, but my four cats prefer Fancy Feast over other brands of cat food.  They like "grilled" "classic" and the shredded "elegant medleys."
This is a good value, we save even more with scheduled monthly delivery. Really helps with a 4 cat family! Saves us about $2.00 over chain stores.

Fancy Feast is always a good product.  The food is fresh without ever smelling catfoodish.  The critters love it. It is a wee bit more expensive getting it through the mail than it is from the grocery store but it is worth not having to deal with the bulky boxes.

Naturally, liking or not liking a particular food product is a matter of personal taste. I happen to like this particular Russian dressing better than any other I've tasted. It's very flavorful, but not too sweet. It does not overwhelm the salad. I also find it better than Thousand Island, which is close in taste.

column9: I love these and I'm back to order more!
column10: I was a little nervous because these were so much cheaper per pound than many other chocolate coffee beans I had seen.  However, the price was so good, I went ahead and took the chance.  They are wonderful and very addictive.  My brother-in-law loves chocolate covered coffee beans too, so I'm going to pick up an extra bag as a gift for him!I did create a litle problem for myself:  I was snacking on these at night and wondering why I was suddenly having trouble getting to sleep.  :-)

As others have reported, these are wonderful and it's hard to eat just a few, which of course is what one should do. (Although the reported serving size is 1/4 cup, so go for it!)The label says: "Hand picked real Hawaiian Kona coffee beans dipped in dark chocolate."Ingredients (because I was wondering, before ordering): Semisweet chocolate [contains sugar, chocolate liquor, cocoa butter, soy lecithin (an emulsifier), vanilla], Kona coffee beans, natural cocoa powder, confectioner's glaze, gum arabic, natural & artificial flavors.They are marked with the Kosher K / pareve symbol.The chocolate and the bean are both good to my mind, and the proportion of the two as well. These are just what I was hoping for, in all their dangerous goodness.There are a LOT of beans here, too. I filled almost 5 24oz mason jars with this 5-lb. bag. (Yes, I know that doesn't add up... the difference between an ounce as a weight and an ounce as a volume... It's over 14 cups.)

Love these!Too bad they're unavailable now, but when I bought my bag, I found these to be fresher than the competition and appropriately priced.  They are a little more spendy, but boy do they taste amazing!The dark chocolate on the outside is smooth and bitter-sweet; going very well with the bitter espresso bean inside.  The bean itself isn't very acidic so it doesn't take away from the overall flavors.If this comes back.  BUY IT.

column9: Excellent item for a great price
column10: I ordered this item for my wife for christmas, she had been wanting some chocolate covered beans for a few months. We had seen some at different places but the price was usually over $1.00 an ounce. So when I found these on Amazon for $38 for 5 pounds I decided to give them a try. We were both very pleasantly surprised by not just the quality of the item, especially since it was in 5 lb bulk bag but also the flavor of the dark chocolate and the Kona bean together. It was a perfect combination. I would definitely recommend this item to anyone, and I plan to buy more very soon as we are down to our last pound.

I have tried many different brands of choco covered espresso beans, from amazon to the local coffee shops.These are far superior to any I have tried to date.  There is only a small amount of dark chocolate (which is what I like, less calories more caffeine) and the espresso bean has a great taste basically the bean melts in your mouth.I say this as I have tried some where the bean is like eating bark or some have so much chocolate covering them you can barely find the bean so you feel sick before you get the desired pick me up from the caffeine, so this is a refreshing change as the bean to choco ratio is perfect..These are pretty spendy but in the long run well worth it since you only need a couple beans to perk you up vs the other brands that are out there... will be buying again:)

column9: Really Delicious Dark Chocolate Covered Coffee
column10: I'd had chocolate covered espresso beans and liked them.  They were really strong, though, and I had to watch how many I ate or I'd get a real buzz.  I really like the flavor of these better, and the strength is just right!  I'm definitely buying these again!

column9: Great taste but a little pricey now
column10: Great product, great taste.  Just couldn't find the great price as I ordered in April 2011.  It was $38 with free shipping by then.  :-(  Will definately buy again with the same old price, not the price in 2012 $50+ plus shipping.

I wasn't quite sure what to expect when I ordered these chocolate covered coffee beans, but WOW they are really good.  The chocolate is very tasteful and the coffee bean in what I had hoped for!!  The price was not bad at all either.  I decided to purchase these when I went to a local cafe to buy chocolate covered coffee beans and they no longer sold them.  The Koppers are much better than the local cafe had!!!  I will be buying them again.  They will make wonderful gifts!!!
These little devils are so addictive.  You just can't stop after a handful.  They are right next to M&M's.  This is a very good bargain.
Yummy! I can't believe its 5lbs, I had to give some away there's so much! I personally wouldn't have purchased this at the retail price, but had to jump on it during Amazon's 50% off chocolates sale!

I was on a ferry from Seattle to Victoria and the waters got rough and the crew started passing these around.  I was skeptical, but tried them and found that while my stomach was a little uneasy, I was certainly not as sick as I had been in similar experiences in the past.  I was still skeptical as to whether it was the ginger that helped or if, maybe, I had just outgrown sea sickness, but a couple of months later when I went whale watching, I realized that I had definitely not outgrown it.  So, when my family came to visit and we decided to go to Disneyland, I decided to buy this candy.  A lot of the rides make me queasy and can send me to the sidelines for 15 - 30 minutes - way too long for kids to sit around and wait.  Anyway, I found this candy really did help.  I had a piece about every hour and then also immediately before and after a fast/crazy ride.  It wasn't as though the motion sickness was completely eliminated, but it was greatly diminished.  I went from being sick to being a little uneasy - and it definitely didn't last long.  I didn't need to sit down at all, I just kept going and a few minutes later, I was completely back to normal.BTW - these don't taste bad, especially after you've had a few. They are different tasting enough that your kids probably won't be bugging you for a piece all the time, which is a bonus.

I ordered these for help with my "morning" sickness.  I overlooked that these were not the hard candy version that I've used in the past, but I still like them even though they're chewy and don't last as long.

I got some of these and some of the less intense ginger candy. I like this one better than the less intense. Some of the little packages wrapped around each piece of candy are a bit hard to get open, but most opened well. I carry some with me in my purse now!

This is a strong, smoky coffee that can make you feel like a sophisticated coffee snob in the morning. It's smooth, rich, and velvety, and I always feel like a genius after brewing it, like, 'yeah, I just brewed this and it's so good. I am a coffee master.' That being said, it's almost a tad too strong for me - but I tend to prefer medium roasts. If you're looking for a strong coffee, I'd recommend checking this out.

column9: One of the best kcups out there
column10: I found this to be one of the best kcups available.  The Colombia has flavor typical of a coffee chain's brewed coffee- bold, lots of subtle flavors, not bitter, smooth, etc. Type "Colombia barista prima" into Google for detailed tasting notes from other folks.  I REALLY enjoyed it and will be purchasing the largest box possible for my next order.

column9: Finally, a coffee that makes K-cups worth converting to!
column10: When I recently started using K-cups, wasn't sure that the quality or the intensity would be up to par.  I wound up trying many of the standard k-cups which for the most part were ok but not great.  The Barista Prima French Roast is well worth trying.  Very intense and flavorful. No more concerns about throwing away my old coffee pot.

WHILE BARISTA ITALIAN ROAST COFFEE IS A BIT PRICIER THAN MOST OF THE KEURIG'S STYLE COFFEES, IT HAS A GREAT RICH FLAVOR AND IS WORTH IT.BY ACCIDENT, I RAN A SECOND CUP OF WATER THROUGH THE KEURIG ON A PREVIOUSLY USED K-CUP.  THE COFFEE WAS STILL RICH AND YUMMY.  SINCE THEN I HAVE DISCOVERED THAT I CAN GET AT LEAST TWO SERVINGS PER EACH K-CUP.

I've tried a lot of KCups, looking for the fresh, dark, really rich espresso-roast flavor that I love; all of them seemed weak and/or flatly bitter compared to my dark beans-by-the-pound favorites. I'm almost a coffee snob and only bought the Keurig because my mornings are just too rushed, sort of a shocking decision. I love the convenience of the machine, but it was like grabbing a cup at the convenience store taste-wise - just the required morning medication, eh.So I was really, really surprised and delighted when I discovered this one. I hear they pack the Barista blends with more coffee - that does seem to be the case, they're plump little cuppies.And wow, a real espresso taste, zero acidity, darkly fruity and full-bodied, and for once not tasting watered down. If you don't like espresso you won't like it, especially neat. But with half and half and sugar this one's really wonderful, too.  Love it, love it.

I have to say the new offerings are great. the french roast and the Italian roast have a nice strong coffee flavor. I would say remember your first cup out of a keurig, the reason you bought a machine, these two flavors remind me of that.Those first few lines are from my review for the Italian roast, they are both excellent.

column9: Bold But Not Rocket Fuel Bold.  Nice, Smooth Flavor.
column10: This Barista Prima kcup is my favorite of the four Barista Prima varieties that I've tried (House Blend, Columbian, Italian Rost & French Roast).  It has a nice dark, moderately bold flavor that creates a smooth wake-me-up in the morning.  There is no kick to it - just a even, enjoyable experience.My coffee preferences are medium-bold blends.  I brew a 10oz cup & this coffee maintains its flavor in this size cup.This is a kcup that I would put on my shelves.  Recommended.Disclosure:  I received this kcup in a sample variety pack sent our by Keurig to its customers.

I love a high quality French roast. Since I was in college, coming home to visit my parents and drinking my mom's amazing coffee has never been beat by my Keurig.  Until now.  I love it.  It's super rich and flavorful.  It's not overly dark and there is no burnt taste like "other" coffees (you know who I'm talking about).  This is truly a lovely coffee.

I've been a Timothy's Rainforest Espresso fan for a couple of years now but this coffee is giving it a run for the money (well not really because it's overpriced).I delayed purchasing it (I have a $.50/cup limit and Barista runs twice that) until I found it on sale. Having used Keurig pots since they first came out a decade ago and having tried about 80 flavors, I find myself choosing this one over the Rainforest for my first cup each morning.  It's flavor is bolder and clearer than Rainforest and seems more satisfying.  We have a house full of guests now and the carousel has dozens of different coffees on it but the Barista coffees are the ones I keep having to refill.Still I ding it one star because of price.8/12 - found them for $.60 a k-cup (box of 96).  Bought two boxes which will last me two months.  Love this coffee.10/12 - Been drinking Barista Italian for 10 months now and have tried over a dozen new options in the interim.  None came close to the robustness of this coffee.

Got this in a K Cup sampler, definitely on my reorder list.  Very smooth, no bitter after taste, dark coffee.  So far one of the best, tied with Caribou Mahogany.  If you like good strong coffee with out the bitter after taste, this K Cup is perfect.
Absolutely the best French Roast k-cup I've had so far.  Rich, bold and satisfying.  A little pricey but worth it.

column9: Best dark roast k-cup by far
column10: I am pretty picky when it comes to my coffee.  Tried just about everything.  Can not stand the weak blends and only like dark roasts (extra bold).  Used to drink Timothy's Parisian Nights, Midnight Magic and Green Mountains Dark Magic on medium water selection to get a strong enough brew, but now Barista Prima French Roast ONLY, on the large water setting.  Even with extra water it is perfect.  Little pricier than some of the others, but it is worth it, plus I get a full cup of coffee now when I brew on the large water setting.  I should also mention I only use filtered water when I brew my coffee, makes a huge difference.  Filtered water and a Barista Prima French Roast K-cup and it will by far blow everything else out of the water.  Nothing else compares.  If you like a really dark, smooth, flavorful coffee, you must try this.  You will not be disappointed.  But keep in mind, this is only for people who truly like the darkest roast (i.e. I think it curls my hair). Serious coffee drinkers only!

column9: Good Coffee for a Designer Coffee
column10: I have gradually come to realize good coffee doesn't have to bite your head off. People have been convinced that the more your socks curl, the better it is. This is a pretty mellow but substantial brew. It doesn't have the hardcore after taste and isn't bitter. No fruity or whatever else descriptors. It's just a good basic cup of coffee for the average person. Basic is what I'm looking for in the morning.

One of the best k-cups we've had.  If you miss the way starbucks tasted on the Tassimo, this is the closest thing you will find in the k-cup world.  Coffee was great and the price was very good too.  Super saver shipping took FOREVER.  They sat on the order for a week before even shipping it and then it was another 4 days to get to us.  I actually had to go out and buy a box before this arrived which was what I was trying to avoid by ordering it online.  Used to order all my coffee online from Amazon before they dumbed down the free shipping.  Now, not so much.
This is one of the best K cups out there. Nice bold flavor.No bitter after taste. If you want a bold K cup try this!

Amazon seems to have combined the reviews for three different products here, Italian, French, and Columbian. I picked up a box of the Italian Roast at the grocery, and I really like it. It is strong and full flavored without bitterness. For hot coffee, I make the larger size cup, and the smaller for iced coffee. I checked Amazon to see if I could save money, but it looks like the same price I paid at the store ($9.99 for a box of 12).

column9: bitter hot, but great for iced
column10: At first I thought I had wasted my money. I hated this coffee. It is very bitter. Then I had a great idea...use it for iced coffee.  I brew it for a medium cup. Fill a tall glass with ice. Fill glass 1/3 full with milk. Add your favorite creamer. Add coffee and stir. So if you hate this coffee hot, try it cold.
This is my favorite of all of the bold coffees. No bitterness at all. Just very smooth and delicious. I was very surprised to see that it is a product of Green Mountain.

Some time back I ran into an offer of free samples of Barista Prima Coffeehouse Coffee.  When the samples arrived, I fell in love with the brand.  It's rich and delicious.  Now, it's what I use on a regular basis.  Had I not had the samples, I would never have known that this brand I had never heard of would be a stand-out.  It's just a great product for people who love a rich, full-bodied coffee.

This is my favorite k cup, and I've tried alot of them!  Love the smoky flavorl  I recommend you buy it straight from Keruig, as a member (which is free) you can get a box of 24 for 17.24.  I always order 3 boxes at a time and get free shipping.  Also like the Italian roast, but is a bit stronger and, I think, harsher flavor.  Where ever you end up buying Prima French Roast, you'll come back for more!

This is my favorite brew by far. I have always been a french roast fan because I just love the flavor of coffee. This delivers that bold, rich taste without tasting "strong." It's smooth with no hint of bitterness at all. If you love the flavor of coffee, give this a try.However, it's much cheaper at Walmart. I buy 18 K-cups for $13 there. I wouldn't pay the prices here.

My wife is a coffee snob ( she calls herself that too) and we have browsed Amazon for K cups for  a couple years, We must have purchased every dark French Roast there is. All the coffee was good but just was not "it" until we ordered this coffee. Finally a coffee dark, bold enough yet smooth and not bitter. She even runs it thru the machine twice and still gets a good cup of coffee. May cost a little more than others we have purchased but well worth it. Now when re-ordering I can just go to my last coffe order and re-order same. Simple, quick and satisfing. Plus it has a cool picture of the Eifle Tower on the box.
This is by far the best K-cup coffee I have tasted. Has a big bold taste with lots of flavor. Unfortunately the price is too high so will only buy on special occasions.

I was so disappointed in this coffee. I guess I was fooled by the "Oooh it's more expensive than the others, there must be something special to it! I have to try it once!"I never get taken in by price!! There was absolutely nothing to it that was any better than other K cups from other brands that sell Colombian coffee. Don't waste your money on it, not worth it...

This was just not my cup of tea - er, I mean coffee (har har). It had a sharp, acrid taste to it, and left a bitter aftertaste. I'm not a coffee connosisseur by any means, but I know what I like and I know what I don't like, and I don't like this. I would not recommend it, especially with so many other Keurig coffee options.

column9: Advertised as Medium-Bold, but more Medium than Bold.  Slightly Bitter, but Not Harsh.
column10: This Columbia Blend leans more to the medium side than the bold side of coffee.  However, there is a slight kick to it, so solid medium coffee drinkers may want to take a pass.The blend is also slightly bitter, but not so bitter that it would be considered a harsh taste.  The bitter can be toned down by milk, which would leave no significant aftertaste.I would put this kcup in the same category as Caribou Coffee, Caribou Blend, 24-Count K-Cups for Keurig Brewers, although I would choose this Barista Prima Columbia blend over the Caribou Blend.This is an OK blend, but there are better coffee blends on the market.Disclosure: I received this kcup in a free sample pack mailed by Keurig to its customers.
Not bad, and perfectly drinkable, but bland with no liqueur. Not as bitter as some Columbians I have had, but that, unfortunately, goes back to the 'bland' bit.

This coffee was substituted for a coffee I had ordered in a coffee club. It was $4.00 more than what I usually get and like. It was bitter(harsh) and strong. I thought it was terrible. Quit the coffee club and would not order this again.
It's too bitter (read: over-roasted), but a pinch of salt calms it down nicely, and it does have a good full flavor which, again, would be more noticeable if it weren't so burnt.

column9: Medium to Bold, but Not Real Bold.  Bitter with a Distinct Aftertaste.
column10: This Barista Prima Italian roast is suppose to be full bodied with a sweet edge.  It is not.  It is Medium-Bold (not extra bold), and has a bitter taste and a distinct aftertaste.  Milk & sugar help, but the bitter and aftertaste are still there.Tully's Coffee Italian Roast, 24-Count K-Cups for Keurig Brewers (Pack of 2) is a much better choice if you want a good Italian blend.Disclosure: I received this kcup in a free sample pack mailed by Keurig to its customers.

Got this k-cup in a selection that came with my new Keurig. I usually make the small, 6 oz. cup. The resulting brew was so bitter and acrid that is was undrinkable... not just bad. Thinking that I must have done something wrong I tried again.....this time making a 12 ouncer......absolutely no difference. It tasted distinctly burnt! I was very disappointed as I like strong coffee and, usually, Italian style roast is my favorite. I would give this one a pass.......

column9: really tasty, nicely crunchy, NO GLUTEN, low in sugar, high fiber with protein...and 180 calories!
column10: If you're one of those folks who craves chocolate bars with some protein as a snack or dessert or on-the-go emergency mini-meal, and you need no gluten, and you want it to taste nice, and you don't want a lot of sugars, and you do not mind soy (this has both soy and whey isolates), this is a nice option.I can't have a lot of soy. But sometimes, ah, well, I will give in--for some grilled tofu or some tofu red curry or nice miso soup.
