The noodles are thicker, which means that you can cook them to the right degree (just until firm, not mushy) MUCH more easily than other brands of American noodle. It's really not that spicy, just enough to clear up your sinuses, and it's not a spicy-for-the-sake-of-it kind of spicy, it's really quite full of deep flavors. I prepare it as per the directions on the packaging except I reduce cook time by 25-30 seconds and, when they're done, I crack one or two eggs into the pot after I bring it off the burner. The residual heat in the pot is more than enough to cook the egg, you just have to remember to break up the yolk and stir the egg around the pot. It helps to thicken the soup as well, which means it tends to stick to the noodles much better.Overall, the noodles are quite delicious, and the best American-made noodle I've ever had. I definitely recommend them.
My family like  all kind of Ramyun. I like spicy but my children doesn't.But this Rymyun my chuildren like very much. All family enjoy Shin Ramyun.

I ordered these noodles based on a previous review.  Indeed they are much better than the ones found in grocery stores.  The spicey picante is the perfect flavor and not reach-for-a-glass-of-water hot.  I enjoyed these very much and will order again.
Off all of the different types of Ramen that I have had this is the best thus far.  I highly recommend to any who enjoys Ramen and spicy foods.
I am gonna buy this again for the future for myself, when I ate this completely. Thank you so much for this product in Amazon.com.

I love these noodles so much. They are the perfect winter comfort food. I only use half of the seasoning packet, so it's not too spicy. Also try cracking an egg in the soup, mix in some mushrooms and other vegetables. So yummy!

column9: Ramen noodle with a spicy kick!
column10: This is like Ramen noodle soup but with a spicy kick.-You can control how spicy the broth is by adding less or all of the seasoning pack.I found adding the "vegetable" pack doesn't really add or take away from the flavoring.On a side note the package says to boil 19.5 fluid ounces of water. This converts approximately to 2-1/2 cups of water.I would rate this product:4 out of 5 for TASTE.3 out of 5 for VALUE.5 out of 5 for being made in the USA!Nong Shim Shin Noodle Ramyun is $17.9920 which comes out to be .90 centspackage.Maruchan Ramen Noodle Soup is $15.9736 which comes out to be .44 centspackage.Seems like Nong Shim can be more price competitive.Overall though I am likely to order again.
Have had other brands...this by far is the best one out there.  Not your typical 10 for 1 dollar grocery store noodle.  Spicy and refreshing....great for hangovers!
I love cooking this in between meals and they are delicious. They are just a little bit too hot for me. Overall I recommend this product.

I tried this in college, from some friends overseas...have trouble finding it now, but when I do I buy the store out. It's great on it's own, but I add as much dehydrated veggies(from Central Market) as I can and you've got yourself a meal...not just "ramen."
Shin Ramyun is very classic Korean Ramyun. It is spicy too. I recomment to put less soup base because it contains lots of sodium.

The spice packets that come with the noodles are NOT spicy at all. I'm guessing the flavor packets were dulled to appeal more to American tastes, but they definitely are not on the same level as what I'm used to. Very disappointed. With the normal noodles, I could only use half a packet or risk burning off my taste buds, with these a full packet barely tingles my tongue. With the cold weather coming up I was really looking forward to bowls of hot spicy noodles, now I have to make do with the dulled down versions.

My roommate in college used to buy the Nong Shim Shin Cups and I loved them a lot, but didn't want to cook in Styrofoam every day.  These noodles are soooo good, but beware, they contain MSG.  I think everything is ok in moderation, and really love the taste of these noodles.  Sometimes I buy beef or chicken stock, and cook the noodles in that instead of the soup flavor pack included.

Mashithhaa !!Tried this when stationed in Korea on a "remote" tour for one year (first of two times... remote being you couldn't bring your family). I have been hooked on this ever since. My friend and I survived on this and Goobers peanut butter and jelly (the one where both are in the same jar) sandwiches!! Love the spiciness first of all, and the noodles are bigger and tastier than the 20 cent americanized brands. I have tried many additions to this such as: mixed vegetables, tuna fish (uh.. not with mayo), hot dogs, mushrooms, olives (black and/or green), pickles, hot pepper rings. No, I never put hot dogs, eggs, or tuna together... ugh!When I was stationed in Korea there was some smaller restaurants around the bases that would serve Cheese'Ramien. they cooked the noodles and added the spice packets. Then they would drain the water (some of the spiciness was left behind in the noodles) then right away added cheese to the steaming hot noodles in a bowl and mixed. Voila! Cheese Ramien... Korean style.I am retired from active duty military now but the commisaries (on base grocery stores) stock this item and I have been eating it probably at least once a week ever since that first Korean tour 20 years ago. Chajamyun/g (ja ja myun) is also awesome !! They make an instant version of that also, not spicy, but made with a black bean powder.Korean food ROCKS !!By the way, it's cheaper in the Military Commisary too.

Nong Shim and this flavor especially (love the heat and spiciness) is by far the best ramen I've tasted. Introduced to me by a Japanese friend, I've been hooked on this brand ever since, This is not like any of those 5/$1 ramen packs you see in every grocery store - this is a real ramen noodle.Highly recommended - but spicy - so beware!

column9: Not your everyday ramen (but it should be!)
column10: I first picked up Nong Shim Shin Noodle Ramyun in a local Asian Specialty store near my office. I needed a cheap lunch and this was my choice.  Since that day I continued to buy it a couple packages at a time to keep at work for those days when I don't have a lunch planned. Now though I have an entire case because Amazon had such a great price. It's easy to cook up in the microwave and very filling. The one change I make is that I only use about 1/2 the seasoning pack, any more and it's too spicy for me to finish the entire bowl. Also I'm one of those "picky" people that doesn't like mushrooms and there are usually a couple small dried pieces in the vegetable pack that I pick out.  Minor I know, BUT if you don't like mushrooms it's something you should know.While I still buy the "other" ramen for home because my kids like it, Nong Shim has won me over with theirs and it's my treat to myself.

I love these noodles.  The quality is a cut above cup-o-noodles.  However, if you use the entire seasoning package they will be too spicy for most Americans.  Fortunately, you do not have to add all of the seasoning.  So most people who like spicy food should be able to enjoy these.  I will watch the sales and buy them again.
I am Korean and I have tried hundreds of different kinds of Ramyun. This is always the best.Shin Ramyun is the best selling even in Korea too.

I like this Shin noodle very much I couldn't find this kind of instant noodle after I moved to where I live now, so I purchased this online. It taste just like the one I used to have. A friendly reminder, it is very spicy.

column9: By far the best Ramen I've had
column10: I admit it.  I love Ramen noodles.  I ate enough of them in college where they became a part of me.  I regularly still buy Ramen noodles just because I like them.  I saw these listed on Amazon so I was curious.  Hmm, a new Ramen that I've never tried and gets good reviews...I need to try these.  They are fantastic.  I really like the spice in these.  I eat a ton of Thai and Indian food so for me these aren't spicy and are just perfect.  I used the whole packet and found the spice level just perfect.  Anyway, as others have said these are much better than your standard Ramen noodle.  If you like Ramen noodles at all I highly recommend you pick up a box of these.  But, as others have noted, if you don't like really spicy food you might want to start off with just a half packet of spices and see how it goes.  Another great product I found through Amazon!

I love spicy food and where I live you can not find spicy ramen. My Korean b/f said that these were the spiciest noodles he has had in America. I did not take it too seriously and I was not going to buy ramen online. So as insisted that I try it and he sent me a box of these from Amazon and wow they really are spicy! I like to add kimchi and egg in mine personally but you can put chicken, lamb, shrimp, white fish or beef in this.  I suggest if you want to do meat to add a bit of oil in the pot with the seasoning packet and cook it like that first after it is almost cooked add the water. and cook the noodles separate and drain them add the noodles in a bowl than top with the broth meat and veggie. It is a little extra work but really worth the time. (the reason to cook the noodles separate is because i find that cooking the noodles with the meat makes the meat chewy)

column9: Add some Spice to your Life!
column10: I love noodles, although I really have to be careful of the amount of sodium I eat.  Nong Shim Shin Noodle Ramyun, Gourmet Spicy Picante noodles add a little kick start to your day!  To start, don't add the entire spice packet because it may be a bit too spicy for you; I don't use a lot of water (just enough to cover the noodles), so I don't use the entire packet for that reason.  I have learned that the Asians add a poached egg to their noodles.  I tried it and I find that just adding that little bit of protein keeps me satisfied longer.  These are really not your standard noodles, so if you want to add a little spice to your life, try them.  They cost a little more than the standard noodle, but as the old saying goes, you get what you pay for!

the noodles are great. i love spicy foods. i guess its just the Asian in me lol. i like the free delivery when you subscribe. the only thing that sucks is they raised the price 5 bucks since i last ordered... i guess i can't complain since they are still cheaper than what i can find at the stores around my area.

These noodles are very quick to make and quite tasty. It comes with dried vegetables and a spicy seasoning.  It can be made in less than 8 minutes on the stovetop. 3 minutes for water to boil and 5 minutes to cook.I am a fan of spicy foods but these noodles can be a little too spicy. I use about half the packet to cut back on the spiciness and sodium.If you need something quick, easy and tasty to make for a meal this is definitely it!

The spice and flavor go hand-in-hand, so I usually add all of the flavor packet. I make these slightly soupy, and I often discard a little of the broth to reduce sodium levels + spare my digestive tract from the ravages of my taste buds. Also great (and more of a meal) with egg stirred in near the end. I could eat these every day, but alas, that would have dire consequences.Taking the nutritional drawbacks as a given, these are 5* for price/flavor.

column9: best spicy noodles ever!  update 1-12 but have the noodles changed?
column10: i have eaten this product for 3 or 4 years and i LOVE it!  i am so glad i found this on amazon so i do not have to worry about finding it in stores anymore.  our grocery here charges $2+ for 1 packet of it!  can you say rip off!  i only cook the noodles 3 minutes after i put them in the boiling spice mix.  and i have been adding raw shrimp to the spice mixture and that makes this a great meal!  my son started eating this at age 10..he calls it moms spicy soup...he loves it too.so here is my question..have they changed the noodles?  the last bunch i got (get the pack of 20) the noodles have been almost slimy..  i never cooked them as long as they say, sticking with 3 minutes which had worked for years..  now i have tried cooking less time, more time and the oodles are just ... different..  as i said, almost slimy feeling or something like that..  i don't know..  anyone else notice that?  and didn't these used to come from thialand?  they are made in america now and the directions on the back are more american-ized..  i am wondering if they changed the noodles if they did move the product to made in the usa..another update!!  whatever was going on seems to have only been with that one shipment and not all of them.  i have gotten a couple since then that have been fine.

If you like spicy noodles and don't really feel like taking time to make it, this comes really close.  Instant noodle at its best!  Just boil some water, toss the noodles in, add some vegie, kamaboko, tofu (whatever you like and have)..., that will actually look like a fancy bowl of noodles when you are done in less than 5 mins.

If you like spicy Ramen noodles, these are the choice for you!  These are just like the ones my husband used to eat in Korea as a kid, so naturally we love them.  Also, they are pretty expensive in stores, so Amazon usually sells them at a reasonable price.
It's the same taste as the one I bought in Asian supermarket which can recall me the Chinese style noodles. Very delicious!

First of all, kudos to the Super Saver shipping option that I got on ordering two cases of Nong Shim Shin Ramyun. It's made this the most affordable of this type of superior three-minute ramen one can get, especially in Hawaii where most food is imported and thus, more expensive. I've become an instant ramen snob (an oxymoron?), and this brand has great quality noodle texture.

I love these.  It's hard to think of anything else as cheap that is as warming, satisfying, and delicious.  I use a little more water than called for by the directions, then add a few tablespoons of dried diced bell peppers for a bit of nutrition when adding the noodles and packet contents.  (The extra flavor is nice, too.)  When the noodles are cooked, I turn off the heat and add a beaten egg, stirring quickly.  The package makes two lunches for me.  A hungrier or bigger person could eat a whole package, although the sodium total would be high. I can get these in one of my local grocery stores, but they don't restock when sold out and since Amazon's price is the same, I bought a case here.

I will preface this to say that I like spicy things. From salsa to buffalo wings, I usually like the hottest variety of everything. Imagine my surprise then when I heard of this magical "splcy picante" ramen. I figured it couldn't possibly be that bad, so I ordered this box of 20 to check it out.When it came in, I eagerly prepared a package as I normally make ramen. Needless to say I was unprepared for what came after I had my first spoonful. I honestly wondered if I could finish it... whew. The quality of the noodles was fantastic (a far cry from any of the brands you can buy at the supermarket) but that broth! Spicy didn't even begin to describe it. So there I sat, sweat pouring down my face as I polished off the last of it.Feeling exhausted, yet quite proud of myself, I checked out some reviews and saw many warnings about the heat in this stuff, in addition to the most helpful suggestion ever--only use half of the seasoning packet! I actually use even less than half, and that's still plenty of flavor and plenty of heat for me--making the bowl not only bearable but actually pleasurable to eat. Also cuts down on the heaps of sodium present in there.I really love these, but they're just plain unhealthy so I don't eat them very often. But as long as you don't dump that entire packet of fire in there you've got a pretty spicy tasty bowl of awesome.And if you do use the whole packet and enjoy every drop? You're a mensch in my book!

column9: The best noodle I've ever had
column10: this is the best noodle I've ever had. Every time I'll add some eggs, vegies. Once you try this, you will never forget it.

I was browsing amazon when I came across these noodles and realized I had not had noodles in ages. I used to eat them all the time. The hard brick type noodles you boil in water for 6 minutes.Now, I love spicy. I add spice to almost everything I eat. I have lived in the middle and far east.. so when I cooked up my first packet of these I was surprised to find I was reaching for the water. Wow, these are spicy. I normally like to drink the soup at the end but was unable to. The 2nd packet I had was not too bad or I got used to it. For the 3rd packet, I mixed in a raw egg just before microwaving and it made a huge difference. It seemed to take the kick out of the spice and I enjoyed it much more.If you like noodles and spicy, buy these.
This is the best tasting, artery clogging, high blood pressure inducing ramen I have ever tasted.  Yumm!

Noodles are fine and filling. They make a simple and cheap meal with some vegetables, slices of meat, and eggs thrown in. The spice packet is a bit overwhelming if you're starting out, so stick to using a quarter of the packet first. The dehydrated vegetables are a nice touch, though they do take a bit more time than the noodles to be rehydrated. Instead of following the instructions on the package to the letter, try throwing in the veggies a bit before time, say 2 minutes or so ahead, or while the water is boiling set the veggies in a separate container of water until it's time to cook the noodles.

my first exposure to shin ramyun was about 10 years back at a japanese grocer. all that was available were the shin cups which i picked up as i thought they looked to be the best seller there. at almost $2 a cup it became a pricey treat for me as i feel in love immediately. the hearty noodles, the rich fiery broth and endless ways to dress it up. i never found the packaged noodles until recently and with the subscription service i am now always stocked and at a price that cannot be beat. my current favorite to make a package into a meal is adding in a scallions, sliced mushrooms, broccoli sprouts and an egg poached in the broth.
I bought this product strictly on the review of others and they were right, these noodles are great, way better than top ramen.  I will be buying these again.

column9: A delicious noodle with good price
column10: It is hot and delicious. the noodle is very good. although later I found it a little cheaper at local Asian food mart.

What can I say?  They are very spicy, tasty noodles.  My wife loves these noodles and buys them from an asian market that is about 20 miles away from the house.  I'm very happy Amazon sells them for a comparable price and includes free shipping (as of the time of this review).  It saves us the expense and hassle of driving across town.

I have purchased this noodle from local supermarket for years. Due to the rising cost of everything, it got more expensive then ever.  I was please to find that Amazon carry this, with the promotional offer, I paid a lot less then the market, and the delivery was quick too.  About the taste, it is spicy, I don't put whole pack of seasoning at once.  The portion also good enough, 4.2-ounce compare to some smaller package.  It's good buy, I am very happy with it.

column9: To steal a tagline...mmm, mmm good!
column10: This stuff is awesome! It has the right amount of spice (a-lot) and the noodles are much thicker and more flavorful than the standard $.10 a pack stuff. Don't get me wrong, I love regular Top Ramen, but this is so much better. Throw in some left over chicken (or even better, tri-tip), frozen corn and peas, an egg, and you have an excellent meal. Add an ice cold beer, and you will be in foody heaven.

Just about any nong shim soup is good. Most of them are very spicy and addicting. I really like the chicken and original spicy noodles...Yeah it has MSG but just about every soup does including name brand soups like Cambells and Chef Boyardee its in a lot of salty foods! The list goes on including chips! So don't complain about that! Its to be expected! Just dont overdo it by eating a bunch of these its just not good for you just like eating a bunch of salty chips isnt good for you... But anyway this stuff is AWESOME and it is not for any one who hates spicyness because this stuff is hot! But its packed with soo much flavor,it makes those 15 cent ramen noodles taste like noodles in salt water. These are worth the extra cash because this is quality.

column9: Yummy al dente noodles in my bowl!
column10: I bought these on a whim because they were a deal of the day.  Boy am I glad that I did.  As a big fan of Maruchan and Top Ramen, I read the reviews and saw that these were very close to the real thing.The noodles have such a great consistency and cook in just 4-5 minutes.  Very al dente, even after they sit in your bowl for 5 minutes cooling down.  Another plus for me was the fact that there isn't only the flavor packet but a vegetable packet as well.  That vegetable packet adds another dimension to the soup.As other reviewers have stated before, this is for the Spicy Picante pack.  If you can't handle spice then I suggest using a 1/4 of the spice packet.  If you are a seasoned professional then use the whole thing.  My first time around I did that and found myself actually finding it overwhelming and I ALWAYS eat everything hot and spicy including Jalapenos.  So from now on, it is half a packet for me.Take a chance... they are great; can't wait to try other flavors now!
Apparently they used too much synthetic flavors that it just burns your tongue. Also there's too much oil ... almost made me choke ...

column9: What else can you ask for at a discounted price?
column10: Stacks of these shin ramyun are stored and sold at each and every Korean airport Duty Free Shops (in a different packing style). I for one am not complaining for buying it at an average of under 1 buck a bag. Extra spice needed if you are really in for the hot flavor. Cooking it in a stone pot with an extra egg, some fresh kimchi and some beef (or spam;) will bring out the real korean taste.

I been to several places around the world, including Russia and Mongolia. There, if you ask for "ramen", this ramen (Shin Ramen) is the one they give you. it's the best!While by itself is tasty, to enhance the flavor, i often throw in shrimp, mushroom and sliced onion. Mucho delicious !
This item is really over price, i can buy the same from local Asian grocery stores and it is a lot cheaper.
I would have to say the noodles packaged with this product are just plain bad. The spice packet is on par with whats to be expected but the noodles just taste bad.

column9: My new favorite ramen, thanks to amazon
column10: I originally decided to purchase this particular brand of ramen after seeing all the other positive reviews here on Amazon. I was a bit apprehensive at first, fearing that I wouldn't enjoy it since I had never tried this brand before but I'm glad this turned out to be delicious. The spiciness, although explained in the reviews, was still a bit surprising when I first tasted it. I'm glad something is actually spicy for once instead of just claiming to be spicy and having the spiciness equivalent to a chocolate bar.
this stuff is awesome.  for best flavor boil it in water, drain the water, add spice packet and then add hot water.
I love these noodle.  A little to spicy for the wife but perfct for me.
I just love it and will buy another box when I'm done with last one!

My late father in law used to have a rating system for meals: if it was particularly tasty, he'd say "This tastes like more!" That's exactly how I felt the first time I tried a spicy picante ramyun. I ordered these on a whim when they were featured as a gold box deal. I'd enjoyed ramen noodles in the past, so even though I'd never tried this brand, I figured for less than a dollar a package, I could afford to take a chance. Boy am I glad I did! They were spicy, flavorful and delicious. I immediately wanted a second helping and had to talk myself out of it. I used less water than it called for but the full spice packet, and I think that combination intensified the flavors. The only reason it didn't get 5 stars was because of the strange dried meat bits that popped up every once in a while. The tough texture of the mystery meat kind of threw me off my game, but luckily I only found them when I was almost finished. I'd recommend these to any ramen lover (adjusting the spice to taste for some).

This is my favorite brand of Korean ramen. It is spicy so if you are not used to eating spicy food, make sure you don't use all of the spice pack. If you add an egg to the soup, it makes a great snack.

I do like these noodles although, to say they are spicy is somewhat of an understatement. No one else in the family tolerates spicy very well so, seeing these, I was looking forward to an extra little something for the palate. I was not disappointed. To be completely honest, I usually drain most of the liquid as it is almost too much!

column9: This spicy noodle cures my cold, upset stomach, and headache every time!
column10: I love this noodle and have it once or twice a week. The amazing thing is that when I don't feel well because of a cold, a hot bowl of this noodle will cure my upset stomach, headache, and running nose! This may not work for you, but you should definitely try it.

That's pretty much what these ramen noodles has, spiciness. I love spicy noodles like the next guy but even after using only half the packet, it still leaves your mouth hot and spicy. And can barely appreciate the quality of taste these noodles are suppose to bring.It's like when you order the most spiciest buffalo wild wings. You cannot taste the meat but just how hot they are. The same can be said about these supposedly top brand ramen noodles.
The taste is great! especially when you cook it with some vegetable and egg.I like it very much, though it's more expensive than the other noodles
This is the best instant noodle I have tried.  Very spicy!  Yes, I like it very spicy.  You can always dilute it with more water to reduce the strength and make it less salty too.

I don't see how anyone could say anything bad about these noodles.  These are the number one Nong Shim noodles!  Great to add an egg, some green onion and every once in a while a good handful of firm tofu.  I enjoy eating these with a nice hot cup of Bigelow Earl Grey Green Tea, 20-Count Boxes (Pack of 6) and an episode of classic Doctor Who. :)

These are very good noodles - better than the ones you find at the supermarket.The flavor is very real and these are pretty spicy.. not crazy hot but just right.OK OK it's not Momofuku but for a quick 5 minute lunch on the job.. it'll work!mj

Very spicy packaged ramen. Good for someone who wants easy ramen but wants something better than 25 cent beef ramen from the store. Best to use only half a packet unless you feel like burning your tongue.
Delicious, awesome spicey noodle has there own flavor. If you like spicey ramen noodle, this is the one your looking for. I am re-ordering.
Always good.  I do not have a better choose in America. This is the best I can buy in the US.
It's quick to cook and pretty dang tasty. I think there's way too much sodium in the seasoning, but it's easy enough to not add it all.

column9: nong shim shin noodle is my Favorite instant noodle
column10: the deliver is on time. And the noodle's are great. But the pack is quite large so I probably will finish it in a few months.

Love this soup!  Boil water, add a spice packet, a seasoning packet, and then the noodles. Four minutes later you have spicy ramyun soup.  It probably is a tad spicy for the "average" palate but if you love spicy, give this a try.  When I have a stuffy nose, I even add a couple splashes of hot sauce or sriracha and it clears me right up.
bought 2 package for the family and it's almost gone. the noodle is good even though it's so spicy to me

Shin Ramyun (since it's Korean) is an awesome:- Late night snack dry- Home cold remedy- Depressed-mood solutionIt's easy to make and it's straightforward. However, NOT for the person with acid-reflux, which I have unfortunately obtained recently. :( Eating shin gives an extremely bad heartburn afterwards.However, if you don't suffer from GERD, gastritis, ulcer, heartburn, etcetera, eat to your heart's content!
You get what you pay for, forget those .10 ramen from walmart, these are authentic spicy noodles. Makes me sweat and cry but so delicious

I received Nongshim shin ramen through subscribing. It was great deal because I paid less money than offline stores and it was more delicious than any other ramens. Additionally subscribing is very convenient and time efficient way. So I strongly recommend to you.

column9: Nice quick noodle, a bit spicy
column10: Good for a quick meal such as breakfast, a bit spicy,half sources pack is good enough to cook

These are excellent inexpensive noodles but they are quite salty for someone who rarely adds salt to food, even when cooking, as I do!  They are more expensive than grocery store Ramen and taste a good deal better but seem to have about the same destructive amounts of salt- 2020 mg or about 80% daily salt intake/bag which claims to be 2 servings but I assume that most adults would consume the lot unless using this as only part of a meal rather than a quick comfort food.  Other reviews alerted me to this and following their recommendation, I only used 1/2 the soup base package.  I added some dehydrated green onions and dried oinions when preparing on the stovetop and added a fresh egg, covering it with the noodles after removing from the heat.  This had excellent flavor and with half of the salt, I did not feel like my blood pressure would be so imperiled as I had used the whole soup packet.  I like and regularly consume very spicy food (I frequently consume 4-5 jalapenos with a meal) but as prepared it was quite delicious and spicy enough.  There are other brands of noodles that I frequently buy from Amazon Annie Chun's Korean Sweet Chili Noodle Bowl, 8.4-Ounce Units (Pack of 6) that I relish but the salt is still high and the price is somewhat higher.  I will alternate varieties in the future.  I only eat Asian Noodles no more than once a week since I do have some sodium issues.  I am on disability and do not get out often from my house in the country so I have tried many of the long shelf life foods that Amazon sells.  They sell many dehydrated vegetables in medium sized quantities that make them easy to have on hand and still be way cheaper than grocery store prices.  I even found some non refrigerated tofu Mori-Nu Tofu, Lite, Silken, Firm, 12.3-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 12) that I have received but not yet tried.  The customer reviews claim that it is excellent quality and it is actually cheaper than the fresh brand offered in the local grocery.  I expect to add some to my next bowl of noodles and the soups that I frequently make from scratch.

column9: Delicious and spicy, good quality ramen
column10: I love this compared to the ones I used to eat, like Nissin and Maruchan.  You can really tell the difference.

These are perhaps the best instant noodles available; hot & spicy, and substantive, it'll satiate any craving for a snack, anytime. The product was shipped in good condition from Amazon (USPS). Convenient!
One box of Shin Noodle costs around $15 in Asian store near my house. The same box sometimes sells for $11 during sale. $20 for this box is way overpriced. Check your local Asian markets.
Man this stuff is spicy and tastes great!!!  I like spicy stuff and this is probably the best I have had out of package.

One of my favorite brands of ramen.  To make it a little better for you most people dont use the entire seasoning packet to cut back on the sodium.  Noodles are substantially better than ramuchan and top ramen, but you must add other items such as onions, maybe some meet and an egg to truly make this a satisfying meal.

I stated on the batch this week and it goes well with everything I have tried to put in it.  It taste great with hot dogs, Vienna sausages, eggs, spam, various veggies, and slices of old pizza.  I thought I would only eat half of it, but it tasted so good, I just gulped it all down.  The spice is really intense, I might just save a few packages and put it in my other bland foods.

column9: Satisfied by delivery time, quality, and taste!
column10: Fast shipping, always service and a really great taste! What more could one ask for!!!
I've tried many noodle varieties over the years and these are by far the best. A little spicy, but very flavorful. Try them with some scrambled egg and chopped green onions for a tasty breakfast.

column9: Best Spicy Ramyun on the Market
column10: As a Korean native I've had many different kinds of ramyun because it is a big part of our culture.  Shin ramyun is by far THE BEST spicy ramyun on the market and most Koreans I know agrees with me.  If you're not good with spicy food then I would not recommend this ramyun because you will be sweating like pig!  If you love spicy food and if you love ramyun then this your best bet.  Won't regret it!

column9: Filling noodles and flexible (no pun intended)
column10: These noodles are quite spicy and a big bowl of food.  They are, however, a very flexible base for simple meals.  You can control the spiciness (and sodium level) by how much of the seasoning packet you put in and you can add cooked meats and other vegetables to the soup to make variety.  I've found that poaching an egg or two in the soup is very tasty, as well.  Far superior quality of noodle to most grocery store brands.

A delicious night snack at an awesome price! You will not regret getting these noodles! Be aware though, they can be very spicy if you use the whole package of spicy stuff.
Perfect Noodles every time, just enough spicy.  Vegetables are just the right amount and cooks up plump and nice in minutes.
Very tasty, especially for a spicy food lover like me. Subscribe & Save makes it economic. However, these are fried noodles so a lot of calories.

They're not for the faint of heart. I get so bored with most foods that claim to be spicy hot, but Shin Ramyun delivers. And it's not just hot, it's got great taste. I've been buying them by the 20-pack for years and loving every bite.
Dont hesitate, get these and put them in your mouth. well cook them then get those noodles in your mouth.

This is best selling and most popular ramyun in Korea. It has been copied by many Chinese companies.This is really hot and spicy...not for everyone.Comparing with cheap ramyun brand is just non sense....I don't enjoy ramyun as much as others but this is the one I eat!

I gotta say it is less spicier than Korean-made Shin, and somewhat blend.However, Shin is the best among I have tried.I haven't tried Mama's but, the distinct spicy taste of shin cannot be replaced for me.I always add raw egg into 1 min of boiling, and drop chopping green onions after the cooking is over.

flavor could be better, I do like the vegetable packet though.  In future, would just by the generic twelve packs of soup at the local grocery store for under 2 dollars though

column9: Ramen made in the USA = bad ramen
column10: I can't believe this product has such high review. The noodles taste like rubber and it is NOT spicy at all. Please just go to your local oriental store and look for ramen made from japan or korea. Those noodles actually have a nice texture and the spices they use are actually spicy.

I was just about to buy this, until I saw in the ingredients that it contains MSG. At least this product description tells you (the others don't). If you are like me, that means you'll get a nasty headache after eating this. How about offering MSG-free noodles like I can get locally?

column9: Beware, not the same as the one from the Korean Market
column10: Just receive the noodle and try one.  The package looks similar but not the same as the one that I got from the Korean market.  I just finish the box of Shin noodle that I bought from Korean town so I know the differences right away.  I thought I got a good deal and save a trip to Korean town.  Guess not, I am wrong.  I am going to the Korean town this weekend to get the real stuff.  A little disappointed, I really want my authentic spicy red Korean Shin instant noodle tonight...This Shin noodle is made in the USA and it is a American version of the very popular Korean instant noodle.  This American version is only one-third as spicy and the noodle get soft and mushy very fast like the regular instant noodle.  The dry vegetable package does not go soft even after 10 minutes.  To use the dry vegs in the future, need to soak it for at least 30 minutes so the dry mushroom will get soft. The spice package is orange color, the real Korean Shin noodle is bright red in color and the noodle will not get mushy after 10 minutes.  I think it is something to do with the red pepper that the Korean use and not the picante in this USA version.  It is spicy but taste totally different than the Korean kind of red pepper which make it so special.Really want to return it but since I got it with the lightning deal discount, I will eat it like regular instant noodle to save the hazzle.  So beware if anyone reading this is Korean or have tried the real Korean Shin instant noodle.  This is not the real thing, do not order this and do not pay full price for this American version of the Shin noodle.  Before I was skeptical when reading some of the reviews with only 1 star, now I know they are right.

column9: I'm sold on the taste but not all the hype.
column10: I ordered these noodles after reading stellar reviews.  Some folks in the reviews almost acted as if these noodles were sent from God.  I've eaten Ramen Noodles for quite some time and have found them to be a super inexpensive meal at .10 a package and sometimes cheaper.  I also like other readers mentioned don't always use the entire seasoning packet because of the high sodium content.  I found these noodles to have even higher sodium content.  Which I guess isn't too bad if you don't plan on eating the soup.These noodles to me tasted just about the same as Ramen Noodles except the noodles were a tid bit larger in size.  If we are reviewing just the flavor packet, I would say it was pretty good.  Especially for those who like spice like myself.  I am use to eating super spicy foods and have a high tolerance to spice.  So they were right on par with what I am use to as far as the heat goes.  But I can see someone who doesn't eat spicy foods to find the seasoning super hot and spicy for them.  I like the idea of the dehydrated veggies that are enclosed to accompany the seasoning.  I am giving these noodles 3 stars because they are just overpriced Ramen in my opinion.  Plus the sodium content in the noodles is just unacceptable.  They surely can come up with lower sodium options. And lastly I give it 3 stars because of the price.  I would not expect to pay more than .50 cents a package for these noodles in a retail store. I would definitely buy these again but not in bulk.

I love ramen type soups.  I've tried many over the years.  This Gourmet Spicy Picante is ok. The noodles are your regular, fried ramen...a tad thicker then common grocery store noodles.  One trick I use is after cooking the noodles, I rinse with water well...it takes that starchy flavor away that I don't care for and makes a fresher tasting soup.  The heat of this is strong, use a quarter packet to start, you can always build up.  Not much more flavor going on except the heat of the chili.I do love the Hoo Roo Rook noodles; they aren't fried and the noodles are round to fit your saucepan.  They aren't in the same heat category as these noodles, but they are nice for a more 'tender' palate that likes things not-so-spicy.*NEWSFLASH*  Okay, I'm coming to the end of this box of Spicy Picante and realized that I would sort of miss having my mouth burning while eating soup this winter...so on that note, I just may buy this noodle again -- it's a heat that kind of grows on you.  I did order the spicy seafood flavor and will see how that one goes.  All in all, this is an acquired hotness that takes getting used to if you're not used to heat (like me).

I purchased several different Korean Noodle Soups but I prefer this "Bag" version of this soup over the "Big Bowl" version. The product is a great soup with much flavor, a nice spicy hot taste and lots of noodles. I modify the soup a little by adding some cut-up pieces of 3 or 4 green onions and some cut-up pieces of roasted chicken breast "after" making the soup to make it higher in protein. I usually have this and other Korean soups every day for a great "power lunch". Love this soup, fast and easy to make in a pot or by pre-heating the water in a microwave and then pouring it over the dry soup in a bowl.

column9: Add a little spice to your life
column10: This product is a must-try!  We've had every brand of ramen out there, but Nong Shim makes the best.  And the spicy picante is so quick and easy, filling, and flavorful, it doesn't last long at our house.  The auto-delivery is a big help. If the whole spice packet is too much for you, try adding just a third or half to your batch.  Finally, the 20 pack price blows away any supermarket price you'll find anywhere.

Although admittedly not very healthy, having tons of sodium and MSG, it is delicious, quick to prepare and cheap. Just throw a bit of everything in the pot when you make it. You can boil dumplings with it. You can throw in any type of meat with it. You can add in beaten eggs for a different soup texture, or just crack an egg right into the soup before or after cooking depending on how cooked you want your egg to be. Add milk to the soup if you want a more milky flavour. Add a few slices of cheese on top after it's prepared and enjoy the melted cheesy deliciousness. You can also add literally any type of vegetable you can think of. If you're not feeling like having noodles with that soup base you can use the noodles with your own broth or make fried noodles. Then you can save the soup base for seasoning any future dishes you make.These noodles make for some really flexible meals when you're tight on time or ingredients. I wouldn't be alive without them!
i usually use 2 bags and 1 of the spice packets and drop an egg in it.good stuff

Just be sure and try 1 packet before plunking down $19 for the whole crate of 20.  Bought a pack at the store today and could not get past the 2nd bite.  The heat is intense, but the flavor is flat.  It's probably better once you dress it up with a poached egg or some veggies, but it wasn't the flavorful kind of spicy I was looking for.

column9: Almost feel like I got the wrong product
column10: After seeing these hyped up over and over again as the "best" ramyun noodles, I had to try them. Verdict after two boxes? They're OK.Every review on here is how flavorful and SPICY these are. Well, they do taste pretty good. Do they taste that much better than the 10 cent ramyun at the local grocery store? To my taste, they don't. I will concede they are slightly better and certainly more filling.As far as spicy.. I'm so confused on this. Every review says to use half a packet as these will burn your mouth off. So needless to say, I was expecting HEAT! These aren't spicy at all. To give you a frame of reference, I'm usually sweating after eating "hot" wings at Applebees. If you've ever gone to Buffalo Wild Wings, I have a difficult time eating the "Asian Zing" wings. I can't tolerate heat very well. However, I have a pretty mild burn going on in my mouth after eating a bowl with full spice, and it's not unpleasant enough to warrant a drink.So, all in all, not bad noodles. Don't think I'd ever pay $20 for them again, though.

Hand these out at Halloween instead of candy for an instant reaction!The kids who raise their eyebrows are probably paranoid about their sodium intake and shouldn't be allowed to trick-or-treat anyway!

This ramen is so good. I also bought the Neoguri- also a good choice if you like seafood. I would highly recommend this. It microwaves well, I use pyrex. I'm deployed on a ship and it was sent out here pretty quick (relatively speaking ok? lol) and none of the ramen was damaged during VERTREP. It is spicy! Definitely seriously spicy. I cook it with minimal water so it stays that way. I love it. Will buy again. It's pretty much the highlight of my day.

A very consistent, tasty choice when one does not want to cook. I gave four stars only because I had imported Korean soup before that was even tastier.The Amazon delivery (through Prime membership) was free and earlier than promised.Recommended.
Excellent noodle quality and very tasty. Way better than American ramen. Highly recommended for anyone that likes spicy foods and wants some better quality ramen.
i practically lived off these stuff during my college years.they're one of the best instant noodles i've ever had.i will buy from again and again when they're on sale :)

This is the best ramen that I've had and it's the kind my family has been eating for years. It is definitely more spicy than other types of ramen out there but it is so good and you can always add less seasoning if you don't want to have it as spicy. It's really quick and easy to prepare and it's perfect for college students because you can eat it on its own or add more ingredients (like eggs) that you want to dress it up.

This has awesome  flavor ... nutritional value in itself is little to none .. BUT .. a great base and low in cals ... you can add this to other soups or add vegies ... or on it's own ... great product ... very happy and i will order it again

This Korean-style ramen is one of my favorites. As an individual whom doesn't often eat spicy foods, the spiciness of the seasoning in the ramen is very near upper tolerance level and nothing goes better with it than a cold beer. The texture is a bit chewier than the generic American ramen but that's what ramen should taste like.

column9: The best go-to meal for anything!
column10: This is the best hangover cure you can buy.That being said, I've been eating this ramyun ever since I was little. It is great just the way the package tells you to eat it. Sometimes, I'll just make it by pouring hot water over it, and the noodles are still a little crispy that way. You can also make this really fancy. Stir in a can of tuna (flavored or not!), some vegetables, leftover meat of any kind...you can make this into a really great and filling meal! I just wouldn't recommend adding rotisserie chicken (that was the saltiest thing I think I've ever eaten...).I love this stuff and I don't think I'll ever stop eating it. The price on Amazon is alright -- if you have an Asian market nearby, it is cheaper there. Some Walmarts will also sell the individual packs for about $1 each, so Amazon doesn't really save you any money, but it does provide convenience if you have Prime.

I was introduced to this ramen 15 years ago while overseas in the ROK. Its a spicy Korean ramen comparable to some of its Thai counterparts but has to be one of the tastiest ramen noodles I've ever had. The quality of Nongshim is superb and I would recommend this product to anyone. Add an egg to this noodle soup while its cooking and you got an awesome meal.

Good spicy ramen,and when purchased through Amazon, pretty cheap. In NYC you can't really find these in bulk at these prices (under a dollar per soup with Subscribe & Save) unless you go bargain hunting at the Asian markets. I still have most of this case left, so I'd imagine one case is good for 6 months, if you're a relatively light eater of freeze-dried ramen.You can add all sorts of things to hearten this ramen up: eggs, spinach, tofu, kimchi, bean sprouts. This ramen IS salty (and moderately spicy), so you can add extra cooking water and dump it out after serving, or half the seasoning packet.

I began looking at Amazon's offerings of ramen noodles because I was tired of Top Ramen and the few limited brand varieties most stores carry. I settled on Nong Shim Shin Noodle Ramyun Gourmet Spicy Picante because of the high ratings. I don't mind spicy foods, but sometimes I find that when food is overly spicy it overpowers any appreciation for the flavor. This is my experience with Nong Shim noodles. My dh, who enjoys ramen noodles says these noodles have a slimy texture and I did have to agree with him the next time I tried to "get in" to them. However, I'm still curious about Nong Shim's other ramen noodle offerings so I may purchase one of their non picante flavors.

1. Add an egg while your noodle is being cooked. The timing decides whether the yolk will be soft or hard. To preserve the original spicy flavor, the egg should be hard-boiled in the soup. But some prefers to blend the soft yolk to the soup for a milder taste. There are a lot of people who blend the whole egg to the soup during cooking, this makes it a wholly different kind. Note, as more egg blends into the soup, you are more inclined to finish the whole soup, which is not too great for your health (too much sodium).2. Add a slice of cheddar cheese on top of the prepared Ramyun in a bowl.3. Do both 1 & 2.I gave 4 stars because Shin Noodle is too spicy for me.
Very filling but not too oily, like other instant noodles out there. The noodles are just chewy enough and the right size for the hot, spicy soup. A fantastic quick meal for a chilling winter night.

I could not wait to get this noodles in the mail and right when they arrived, I whipped up a bowl and could not have been more satisfied. I love spicy foods and not only does this satisfy my craving, but it's also full of flavor. The possibilities are endless when it comes to adding ingredients to this ramyun, but even if there is nothing added, it is still very good. I really like the packet of freeze dried vegetables that come with it. I have half a box left and I already know that I will be ordering more if I can't find something similiar in the grocery stores in my area.To address the sodium issue - yes, there is about half your days worth of sodium in one flavoring packet, BUT you most likely won't be able to handle the heat of one whole packet so you won't be consuming the full amount of contained sodium and if you do use the entire packet, just watch your sodium intake the rest of the day and double your water intake (you will probably do that anyway to cool your mouth from the heat, but it's a good burn :)). These aren't incredibly healthy. My boyfriend and I usually split one because there is a lot of noodles per package and it is so filling. You do not want to eat this for several days in a row, but a lot of things are okay in moderation. I whole heartedly believe that one package of these noodles is a heck of a lot healthier than anything offered at a fast food chain.

Great on a really cold day and if you're really congested.The spiciness of the ramen really clears my sinuses when I have a cold.I wouldn't recommend this for those who only like mild-medium spiciness.This is a very spicy ramen, and will really make your lips tingle and tongue burn.If you can handle it spicy, this is the best ramen.

column9: tasty, but loaded with sodium and better prices locally
column10: This is probably the #1 Ramen in Korea which I also enjoy, but you should be aware of the nutrition facts.The nutrition table on the bag is for 1/2 a serving, which equates to 1/2 a bag.  The cooking instruction is for full bag, so it's fair to note the nutrition contents for the whole bag as below:Calories: 560Calories from fat: 160Total Fat: 18g, 28% of daily valueSaturated Fat: 9g, 46% of daily valueSodium: 2080mg, 86% of daily valueWhile the sodium content is on the higher end of foods, you have some control over this by adjusting the amount of power soup base.  Once I learned the nutritional facts, I use the full bag of noodles with half packet of the soup base.  The other method would be to cook the whole bag as usual, but immediately throw away 1/2 the soup to avoid the temptation of eating the whole thing.Lastly, my secret to best ramen is no secret to Koreans - after the noodle is dropped in boiling water for 1 minute, drop an egg and sliced spring onions and cook for 1 more minute.  Then, pour into a bowl by 3rd minute.  You'll know you did this correctly when the noodle in the bowl is "almost" 100% cooked where the noodle have come apart, but still somewhat undercooked.  If you cook more than 4 minutes as instructed on the bag, then the noodles will get bloated and taste nasty by the time it makes it to the table.Enjoy!

column9: Too expensive and too much fat/oil !!!
column10: 1) I would recommend to purchase this product at the nearest any Korean markets where you can buy it around $18 or less.2) As far as this product itself concerned, it contains too much fat/oil compared to Samyang Ramen, which might upset your stomach.

column9: Hands down the Best Spicy Ramen
column10: These are, by far, the best Ramen Noodles I've ever had the pleasure of eating.  I practically lived on this stuff when I was in college.  A packet is included containing the spices which allows you to control the level of heat in the dish by adding more or less of the contents to the noodles.  One important note, the spices provide a tasty spicy hot, not a hot-just-to-be-hot flavor.

As far as packaged ramen goes, this stuff is about as good as it gets.  I haven't found any other ramen that I like as much as this.Most ramen I eat as drained noodles sprinkled with the seasoning packet, but this one is much better as a soup.  The seasoning is far too spicy to eat these noodles dry, but the seasoning packet is perfect for seasoning soup.  Other types of ramen don't make the kind of flavorful soup that this one makes, but there is enough flavor in one packet of this stuff to flavor a LOT of water!A word of warning... this soup is VERY spicy.  I regularly eat hot wings, spicy potato chips, and I put extra hot sauce in spicy chili.  I like spicy food.  But this stuff is pretty harsh.  If you're very sensitive to spicy foods, I would avoid this one.  If you're mildly sensitive to spicy foods, just use a little extra water in the soup.  I wouldn't say this stuff is over-the-top spicy, but it has a pretty strong kick.I think the thing I like most about this type of ramen is how flavorful the noodles themselves are, even when they are made as a soup.  When I make ramen as a soup with other types, the noodles are almost flavorless.  But these noodles really soak up the flavoring very well.The one complaint I have is that I don't care for the vegetables that come in the vegetable packet.  Fortunately, they are separate, so I just don't put them in.  I find that they don't get soft enough, and I don't like the texture or flavor of the vegetables.

column9: Way better than the typical store ramen
column10: I bought these in preparation for long nights during finals week with the thought that they may be more interesting than the typical chicken ramen noodles. I like spicy food too, so this seemed like an interesting trial for me, although a bit of a gamble when ordering a whole case. These noodles are fantastic, they have so much more flavor than typical ramen, and in many ways are much better tasting than the typical meals i eat. They a slightly-moderately spicy, so i can still give a pack to a friend who isn't into spicy food and expect they will still enjoy it. Ton's of flavor, a bit more volume, and no MSG like normal ramen noodles. Highly recommended.

The big problem with most instant noodles is that the thin noodles get soggy and mushy when sitting in a bowl of soup, then loose quickly their flavor. These thicker noodles avoid that problem and are tasty until you finish the whole bowl. Yes, the soup is spicey, but you don't have to use the whole spice packet if you are a wimp. Just be careful if you are on a diet, since one package if 500 calories (the "per serving" label is for less than half a package).4 stars instead of 5 because instant noodles have so much fat and salt. Regular dried noodles are much healthier, if don't mind waiting a few more minutes for them to cook.

I first got these because I was looking for something hot, something yummy, you know... a quick snack or a fast meal for when I was in a hurry.  I had fond memories of rice and noodle concoctions from my student days and I was drawn to these because of the many excellent reviews.  Indeed, after reading some, I fully expected my toes to tingle after eating these!  :)At first I really liked them, and yes, they are truly spicy.  I like spicy.  The spicier the better.  Besides, the reviewers are right- you can just put in as much of the spice packet as you want.  After a few of them, though, it occurred to me that the spicy wasn't like any Thai or Cambodian food I've had, or even straight up hot chilies like habaneros; the spice struck me as more chemical-induced.  Was it the MSG?  The other salts?  Whatever it is, it doesn't settle well with these taste buds.The more I ate, the less good they seemed to me.  After a while, I noticed that they always left kind of a gummy, coated feeling to the inside of my mouth.  Then I looked at the ingredients.... Maybe it is all the MSG, or maybe the beef tallow, or maybe all the sodium variants that I can't even pronounce.  Whatever it is, these are losing their appeal with every serving.  Now, I'm not a health foodie and despite the fact that one package doses you with 88% of daily value of sodium and 40% daily value of fat, I'm not holding that against it.  (to be fair, the previous amounts assume that you use the entire spice packet and each package counts as 2 servings)  It really comes down to that gummy feeling left in my mouth after eating a package, even using 1/3 of the spice packet.  I just can't get past that.The noodles seem like any other ramen noodles, and they are yummy.  It's also nice that they have a decent size packet of dehydrated veggies inside, separate from the spices.Taste is totally about preference, and I don't think this is a bad product just because it didn't work for me.  Also, I think they are priced right, especially if bought through subscribe and save.  I've got to go with my experience on the rating, though.  Though I won't be getting these again, I wouldn't steer people away.  I would suggest, though, first looking at the ingredients list to see if you are cool with what's in it, and also get a few to try before committing to a bulk buy.

column9: Great consistency, less flavor than expected
column10: I enjoyed these noodles, the noodles themselves were thick, per the other reviews, which was very nice. I didn't find them too spicy, but I do enjoy spicy foods. I added some pre-cooked ham and an egg near the end of the cooking process which added a really nice texture and flavor. I would give 5 stars, but based on the other reviews I expected a little more flavor with the spiciness, but nonetheless, I will probably buy these again.

This product was good as are most instant asian noodles....be careful about using the full package of flavoring as it is very hot....the dried condiments are ok....I prefer to eat this package with some chicken broth added....then wait about ten or fifteen minutes until the noodles get rehydrated....a relativewly low calorie lunch.

I generally like my food spicy, but these noodles are just too hot for me.  So much so that it takes away from the taste.  Unless you really, really, really like spicy hot food food, these may be too much for you.
I like this grocery.It is too spicy and famous noodle in Korea.I'm not Korean but I can eat it.Customer service is so good because it is so speedy

column9: Instant noodle with best taste and texture -- see Recall Info
column10: I just researched about the korean noodle recall because I love this Shin Ramyun noodle -- the best taste and texture instant noodle I have ever tasted. It is the Neoguri Seafood & Mild Noodles and Neoguri Seafood and Spicy Noodles that are problematic, not this Shin Ramyun type by the same company Nongshim, read this article:[...]ADVICE: Because of high sodium in instant noodles, put only partial seasoning package and also try not to drink the soup!

As a general statement I do not like Ramen Noodles; however, this is one of my favorite quick and easy meal.I can't find them in the grocery stores any more so I buy these cases on Amazon. It's a great price!

I can't speak to the these noodles being genuinely Korean. I can only speak to my personal experience with them. I find them absolutely delicious! They are my favorite quick meal after a hard days work where I don't want to spend a great deal of time cooking and I even enjoy them as a comfort food when feeling a little down.The quality of noodle is definitely greater than your typical Maruchan ramen you find in the grocery store. That being said, this is no gourmet meal. If you're looking for something quick and cheap that doesn't taste like garbage, you found it. Those who don't like spicy food should not purchase them, however. They do have a kick, but nothing extreme.If you want to reduce your dishes, try steaming the noodles by boiling water on the stove. Put the dry noodles and dry flavoring in another bowl with a lid. Pour boiling water on top of the noodles and close the lid. Instant noodles in about 10 min.And one warning: always rinse your bowl out when you're done. Never ever leave it sit out for more than a day. You'll only do it once before you figure out why. (Stinky!)
The noodles are awesome. Package came quickly and expected.  Maybe it's just me, but the noodles aren't as spicy as I remembered them back from my college days.
if you like spicy you'll love this way better than the kind you get at the grocery store!it is so warm and delicious! buy it

Very cheap price and very good instant noodle quality and taste!!Even compared to the Korean domestic market price, the price differential isn't too big.There is a slight taste variation compared to the real shin ramen made in Korea, but the difference is very minute.Overall, very satisfied but beware to not eat too much instant food!
The item delivered on time. The ramen is definitely much more delicious than the famous nissan cup noodle. The spiciness of korean ramen is what I miss most after coming to the states

I had tried these when I brought them from my local asian store and fell in love with them. So I thought why not just buy a whole box. I love how spicy these are and tastes a lot better than the other ones that is sold at the grocery store.
as an asian I loveeee spicy food and we eat instant noodles a lot,my husband introduced this to me and im falling love instantly!
So delicious!!!Spicy noodle. I love the taste a lot. It's really difficult to find Shin noodle in US supermarket except California.

column9: OK, but not nearly as good as the Nong Shim Neoguri Spicy Seafood noodles!
column10: Just ordered these by accident (I usually get the Nong Shim Neoguri Spicy Seafood), and they are OK. Seem to be missing the depth and complexity of the Nong Shim Neoguri Spicy Seafood noodles and are just a bit spicy & perhaps a bit citrus-y. Not sure why these sell better than the seafood noodles. I usually add a few shrimp to my noodle bowls during the last minute or two of cooking, with this noodle bowl they just taste like shrimp in a salty broth. In the Nong Shim Neoguri Spicy Seafood noodle bowl the shrimp meld perfectly!

I don't know if this is the BEST ramen in the world, but it's pretty damn good.  This flavor is very spicy.  Nothing to be afraid of, but it is indeed very spicy.  It doesn't burn your tongue, but it will give your lips a good tingle.  The spice of it has caused me some digestive discomfort, but only occasionally.  The dried vegetables are a nice touch that you don't get with the grocery store ramen, I just wish there were more than a tiny little packet.  This is a good product, I just don't know if it's worth the money.

They are great noodles. I was hoping for the Korean version of the noodles, but these are the US version. These were cheaper than the ones from the grocery store. With the amazon prime, they came in two days.

When I lived in Korea, this brand of ramyun was my favorite so I was happy to see that it's for sale in the US, too. In my opinion, this is the best cheap(er) choice when buying this kind of food. I agree with other posters that poaching an egg with the noodles makes the experience infinitely better.One word of advice: They are pretty spicy so if you don't like that, maybe look for another product from the same manufacturer (Nong Shim).
Very tasty, great noodles. They are a little spicy, so I only use about half a packet of the seasoning.
I enjoy these noodles over most other noodles. It's spicy enough to make my nose run, which I like, and the noodles have a nice texture to them.
Great ramen.  Delicious with an egg.  Don't overcook it and it's even better.  Amazon ships promptly as long as it's in stock.

Definitely better than the cheap ramen you find at the grocery store. A dollar a packet really isn't that steep, and you realize this when you try them. First off, the packets are noticeably larger than other ramens, with quite a bit more noodles. Then there's the fact that it comes with a spice packet that seems larger and more filled than competing ramens. It also comes with a dried vegetable packet, a very nice touch. Make sure to read the instructions, they're a little different then other ramens (you just place everything in at once and cook). The taste is phenomenal, nice and spicy (especially if you add the whole packet) with firm noodles that are more chewy that "normal" ramen. A very nice Asian spicy flavor. If you are not one with hot/spicy foods, consider using half a packet of seasoning. Definitely a must try, and I will be ordering more in the future!

Maruchan ramen can't not compare to asian made ramen.The quality of the seasoning stock and dried ramen noodles beats maruchan ramen by a mile.Sometimes its cheaper to buy it on amazon than going to cub foods/asian grocery stores.

My iPad has been in Netflix mode since Korean Drama was added to my que.  Watching "Boys Over Flowers" inspired me to buy some ramen noodles.  Since I live close to the Korean Market I stopped in for some Shin Ramen.Just finished a bowl made exactly as directed.  Results:  Delicious!  Behind the heat the noodles definitely have flavor.  About 3 bites in I had to add some water to the broth.  I was on fire!  But I am not a heat person.Next time I will Dr. it up with some salmon, shrimp and green onion....it's great with ramen!

I usually make two of these at a time, using both vegetable packets and one-and-a-half seasoning packets. I also break three or four eggs into the pot and stir it well. The sodium's pretty high, sure, but the resulting meal is spicy, delicious, and full of protein.
I subscribed the Nong Shim Shin noodle Gourmet Spicy and Kimchi flavor, and I LOVE them!! Recommend the product to anyone who wants a fast and also delicious meal.
Nice flavor and very economical.  At first I have them every day for 2 weeks and got tired of them.Now I just have them once or twice a week and they are enjoyable.

It's not bad, the quality of the noodles is excellent, the packet comes with a good amount of flavor powder so you can pick how hot you wanna make the noodles. The full packet is pretty spicy, half the packet is better for my taste. It's a good product.Two negatives for me were:- Not my kinda flavor, maybe you'll like it, I thought it was a little bland, spicy but bland, I want to try their other flavors later though cause the quality of the product was excellent.- Really high in sodium.

column9: You like heat? This is for you!
column10: This is a very high quality ramen.  However, unless you like it extraordinarily hot, you will want to start with only a bit of the powder and increase the amount from there. THIS IS FIRE!

column9: Two Tastes - Salt and Red Pepper - yet I like it. Add an egg and it really improves. Unfortunately it is far from healthy
column10: Don't under estimate the appeal of salt and cayenne (red) pepper for many "soup lovers" and reviewers. That includes me.However, this is nothing more than a watery Noodle Soup with lots of Red Pepper and a tremendous amount of salt. Add an egg and it tastes much better. Chop up some scallion and it further improves.There is nothing terribly impressive about this soup YET I like It. This dry soup mix consists of a large packet of noodles (essentially tasteless yet ladened with 500 calories of saturated fats) and two much smaller packets. One of these small packets contains less than a tablespoon of chopped dried vegetables and the other is a "spice" packet consisting largely of salt, msg and red (cayenne) pepper.Add some water and you have 2 1/2 cups of soup.Impressions: Beyond the watery base (there are no thickeners), my first impression was that of salt followed ---- after a few more spoonfuls -- of the emerging heat of cayenne pepper. As is typical with cayenne pepper, the heat builds up on the palate over time. Some might call this soup "medium hot" but for many I'd imagine they would call it "very hot". However, it easy to adjust the heat level - just add less of the salt/spice packet.But the only real tastes here are those of salt and cayenne pepper. The noodles are essentially tasteless and the vegetable packet is so small that it can add nothing more than visual appeal. However, I'll say it again, don't under estimate the appeal of salt and cayenne pepper!This soup can be greatly improved by cracking an egg into the mix and stirring it in during the last minute of boiling. The egg not only adds a much needed third taste but also thickens the soup considerably. I was quite surprised how much an egg improved this soup. Make no mistake - adding an egg really changes the character of the soup.At the [...] I paid - with shipping - for a case of 20 -- this soup was a good value.I'd give this soup 3 or 4 stars with an egg but I'm a bit biased toward anything "hot". Maybe 3 stars with an egg is most appropriate and 1 or 2 stars is more accurate for this soup without an egg?HEALTH WATCH: One packet of this soup provides almost 90% of an individual's daily allowance of salt!!!!! That is a stunning amount of SALT. Plus this soup has 40% of the daily allowance of SATURATED fats (thanks to the palm oil used to fry the noodles). With almost 500 calories, you'll be adding a few inches to your waist line if you eat it regularly. It is shame the company choose palm oil to fry its noodles in (presumably to save a few cents) and added so much salt. It makes this soup needlessly unhealthy. It is, in fact, a poster child for all that is wrong with processed foods. I have to add the ingredient list is truly frightening with a long list of chemicals - far more than is typical - even in processed foods. This is probably not a soup anyone should serve more than once a month. View this soup as equivalent to a bag of potato chips, no more or less healthy.Another HEADS UP - some of the reviews on Amazon strike me as a bit suspect: There are a number of 5 star reviews generated by One Time ONLY Amazon reviewers. Once these "reviewers" have promoted this company's product - they never publish another review. I've seen this same pattern, time after time, for all the other soups made by this particular company.Finally, everyone should keep in mind how hard it is to believe that any dried soup with a tiny "flavor packet" could ever rate 4 or 5 stars among people that have a serious love of soup. Consider too, the simple fact that very few of the soup's ingredients are even readily identifiable as a "food".My thanks to the previous reviewers who suggested adding an egg. It made a world of differenceTHIS SAME SOUP IS SOLD in CASE LOTS OF: 20 PACKAGES, 30 PACKAGES or 40 PACKAGES. ALL OF WHICH ARE LISTED SEPARATELY ON AMAZON. The prices differ on a package by package basis too. Generally the 30 pack, which ships for free, is the better value.

column9: bought it just to see if it was any better than regular ramen
column10: It is.  I'm a white dude from TN so i'm not the hugest ramen authority though.I just got this in the mail, ripped it open and threw one in some water:- Spicy as hellllllll.  I used half of the packet and it was still pretty hot, but tasty nonetheless.- Each packet comes with a little pack of dehydrated vegetables to mix in.  I was skeptical of them, but it added to the ramen nicely and tasted good.- I added in an egg.  Eggs make all ramen better.  This ramen was no different.Yep, its a bag of noodles.

column9: Not bad, will compare to Korean Shin
column10: Giving 5 stars so more people will read, actually rate it @ 4 stars.From what I can tell, American made Ramen is worse in generalFor unknown reasons, even though I cook with the same pot I would in Korea, perhaps it is the stovetop instead of the gas stove I would use in Korea, the ramen is harder to cook to the right degree, probably meaning that the noodles were prepared differently in the factories.As for the spiciness factor, anybody who eats regular asian / indian hot foods should be able to taste the flavor behind the spice. In my opinion, everybody here complaining about the whole spice packet being too much must have grown up on hotdogs and hamburgers, or equally not-spicy foods.A tip when cooking the noodles is to cool them in air while the noodles are boiling. Repeat until you see noodles become firmer, perhaps about 5 fork/chopstickfulls for the whole bowl (alot of noodles per utensil-full) and you can taste the difference.As always, eggs, garlic, ground red pepper, sri rancha(?) sauce or other condiments are good.In Korea the standard for cooked ramen would include 1egg, green onions, sometimes onions, and sometimes small dumplings.Red meats are okay to put in, but are less cost-to-taste effective when compared to hams or dumplings.

column9: great raman if you dont put as much water in it
column10: I was expecting spicy noodles and I was originally disappointed. You buy a pack of Maruchan chicken noodles and you get chicken flavored noodles. A pack of Shin noodles sits in a screaming hot spicy broth (soup?) that runs off when you pull out a bite. The noodles you get on the end of your fork are left mostly flavorless after the broth runs off. This then leaves you with a bowl of screaming hot spicy broth, not a format that I enjoy.BUT - I have found that if you don't follow their "soup" directions and instead add just enough water to hydrate the noodles you get quite a different experience, the noodles retain all the flavor and there is no broth. I just ate one of these for breakfast and I am thinking about seconds, these are really quite good in this form.I'm increasing my star rating from 3 to 4 and considering renewing my previously cancelled subscription.

This is one of the new foods that we are eating to help us lose wieght.  We are  into  spicy foods so I find these noodles to have plenty of flavor. I will experiment with the amount of the spice packet I include when cooking and see if I can come up with a happy balance These noodles are truly delicious but they are very spicy!

These noodles are truly delicious but they are really spicy! I am no stranger to spicy food but I find these noodles a bit too much for me. I will experiment with the amount of the spice packet I include when cooking and see if I can come up with a happy "medium".

These noodles are great if you like spicy food.They are seriously good and worth the slightly higher price than inferior ramen. Tip: subscribe and you get 15% off. If you don't want more in a few months it is really easy to cancel.

This is a great ramen. It contains a vegtable packet along with the soup/seasoning mix.  It is on the spicy side however in my opinion it is not over the top spicy.  Has just enough heat to be noticable and if you drink the broth you will get the full effect of the heat. These packets also make a slightly larger portion than your standard Top Ramen and Maruchan ramens. I nomrally make this with egg whites from two eggs. If you like ramen, you would not be disappointed with this product.

I've tried 20 to 30 different products - these are the best available. They are a bit salty, and spicy, but that's not always a bad thing and sometimes really hits the mark.  They are easy to make, have good instructions on the package, and are of excellent quality.  I think they are definitely worth the price, which is higher than many similar products, and can easily be doctored up a level with the addition of some onion, chive, or egg.Also, and not a small matter, they are made in USA, which I think means less concerns about food safety and labeling accuracy.Upside - taste, qualityDownside - prepackaged ramen is generally not the healthiest thing you can eat, and this product is no exception - it has 44% of the daily allowance of sodium, and 8 grams of fat, mostly palm oil.  All things in moderation!

After reading the rave reviews about these noodles for months & months.. I finally took a leap of faith and ordered me up a box... and I was not disappointed! Now, I love noodles of all kind, even the cheap ramen, but these noodles are fantastic! Definitely a more hearty texture to the noodles and the spice has got some serious kick! For those who don't like spicy, I would recommend starting with maybe 1/2 of the pack of seasoning & working your way up, but for me, the whole packet is perfect! I've been adding fresh veggies, an egg or two & some shrimp to these noodles & it makes enough for two people easily! I'm sold & will definitely continue to buy these noodles! Worth the extra $$ :)

These are absolutely amazing. The spice pack has extremely thick flavor, and the bag packs a fairly decent amount of noodles. Bit spicy for some but perfect for me. I have sampled up to 30+ different kind of bagged noodles in the past 4 years of college and these hands down top the chart. Although slightly more expensive compared to other TOP, Maruchan ramens. It is however worth the price. I'd definitely recommend these to all those want to try something slightly heavier taste.

I like the Nong Shim Shin ramen better than the much-less-expensive grocery store ramen  because Nong Shim is hot-spicy instead of just salty. You can add veggies/meat/egg/shrimp as extras and the result will still be spicy. This makes it a good sink for your least favorite veggies or leftovers.The product has a reasonable calorie to fat ratio but is not particularly low-calorie itself.Sometimes I pour out most of the water and eat the noodles and seasoning as a snack in lieu of potato chips or crackers.

column9: Love the taste.  Not crazy about the ingredients
column10: I love the taste of this product.  Great texture and a good kick.  But, I am not crazy about the ingredients.  Wish there were some natural options.

column9: Not as good as the Korean Shin
column10: This is an incredible product, and to the few reviewers who felt the noodles weren't as good as they remember them: as far as I can tell, there are two versions of Shin.  Like other reviews on here mention, I got these noodles at my local asian market and they were awesome - thick, springy noodles that put regular ramen to shame.I then saw Shin at my "regular" grocery store, and picked some up - big difference.
