column10: I CANT REVIEW THIS FOOD...BECAUSE THE KIBBLE SIZE IS  H  U  G  EUNLESS YOU HAVE A GIGANTIC DOG....I DO NOT THINK YOUR SM-MED DOG WILL WANT TO CHEW THESE! IM SO UPSET BECAUSE THEY LOVE THE CAN OF THIS WANTED TO MIX THE SAME AS CAN WITH THE DRY!

column9: Dog Health is Important to Our Dog VitaHound
column10: Our family has 2 dogs- a lab energetic and healthy named Jake, and a Terrier named VitaHound with certain health issues: VitaHound's digestive system is sensitive to typical commercial dog food.  The high grain content triggers allergic symptoms and causes him to have bad dog breath.On the recommendation of friend that has tried tried several premium dog foods and determined Wellness to be a superior brand, we started to to feed VitaHound the rice and duck formula.  VitaHound's bad dog breath disappeared and his allergic symptoms reduced to manageable.  I believe the few extra bucks is a good investment for VitaHound's dog health.
There were none left from the Wedding Candy Bar.  That says it all...Wish there had been white chocolate pretzels available.

column9: Like drinking from a young coconut, fresh off the tree!
column10: I don't get it -- everywhere I go now, mediocre coconut juice is in stores now for 5 times the price as this brand.  This brand uses young THAI coconut, which is far sweeter than the young coconut from the Caribbean and Brazil that other products use.  I am such a fanatic that I cut down several young coconuts fresh from trees while on trips to both Hawaii and Puerto Rico and those were not even as good as this product.  I've been fortunate enough to also sample fresh young coconut juice once while on a trip to Thailand and while, admittedly, this product was not quite as good as having it fresh off the tree in Thailand, it does give you an approximation of what that is like.

column9: The Best, Most Authentic Coconut Water - Amazing seller!
column10: I just got back from Thailand, and  I think I drank at least one coconut per day.  Upon my return I wanted to find something that compared to the original (it's hard to keep coconuts in the fridge!)  I thought Zico was ok, but it tasted watered down and nothing like the Thai Coconuts I was used to.  I tried Amy and Brian's on a whim at whole foods and fell in love.  It's naturally sweet, so flavorful, and I love the pulp's texture.  I was hooked.  Finding it here at an amazing price was the kicker.  I saved SO much money, which is good because I didn't think I could afford my new addiction.  Thanks for the fast, free shipping!!

The other reviewers are right: hands down the best coconut juice out there. The flavor is natural, good-bodied, and with none of that tinny after-taste you get from supermarket brands. One 17 oz can is amazingly filling and low calorie, which makes this an ideal mid-afternoon snack with none of the suspect ingredients in protein bars. With summer coming up, here's a tip: we also use Amy & Brian coconut juice in our hotel bar to mix unusual and refreshing cocktails - big hits. We prefer the version with pulp.

If you're going through chemotherapy or radiation you truly know how dry a mouth can get.  A whole body can get.  This juice was the only thing we found to alleviate that dryness.  It's slightly sweet, but not too much, making it easy to get down and stay down.  While this may not be appetizing to non-cancer sufferers, it means the world to someone going through cancer.  It's price makes it a bit prohibitive, but believe me, the cost is worth it!

I was recently introduced to coconut water and really enjoyed it, however it was one of the sugar added brands that only had 80% juice (with pulp). After some searching, I found some pure coconut water (for twice the price as the sugar added one) at a grocery store and was eager to try it only to be let down. It was decent enough, but pretty bland. There weren't other options, so I searched Amazon. Amy and Brian's was a great deal compared to the bland grocery store option and had good reviews so I ordered a case.A couple cans came slightly dented as others have mentioned, but it clearly happened during shipping and did not compromise the product in the least. When I finally opened a can, I was so excited by the amount of pulp in it (a lot!). Even better, they had the same sweetness as the sugar added ones but with a much cleaner taste. They use Thai coconuts, which are naturally sweeter than others. I love the pulp - it's really soft, so you can easily drink without chewing it. I've got a major sweet tooth but I've been working on eating better. A cup of it after dinner or throughout the day provides just enough sweetness to curb my dessert cravings, especially taking the time to chew the pulp. I definately enjoy it more at room temp too.A wonderful side effect I've noticed is it helping with dry mouth! A medication I'm on causes pretty bad dry mouth and this helps much more then those dry mouth mouthwashes. It's rehydration properties are amazing for hangovers too(or preventing/lessening them when drinking a cup before bed).

I love coconut water and juice beverages, and I've tried the majority of coconut water/juice brands out there ranging from Zico, Vita Coco, O.N.E., Harvest Bay, C20, Naked, etc. I've tried coconut juices/waters when I traveled to places such as Hawaii, South America, and Thailand. I've actually also drank straight up from real coconuts while I was in Hawaii, South America, and Thailand as well. In my humble opinion, the country that produces and makes the best coconut water and juices is Thailand. Maybe I'm a little biased because I'm Thai American, and the majority of my relatives live in Thailand. But I've traveled to Thailand many times in my life and drank coconut water and juice beverages several times while in Thailand. The Thai-based brands that Amazon currently sell are: Amy and Brian, Taste Nirvana, Nature Factor, Foco, and Chaokoh. And of course, as a Thai American, I've drank from all these Thai-based brands as well. They're all pretty good - Amy and Brian, Foco, and Chaokoh have been around for a long while when it comes to coconut drinks. Foco is a Thai-based company that make many Thai exotic drinks including dragonfruit, basil seed, mangosteen, chrysanthemum, lychee, and even pennywort. I've tried many Foco drinks over the years, and even had their canned pennywort drink in February of this year at Ha Long Bay restaurant in St. Petersburg, Florida (By the way, that Ha Long Bay restaurant has an excellent variety of delicious Boba Teas. I love Boba Teas! The best use of boba pearls I've ever seen was when my sister and I visited a Yogurtology store in St. Petersburg, Florida in early June. You get your choice of frozen yogurts self-serve style, and then you put whatever toppings you want. They had different flavored boba pearls to choose from besides fresh fruit and other dessert toppings. My sister and I thought that was a great idea, putting boba pearls on top of frozen yogurt. Yogurtology is a new chain of stores based in two states so far, Arizona and Florida, and it's such a great place, that they should have this chain nationwide!) and it was the most unusual drink I've ever had so far in my life. It tasted different and unique at first, but I read on the Internet that Pennywort/Gotu Kola is supposed to be good for your body helping strengthen your immune system, reduce arthritis, and helping alleviate other health-related issues. There's even a blog on the website, Too Many Chefs, and people have been exchanging, over several years, their opinions on what they thought about Foco's Pennywort drink. I never read that blog until after I drank the Pennywort drink in February. The reason why I chose that drink is because the name caught my attention at Ha Long Bay restaurant's menu, and I'm often the curious type who always tries my best to try something new at least once. It's kind of amusing to read people's opinions on that Pennywort drink. Chaokoh, besides their coconut drink, make the best coconut milk to cook Asian and Thai meals at home. My family uses Chaokoh coconut milk all the time to cook Thai meals, and Chaokoh also sell a lot of canned Asian/Thai items such as: rambutan, longan, bamboo shoots, sugar cane, banana blossom, and jackfruit. Taste Nirvana, of course, is known for all their coconut beverages and their Thai teas and coffees. They also sell Thai chili sauce as well. And finally, Amy and Brian are known for their excellent coconut juice beverages. Amy and Brian also sell an amazing line of mangosteen juice beverages. In the end, when it comes to the best tasting Thai coconut beverages, Amy and Brian and Taste Nirvana are tied for number one. (In fact, Thai coconut water is so good that even my favorite tea company, Harney and Sons Fine Teas, currently sell Taste Nirvana products directly from their website. They admit that they love Thai coconut water and beverages. Click on Harney and Sons' bottled beverages link on their website and you will see what I mean, and Taste Nirvana is not their own brand or product! Now that's a true testament to how excellent Thai coconut water is! I'm being really truthful when I say that you haven't really tasted good coconut water or juice if you haven't tried Amy and Brian or Taste Nirvana! I've been drinking Amy and Brian's coconut juices (with and without pulp) for many years now, and the majority of coconut waters out there don't measure up to this brand (or Taste Nirvana). You truly get your money's worth when you buy Amy and Brian's drinks.

column9: Fabulous tasting coconut water...NOT unnaturally sweet in the larger cans. YES, too sweet and AWFUL in the small cans.
column10: I was leery of trying the Amy & Brian's again after having this experience: AMAZING pulp-free tall cans. Horrible candy-water 10 oz cans. So, I have several cases of the short cans I refuse to drink. Awful. But I went through the cases of the tall cans. Wonderful.I wondered if the inconsistencies would show up in the tall cans, and I did not reorder. THEN..this big sale and sub/save showed up. Tempted me. I ordered TWO cases of this one, with the pulp.WONDERFUL. I like it even better than the pulp-free (which is weird, as I normally avoid pulp-containing packaged coconut water). I even found myself enjoying chewing the bits of pulp.The flavor is NOT too sweet, very nicely coconutty, not at all sour or weirdly salty like the new Zico, nicer than ONE and VitaCoco.So, I feel free to order more now. Clearly, there is some issue with the smaller cans. I strongly recommend you avoid those like the plague. They taste nothing like coconut water. They taste like you dropped some generic sugar candy in water and let it dissolve. Really icky sweet and NOT AT ALL coconutty. (I have had fresh out of the shell coconut water since childhood, my family being from the Caribbean, and have tasted virtually every brand available locally and on Amazon, and I know coconuts vary according to region and even harvest areas etc. Coconut water IS variable, so I don't expect homogeneous flavor. I do expect it to be coconut water and not candy water (or corn cereal milk like new Zico)). So, yeah, avoid small cans. Amy & Brian really need to look into why that stuff is disgusting, cause it's ruining their reputation whenever someone tastes that horror.The Tall Cans: Yes, buy these. I've sampled out of four different cases sent to me, always good. The pulp-free was more sweet compared to the tetra pak CW's I've tried, and the higher carb count makes sense. I even emailed the A&B people about it, and they said it was due to the blend/selection of coconuts that theirs is sweeter with a higher carb count. I can see how the selection could do this. I like the sweeter flavor, personally, but always have with meals cause it is higher carbs. When I want to drink coconut water by itself--I choose a lower carb variety, like original Zico was or ONE in a smaller quantity than the 17.5 ounce can.Thumbs up. Refreshing, sweet, coconutty, lovely. I love, love, love this coconut water in the TALL CANS.But I beg the Amyy & Brian folks to investigate and revamp the processing for the smaller cans. That stuff is vile and I have two cases plus sitting in my kitchen that I cannot drink. (Add that to the Zico I can't stomach and preordered and that's a lot of my money going to waste cause companies can't get it right/screw with a tried-true formula).Happy sipping!

Easily put, the stuff tastes good. Fresh, slightly sweetened but not overly so, coconut pulp. It's delicious.HOWEVER, I think someone had too much fun joyriding the UPS truck, because each and every one of my cans when I opened the box was dented. The cans seemed pretty tough, so not a single one broke, but it's unnerving imagining just how much punishment the box went through in order for them to get THAT bad.Also, on another note, the can itself is deceptively heavy. Every time I'm almost done drinking one, the weight of the can will trick me into thinking there's more inside. Sadness.
Surprisingly with pulp taste a lot better than without pulp one.Pulp is just few tiny pieces of coconut floating and not really much pulp.

column9: Tastes exactly like the real thing
column10: I've tried all the other coconut waters out there and I have a problem with two things. First....the coconut water itself always tastes musky and sour. Second, the packaging is completely unrecyclable. The whole point of drinking fresh natural coconut water is because it's also sustainable. But to package the water in these useless vacuum packs just adds more waste to the landfillsAmy and Brian's products, first and foremost taste EXACTLY like a fresh young coconut. There is no sour musky taste that is often associated with the vacuum packed waters. Also, ta da...the can is recyclable...a huge plus in my book.I can't say enough about this product. It's delicious, healthy, refreshing, low-calorie.
This one and Naked are the only 2 that I drink.  Shame on Vita Coco - I've tried all of their flavors, and they are all foul. A&B is my favorite, by far.

In the last couple of months, I have been on this adventure searching for the BEST and Natural coconut juice.  I have tasted many brands such as Vitacoco, O.N.E, and many other Asian brand.  Hands down Amy and Brian has the best taste out of all.  I was a firm believer Vitacoco was the best until I tried Amy & Brian.

column9: No additives, good size, good price
column10: I've tried quite a few coconut waters - all of the major brands found on Amazon in addition to imports and the like. Most canned, "affordable" coconut waters (generally, what you find at the Asian and Indian supermarkets) have a preservative in it which really affects the taste. No chemicals here, and yet they still manage to keep the price competitive versus the average $2.79 for 11-12 oz at the grocery!Judging by past personal experiences, I don't think you'll find a consistent taste in a coconut water unless the supplier mixes it all together in a giant vat or something. It's a natural product, so slight variations are to be expected. That said, I've never had a coconut water from this brand which tasted "bad". Just different.The green can has pulp, which I prefer. One reviewer who gave this a low star rating cited the inconsistency in the pulp texture - some was soft, some was harder, chewier. If you've ever cracked open a young coconut after drinking the juice to scrape the pulp out, you'll have experienced the same variations. The pulp layer within is very thin and both textures are to be expected. I don't mind it that way - it seems like more of something to expect than something to be shocked by. Don't order it expecting the pulp to be like that of oranges! Coconut pulp is its own thing.Great for doing yard work, sports, and as a substitute for pedialyte/gatorade when someone's ill (though this does have some natural sugar content).

Most of us are dehydrated & don't even realize it. The effects on our organs, therefore, is usually not seen until there's a major problem, and of course we'd like to eliminate that possibility if we can. Enter coconut water.With all the potassium contained in a single serving (I drink the whole can in two sittings per day!), and electrolytes to replenish after structured exercise, sauna sessions or anything which causes you to sweat, this is the perfect solution from nature to correct the imbalance.I anxiously awaited my order and it arrived yesterday. I immediately popped open a can (it was slightly dented but juice was clear & delicious!) & enjoyed the delicious thirst quencher. I'm going to drink it daily for health food, whether or not I get my sweat on!!PULP: Others have noted dry bits of pulp & that they found this undesirable. I purposely crunched down on many of the tiny bits of coconut meat and found it juicy & tender - perfect consistency, and I enjoyed that it's included in this coconut water.PACKAGING: The case of cans was packed VERY well with many layers of bubble wrap, then the case with cardboard base was shrink-wrapped, but there was still a dent on at least one can thus far, so it must have happened at the packing facility, which is NOT Amazon's fault. No matter. I drank it immediately & it was perfectly delicious. I've got two chilling now, and put the can back in the fridge yesterday after pouring half in the first glass, and it's delicious either way. Room temp or cold - both amazing!

column9: the best coconut juice on the market
column10: Nothing but coconut juice + coconut pulp.  Nothing added, no sugar, preservatives, stabilizers, etc.  Even if you don't care about that stuff, it is the best tasting coconut juice out there, hands down.

I am OBSESSED with this product. Honestly, my husband thinks its a problem! I live in Hawaii so it's sooo expensive here, so I have my local market order cases for me so I wont have to pay the shipping! Thanks for doin what you do, Amy and Brian! Keep on keepin' on!Wendy Taylor

This coconut water was pretty good, although i wouldn't say it's remarkably better than Zico and certainly not better than VitaCoco.  The coconut chunks varied quite a bit with quality, ranging from tender and delicious to a little too thick and tough.Also, almost all of my dozen 17.5 oz cans were dented in some way, with one can being a little too compromised for me to consider consumption.  After reasonably extensive storage in my refrigerator, all of the remaining coconut waters acquired a distinct, unpleasant metallic taste.  Maybe this should be expected with a tin storage container, but I certainly don't get unpleasant tastes with tetrapaks and plastic bottles after extended refrigeration.Despite the overall pleasant drinking experience, I doubt I will be ordering again.

column9: Yummy & refreshing taste, healthful, a little expensive!
column10: UPDATE (10/9/12):I asked the company on Facebook about how much magnesium and potassium are in each can, since it is not listed even though the can advertises having lots of both (?). Their reply was "about 676 mg Potassium and 29.12 mg Magnesium."---It seems that coconut water is one of those love-or-hate flavors that exist in the world (kind of like avocado).  There doesn't seem to be a middle ground, either you really dislike it, or really like it.I'm definitely in the really-like camp. And I had to get to this brand to discover that. I had tried both Vita Coco 100% Pure Coconut Water, 11.1-Ounce Containers (Pack of 12) and O.N.E. Coconut Water, 11.2-Ounce Aseptic Containers (Pack of 12), and found both of them insipid tasting.  But I find this brand refreshing and full of body.I compare the difference between "good" and "bad" coconut water to the difference between apple juice from concentrate and not from concentrate.  The former has a watery taste, like it's not the real thing, whereas the latter is more like drinking an apple.This brand seems more like drinking a coconut (although that's something I've never done). But it doesn't have the icky blandness to it that the above brands have.I also really enjoy the bits of coconut pulp, they had to the experience and taste.This makes a great base for powder mixes, especially flavored ones like Vega Whole Food Shake & Go Smoothie - Tropical Tango - 300g - Powder and Sequel Naturals Vega Shake and Go Smoothie Bodacious Berry -- 10.6 oz, and even Garden of Life Perfect Food Raw Organic Powder Nutritional Supplement, 240 Grams.It's also great to drink as-is, straight from the can, as both a pre- and post-hydrator.  I often drink half the can before a work-out and the other half after I'm done. If you research, it is best to pre-hydrate so your body has the extra fluids/minerals readily available as they are being depleted, rather than only hydrating after you are exhausted and dehydrated.This 12-pack will last you a long time, especially considering each can is two servings (~2 cups).
I ordered this for the 3rd time. The first and second time I liked it and the 3rd time was disgusting. I can taste the tin can, and the pulp tasted old. I never leave feedback, but this was so gross.

This is a great product; all natural with no preservative. However, it's gotten so much more expensive than what I see in the Asian grocery. If price goes even higher, I'll probably switch to the less expensive ones even if they don't taste as well as long as they don't have preservatives.

Amy and Brian and Taste Nirvana are the only two brands of coconut water I like. Both taste much sweeter and have a stronger coconut flavor/aroma than the rest I have tried. As to the drink being unnaturally sweet I frequently purchase young Thai coconuts at my grocery and the water tastes just as sweet. The price on Amazon is a little higher than locally available to me ($2 per can). The pulp pieces can be a little harder, but I enjoy chewing on them and feel like getting a meal.I like the way coconut water makes me feel and frequently drink one in the morning instead of coffee. It may be a sugar rush, but I definitely feel refreshed after that and the feeling lasts quite a while. Overall good product and tastes just as good as water you just got from a coconut.

I have been drinking Vita Coco for a while, but took a chance on a can of this the last time I dropped by Whole Foods. So glad to see it here, because it is excellent! The pulp is very tasty!!I have tried all the major brands of coconut water and this is the best by far.
i think all the brands out there charge too much, but i love the taste on amy and brian's the best -- not too "green" and not to sweet, just right!

I love the Amy and Brian Coconut Juice as an after workout refresher.  I do CrossFit which is a high intensity workout program.  This juice is great for rehydrating and it has tons of potassium to help with muscle recovery.  What sets this coconut juice apart from most other coconut juices you find in the grocery store is that it doesn't have any added sugar.  I'm very into eating natural foods and this juice is just 100% coconut juice, nothing added whatsoever.  There are other brands out there which are similar that I haven't tried so I can't compare this to others but I can say this brand has a great taste.  I also like the pulp but other people who have tried it say they prefer the non-pulp cans, it's just a matter of personal preference I guess.  Enjoy!

The only thing wrong I found with this product is that after a week and a half in my fridge, a couple of cans started tasting "rusty" and the water and pulp were slightly pinkish in color when poured in a glass. Otherwise, when it doesn't do that, it tastes wonderful! The size is perfect for when you're extra thirsty. Very refreshing.

THIS IS THE BEST QUALITY COCONUT JUICE I HAVE TASTED!  THERE ARE OTHERS OUT THERE THOUGH.THIS PARTICULAR JUICE IS FROM YOUNG COCONUTS, A HUGE DIFFERENCE IN FLAVOR, IT'S SWEET.MANY OTHER BRANDS TASTE SOMEWHAT SOUR OR TANGY.  ALSO READ THE LABEL THERE IS NO PRESERVATIVE JUST JUICE!EVERY LABEL THAT I'VE READ ON THE MANY OTHER BRANDS OF COCONUT JUICE FOUND IN STANDARD GROCERY STORES HAVE PRESERVATIVES.I HAVE FOUND ONLY THE HEALTH FOODS STORES, WHOLE FOODS AND AMAZON CARRY THIS BRAND SO I PURCHASE BY THE CASE.ALSO WHOLE FOODS GIVES A 10 PERCENT DISCOUNT ON ANYTHING BOUGHT BY THE CASE, THEY ARE ACTUALLY QUITE COMPETITIVE.COCONUT JUICE IS ALSO SLIGHLTY ALKALINE, I HAVE ACTUALLY TESTED IT WITH THE SMALL METER THAT TESTS ACIDIC / ALKALINE LIQUIDS.WHENEVER I'VE BEEN OVERHEATED OR AM JUST REALLY HOT FROM BEING OUTSIDE, I DRINK ABOUT 6-8 OZ AND IT REVIVES ME.SINCE LIVING IN THIS WARM WEATHER, I'VE BOUGHT SEVERAL BOOKS ON THE BENEFITS OF COCONUT, I READ THAT DURING WAR TIMES COCONUT WATER HAS BEEN USED AS BLOOD PLASMA WHEN NEEDED.HAVE NOT VERIFIED THIS INFO FOR MYSELF BUT INTERESTING, NATURE DOES PROVIDE.

column9: amazing! addictive in a good way
column10: This is THE BEST coconut water out there. I have tried the tetra packs and they taste gross. Not as naturally sweet. I also LOVE the chunks! I could drink 2 or more of these a day- wish it was a little cheaper, but the Thai coconuts DO make a difference so it worth it.

column9: Love this stuff -- no extra ingredients
column10: I also first tried this at Whole Foods and was hooked immediately.  The taste is just like the freshly cut young coconuts you get while vacationing an island.  Take a look at the ingredients... it's just coconut juice and pulp.  Many of the other drinks have sugars, preservatives, water, etc... I have it on auto-ship 2 times a month!

column9: Pricey, so try to get it while it's on sale
column10: This was ridiculously delicious: I've tried Vita and Naked versions of coconut water/juice and they weren't as good.I like how there is some pulp inside- not sure how environmentally friendly the can is.

As a Whole Foods employee I have tried several different brands of Coconut Juice, but none compare to Amy and Brian. This product only lists two ingredients; young coconut juice and young coconut pulp, yet it's so sweet and delicious. The pulp adds a nice little bit of coconut to the beverage that is a nice little snack. I don't know what else to say but to try this stuff! I'm not even really a fan of coconut but this juice is great.

column9: The REAL Coconut Juice, the Healthier Alternative to Coconut Juice BLENDS with Sugar added.
column10: If you have never drank coconut juice fresh from the coconut, you are missing one of Natures most refreshing drinks.  If your only experience is drinks served at Asian restaurants, you need to know - this is NOT the same thing.  Most places sell the cheaper - with sugar and water added - version of this drink.  I am so happy that AMY & BRIAN have stuck with the more expensive PURE coconut juice.It is definitely less sweet.  It will quench your thirst better.  You won't have to worry about the extra calories.  It's the real thing.  You will not want to share the can, so be sure to count all of the 2 servings of calories.I used to buy this by the case on Amazon, but sadly the price went way up (from $18) and I got cases with dented and leaking cans.  So $$ was not worth it.  I can not find it locally, and so am suffering with the sugary stuff again.  I wish the price would come down and shipping did not kill the cans.

We have sampled a good number of different coconut juices from different companies and these Amy & Brian juices are the best, hands down. A number of the other brands had a bitter taste and/or after taste, or seemed watered down (lacked flavor). Amy & Brian's juice is sweet through and through, no nasty after taste, and reasonably priced.The only thing I think they could do better is to package the juice in a better container. It is somewhat annoying to drink the juice from the can due to the "tinny" taste and because the pulp pieces zip through the small opening, which is disconcerting. I just pour it out into a glass and enjoy it fully that way. Another brand we tried had a glass, wide-mouth container which was easy to drink from and cool because you can see the pulp pieces suspended in the drink. If Amy & Brian adopted packaging like that, it would improve the product by a lot!Still though, despite the packaging, this is THE BEST coconut juice out there that we have tried.

column9: So delicious!  Best tasting coconut juice I've tried (other than directly from coconuts)
column10: I've tried a handful of coconut juices and -- in comparison with Amy and Brian's coconut juice -- they've ranged from meh to eh?!  For instance, the vitacoco juice has a slightly acidic/bitter tinge to it.But this Amy and Brian's coconut juice just tastes awesome!  And I love the little pieces of coconut.  Some may find it a bit awkward to "chew their juice" in a way, but I like the texture.  And the juice is sweet without being cloyingly so, with no odd aftertaste.I do wish this stuff was cheaper.  I could easily go through two cans a day, and that's a lotta moolah a month :. So for now, I'm saving it for after or before boot camp workouts.But, despite the cost, I'll likely order this again.  Wonderfully refreshing!(CAVEAT:  Do keep in mind that this isn't exactly a "diet" beverage.  The 17.5 ounce can (which contains two servings) does contain 152 calories, which is about 9 calories per ounce.  But compare that against, say, Coke, which not only has a ton more (non-naturally-occurring) sugar and pretty much no nutritive value at all, but also packs 33% more calories per ounce.  Or orange juice, which has *66%* more calories per ounce :-o.

This is the best coconut water I've tasted.  The pulp is a little chunkier than I expected, which is not a problem for me, but if you don't think you'd like that you might want to try the pulp-free version.  Naked is a close second to this brand, and I do buy that in aseptic packs since the cans aren't always as convenient.  But there is no metalic taste with these cans.

column9: Great taste, natural, no added sugars
column10: Was looking for coconut juice that's not from concentrate and has no added sugars, but is still tasty. This one fits the bill perfectly!

column9: I love It at the 1st drink.
column10: It s better than Zico  because it 's less sodium .I gonna order more.After 3th order I am sure it s the best taste coconut water but my digest system did not go along with the hard chunks (coconut juice with pulp), so my next orderis Amy&Brian coconut juice without pulp.Overall The tall cans are the best canned coconut juice today and you can find it on Amazon.com only with free shipping.It is the best price too.

column9: Taste like it is straight from the coocnut
column10: I could not believe how much this juice tasted just like the coconut water I had from the coconut, no aftertast just pure and refreshing - will buy over and over again!

I ordered the "All Natural Coconut Juice with pulp" & found it rather disappointing...The watertaste a bit stale & the hard chunks of coconut are a big turn off ..I thought that the can would have soft jelly... I know about coconuts & the correct taste, because I grew up with many coconut trees....I was expecting much more....I read the reviews & liked what I read...Another problem all the cans have dents in themthat could be the fault of the delivery service. or distribution center....I also paid for "NEXT DAY" delivery and item wasdelivered in 2 days...(2 days is FREE!)I will not be re-ordering this product...

column9: Not great but I prefer Taste Nirvana
column10: This isn't bad but it isn't anything spectacular. I've tried this and Taste Nirvana's brand and honestly I prefer Taste Nirvana because it tastes more natural.

The first case I received was great! The water was sweet and refreshing and the pieces of coconut (pulp) were tender a few harder pieces here and there, but that didn't really bother me. I liked it enough to go with the "subscribe & save" and had a case delivered every month, that was until this last case came in. The water was great as usual, but the pulp was HORRIBLE the pieces of coconut were very soft and mealy. They didn't really taste bad, it was just the texture, yuk! And it wasn't just a can or two, but the whole case. After about 3-4 being like that, I canceled my subscription. If I were you I would skip the pulp.

I read many rave reviews of this product which is what prompted me to purchase Amy & Brian over other brands.  I love fresh coconut water, coconut milk and coconut pulp but this product didn't resemble any of those.  It didn't really taste like coconut at all and the after taste is unpleasant. I bought it to use as a sports drink for our children but they won't drink it and I can't say I blame them.  Even if I take away the expectations of coconut I can't imagine choosing to drink this.  If you are thinking of buying this product I would find someplace to buy a single can and try it first, wish I had.

I'm an avid coconut water drinker - I've tried most brands sold by Whole Foods and Trader Joe's and this brand is always consistent (flavor/color/freshness). If you enjoy coconut water you need to give this brand a try ...you won't be disappointed.
This is the best coconut juice water I've ever had. My husband and I tried a lot of other name brands and will never try anyothers again. Amy&Brians are the ones

This coconut water tastes good and is well priced. The best thing about it is that the taste is consistent. Many company's coconut water does not taste good on a consistent basis. I have tried many different coconut waters and this is my favorite. I also really like the little pieces of coconut meat in it. For anyone new to coconut water make sure whichever one you get that there is no added sugar. There is a lot of coconut water out there that has added sugar, aside from it being unhealthy coconut water does not need it. Natural coconut water has a slightly sweet pleasant taste.

Some of the cans did show up a little dented, but that didn't compromise the product in the slightest. Amy & Brian is the best Coconut Juice on the market. By purchasing a subscription instead of going to my local CoOp, I'm saving a $1.20 per can. After my 2 cases ran out I bought some VitaCoco to hold me off until my next shipment and it paled in comparison.I just upped my shipment to 3 cases at a time and will probably push it to 4 cases next month.

column9: Good qualities overshadowed by odd taste
column10: I pitted this against another leading brand of coconut water, but I'm not sure I would order it again. While there were undoubtedly some positive tasting qualities, likely owing to good practices and Thai sourced coconuts, these were considerably overshadowed by a metallic taste. I could only say I've known this taste before in... SpaghettiO's. Texture wise the pulp was also mushier, which has the benefit of a higher ratio of the rich, buttery bits, but I'm left wanting a hint of crunch somewhere. That's to be expected from young coconuts though, sought for their fruit rather than the mature nut. I favor a mix, which I at least believe I've found in two other brands. Another problem I found was these arrived in quite bad shape, the cans were variously dinged and punched in. The other guys' cans were too, except those were pressurized and so held up better. The real drawback for me was these practically require refrigeration. Now I'm well aware most people don't like room temperature coconut water, but I actually prefer it and regret to say I found Amy & Brian's too unpalatable to enjoy naturally.

its ok but still not good as taste of nirvana coconut drink. i wonder why amy and brian use young coconut? young cococnut is not ripe. if you like really coconut taste i highly recommend taste of nirvana.

column9: very fresh and nice... better than other brands
column10: i tried this after trying some f the other brands and found it to be naturally more sweet and tastful compared to others. its slightly more expensive but i think its worth it for the nice taste.
We order these as if we needed them to survive.  No added sugar, just juice and pulp, and still plenty sweet.  One of our favorite coconut juices we have found.

This is the best tasting coconut juice around.  It is so addicting that I cannot just drink one can; I have to drink at least 2.  It provides potassium and magnesium which are both necessary for our bodies.  I must be low on those nutrients because as soon as I take a sip of the juice, my body just craves and craves more.  Its not even the same craving as for sweets or junk food.  Its like my body is saying this is just what I needed and just sucks it down!  Yumm.  I enjoy the coconut juice with pulp because the one without pulp seems to taste odd to me. But try it out, you won't regret it.  Your body will thank you for the magnesium and potassium!
I love this coconut water it taste a lot like C20 water and is cheaper too. I just bought 3 cases.. Im hooked

I am a relative new comer to the world of coconut water, and as such have not had a lot of experience with the variety of waters available. column9: Maybe if stranded on an Island?
column10: Stopped in Fresh Market for some things in Destin, FL new to Florida all together. This was the only brand I had yet to try. I have to be honest Nirvana Coconut water has this beat by far. column9: Excellent product!  No sugar, but naturally sweet!
column10: These cans are the right size for a smoothie in the morning and a refreshing drink later.  I bought the version with pulp and I love the crunchy pieces, but not the other pieces.  I will get the pulp free version next.  But this is the best coconut juice/water I have ever tried.  I will definitely be ordering more with my subscription.  Can't beat the price either.

column9: My sons can't get enough of this coconut water!!!
column10: My boys (13 & 14) absolutely love this coconut water.  They have tried less and more expensive brands and nothing compares.  The health benefits are wonderful and this is why I don't get too upset when they drink 2 to 3 a day.  We joke about my oldest son having withdrawals when we run out.  It is just a top quality product.

column9: Amy & Brian Natural Coconut Juice with pulp
column10: Yummy.  I like this coconut juice very much.  I drink about 2 cans a day and I'm happy to have it for my grandchildren when they are here.  There's only benefit to drinking coconut water so it pleases me that we all enjoy it so much.  I'm thrilled to have found it available through Amazon.com..

I love this coconut juice so much I asked for a case of it for my birthday. I'm now panicking because I have only nine cans left. This is by far the most refreshing beverage in existence, not to mention probably one of the best for you.

This coconut water tastes almost identical to that of the water from a freshly opened young coconut.I found the sweetness, texture, and taste of Amy&Brian's coconut water to be nearly indistinguishablefrom that of a freshly opened coconut.  Purchase if searching for authentic coconut water without thehassle of opening up one yourself.

column9: AMY & BRIAN NATURAL COCONUT JUICE WITH PULP
column10: This coconut juice is without a doubt the BEST coconut juice I have ever tasted.  It  comes in a great size--17.5 ounces, it is just sweet enough to be refreshing, and I love the pulp.  Aside from tasting so great, coconut juice is a great hydrator.  I like it so much I am having it shipped to my home monthly.

column9: Best  tasting coconut water on the market
column10: Really love this product. Tried it at my daughters and couldn't find it where I live so ordered it from Amazon.  To save money I tried the automatic shipment.  Really like that too.  They always e-mail about a week before they ship and to give an opportunity to cancel. It has been 3 months now and I still look forward to the shipment as I am always out!

column9: Best coconut juice. Love the pulp!
column10: I am surprised how many people like the pulp! My friends tell me its like having a meal. I always feel great after enjoying a can of coconut juice!  Thanks Amy and Brian

Just got through a case of Amy & Brian's Natural Coconut Juice and it's flat out great.  Other Coconut waters and juices I have tried are so bland and tasteless.  A&B has some flavor to it and the bits of pulp are nice to chew on.  Bottom line give it a try and you won't be going back to your old Coconut drink.
Easily the next best thing to drinking straight from young coconuts. I was curious because I've never had coconut juice that includes pulp and now I don't think I can go back to pulpless.

column9: Does NOT taste like milk from a bowl that had corn flakes!
column10: Try all of the coconut juice beverages out there, and more and more, they are becoming to taste like the milk that is left over from your bowl that had corn flakes in it.This is the best tasting to date. Not artifically sweet tasting, but actually quite good. Slightly sweet, naturally, but not artifically with sugar.Get the type with pulp.Only negative I could say is that nearly every single can is dented. I have tried a few different coconut waters and I was very impressed with the flavor of this completely natural one, the perfect amount of natural sweetness.  Great value.  I crave one after a long run!

We have been trying different coconut juices for quite some time and since we have tried Amy & Brian's we have not been buying other brands. We also like the coconut chunks that give the juice an even better texture.

I drink a lot of coconut water and have tried all the various brands. A chef friend steered me to this brand. I like it. No spoiled or rancid taste as I've found with some brands; slightly sweet but none of that overly sweetened sugary taste from many of the canned products that are on the market. I very much enjoy the pulp. I like that it comes in a can I can recycle (I can't recycle drink boxes in my neighborhood).

I love this product.  It does not have any added sugar and has more potassium than a banana.  This one has pulp in it which is like little pieces of the flesh cut up into small cubes like 1/4 in by 1/4 of inch(easy to swallow).  They sell a pulp free version if texture is an issue for you.  Best served cold, Coconut juice is refreshing and tasty.

My husband and I had tested almost all the coconut waters out there and Amy and Brian's is the best. I grew up in Hawaii where fresh coconut water/juice is a staple. This is by far the closest to fresh out of the nut coconut juice. We're addicted.

column9: acquired taste, try it a few times before you decide
column10: i love this product.  the first time i had coconut water (zico) i did not see what the hype was about because it was salty, bland, and a strange thick consistency.  i tried this next and found the flavor to be better but still nothing i would crave.  the third time i had it, i truly enjoyed it - extremely refreshing.  i've had a couple others since; some have preservatives or sweeteners, some from concentrate.  this is simply the best bang (taste/nutrition/quantity) for your buck.  i drink it chilled after a workout and often blend it with fruit for a smoothie.  highly recommended with or without pulp.
Great flavor with a bit of actual coconut. Only coconut water brand I have found without added sugar.
We have tried other coconut water products (Zico and Vita Coco) but this one tastes more natural.

column9: Almost like putting a straw in a coconut
column10: This is the closest I've ever gotten that's not straight from a coconut.  Still not 100% the same, but at least 97% :)  I personally prefer it at room temp (65-70 degrees), when I think the flavor is the best, but my husband likes it cold, so I think people should try it both ways.

column9: Healthy and Refreshing, Gotta Try It
column10: I recently got into drinking coconut juice.  I tend to be health conscious so I started using coconut juice in the smoothies that I make.  It adds such a light, refreshing and delicious zing to my smoothies.  Since discovering Amy & Brian's coconut juice, I love to drink it straight as well.  My favorite are the ones with the pulp.  They are a great alternative to sports drinks because of the amount of potassium inside and don't have any artificial sweeteners or colors.  I drink them after exercising and they help me from getting sore afterward.  I recommend this drink to everyone I know and they're surprised how good it tastes.  It's become as good as gold in my home lately.  Next time you're in the grocery store and see one of these, put it in your cart and remember that your body thanks you.

Based on reviews, I ordered this bigger size because I read the smaller size had a weird taste. I was happy with some although there are some cans that had a weird taste. I went abroad and since I was enrolled in the auto delivery I received the second batch while I was away. I figured maybe the first batch was just a bad batch but once I opened the first can of the second batch, I still had that taste. Being from the Caribbean and living in Washington DC, I've been going through different products to see if I could find something close to the original. Well, I haven't tried all the products out there, but this weekend I saw this in a local food store and was sooo happy to see that it's sweet and good, not the awful artificially flavored ones that I've tried, even if it said 100% natural they tasted awful.Haven't compared prices but it looks like it's cheaper buying from here.

column9: Way too sweet for my tastes
column10: I gave this one a shot when it was on sale and while I definitely couldn't complain about the price the taste was a little too sweet for my liking. I did like the pulp in the can, but when trying to down one of these a day I just couldn't do it. By the time I got through the entire 12 pack I could no longer bear the thought of having to drink the rest of them. This isn't to say that the product wasn't decent and I might be inclined to want to drink it again, once in a blue moon, i.e., very rarely; it just didn't have the same light refreshing properties that I have perviously found in other brands.As a once a month treat I could find myself enjoying this, but the overly sweet taste makes me refrain from wanting to consume anymore.

column9: Unnaturally sweet; far more carbs than others
column10: I found the pulp to be uncomfortably large chunks, that settled on the bottom. I also found this to be unnaturally sweet. (I have tried many different coconut waters; both packaged and fresh from the coconut.) The product lists far more carbs than any other packaged coconut water I have tried. Given these two things, I'm thinking it's likely this product is boiled, or otherwise condensed.  This may be good for those weaning off sugary beverages, but if you are looking for a coconut water that tastes like fresh from the coconut, this is not it.

column9: Yuck ! Will stick to vita brand
column10: I have now tried them all and choose vita coconut water. This stuff and all the others taste terrible ! Vita is way more expensive but so much better and well worth it!

Amy & Brian's coconut juice is fantastic.  There are only two ingredients in the Pulp variety: young coconut juice and young coconut pulp!  It seems they must have filtered out the coconut fat at some point in the process, because there's no fat content.Definitely a good buy when it's on sale.  I think I'll try one of the pulp-free versions next time (maybe the one with lime).  I do like pulp, but the little cubes were too heavy to float as well as orange pulp--I had to give it a quick stir or shake to set the cubes in motion before drinking.I placed these in my fridge and always looked forward to having a tall, cool glass of coconut juice!

column9: Did not care for this coconut water
column10: Since O.N.E changed their formulae or process or something and has started tasting awful, I have been on the lookout for a different brand. I love eating the tender coconut pulp, so was excited about this product. The "pulp" is not really tender for most part and is some sort of diced coconut flesh. I didn't care for it and that meant that I'd have to strain the water to drink it. My search is still on
Product was good,but each an every can was crushed on the last two orders.i would not purchase it again for that reason.

column9: Delicious Coconut Juice but Dented Cans, Thick Pulp Pieces
column10: Juice by itself is delicious - the best coconut water out of the brands I have tasted (Zico, O.N.E., and VitaCoco).  Very pulp-y, which would be fine if the pieces were not so thick.  Took off another star for the severely dented cans. 9 of the 12 cans were dented, 7 were dented so much at the seam that I have chosen to discard them rather than risk drinking.  Would like to try pulp-free version, but nervous about the dented cans. Will stick with VitaCoco until can issue is resolved.

column9: Nice but I didn't get impressed by the coconut bits
column10: It's nice, but not my kind since I like soft coconut cream, not dried coconut bits in the water.

This is really fake tasting and overly sweet.  The chunks inside the drink to not help either.  This is almost as bad as the Goya ones you see at the supermarket.  No recommended at all.  Try Vita Coco or Naked.

column9: good but not the very tasty
column10: This is good as it doesnt have any sugars added. However i found young brand coconut juice better, it does have sugars added though.

Wheat ChexI never imagined that our cereal would some day be delivered via UPS.  But, since Amazon's free-shipping price is lower than our local Safeway's nearly five dollars per box, that's where we get it.Pros:- It tastes great, even with the non-fat milk we've been using forever.- Dry cereals made from wheat are much more filling than those made from corn, rice, or oats.  I have to eat twice as much to be full, if the cereal is made from those grains.- It stays reasonably crunchy the entire meal, and I have a big bowl every morning.- It stays fresh in an opened box; although at the rate it's consumed around here, that's usually not very long.- It stays fresh in an unopened box for many months.- Good daily dose of fiber, although that's not the reason I eat it.- If you are a regular Wheat Chex customer, save 15% through Amazon's "Subscribe & Save" offer; prominently displayed on the product page.Cons:- The inner bags used to be easy to open by hand, but the geniuses at General Mills now seal the plastic liner so completely, you'll need to cut it open.- Three decent-sized bowls of cereal is all that's in a box.  The smaller the package, the higher the cost per ounce of cereal.  I.e., if the box was 50% bigger, even though the box would cost slightly more, the cost per ounce of product should be less.  Apparently, General Mills is afraid sales would lag if a "box" of Wheat Chex cost any more.I've been eating this stuff for 50 years.  When I travel to a foreign country, one of the things I miss is this cereal.

Wheat Chex: wonderful product, if you are a deep wheat lover, but hard to find these days, especially at a good price.  The prompt delivery and reasonable price entailed in Amazon purchase are both very welcome.

column9: Great product at a great price!

column9: Best-tasting "major brand" cereal, but too little per box

Well, I was looking through the international food section in my local grocery store and I found these three-packet bags of Marukome Miso Soup Mix. All you needed to do was take one of the small packets and add a cup of hot water, stir and enjoy. So easy. Well, I was disappointed. It just didn't mark up. Well, what did I expect? column9: I like it, but flavor may be polarizing
column10: I can imagine that this cola flavor will have ratings all over the place, because it does not taste like most colas available. It doesnt even taste like the other Sodastream colas available (diet or regular). Most other colas will taste very similar to Coke or Pepsi, depending on which flavor profile the generic is modeling itself after.  This cola, however, tastes nothing like either and seems to have a unique flavor profile relative to the ones I've tried.  Its hard for me to pinpoint exactly what the differences are, but I believe that there is a less emphasis on the citrus flavors and more on the vanilla and cinnamon flavors.  I also notice a slight caramel flavor which is not typical of commonly available colas.  I don't think there is a shortcut way to find out if you'll like this... you'll just have to try it out.

column9: Tastes like a fruitier version of Coke
column10: I've tried all of Sodastream's regular sodamix flavors, and they're made with artificial sweeteners so I don't think they taste very good.This flavor (natural cola) is quite good. It doesn't have any artificial sweetener taste, and it has a nice cola flavor. Now, it definitely doesn't taste like Coke or Pepsi. I'd describe it as a fruitier Coke, provided that you use slightly less than the recommended portion to make the drink. And I think that's something worth mentioning: you can vary the level of sweetness by slightly altering how much of the mix you pour in to the bottle of carbonated water.I was pleasantly surprised by this flavor, I would definitely buy it again.

I've had the SodaStream SodaMix - Cola before, and it was fine. It tasted like someone mixed a diet soda with a regular one with the slight aftertaste of sucralose, but it wasn't that bad, and the SodaStream SodaMix - Caffeine Free Root Beer was one of the best root beers I've ever had even WITH that aftertaste. I gambled on the Natural Cola, hoping it would taste like the regular one but without that aftertaste, but boy was I wrong. It tastes like you took some apple juice and mixed it with cola.(The natural rootbeer, incidentally, is freaking awesome - it IS the  SodaStream SodaMix - Caffeine Free Root Beer without the aftertaste. So my order was only half fail, ha. Amazon apparently doesn't sell it.)

column9: It can taste really good!! But you need the right recipe!!
column10: This cola is really good! Yep, I gave it five stars!There's really only one thing to consider here, and that is cost. I'll get to that in a minute.So why do I think the reviews are all over the place? For one, everyone has different tastes. If we gave "real" Coke or Pepsi to 10 people, you will get many people who hate it. I like Pepsi Throwback myself, but to each his own. So yes, some people will hate this syrup. I'm not going to disagree with someone else's taste buds!But let me try to help those who have tried this and thought it wasn't very good. I can relate. Because that's what I thought at first too! Why? The answer is simple. The recipe on the bottle is really not very good.The recipe calls for 1 cap full of syrup and 6 "buzzes" of carbonation. I highly recommend you try 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 cap fulls of syrup to 6 buzzes or even 7 buzzes. I like 7, but 6 was okay as well. Coke and Pepsi are VERY sweet. I thought about this, and added the extra syrup. The difference is like night and day. The additional syrup makes this taste much better to me, and much closer to what Coke tastes like.Now, one selling point Sodastream tries to make is cost. "25 cents per 2 liter!". Well this syrup, with the Natural Can Sugar, is twice the cost at major retailers of the standard Cola (the one that has Sucralose and Sugar). When you add in the extra syrup with my recommended recipe, you really aren't getting that much soda. I think I can get 6 liters of soda out of this with the new recipe. For $10 cost on the syrup alone, that's some expensive soda!But really, Sodastream for us is not about saving money. It's about kids and family having fun making their own soda. The novelty might wear off, sure, but we have given up worrying about the saving money part and are just enjoying the unit for the fun of creating our own sodas.PROS: Tastes great. Made only with natural sugars.CONS: Recipe needs to be altered to taste. If you use more syrup like I do, you aren't saving money versus buying Coke or Pepsi.Bottom line: this syrup tastes good if you alter the recipe and make your soda sweeter than called for on the bottle. If you aren't concerned with saving money on your soda and just with having fun with your creations, this is still a good buy.

When you're out for dinner at a casual restaurant where you'll likely order a burger and a Coke and your server asks "is Pepsi okay?" What do you respond with?  If your answer is "Sure, Pepsi will do," or something along those lines, then you'll find this SodaStream Natural Cola syrup to be just fine.  It is not a Coca-Cola substitute.  It is along the lines of Pepsi in the glass bottle from Mexico which is made with cane sugar instead of high fructose corn syrup.  It's not as good as Pepsi hecho en Mexico, but it's not gross and disgusting like others make it out to be.I enjoy craft pop like most people enjoy craft beer.  Some of it is awesome, like Coke from Mexico and many of the Boylan and Goose Island flavors, and a lot of it isn't too good, like the under-mixed, under-flavored store brands that are only marginally less expensive than the national brands.  Being that this is my first experience with home-mixed pop, I'm delighted that it was much better than a store-brand.Mixing pop at home is not more economical than buying a case of Coke when it's on sale, but it certainly is a lot more fun, it's "greener," and you get to try a ton more flavors than you're used to.  It is about the same price as pop from the specialty items section, however, so if you're the explorer type, then you'll enjoy trying new syrups.
I love coke, but this stuff is great. If you want Coke than go buy a coke. If you want a great cola with no corn syrup or caramel coloring than this is for you. Also goes great with Jack!

I don't like the flavor of the regular sodastream mixes but I quite enjoy this natural cola.  I agree with another reviewer in that it doesn't taste quite like coke or pepsi, but I do think it tastes like RC.  And it's delicious.

column9: Closest thing to Mexican Coke on tap at home
column10: The flavor of this cola is a bit more herbal, kind of reminds me of Boylan's Cane Sugar Soda. If you are looking for something syrupy sweet you probably won't enjoy this. It is definitely more expensive than Soda Stream's usual reduced-sugar mix offerings, and also requires double the amount of carbonation to your water (5-6 buzzes). But definitely high quality and well-worth the money.

column9: Coca Cola clone, yeah it's that close.
column10: The fact that this is made with cane sugar actually has very little to do with how good it tastes, or how much it tastes like Coca Cola. If you find it is a touch sweet, you can a. try using a little less syrup! And honestly, I suggest that you try this anyway because the cap this bottle comes with is huge. Or, b. try using more CO2 when you are carbonating your water. If neither of these suit you then c. doing both should help a lot.I like this flavour a lot. If you really want the closest thing to Coca Cola, this is as close as you will get without spending more for a huge cannister of actual Coca Cola syrup, the kind sold to stores and restaurants. For the price, I think most people will find this more suitable.As a final note I will say that although I love this flavour, I tend to prefer the other Cola syrup, the one that comes in a white bottle--even if only for its lower price. The breakdown to take away from these two types of soda (because I know this is why you are here), this Cola syrup tastes like Coca Cola, and the white (cheaper) bottle tastes almost exactly like RC Cola.
not at all like Coke or Pepsi.......too sweet and too acidic at the same time,...............and little flavor.store brand cola is better.

I agree with another reviewer who said there aren't any shortcuts to knowing whether you'll like it. You'll just have to try it. Our whole family loves it and we prefer it over the two leading brands. Before we got the machine I drank Diet Dr. Pepper almost exclusively. I don't like the Diet Dr. Pete version. I think it's because I want it to be exactly the same and it's just not. My husband thinks it's great and he only drank DP occasionally. It could be that it's the same with this, if you drink one of the two leading brands almost exclusively you might not like it. I think you should give it a shot anyway.

This is 'my' opinion of this product.  I'm going off of what 'my' taste buds is telling me.  I won a Sodastream soda maker off of eBay and was excited.  Give me corn syrup and corn fructose.  I never liked that fake sweetener taste like aspartame and sucralose.  Those are some of the most unpleasant tasting sweeteners I've ever had.  I'm a huge Pepsi drinker and the price of Pepsi keeps skyrocketing so I decided I can make my own pop at home.  I wanted something that taste like Pepsi.  Until I can afford to buy Pepsi syrup this natural cola mix will have to do.  If anybody is looking to make their own pop and like the Coca Cola taste this will suffice you.

I was very excited to find a cola syrup that was not artificially sweetened, and did not have high fructose corn syrup in it.  As for the seller, delivery was prompt and price was reasonable.  I definitely appreciate the seller's part of this, but I must say, the product is so-so.  It has a different taste to it; and is not an authentic cola taste.  For some reason, the taste seems to almost rob the cola of its carbonation.  That said, it is not super sweet, which is nice; and, it has no awful after-taste.  I don't think I would buy this product again; it depends what other naturally flavored colas I find out there.

column9: Cane Sugar makes a Huge Difference
column10: This Naturally sweetened version, though more expensive and making fewer bottles of cola is very very good.  It's almost a dead ringer for a certain famous brand in a red bottle.  That said, it costs a lot to make as you only get 6 liters with one bottle of mix.  The old version was not liked in our household.  Found this in a local store and gave it a try and were pleasantly surprised.  Quality ingredients, quality product.  Wish it was more reasonably priced because 2 dollars a liter is a bit steep.

I purchased mine at Target, but the cost there is comparable to Amazon's pricing. This definitely does NOT taste like Coke. If that is what you base your tastes upon, please stay away from this. If you have an open mind to something along the lines of a Pepsi or an RC Cola or even a Cola generic branded drink, I think you will be happy as this taste like.It has a fruity essence to it without the sharp bitter edge that Coke has. Kind of like a softened soft drink of Coke. Very pleasing to the palette if you ask me.If you're looking for a cost effective solution to having your own cola drink, then this is the way to go.

column9: finally got  rid of the splenda
column10: very good,  I pretty much stopped using my machine because all the syrups had spenda great to have some normal choices now

Go to your local grocery store and buy some lime juice (I use the stuff that looks like a plastic lime with a tiny screw-top).  Make the cola as directed using the Sodastream.  Put a healthy squirt of the lime juice into the bottle and gently mix.  You'll almost swear that it's "the real thing".  This also works with most "bargain brand" cola products...I keep this syrup around in case I run out of "the real thing" and don't feel like going to the store.  The real stuff is better (and cheaper), but I'm really lazy.This syrup makes the equivalent of 3 2-liter bottles. (about $4.50).  Your choice.
This reminds me of Fentimin's Curiosity Cola which has a botanical undertone. I actually like it very much but if you are expecting Coke then you will be disappointed. Try it with an open mind.

I love SodaStream Zero and I love Pepsi Throwbacks (with pure cane sugar, when you can find them).  So I excited when I heard SodaStream was coming out with this flavor sweetened with cane sugar).This was the nastiest tasting flavor that I have had.  I hope SodaStream redoes this flavor.

This is really good.  But as noted in some of the other reviews, it does not taste like Coke or Pepsi.I have to hand it to Sodastream for setting themselves apart by creating a cola with a unique flavor rather than simply trying to replicate one of the top cola brands.So far I really like all of the Sparkling Naturals flavors I've tried.  They're all unique in their own way and they really do taste like they're made from natural stuff.My only complaints are that they are not nearly as concentrated and only make half as much soda as the regular flavors, while being more expensive.And finally, Amazon needs to come down from the $14.99 price.  Bed Bath & Beyond has this in their brick and mortar stores for $9.99, which is still pretty expensive in comparison to the standard flavors.

If you're used to that cola from Atlanta or in the red white and blue can from New York, you're probably going to be disappointed with the taste.But is it an acceptable cola as colas go? Yes. I'd even say as a mixer, it'd be fine. There is a heavy aftertaste of carmelized sugar, and that does impact the taste of the cola itself but it is drinkable even if the folks used to Atlanta's finest despise it. Muddy it up with something like flavored syrup (cherry, vanilla, etc) or Rum and it isn't as noticeable.Also remember that with cola and other "dark" syrups, you have to increase the level of carbonation. I typically do 4-5 buzzes for the right amount of fizz.I'd put it above the tea taste of the Natural root beer as it's drinkable but still below the lemon/lime and Ginger Ale Natural flavors.
This was just the basic ingredients that i could have found at the local harris teeter, but this kit had everything i needed to get me started making sushi.

These are so tasty! I love banana with chocolate with anything. It is a very small bag of treat. I thought I can finish the whole bag when I bought one from Whole Foods Market. But, it was very filling and a few of those was satisfying enough. Maybe 3 to 4 servings in a bag. So, it is not so bad the price wise. However, at Whole Foods, it is $4.69 a bag. Here at Amazon, a bag is $5.54. It looks like a deal with pack of 3, it is not at all a deal. It is too bad the price is not even the same as at Whole Foods. This means it is super expensive at Amanzon!! I never thought of that. It is good to compare the prices...
Delicious, but deadly. I was addicted to these babies for the longest while. But now I've been able to wean myself off them and have a couple every few days. Way too much sugar.

column9: Very finely ground. Strong blueberry color and strong taste
column10: Like all other products from Bob's Red Mill that I have tried, the quality of this flour is excellent. Very finely ground, no lumps at all, very fresh and always come in perfect packaging.The color of it seems almost white when the flour is raw but as you cook it, for some reason it becomes a whole lot darker. Even a tiny bit of it gives to any dish a strong blueberry-like color. That can sometimes look a bit unattractive if you are cooking for others. I made for instance a broccoli soup with broccoli, potatoes, chicken broth and I used this flour to thicken it. I only added a very tiny bit of flour, for a big pot of soup, but the whole thing turned dark purple. Now I guess a dark purple soup does not exactly match what most people would expect a broccoli - potato soup to look like lol. But fortunately I just cooked it for myself and I'm not really picky about how the food looks.It also holds a very strong, somewhat bitter taste. A little bit of this flour will not only be very visible in any dish but also you will be able to clearly taste the black beans. I was using Bob's Red Mill garbanzo flour before this, and that one, instead, had a very mild flavor and a very pale color.Personally, I will not buy this flour again because the color and especially the flavor are a bit too much for me (I will probably go back to the garbanzo flour or the white beans flour), but I still give 5 stars because I think it is the best you can realistically expect from a black bean flour.

While the packaging says that this is creamy, there is an unpleasant texture to it.  Almost like I'm eating peanut butter with ground egg shells in it.  I've had 'natural' nut butters before and have never experienced something like that.  The roasted flavor is a little overpowering.  Adding some agave and/or stevia helps with the roasted taste.

I love the taste and texture of this nut butter.  It is not a creamy butter, but more crunchy with very small pieces of cashew.  It has a very cashewy taste!  Awesome on toast in the morning.  Only 2g of sugar in 2 Tbsp.

column9: Tasty popcorn that doesn't get stuck between your teeth!
column10: Okay, maybe the heading exagerates just a tad... Red Popcorn has a MUCH more tender husk than regular popcorn does and when it pops, it explodes the kernel so well that the husks basically disappear.  When it pops, it looks pretty much like any other popcorn, except that the popped kernels are slightly smaller than usual.  The meet is white, but you can see the little bits of red kernel in them.  You would never know that the pretty, white popcorn you were eating started out red-colored if you hadn't seen it before popping.The flavor is great!  It smelled "toastier" as it was popping than other popcorns we've tried.  We tried it all different ways, with toppings ranging from sweet to savory and every way was good.We also liked the fact that it is grown by Amish people and are happy to support their efforts to raise their crops the "old way."  They believe in sustainable farming and a clean, wholesome way of life.  No ConAgra multi-national conglomerates here, just real, individual farmers making a living off their land.Great products raised and produced by real farmers.  What better reasons do you need to buy some of this really tasty popcorn!?

This is some "excellent" popcorn. It pops up very nicely and is "far and away" better than the "Orville" that you've been popping. Very fine, almost non-existent "hulls" when it pops. Easy on the teeth and a very "clean" taste.Like "Mikey" says, "Try it, you'll like it".
There's no other on the market as good as this.  I've ordered it many times.  My family wouldn't settle for anything less. Simply the Best.
have ordered from this company in the past and very satisfied withtheir popcorn. will order again and again.
We have enjoyed this red popcorn very much.  Very "earthy" natural taste.  Works well in our popper, very few unpopped kernels

I just want to point out that this is not actually "Amish" popcorn.  Look at the company's website-this is "Amish country" popcorn, meaning I guess that Amish live in the vincinity.  Note the lack of any mention of organic popcorn on it.  This is good popcorn, but don't fool yourself into thinking you're getting an organic/chemical free product, or one raised in small batches by Amish folk.  Clever wording strikes again!

This, and all the other Amish popcorn, could very well be the best popcorn on the planet (I especially like the red) I could never go back to the bland popcorn I used to buy at the market. Everyone should at least try this great snack!

We recently got this, which seemed great because prior to this we purchased what we had thought to be "paragon popcorn" sold by amazon and we got this popcorn called "snappy" which really sucked because there were so many hulls, that we decided to buy this after reading the reviews.upside: hardly any hullsdownside: the popcorn is very small, and not as tender as I would have thought it to be since the kernels are so small.Overall, this popcorn is better than the one purchased before but I would probably look for something else.
We use this popcorn in an air popper on the weekends. It is delicious and tastes much better than anything we have been able to find in the stores.

At first I was a little disappointed in the overall size of the popped corn--small compared to the typical yellow variety I'm used to--but the flavor was excellent.  Almost every kernel popped(save for one or two per 1 qt. (popped) serving)!  I love this variety of popcorn and am SO glad to find it at a good price and availability.
If you love popcorn... this brand is terrific.  I like the red because you get big tender kernels with very little hull.  Enjoy!
Love this popcorn, just received my 2nd order, it pops great... little to no hulls, which I really like...also has a great taste, my family loves it also..

I've been on a binge w/popcorn & didn't feel good about eating a lot of microwave brands. This popcorn is great! It is healthy and it tastes great even w/out butter. There is no waste because everything pops. Well worth the money.
This popcorn has the most delicious tase of any popcorn we have tried.  We had almost given up on finding a good one.  The Amish County Red Popcorn is simply the best!
This is very high qulity pop corn, I recomend it.  Almost all kernels pop and they are a crisp white when they pop.  Very healthy and yummy, I have tried almost all of them.

I ordered this and a few other items at the same time. This review is on the red, so I have to say it was great and worth the money. The Baby White was worthless and wouldn't pop right. I called them and was told I could return it for a refund of the purchase price. Problem was I paid to ship it to me, if I pay to ship it back, I may was well forget the refund, its a wash!

column9: We hate to leave this kind of review......
column10: We hate to leave this kind of review especially when we have enjoyed this product so much in the past.  Purchased this item in June 2011 and placed it in our kitchen cupboard upon arrival.  Two weeks ago, we were watching a movie and decided to have some popcorn.  Grabbed the new bag of Wabash (purple) and opened it.  Moths came flying out of the bag.  Yes, moths!!  Quickly closed the bag and to our dismay saw many, many moths crawling around inside the bag.  Did some internet research and found the moths are called Indian Meal Moths.  We have never seen these critters in our kitchen before and are sure they came with the popcorn.  We did a complete clean out of our cupboards and have not found them in any other products.  We wrote an email to Wabash Valley thru Amazon about this incident two weeks ago and have heard nothing back.  We would have thought they would pony up and at least offer an apology, if not a complete refund.  We realize that this kind of thing happens and are saddened by their lack of response and responsibility.  It's just not good business.  They have our money after all.

column9: Good popcorn, great packaging and service
column10: The popcorn arrived ahead of schedule and the packaging was meticulous.  I have never seen better packaging for a bulk item.The popcorn is good, but not great.  I use a hot air popper and have tried Crimson Jewel and other non-Amazon brands of red popcorn previously.  There were very few un-popped kernels, but the popcorn was not as tender as Crimson Jewel.I would buy this product again, but prefer Crimson Jewel.
Really good popcorn, shipping costs as much as the popcorn. Don't know if it is worth it.
Looks nearly black in the middle of the popped kernel, but it isn't burnt at all. Corn-ey taste, we're really glad we've found this seller and popcorn.

column9: Not at all happy with this
column10: I would give this a zero star if I could. It's terrible. Half the seeds didn't pop and the kernels were tough. Do not buy.

With all the great reviews of this red popcorn, I wanted to love it. But frankly, I was underwhelmed. It's a hassle with an air popper, as the kernels tend to fly out before they've popped. What does pop is rather small. I would not buy this popcorn again. The purple is much better.

column9: The BEST popcorn I think I've ever had!
column10: Ok- I read the reviews and wasn't sure if I should buy 12 lbs of popcorn. We just like to eat it a few times a week. I have to say, I'm usually a butter lover when it comes to popcorn. But, not with this. No butter is needed with these tasty kernels! The kernels are very white when they pop and small so they have a great mouth feel. All of them popped and the crunch was tender, yet crisp. All I did was toss on a little popcorn salt and I'm not sure it even needed that. I've never had popcorn so good! This is worth a try!

This is the BEST popcorn in the world!!  I was a white popcorn fan until I tried this a few years ago, purchased from Scheels Sporting Goods.  After I found this on Amazon though I buy this and it lasts me 3-4 months.  We have popcorn at least every Sunday, but this is so good I usually make a batch during the week.
Great Taste.  Use Wabash Valley Farms 25008 Whirley-Pop Stovetop Popcorn Popper and gourmet oil and butter.  Ex-cel-lent.

This is by far my favorite popcorn of all time. Petite, fluffy kernels are delicious and light as air. I pop this several times a week in my Back to Basics popper. One thing to keep in mind: the kernels pop up quite a bit smaller than ordinary corn, so you should measure out more, to fill up the popper. For instance, normally I measure out nearly a half-cup of ordinary corn, but for the Vintage Red I usually use almost 3/4 cup. Happy popping!

column9: Vintage Red a Hit with our family
column10: I appreciated that this popcorn wasn't full of big hulls like regular popcorn is, and that it is more dense and crunchy than "movie style" popcorn. After eating the Vintage Red, regular popcorn seems kind of like styrofoam. The only thing I noticed that you need to watch for is that with some of the gourmet popcorns, shipping is more expensive than the popcorn itself.

Amish Country Red Popcorn - 6lb.Amish Country Red Popcorn - 2lb.We buy the 6 lb. bag because it is SOooooooo incredibly good that we go through it very quickly.  I use a small amount of oil and a little bit of sea salt and it is excellent.Very few hulls on this popcorn so you don't mess up your teeth!Try it...if you are a popcorn lover, you won't go back. Not to mention the better health benefits!
If you are a popcorn lover, buy the red pocorn!!!  I can guarantee you will love it.  After eating it, I have a hard time going back to regular popcorn.
This is very high qulity pop corn, I recomend it.  Almost all kernels pop and they are a crisp white when they pop.  Very healthy and yummy!

column9: Ok, but will look for something better
column10: This popping corn is a mix of pros and cons for us.  It came in a clear plastic bag with the pretty red label.  Very colorful corn - lots of dark red with a few kernels of white mixed in.  As some of the other reviewers have said, for a hot air popper, you'll definitely want to tip the popper backward the minute you plug it in or else the air pressure will send kernels flying around your kitchen like schrapnel.  Trust me - you'll be ducking for cover and then finding kernels for the next year or so.  I did not let go of my hot air popper until there was a good amount of popped corn to weigh down the unpopped kernels.  These kernels are noticeably smaller than others you'll see in the grocery store so when they pop, the end result is smaller.  If you have shag carpet, this is probably not a good thing.  The husks are softer and tend to cause less damage to your gums if they get caughtin your teeth, though it won't happen often.  The cost for this little bag is also significantly higher than we'd want to pay again.  Another big con for us is the number of unpopped kernels that remain - probably 1 - 2 dozen per 1/2 cup batch.
