column9: Marzipan Tastes Bland and Contains Sorbitol
column10: Normally I buy almond paste, not prepared marzipan, but thought that just this once I could save a little time. There is no one to blame but myself for not reading the ingedient list before buying. This is what happens when you rush. By now I should know that when it comes to even old stand-by products, nothing can be taken for granted.The ingredient list begins as expected, sugar, blanched almonds, water but then it veers off into new frontier - sorbitol -- then corn syrup and potassium sorbate finish the list. Potassium sorbate is used as a preservative to extend shelf-life, and perhaps is necessary, but why is sorbitol added to something as straightforward as marzipan? If this wasn't enough, the marzipan does not have a good almond flavor -- it is incredibly bland.Ironically, and a bit off the subject, I just read a book about dental health that discussed how damaging sorbitol is to the teeth and gums even though it is a popular sweetener in sugar-free gums and mints. The dentist who wrote the book stated that the bad bacteria in the mouth actually adapt to sorbitol quickly and begins to feed on it with greater frenzy than pure sugar.Whether the dental issue is of concern, sorbitol is widely known to cause intestinal distress in some people, and people with irritable bowel syndrome limit or completely avoid the product. Bottom line is that sorbitol isn't usually found in marzipan and unless this ingredient is specifically desired by the purchaser, I'd steer clear for that reason alone.I cook and bake in order to avoid additives, so this marzipan is particularly unacceptable for my use. Tallying up the plusses and minuses we have on the plus side, it is the correct texture for shaping and rolling out. On the minus side -- it is incredibly bland and is chemically enhanced with an artificial sweetener. Never again.

Fast ship, great product. Love mini Haribo bears and these bags are my favorite. Great for grabbing a few and throwing them in purse or pocket. They keep fresh since they are in individual packs.

They are great. The pack had nice, fresh bears. I ordered the same item through Amazon and through Penguin Caffeinated Mint company.The amazon product was perfectly packed and delicious.The other vendor, not so much.If you want to get your gummi bear fix, you have found the spot.

This is an excellent value from Amazon - three one-pound bags for $9!  Also, unlike buying the five-pound bulk bags, these stay fresh for longer.  I love this particular configuration of Haribo Gold Bears for the portion control it provides.  Each mini-bag contains 35 calories and there are six to eight mini bears per tiny bag.  Thus, this is the perfect size to pack in lunch bags, hide in purses, or sneak into the movies.  While gummy bears may not be the perfect health food, these mini baggies of YUMMY gold bears are a sensible sweet treat choice for the calorie-conscious.

This product just came out in my local grocery/health food store. I have bought the original Annie's Homegrown Gluten Free Mac&Cheese for my son who is Gluten intolerant. He has always enjoyed it and we as a family ate it as well. We would just add extra cheese to make it creamier but now we don't have to do that with this new product. It is very creamy and taste as close to regular Mac&Cheese that you can get from a box. It's also great because it contains almost twice as much as the other kind and since it's not a powder mix the ease allows a simple,quick dinner for my always,ever so demanding four-year old. So this gets a thumbs up from a spunky toddler. Also,we like to add things like left over taco meat or tuna to add varity to the dish. We love Annie's products!

This mac and cheese is creamier than the regular gf mac and cheese. And I LOVE more cheese! Make sure that you cook the noodles until soft and tender, or they will be very chewy. The cheese for this mac and cheese is an actual cheese sauce, not a powder. Which saves some time if you are short on it. Overall, very good, and I even hope Annie's comes out with an even cheesier mac and cheese! :)
Finally a GOOD GF mac and cheese!  I don't usually leave reviews but i HAD to for this!  It's just like the real thing!

column9: Taste is amazing, cost is a little high
column10: This product tastes wonderful, and since its Annie's its made with better "Stuff" than the Kraft variety. It cooks up almost exactly the same, so its easy to make and pretty quick! I keep a box in the closet for last minute dinners.The cost is a bit high though, I wish the cost were under $4 a box.

I am so glad to see Amazon carrying this; the pasta has great texture and the cheese is very tasty. If you're like me and celiac now but grew up eating the Kraft Mac&Cheese with the can in the box (not the powdered stuff), you'll love this.

My 14 yr.old grandson was diagnosed with Celiac in July 2010.  I have been searching for foods that he and his family can prepare easily.  So I was lead to Amazon.com and started reading the reviews on some of the products.  I ordered Annie's mac & cheese and found on the box a lasagne receipe.  I fixed it and my grandson and everyone in the family loved it. It was simple and easy to prepare.  A great fast meal for any family.

column9: As close to Kraft Cheezy Shells as you'll get
column10: I grew up on the blue box so if that is your taste standard look no further then this product.  Sure... if you're used to home made this probably won't compare but I actually like this BETTER then the original Kraft version as the noodles are a bit larger and stay firmer (took a few minutes longer to boil).  Growing up my mom never just served it "as is" but always doctored it up with extra grated cheddar cheese so I tried the same.  Even though the cheese comes in a foil squeeze pack I added a bit of milk and a Tbs of real butter then plenty of grated cheddar cheese - the results was awesome and I just make this instead of the Kraft brand for the whole family even though I'm the Celiac in the house.  It's so nice to stumble upon good GF substitutions and this is one I'll be using regularly.

column9: Finally, Mac and Cheese that reminds me of being a kid.
column10: I was diagnosed with Celiac Disease at 17, and since then there are certain foods I have not been able to fully replace.  Mac and Cheese is one of them.  Before this, the closest I had come was making my own Velveeta Mac and Cheese, to imitate Kraft's version.  I have had the other Annie's gf mac and cheese, which is widely available in stores, but I've never been a fan of the sauce, which is made from a powder and just doesn't do it for me.  I saw that this deluxe version was available, but couldn't find it in any local store, so I took the risk and bought it here.  I am so glad that I did!  It tastes similar to the Kraft Dinner I used to eat as a kid, but I have a feeling that due to the better quality ingredients in this product I would still prefer Annie's to Kraft if I could eat both.  Now I have five more boxes stored in my cabinet and some left over mac and cheese in my fridge.  I think this will last me a while.

As a gluten intolerant person, I loved it when I found Annie's Macaroni and Cheese, which I always made with lactose-free milk because I'm also lactose intolerant. Found it creamy and yummy and healthier, but otherwise much like those other mac'n'cheese box dinners I ate as a child.  For some reason, the cheese in Angie's original gluten-intolerant Mac'n'cheese didn't bother me.  (Hard cheeses generally don't bother my lactose intolerance - always safe with parmesan, swiss, aged cheddar, but cream cheese, marscapone, brie, etc., are trouble).  Unfortunately, this creamy deluxe max dinner triggered my lactose intolerance.  Tried it twice, thinking the first time must have been a fluke, but it wasn't.  Something to think about if you are both gluten and lactose intolerance.  I'm back to Angie's original mac'n'cheese and not feeling like I'm missing out at all!

column9: Fast, easy, and a kid favorite!
column10: This is a very delicious product!  It has the cheese mix already prepared in a foil packet, so there's no need to add any further ingredients (as opposed to the powder, butter, milk version).  I have to have this around the house because we often find ourselves in a situation without milk!  Also, in the powder version of GF mac and cheese, the noodles often break apart in trying to blend the powder/butter/milk, so with this pre-mixed variety, the noodles maintain most of their integrity through less stirring.I also find the flavor of the cheese sauce to be superior to the powder.  Don't add much salt to your water, though--it's already a bit saltier.The packaging looks very similar to the NON-GF version, so be careful which one you're purchasing!

column9: As Close to My Favorite Non-Gluten Version
column10: Everyone likes this in the family and it is easy to make since it comes with a sauce package.  Just cook macaroni and drain.Mix in sauce.  Side dish in a few minutes.

Anyone with Celiac Disease that has been missing a great, quick mac & cheese...here it is!!! This stuff is the BOMB!!!!!! Tastes like my Granny's mac & cheese (she used Velveeta!) and you usually can't beat Granny's cooking!!!!!

column9: Feel like a kid again-eat your mac & cheese!
column10: When I had to go gluten-free to achieve better health, I thought my days of mac and cheese were over forever.  Macaroni and cheese had been a family tradition my whole life (it was one of only three dishes that my grandmother would cook) and I hated the thought of abandoning it.  I decided to give this product a try, since I had eaten other Annie's products and enjoyed them in the past.  This packaged dinner has all the flavor of a home cooked dish without all the fuss.  Easy to prepare, easy to serve.  My husband had no idea he wasn't eating "regular" mac and cheese.  Thank you Annie's for letting me feel like a kid again!  If you enjoyed those "deluxe" mainstream wheat based products in the past, try this.
I just made my first tuna casserole with this product. It was so nice to have a dish that I didn't think I'd ever taste again. This product is good by itself or used in a recipe!

column9: Better than the name brand luten product!
column10: Annie's hit a home-run with this one.  So much better than the other (Velveeta) and better for us being gluten free.  Super simple to prepare & excellent with added protein (ground seasoned turkey burger or GF hot dogs) and wonderful by itself.  Thank you for developing this great product.

Dependable pantry item for the gluten intolerant, we order in bulk for our college son who loves the taste and easy preparation. No hidden gluten at all as can happen in other products, and excellent taste.
This is way better than the other boxes of Annies that you have to add the milk into. Its creamy and yummy, not good left over though it gets very hard. But overall impressed.

This was seriously revolting - the sauce was sour-ish and smelled awful. Even hot sauce could not save it. I was disappointed because Annie's other gluten-free mac and cheese is so much better and cheaper.

I love the regular Annie's Rice Mac and Cheese, Love. This stuff tastes totally artificial. The cheese has more resemblance to processed Velveeta oil-based cheese than the quality flavor I'm used to from Annie's. Frankly it was kinda gross, texture and flavor. Buy the powder version of Annie's Rice Mac and Cheese instead.

column9: Past the test of my  picky eater
column10: Both my kids and I love it,it is supper tasty.My youngest is super picky,and said it was better than the other kind of mac&cheese Which the one she is referring to is Velveeta.So that Really says allot!
The whole family (even those who are not GF) loves the flavor of this mac & cheese.  Tastes like the Kraft velveeta cheese & shells. We made the recipe on the box which was yummy.

I was surprised, but I really liked this.  The noodles weren't gummy, the cheese sauce tasted like Kraft Dinner, and it was super easy.  I don't have to eat gluten free, my husband and son do, so I actually treat myself to real KD once in awhile and this really is just like it.  In the past, we were using DeBole's, and I always had to doctor it up with Horizon cheese slices and real shredded cheese.  And rinse the pasta off well.  And have butter and milk on hand.  Even with all that, I still couldn't stand the taste and wouldn't eat it.  This mac & cheese is good enough that I won't have to buy Kraft Dinner anymore and just enjoy this with my gf family members.

I've been gluten free for a few months now and I can honestly say that products like this one make the transition much easier.The noodles are great, provided you cook them long enough.  The cheese is very flavorful.  Many reviewers seem to think that means it's artificial, but if the packaging is to be believed, this is a completely natural product.  "Totally natural, gluten-free product, consists of no artificial flavors, colors, or preservatives, free of GMOs, trans fat, and cholesterol."Also, I've tried the regular mac and cheese from Annie's, it's not bad, but in terms of flavor, it doesn't come close.So for something that's affordable, tasty, and ready in less than 15 minutes, you can't go wrong.

I recently discovered I have a gluten intolerance and have been struggling to find foods that are quick and easy to make as well as gluten free.  I was cautiously optimistic when I ordered this product after reading other reviews here on Amazon.  When the macaroni and cheese arrived I couldn't wait to try it out.  My husband (who is not gluten intolerant) and I shared the box and we were pleasantly suprised at how delicious this macaroni and cheese was.  I've tried other gluten-free pasta products and have definitely noticed a distinct "rubbery" feeling to the pasta.  The macaroni noodles in this product did not seem rubbery at all and upon eating you could not tell that this macaroni and cheese was gluten free.  I liked this so much that I signed up for Amazon's Subscribe and Save!
this is a great product for celiacs.  ordering online saves us a ton of money.  This mac and cheese is very close in taste to the wheat version

Anyone who eats gluten free knows that it is VERY difficult to find a food product that tastes like the "real thing".  If you hadn't of told me that this was gluten free, I wouldn't be able to recognize it by taste alone.Yes it's more of an artificial cheese flavor, but what do people expect?  Fresh cheese isn't going to magically grow out of the box!  Compared to the other Annie's gluten free mac & cheese, this one is better (if not VERY close).  The reason why I like this better is because everything is in the box.  You don't need milk, butter, nothing.  Just boil the noodles, drain, add cheese sauce, and DONE.It's quick, easy, delicious and worth it!  Highly recommended!

This Gluten Free Mac and Cheese is awesome.  Sometimes gluten free products are hit or miss, but this one nails it.  It is super easy to prepare, the pasta is good, and the cheese sauce creamy and tasty.  I definitely recommend it.

As a new member of the GF community, I have been trying to find products that are not only GF but also delicious! Sometimes, this seems like a challenge. Because of all the other recommendations on here, I decided to try this mac and cheese. This mac and cheese is better than its Kraft and Velveeta counterparts in my opinion. The cheese is real and the noodles are great. I ate a noodle before I put the sauce on just to see what they taste like. You can't tell the difference between these noodles and regular ones.And today for lunch I reheated the leftovers from Monday (it is now Wednesday) and they are still delicious! That is the true test for mac and cheese.I will certainly be trying more of Annie's GF products.

column9: Best mac and cheese around for gluten allergy
column10: I LOVE THIS PRODUCT!  I bought a second order a long time before I thought that I would and have signed up for subscribe and save.

I love the regular Annie's Rice Mac and Cheese, but this stuff tastes artificial. The cheese has more resemblance to processed Velveeta oil-based cheese than the quality flavor I'm used to from Annie's.  Bottom line, the convenience isn't worth it.  Buy the powder version of Annie's Rice Mac and Cheese instead.

column9: Mac & Cheese Leftovers That No One Wants
column10: Our gluten-free family of five has tried this several times and everyone seemed to lose their appetite when this was prepared.  The cheese sauce comes in a packet that you squeeze on the noodles.  Everyone agreed that the sauce is too cheesy, thick, and the flavor is not as good as other brands/styles.  Mac & Cheese is a staple in our house, but we won't order this one again.

column9: Tastes completely different than the 'regular' Annie's GF Mac and Cheese Dinner
column10: I have subscribed to the original (not deluxe) Annie's Gluten Free Macaroni and Cheese dinner for over a year.  The sauce is light, creamy, 'customizable', and very tasty.  About a week ago, I decided to try out the deluxe macaroni and cheese dinner by Annie because the subscribe and save price was slightly cheaper and possessed roughly the same amount of product.  To be frank, the sauce is completely different.  I am not sure how the recipe for the cheese sauce can vary so much between these two products, but I definitely taste a significant difference.  The deluxe cheese sauce tastes overly artificial and more like cheese whiz compared to that of the original version.  Perhaps the variance can be attributed to the fact that the deluxe version's sauce comes pre-made in a packet, whereas the regular version's sauce may be customized to your individual taste by tinkering with the amounts of butter/margarine and milk.  Either way, I am going back over to the regular GF Annie's macaroni dinner (it earns a  five star rating in my opinion!).

column9: very close to the real thing
column10: This product is very cheesy.  It tastes very similar almost identical to kraft.  it is very cheesy and the noodles are perfect.Even if you are not gluten free you would enjoy this product.Amazon's price is the best deal around.It is more expensive to get this deluxe kind than the regular mac and cheese but it is worth every cent.
Annie's Deluxe Macaroni and Cheese was quick to prepare and tasty for a speedy meal.  I've sometimes added cubed ham and peas to package as another option.  Bulk pricing at Amazon is a plus too.

I tried other brands and they were comparable to the non-gluten brands that you would find on sale.  But when I tried this brand, I was pleasantly suprised.  It was cheesy (no punn intended) and creamy.  I will definately buy again.
I think this is an excellent product.  I actually thought the cheese was consistent with regular mac & cheese.  My daughter loved it.

I was excited by the extra cheesy on the box but didn't pay enough attention to realize that it wasn't just more cheese powder, which I think the non-deluxe kind needs. This cheese sauce, while creamier, is pretty disgusting.

This is a staple in our house, and the kids really enjoy it -- much prefer the pre-mixed cheese goo over the powder.  That said, not sure why Amy's feels the need to make the stuff neon orange.  I'm assuming it's the turmeric they use to make that orange color that is giving it that slightly bitter aftertaste (that the kids don't seem to notice...).

column9: Just right to learn to eat
column10: First I have been gluten free for awhile now. And my son who is almost a year is also gluten free. It is a great product for young children. You need to cook it longer than what the box says and add more cheese.  Otherwise it lacks flavor.

Sometimes eating gluten free means lowering your standards of taste when it comes to boxed products. Annie's regular gluten free macaroni is okay, so I thought I would go one step up and try the delux. I think the main difference is the amount of cheese, otherwise the taste is the same to mean, however Annie's is still one of the better boxed mac n cheese brands on the gluten free market.
The noodles were fine, it's just the packaged cheese sauce that I found awful. I tried to add things to it to make it edible, but ended up tossing the whole box. Unfortunate!

I am from the South and this is the first time I've ever tasted a pecan "pie" that was this good. The key is the sweetened crust, in my opinion.My husband, who detests Pecan Pie ate this and loved it! However, that being said... the merchandisers selling this one box for $10 are ridiculously crazy! Overpriced and beyond.
This is the best whole wheat pasta my family has ever had.  You would not know that this was whole wheat unless you read the package.

I am a very reluctant somewhat healthy eater but when my wife forced me to switch from white to wheat pasta my Italianess revolted.  To be honest I HATED whole wheat paste - it tasted weird, had a poor texture and tended to ruin dinner...until I found Gia Russa.This paste is amazing - great taste, awesome texture and I actually prefer it to regular pasta (I am in hiding from the Italians...).Seriously, give this pasta a try - your entire family will love it!

column9: Simply the best whole wheat pasta
column10: Gia Russa Whole Wheat Angel Hair, 16-Ounces (Pack of 5)I used to buy this brand from a specialty grocer, but it is no longer available there.  I am glad I found it here on Amazon.  Excellent food value and flavor.
great full taste,  use the smallest brewing size for full flavor.  best hazelnut out there in a k-cup.  i only wish the green mtn regular hznt was as good as the decaf.

column9: disappointed it isn't hazelnut CREAM decaf
column10: The picture shows hazelnut CREAM decaf coffee, but I received plain ole hazelnut decaf.  The hazelnut decaf flavor is fine. I'm not sure there'd even be a taste difference, but I was really looking forward to experiencing the hazelnut cream flavor.

Even though I would marry my Keurig (simplicity, consistency, brilliant!), I've yet to find a k-cup that I *love*. With coffee I generally go decaf, and Green Mountain does decaf well. The hazelnut flavor is nice, not overwhelming. But overall it's a cup of coffee that, while very good, won't keep you salivating for your next one.
Didn't expect much from a decaf flavor, but this one suprised me. A great buy.
Ordered the Hazelnut Cream Decaf. and received Hazelnut Decaf. I was dissappointed I did not get what I ordered, but the flavor is great.

This coffee is good, but a little weak.  I've made it on both settings, but it doesn't seem to matter, it's still weaker then I would like. I'm still in search of the perfect cup of flavored decaf with a rich bold flavor.

I have always been happy with Green Mountain Coffee.  However the last 2 times I have ordered Hazelnut Cream Decaf I don't get what I ordered.  I get boxes of Hazelnut Decaf instead.  I needed the coffee so I didn't waste time to return it so I don't know how Amazon would have handled the return.  Hopefully they will get on the ball with this and send correct coffee!!
My whole family loves this cereal. It's crunchy and just sweet enough to taste good without being so sugary that it resembles breakfast dessert.  Great with milk or yogurt!

Next to his chardonnay and competing with organic walnuts, my husband adores Lundberg organic popcorn-rice cake snacks, which cannot be regularly located locally.Therefore, I was delighted to learn that Amazon carries this healthy food product.  Healthy food products are those which are NOT genetically modified with something other than a plant to either become a potentially toxic pesticide (as in the case of Bt) or withstand more toxic petrochemical herbicides, like Roundup linked based on the weight of evidence to cancers, immune system damage and other irreversible diseases.I'll spend more to purchase organic and to support certified organic farmers.Thank you.

Like the person in the other review, I just happened to pick out this water at Whole Foods one day when I was thirsty.  I was about to reach for my usual water, then suddenly decided to randomly try something different, since Whole Foods has soooo many choices!  Anyways, this was the winner, even though it was on the top shelf (and I'm only 5 feet tall).  It must've been my intuition or something because I fell in love with this water at first swallow!  The texture is so smooth and soft - it's like drinking liquid silk.  That's the best analogy I can come up with!  =D  Even my teenage daughter - who doesn't drink NEARLY enough water for her own good - tasted it and said, "Wow this makes ME want to drink water!"  And she really meant it b/c the next time I went to Whole Foods she asked if I would get her a bottle.  =D  It has such a clean taste, too.

I have never tasted water so good in my life.  I just happened to try a bottle I picked up at a Health Food store last week.  It tastes like it comes straight off a glacier.  I don't know how to describe it really, other than it reminds me of the flavor of tasting snow.  It is so fresh and clean tasting.  I only wish you could buy it in gallon jugs.  I have tasted plenty of fancy waters, and none of them really stood out far and above the average water, until I tried this.

column9: The best drinking water in the world
column10: The purest and the most refreshing still water you will ever have. Do a blind taste test and you can tell the difference between Ice Age natural purest water containing only 4 dissolved solids parts per million compared to any other water in the market. So light, fluffy refreshing and smooth. Probably the purest all natural drinking water in the world!

this is clearly the smoothest best tasting bottled water you can buy.i believe there is more to water than just how clean it is or what its ph level is .dont know what exactly makes good water like this taste so great .if  it came in glass bottles it would be just over the top unreal.but as it is in plastic its still ok.thanks amazon for making this available.

column9: McCormick Grill Mates. GO BIG, OR GO HOME.
column10: Buying the little containers at the store no longer makes sense. They are too EXPENSIVE. Now that I know I can buy a big one and refiil my little shaker, I will always trun to Amazon for this product. It's half gone already.

My dogs love these bones.  I bought all sizes.  My jack russel loves the big ones and the small ones.  My 60 pound mutt loves the big ones. They are great.  They are able to digest them and able to enjoy the bones.  I bought so many of them.  Petsmart for some reason discontinued them I was so upset.  I was so happy to see them on Amazon for a great price. I highly recommend them.

column9: Doesn't last long for agressive chewers
column10: I don't like all the controversy surrounding rawhide bones and don't want take the risk of my Lab getting a blockage so I exclusively give him Booda bones which are safe. My lab is an aggressive chewer and considering this is edible it makes him that much more excited as he LOVES food. He enjoys these bones but devours them in less than 20 minutes. I usually give it to him for a few minutes until he eats half of it and then I take it away to save for next time. This obviously would get very expensive so he has his non-edible Nylabones most of the time and these are special treats.

column9: Great for dogs with stomach problems
column10: My dog gets sick eating a lot of dog treats (even Milkbones), but has always done well with all the Booda bones.  She really loves them & they're good for getting rid of the tartar on her teeth.  I highly recommend these.

Our Siberian Husky is overweight and on a diet.  She also is great at building placque and tartar on her teeth - baad breath! She has a touchy stomach on top of it all.  Tried these bones in all flavors and she loves them.  They help with her teeth and breath.  She gets one bone for her lunch (she's a 3 meals a day gal).  Her other meals are now canned green beans with either yogurt (plain) or low fat cottage cheese.  She has lost about 11 lbs and is doing great!  No more throwing up her food!

column9: Goodbye Rawhides! Hello Peace of Mind - & Dogs Love 'em!
column10: Love these! Well, because...we have 3 dogs (2 were unplanned children ;-) & our 60-LB German Shepherd AND our 40-LB we-have-no-clue-what-she-is dog have both choked on various shapes & sizes of rawhides. The Shepherd choked so badly that, this time, it wouldn't come up. She couldn't cough & started to literally choke to death. I actually straddled her back, attempting the only thing I  knew how to do - the human Heimlich Maneuver! Like where exactly is a dog's sternum, anyway? Well, I tried anyway and thank God it finally did dislodge & we got it out! Was it the Heimlich? I don't know. Probably not. I mean, she still won't tell me... After all, I guess it was very traumatic for her.But in all seriousness, what I do know, is that was the last time any of my dogs have had any kind of regular rawhide bones! Which, I really wanted to let everyone know of my personal experiences; I believe anybody who is at all concerned about giving their dogs rawhides and/or experiencing a similar problem is on the right track to avoid them.Our small part Chihuawa/part something else, first 2 times in-a-row, threw up repeatedly w/rawhide pieces and w/foam. He was VERY sick the 3rd time, so we definitely stopped that! The ONLY kind I did finally take a chance with were granulated rawhide munchy sticks, & they're all fine w/these; though I'm still nervous about them choking on a piece, but neither of them have had any problems with Boodas so far, & they don't swell up in their throats like regular rawhides.So, now... It's Booda Bones!Yes, they are a bit on the pricey side, especially for my 2 larger aggressive chewers. I agree with some other reviewers that they are not very long-lasting. But it's all I'll give them now. But, for my half Chihuahua/half something else(20lbs), I give him the smallest ones and they are like mega-saurus bones for him(it is my hope that the manufacturer will start selling these in bulk packages, for less $). I get 3 different sizes for my 3 different whatever-they-are-dogs. They absolutely love them! This includes the assorted flavors, the bacon-flavored, and the yogurt-flavored. Whichever is cheaper at the time and shipped by Amazon.And I owe a big thank you to Brian Amazon, all of you for all of your reviews, Booda Bones, and Amazon!** Confession: This was originally a comment I posted to a reviewer by the name of "Brian Amazon" a long time ago. I have been buying Bones from Amazon, and, only Booda Bones, ever since. They are so great that I've been wanting to write a review, & now finally have the chance to (I have, however, resorted to copying and pasting much of my original [brief... LOL] comment, with some editing).
My dog loves Booda Bones.  They are a bit pricy so I only give him a couple a week as a special treat.  I'll continue buying them from Amazon for the best price.

We have a dog with a liver shunt - so she can't have a lot of protein / can't digest protein.  Booda Bones are the BEST treat for her (and our other dog loves them as well!).  The only 'downside' whatsoever is that they're a tad expensive - but they're worth it!

column9: More of a treat then something to keep your dog busy.
column10: Let me start by saying our dogs love these. As soon as they see the bag they stop whatever they're doing and run to their crates (where we typically give these to them). However, for our dogs these are definitely more of a treat then an activity. I have one dog who is an aggressive chewer who finishes these in under five minutes. He doesn't chew them as much as bite of chunks of it. My other dog isn't quite as strong of a chewer but it usually takes her just around fifteen minutes to eat the whole thing (this review is specific to the Biggest Boodas). So for my dogs this is less of a chewing experience and more of a treat. And when the eat them this quickly, they do get expensive quick.

My dog loves the chicken, steak, and peanut butter booda bones, but he's not as fond of the spearmint/peppermint variety.  My dog will eat it if offered, but my dad's dog who I often sit for will not even touch these.  I wouldn't recommend for a dog who prefers meat.

column9: My dogs have rated Booda Bones 5 Stars!
column10: I have three King Charles Cavalier Spaniels and they are picky, picky eaters even when it comes to Treats.  They love the peanut flavored Booda Bones and have one every day.  They insisted I write this review on Amazon so their opinions could be known.  They're pushy that way...

I was very disappointed by the product.  They are NOT long lasting as I was lead to believe.  I was going to buy Chewlotta's which take my dog about 2 hrs to go through 1, but I thought it was too pricey at $3 a pop.  My dog could eat this whole bag in less than 2 hours.  He does enjoy them though.

column9: Dog really likes, but they go fast.
column10: I have an 11 pound Couton De Tulear.  Small sharp teeth.Dog loves them.These don't last long.  From a value standpoint, I prefer "Checkups," when Costco has them in stock.

column9: love that these are yogurt flavor!  my dog loves booda bones!
column10: I have no problem w/my dog eating these.  He loves these booda bones. I had never seen the yogurt ones; he loves them.
Our dog, a Siberian Husky, just loves Booda Bones.We give her one for lunch most everyday and shepesters us till we give it to her.

Our Boston Terrier loves these bones - we give them to her as a treat or to keep her busy when we have company.  For a 16 lbs. dog she's a mighty chewer and these last her a couple of hours, with breaks to investigate if she's missing anything!  We'll buy more of these!

column9: My dog goes crazy for these!
column10: My chihuahua loves these, especially the peanut butter, chicken, and bacon varities. They have become increasingly hard to find at pet stores so I was happy to find them on amazon. I like that they are safer than rawhide bones and easy to digest and she really seems to enjoy them more than other bones I've bought for her. I tried a few other brands when I stopped being able to find the booda bones at pet stores and she would not even eat some of them. You can't go wrong with these, they are reasonibly priced, safe, help reduce tartar, and dogs seem to love them.
