I recently ordered these and was extremely disappointed.  Here were the problems:1) OLD!!  They actually tasted dusty and I could feel no potency in them at all.2) Wolfberries not Goji Berries.  Since I've consumed Goji's from many sources over the years, I know which are the highest quality Goji's (usually quite expensive), which are less potent, and which are the different tasting Wolfberry variety that many sellers pass off as Goji's but are not the same.  Wolfberry has its own benefits (not nearly those of Goji IMO), but for Wolfberries these are widly overpriced.  You can get the same in Chinese stores for probably closer to $10 for twice the amount.With the dollar devaluation top quality Goji berries have gotten very expensive for regular use.  So if you're looking for cheaper alternatives like I was here, look elsewhere.  Check out some of the cheap goji berries (that are in fact wolfberries and usually say so) on Ebay from Chinese sources.  They'll be quite a bit cheaper and likely quite a bit fresher.

I was impressed by the price, so I ordered these.  They are horrible...hard as rocks, stale-tasting, full of stems, and they leave a bad after taste in the mouth.  I am a raw vegan and use lots of goji berries; I have never experienced any as awful as these.Perhaps this is only a bad batch, as others seem to have gotten good ones.  If that's the case, then the company has terrible qualitycontrol, as well as terrible goji berries.

These berries are a bit drier and chewier (and less sweet) than I expected. However, I found that if I add a hand full of them to a bag of sweetened dried cranberries, it makes it much less noticeable.

column9: I've tried many bags of Goji Berries, these are the worst...
column10: I've tried many bags of Goji Berries from different companies.  Some are good and some are not so good.  I later found out that the Goji Berries from China are not the best quality.  So, I found a brand that said that they are the "authentic Tibetan Goji Berries" at my local health food Co-Op.  Although they were expensive, they were good. They were the best that I ever had, soft and delicious.When I saw that there were some inexpensive authentic organic Tibetan Goji Berries on Amazon, I became excited.  I made the purchase and couldn't wait to get them.  When I received them and tried them I was very disappointed.  They are the hardest, driest, discolored, worst tasting Goji Berries that I ever had.  I immediately felt that I was sold and inferior product in a nice bag.  These Goji Berries have a bad taste and have sediment on them as if they were not clean.  I called the company to inquire about the origin.  Of course they did say that they are authentic Tibetan Goji Berries.  I just don't believe them.  There were two bags that came with my order. As of Nov 2007, each 16 gram serving contains 2 grams of trans fat!  That is 1/8th trans-fat by weight, and more than 1/8 by calories!!!  (Please consult the packaging for more current information, many manufacturors are removing trans-fat. Beware: they may legally claim 0 grams of trans fat when they have half a gram PER SERVING, which is very significant for small serving sizes.  So you should look for the words "partially hydroginated" in the ingredient list.  If you see "partially hydrogenated" then you know the product has artificial trans fat and you should NOT buy it.)Don't take my word for it that this is bad, because here are some quotations from the survey articleMozaffarian et al "Trans Fatty Acids and Cardiovascular Disease,"The New England Journal of Medicine, volume 354,pages 1601-1613 (2006).Here are a few quotations from this article:"given the 1.2 million annual myocardial infarctions and deaths from CHD ["coronary heart disease"] in the United States, near-elimination of industrially produced trans fats might avert between 72,000 (6 percent) and 228,000 (19 percent) CHD events [i.e. "heart attacks"] each year. These estimates are based on the replacement of trans fats with carbohydrates. In practice, however, trans fats in partially hydrogenated oils would most commonly be replaced with unhydrogenated (cis) unsaturated fats,6 which may have additional potential benefits as compared with carbohydrates. If such additional potential benefit is considered, greater proportions of CHD events (12 to 22 percent) might be averted."Note that the disproportionate percentage of heart disease attributable to trans-fat is astonishing, since the authors point on on the first page that trans-fat makes up only a tiny proportion of the american diet:"The average consumption of industrially produced trans fatty acids in the United States is 2 to 3 percent of total calories consumed."They conclude"On the basis of evidence from in vitro experimental studies, dietary trials, and prospective observational studies, the consumption of trans fatty acids from partially hydrogenated oils provides no apparent nutritional benefit and has considerable potential for harm."Professor Willett (one of the co-authors of the above article) is the chairman of Harvard's nutrition department, the author of the medical school textbook "nutritional epidemiology", and the most-cited author in his field. He has also written about trans-fat for a general audience in his book "Eat, Drink, and be Healthy: The Harvard Medical School Guide for Healthy Eating."

I am not a big fan of boxed meals, but when you are short order cooking for several people with varying dietary needs, it is nice to have something like this on hand. This dish tastes good to me and to my oldest son who is EXTREMELY picky. I like the texture of the noodles and the taste of the sauce. Definitely something to keep on hand for emergency or just a change of pace. It's been a lifesaver for my son who is on a very restricted diet. When I reheat it, I just add a little milk and nuke it in the microwave for about a minute or two.

column9: It's not gourmet, but it's tasty and easy for weekday nights!
column10: Having been gluten free for most of my life, I was really excited when I found Mrs. Leeper's packaged meals. I never imagined that I would ever be able to have the gluten free equivalent of "tuna helper" or "hamburger helper." When I tried this boxed meal, I knew I had found a winner, and my (non GF) husband agreed. The corn noodles are very tasty and we both enjoy them equally- and the creamy, cheesy sauce is simple but goes very nicely with the tuna. I usually add some kind of fresh or defrosted vegetable- peas, green beans, etc. to the dish while it is simmering and then serve it with freshly chopped tomatoes and red or orange diced peppers on top. I doctor mine up with some freshly ground pepper and vietnamese hot sauce, but my husband likes it plain. Very, very good. My husband likes to make this when it is his night to cook, and I'm all too happy to let him. It may not be the most gourmet food product, but it's not horrible for you if you use lowfat milk, and it really is tasty for such a quick, easy GF meal.-happy GF pasta chomperPS I do have to say that this is my favorite of the Mrs. Leepers meals, perhaps because we don't eat meat or chicken. However, I do think the corn pasta and cheesy sauce is a real winner and superior to the other sauces and pastas. (For example, her chicken alfredo box meal is based on a rice pasta... it's ok, but seems a little lacking...)

column9: Quick, delicious & easy go to meal...

The noodles cook up with a nice firm texture and the sauce is very flavorful...except for some fresh ground black pepper and a bit of salt it doesn't need to be "doctored" at all. column9: Tuna Helper is Better and It's Cost Effective to Buy Instead

It's no more expensive than buying the Mrs. Leeper tuna dinners and in fact is probably a bit cheaper, it tastes better and I can satisfy the needs of both the diabetics and the gluten intolerant members of the family. I can also add as little or much pasta - either low carb or gluten free - as is necessary for how many people will be eating it. Like alot of the other reviewers, I also add more tuna than the recipe calls for and a veggie.My husband and I are both type 2 diabetics. I save the regular pasta that comes in the Tuna Helper meal and when I have guests who can eat regular pasta, I serve it to them so we all get what we need/want and I'm not wasting anything.One last thing is that Tuna Helper comes in several varieties so we don't get tired of it. I serve it probably at least once a month.

This is absolutely one of my favorite quick gluten-free meals.  The pasta is tender and the seasoning is perfect.  And even better, the directions are really clear, so you can't mess it up (which is common with gluten free foods). I find that one can of tuna isn't usually enough, so I'll throw in an extra can for one really big dinner or a can of Veg-All for two meals.
This is a fantastic product for those with celiac. I would definately add a 2nd can of tuna as well as frozebn peas. It's like I remember as a kid. Highly recommended!!

hmmm -- well i don't have a gluten problem and had never even had corn pasta.  it stays al dente.  i found this to be a really tasty meal.  yeah it does need 2 cans tuna, unless u just want a tuna flavored sauce, which is also very good.  i had read the reviews but first tried with one can.  if i feel hungrier, will add 2.  this is certainly a good stock-up item for the winter.  ; )
My gluten-free children love this dinner. It's creamy and has a nice flavor. My 15yr old makes it for herself and her brother. It's easy and definitely a favorite of theirs.
Great tasting ,easy to prepare. cost is a little high, but for the convience of dinner within 15 min. its worth it. i have tried all of the mrs. leeper products and am very satisfied.

This is a staple in our household and our favorite of Mrs. Leepers dinners.  It is one of the few convenience foods we have to rely on that is gluten free.  Cooks up so easy even my husband can do it!:)  We usually add peas and top it with shredded Parmesan.  Sometimes I prepare it with leftover cooked chicken and steamed broccoli for a change of pace.

This is one of my favorite gluten-free meals. The noodles are good and the texture is just right. The spices and flavor are great. I use canned chicken instead of tuna for a different taste. I also use more water and milk (I use soy milk)than called for to get a jucier dish. You can experiment by gradually adding more each time you make it until you get it just right. I also double the amount of canned chicken or tuna. I buy it by the case to make sure I always have it on hand. Super product! And super service from Amazon!

This taste very yummy as my 6 and 7 year olds say.  We have recently found out that my daughter and I are gluten intolerant and we tried this for dinner one night.  My 19 year old said it was better than the tuna helper I had gotten in times past.  We did not have any left overs and my family was asking for more.
We just love this.  I use 2 cans of Garlic Tuna Fillet in Olive Oil (and leave out the margarine)  Has great flavor.  Also super with the Hickory Smoked Tuna Packs.
Throw it all in one of these Micro-Magic Microwave Pressure Cooker with some greens for 12-15 minutes and you've got yourself a meal.

I'm new to the G.F. life. Everything I get is compared to non-GF foods. I was pleasantly surprised when I made this meal and my kids and husband LOVED it!! I loved it as well. I work full time and have two small children, this is GREAT for a quick meal and I don't have to feel guilty. I'm definatly a fan of Mrs. Leeper's. I love her corn pastas as well. My italian husband also enjoyed her pastas. He said he would have never known it was GF if I hadn't have told him. The only complaint I have about Mrs. Leepers pasta, the next day cold pasta salads aren't as good as when warm. Still tastey, but the texture toughens up a bit. I'm still a fan! I'd recommend it. Heck, if you GF with kids who are or aren't GF, I'd even recommend the case!!

I tried this for the first time last evening and was surprised at how well it turned out. The taste was outstanding and the pasta was perfect! I have found a less expensive source or I would be buying it by the case here. It only took 15 mins to make a meal for me and the kids and they loved it. Outstanding product! I can't wait to try the rest of the product in this line.

column9: Best tasting replacement for Tuna Helper I've had
column10: If you have to eat gluten free and are craving the ease and taste of Tuna Helper, you owe it to yourself to get your hands on a box or so of this.  It's a little bit soupier than the Tuna Helper you're used to, but the taste is great and it's easily the best gluten free option for a meal like this.

I've made this product as per package instructions and it was good.I've also made it by first sauteeing celery and onions and baking it into a casserole topped with crushed potato chips and it was wonderful.I've also made it per instructions and added mushrooms while it simmered, then topped it all with grated cheddar cheese and again it was yummy.

column9: An excellent product with excellent taste to be used with prudence.
column10: I drink this Diet Cranberry/Pomegranate juice specially in the evening as it doesn't contain any calories. It has a delicious taste. That is a product to use with prudence as all those "Diet" beverages are associated with Alzheimer desease. Use it but do not abuse it.

I am glad you ask for a review of this product.  The Cafe DuMonde is excellent but the company that ships it for you leaves a lot to be desired.  Of the 6 cans we received, 3 of them were badly dented in and it did not happen in shipping because the box was in excellent condition.  This leads me to beleive that they were dinged that badly when they were packed.  If I had ordered them all for gifts, they would not have been suitable.  I then called the company to let them know I was unhappy with the condition of the cans received and I left messages at least 3 times with my name & phone number and none of those calls were returned.  I will not ever order this product again through Amazon and I think you should check into this since it is a reflection on Amazon as well.

I recently returned from New Orleans where I tried this coffee and loved it! The coffee was very strong, but not bitter. The chicory root evened everything out. However, 3 cans were very dented upon arrival, and the coffee was, well, disgusting. I am rating this a three, because I did not contact the seller about the dented cans, because that should not affect the quality of the coffee. However, this coffee did not taste at all like the coffee from Cafe Du Monde that I tried a month before in New Orleans.

Ok, Starbucks is awesome too, but this coffee is an acquired taste and is without the doubt the most unique and great tasting coffee.Since it has chicory, you do not mix as much as you would normal coffee. (To be precise, you would mix about half as you normally would).However, even know it is robust, it still contains less caffeine then normal coffee. By the way, chicory is extremely healthy for you.Try it today, taste what New Orleans has had for well over 140 + years.

We visited New Orleans this summer and had coffee and beniets at the REAL Cafe Du Monde in the French Quarter. This product brings that taste home. It's a deep, rich blend of coffee and chickory that is unique in my experience. Very strong, very tasty! Highly recommended.
We've had this product before; either you like it or you don't.We put a scoop in with our regular coffee and it makes such a wonderful cup of coffee!
My family has become a fan of Coffee Du Monde upon a visit to Cafe Du Monde in New Orleans. I am a coffee snob. It is by far the best coffee. We buy it by the case for home enjoyment.

I discovered this coffee in New Orleans at the Cafe Du Monde, during my honeymoon, in 1987. It has a distinct taste and, in a day when the word unique is overused, I can say I have never tasted anything like it, including other coffee flavored with chicory. This offer was spectacular in its price. It arrived in a timely manner. The shipper packed it well.You should consider this product and seller if you want a unique coffee experience.
Couldn't find in any store near us then we found this seller. We got great pricing and fast shipping. Great transaction. Plan to but again.
Great to be able to get this coffee rather than having to find a way to purchase it from New Orleans.  It is so good as I share it with a friend who loves it as much as I do.
Great rich taste,  with much lower caffeine, with Chicory.  The New Orleans way of drinking coffee. Absolutely a great morning drink.

I grew up with this coffee around.  It a Southeast Asian staple in the pantry!  And yes I'm talking about about cafe sua da (iced coffee w/milk) in Vietnamese (but I'm Cambodian and we drink it as well). This is ten times better than starbucks. :)  Yum!

All you you have to do is search the web for Lecithin and Cayenne.  Lecithin is a natural emulsifier that suspends fat in your bloodstream instead of on your arterial walls.Cayenne is a vasodilator that lowers blood-pressure and increases blood-flow.This unique combination both lowers cholesterol and reduces blood-pressure plus it reduces plaque on arterial walls.  There is no excuse not to try this homeopathic remedy.Personally, I take one cup of hot water with one dropper-full of cayenne tincture (homemade) and one tablespoon of lecithin with one teaspoon of granulated garlic per day.  I don't take any statins whatsoever; nor, do I take the hypertension drugs at the high-dosages I used to.  My blood-pressure and cholesterol are both within the safe ranges.As a replacement for the statins, I take presciptions fish oil (Lovaza) and niacin (Niaspan) daily as medications.Comment if you want to know how I make my cayenne tincture.  Also, check lobelia if it applies to you.

I was looking for emulsifier when I encountered a few website suggesting lecithin. Then I realized it is a much healthy suppliment to kids' and adults' nutrition. Have been putting it into everything I bake, can't taste any difference if I keep the addition within couple of tablespoons.Wish there's a smaller package, or local grocery carried it.Wish there's this powdered form to act as cake emulsifier, which provides better distribution of oil among flour, and makes cakes tender without excess amount of fat.Overall, it is a good product and serves for healthy cooking.

column9: Tastes Great and Great for Your Health
column10: I buy a case every few months along with a case of Bob's Red Mill Muesli. I combine the 40 oz bag of Muesli with the 16 oz bag of the Lecithin, and mix it all together in a large zip lock bag. It tastes great. I eat it for breakfast, and then snack on it throughout the day. Quite filling, and a healthy alternative to most snacks.I had liver failure several years ago, and one of my doctors recommended Lecithin Granules.  Lecithin helps your liver produce Choline which ultimately helps your liver process fats more effectively.  I can really feel a difference when I skip it for a few days.

column9: GREAT FOR MY PURPOSE: CORTISOL CONTROL
column10: I've been eating 2 TBS per day of these soy lecithin granules as part of a campaign to bring my cortisol levels down. I've not tested outside of the normal ranges for cortisol in medical lab blood work tests, but I've had a small pot belly, blue baggy under-eye circles, and chronic "tired" my whole life. So, I've researched how to combat cortisol with nutritional supplements. I don't do anything fancy. I simply measure out 2TBS of the granules into a cup, pour it into my mouth, and start chewing. Tastes fine to me.

i heard from quite a few that there are health benefits in using a product like this. so i thought i would try it out for example in smoothies and other things. good quality product. i am happy with this purchase. i hope to reap some health benefits from using it. bob's red mill products are high quality.

I was pleasantly surprised when I tasted the pleasing, slightly nutty flavor of this product. That's a plus because I really purchased it for its health benefits. It's yummy in yogurt, smoothies, and protein shakes. It's also good sprinkled on salads because of its mild, friendly flavor. BOTTOM LINE: This is now another staple in my home; it'll keep my liver from having to deal with the capsules, etc. TIP: Store it in the refrigerator or freezer.

love this stuff.  i can tell a difference if i dont take it. quality is exceptional. i cannot say enough great things about bob's red mill products. great in smoothies, mixed with yogurt, salad. bob's flaxseed, lecithin, sunflower and pumpkin seeds make a great dressing for salads, mixed with some olive oil and garlic. diagnosed w/ a metabolic disorder affecting thyroid and adrenal glands, endocrine system, i'm re-evaluating life. simplify and back to basics. bob's red mill products fit into getting healthy. they are such high quality products. and the price is wonderful. thank you amazon and bob's red mill. happy, healthy new year !!

column9: best little waxy things I ever ate
column10: I don't know why lecithin is good for you, but Bob's makes it good and affordable.

column4: A. Ward "Audio addict answering to Alexis."
column10: My on-going love affair with Amoretti syrups continue, the latest installment is the cherry syrup.This syrup is cherry syrup, not like Slurpee flavoring, but a true cherry flavor. We made our morning coffee in hot mode for me and frozen for my husband. The flavoring tasted better in the frozen mocha, most likely because he also used the good Amoretti dark chocolate syrup in his.Another win!I've been in contact with this company about different flavors so I could make the right purchase (quite a few flavors have multiple options. Vanilla, for instance.) This company has taken AMAZINGLY great care of us. When I asked some questions and told them that we were amassing enough syrup to last through the next nuclear winter, Paul overnighted the standing order of this syrup. We also received a goodie box out of the kindness of their hearts.So far, out of all the companies I have dealt with, I have received professional customer care at best and have dealt with frontally lobotomized troglodytes at worst (somehow it takes something out of it when you have to explain the insult to the identified individual). This company has been like dealing with close friends, to the point that even the thank you note was hand written!! High class company selling high end products, a rare combination and I'm glad I followed the winding links to them. It's been a real treat, from purchase to consumption.

We use flavored syrups (such as Torani) to make Italian Soda or Seltzer with sparkling water. We like the light taste better than soda and are glad to be reducing our intake of sugar and sodium. I just received my Amoretti Cherry flavored Syrup. Let me just say, this is DELICIOUS. I absolutely love it. I cannot wait to try the other flavors we received. Also, the company provided AMAZING customer service!!One helpful hint when using these syrups: If using them in cold drinks, such as soda, first place a small amount of the sparkling water in your glass. Add the syrup and stir until dissolved. THEN finish adding the sparkling water to fill your glass. Also, it is better to start with less syrup than what you need, then add a little at a time to taste.I love the Amoretti bottles. They are very attractive and I don't mind leaving them out on the counter at all. Plus they are made of plastic, so if the kids knock them over, I don't have to worry about them breaking.

The flavors are very nice and I am enjoying them.  I only wish I could find a greater variety of decaf flavors AND could find them at a better price.  I love the convenience of the single serving disposable container, but hate the high prices. ;-)

Then you've noticed that they aren't that common in the stores any more. I can never find the Tropical Fruits and they're my favorite. These ship fast, you get enough to last a while, and the price is right.
Great packing - fast shipping - perfect for My Husband who is "addicted":-)) to all LARGE - hard Lifesaver rolls.

This company was excellent to work with.  I was working on a deadline and they were so quick responding and setting up the graphics.  The gal doing the graphics wasn't happy with the crispness of the first take and re-did it on a Saturday morning!  I had these well in advance of my event and they were a hit with the employees!
The rapper has changed but the flavors are just as i remember. The delivery was fast and the product came in great shape.
Order was shipped in two mailings. Communication was good, though. Items were VERY well packed for mailing! Highly Recommended!!! Thank You!

column9: Candy that tastes great-and made with Splenda
column10: I've tried all the other sugar free candies sold at the local stores.  All of those other brands made with sorbitol or maltitol will rip apart your insides.  Then I found Go Lightly.  I immediately hit up Amazon and here they are-shipped right to my house.  What can be better than that.Go Lightly candies use Splenda and this makes all the difference in the world.  I can eat a handful of caramels with no upset.  I am so glad I found this brand.Taste:  they taste just great.  I gave some to friends who do not eat sugar free candy and they like them.  I can't even tell the difference, I think they taste great.

I ordered my sportea and it arrived within 10 days.  I brew a fresh pint daily and drink it on the rocks with a slice of lemon or orange and a little bit of sugar. It is caffeine free but still is a picker upper in the afternoon.  Refreshing and delicious! I would highly recommend it over any tea I have ever tasted.

column4: Meryl K. Evans "Content Maven behind meryl.net"
column9: One of the Best Sugar Free Hard Candies
column10: Since I cut back on sugar, I stopped buying sugar-filled hard candies. Brach's Butterscotch was one of my favorites. To me, Brach's is one of the best brands of hard candy and candy corn out there that I use its products as a yard stick. None of the local stores carry the sugar free Brach's Butterscotch. So I took a risk in ordering a box of 12 because I couldn't find any online store that sold it in individual packs without ridiculous shipping fees. The first time I had one of these, I wasn't sure I liked them. I figured my tastebuds remembered the originals and needed a little time to adjust. Over time, I grew to love these and don't miss the originals.A word of warning: These have sugar alcohol in them, so they can irritate the stomach or cause gas pains. If Brach's tries to make them a different way without the sugar alcohol, it probably won't taste as good. The advantage of this, however, is that it helps you from eating too many knowing this could happen. I never eat more than four pieces a day (three pieces makes a serving for 35 calories!).Each candy is the same size as the originals -- about the size of a quarter on the outside and a thickness of about a stack of 5 quarters. They taste like a mix of buttery salty flavors.

This is the best sugar-free butterscotch candy ever made.  I have been a diabetic for over forty years and I used to love the regular Brach's butterscotch candy when I was a kid.  This tastes every bit as good as the old Brach's butterscotch candy with one exception...THIS IS SUGAR-FREE!  If you are a diabetic, do yourself a big  favor and buy this outstanding sugar-free candy.  YOU WILL LOVE IT!  Thank you Brach's.  A++++++++++++++++.

I buy this product for my husband.  It's the only hard candy he likes, and local stores have discontinued it.  I finally found it here at Amazon.com at a very reasonable price.  I was so happy to find it, and it's very convenient to order it online and have it delivered to my house in a reasonable length of time. Hopefully, I will be able to continue to get the Brach's Sugar Free Butterscotch hard candy from Amazon.com for a very long time.

column9: Brach's Sugar Free Butterscotch hard candy
column10: This is a very tasty hard candy.  If you have to, (or simply want to), restrict your sugar intake, I highly recommend it.
Doesn't taste like sugarfree candy at all. The best butterscotch taste of any I've tried. Would definitely buy again.
This candy is hard to find, not sold in retail stores, Amazon has a good price and they are dependable, wouldn't have any other candy!
My husband, mom, and I LOVE these candies - taste as if they were made of sugar. YUMMMY!!!

column9: Brach's sugar free butterscotch hard candy
column10: All you diabetics this will do the trick - Excellent hard candy - I was pleasantly suprised by the flavor - reasonable cost - just don't eat too many at one time
We love these candies.  Probably the very best sugar free hard candy made.  Try them you will love them. We sure do!
Tastes better than Brach's regular hard butterscotch to me, and satisfies my occasional candy craving without ruining my weight loss plan.

column9: Wonderful - not artificial tasting at all
column10: I was so very bummed when Walgreen's and CVS stopped stocking this! (For some, reason, they still stock the Brach's S-F Cinnamon ones, which I detest, though my husband loves those.) Now, though it's a drag to have to buy 12 at a time, I'm grateful that it's still available.
These are the best that I have tried they are so much like a normal bread item. Not rubbery or crumbly. I get these all the time.

I'm eating this right now and I don't think I can finish it.  It tastes nothing like Kraft's regular Mac & Cheese (which I love) -- this is almost inedible.  The cheese flavor is very artificial in the worst way possible.  I don't know how this got past product testing.

This is delicious, yes its still Kraft mac and cheese, so its not going to be as good as homemade.. But it is really very good. Its much more creamy and "cheesy" that the regular. Its like using 2 packs of cheese powder and one box macaroni (if you've ever tryed it).

column9: It's edible but that about it...
column10: You can eat it but I wouldn't call it cheddar explosion. Far from it, more like a fizzle. Bigger shapes? Yeah right, if this was bigger I'd hate to see the original versions. Yeah you can use more milk and less butter but it still tastes like buttery slightly cheesy slippery cardboard. If you need something in your stomach and don't really care about taste, quality, actual cheesie-ness and care more about cost, convienance and packaging this is for you. The box says it feeds mulitple people (don't remember how many servings total) but when I made it it barely came out more than 2 rather scrawny looking bits. If you plan on having three sides with your entree then have fun. Our family was not impressed. Plus the original chessiest tastes better than this crap. Will not be buying again and the food pantry will get the rest.

column9: Don't Get Milked Out Of More Money!
column10: I was initially excited to see this product in my local grocery store. I love the original Macaroni and Cheese recipe.But after inspecting what this product is made of, I realized that also buying a 'store brand' and just adding more milk to that product is what produces the same increased cheese taste. And I can save money in today's ever-tight economy. This is very important when every penny counts.Given a choice, I'd rather save money for a product itself. I don't want to pay money for the packaging.

I was very happy to see that I could order just the blueberry tea like the tin that came with my iced tea maker, it's the first blueberry tea I've tried and I love it. I ordered the 4 pack tins and I will for sure order it again!!

Their web page on Amazon.com is extremely misleading - it implies that for $12.99 you get a 3-pack when it is actually only a single bottle (single bottles on Amazon are available from other vendors for only $2.99).

I tried several of the varities to pad my orders, including the Kona Coast Chai, Lahaina Spice and Hawaiian Breakfast.Lahaina Spice is the best of the three, and it is between 2 and 3 stars. It is not real Chai tea, but a Hawaiian version of it.If you need something to pad an order for Free Shipping, consider the Lahaina Spice. The other 2 varities taste like Lipton black tea.

I bought the vanilla, orange, mango, lemon and peach flavors of these.  They are OKAY in hot foods - I used them in herbal teas and to punch up my orange chicken.  However, these were only good in hot foods and in very small quantities.  They were extremely bitter and were completely useless in cold foods because even a couple drops made the item so bitter the food was inedible.  Even in hot foods the bitterness came out after a couple drops.  Save your money and use a better brand like truvia and just flavor your food with pure extracts from the baking aisle.  No bitterness and you get to control the level of flavor.
Tastes ok, but what you get for the price, it is a bit disappointing.  By the time you pay for shipping, you are a loser.  Too bad my hubby LOVES peach flavoring.

This tastes metallic and about as far from peachy as you can get. I love this company's stevia packets, and I like the liquid vanilla and cinnamon, but I will never purchase this one again. I wish I could return it, but that would cost me as much as the refund would be. Aargh.
My kids and I really like this flavor.  It is especially good in oatmeal.

I ordered chocolate, vanilla, and peach.  The peach is okay, but it is not my favorite.  The flavor is subtle and it doesn't end up being very sweet or peachy.  On the plus size, it is flavored with natural flavors, which is why I am switching to stevia in the first place.  Overall, though, I don't think I will get this flavor again.

Purchased several flavors while they were on sale.  The lemon and vanilla are both quite good. I use them in tea, and these flavors hold their own. The fruit flavors (peach, mango) seem too mild to make a flavor difference.The directions say one drop per 2 oz, but I end up using closer to 8-10 drops...but I do admit to having a sweet tooth :)...and even at that level, couldn't discern any peach flavor.
I am trying to get away from drinking diet drinks with aspartame or Splenda, but I simply do not like the taste of this at all.  It tasted like I was drinking chemicals (gee, I wonder why)

I absolutely love these, healthy and yummy with an awesome texture. I love fruit snacks, but am kind of particular about them. These ones are great! One of the best I have had. This particular flavor, the berries and cherries, is delicious! My boyfriend, who usually dislikes all fruit snacks, enjoyed these as well! We are both partial to the dark cherry flavor. Texture is also really important to me when it comes to fruit snacks, and these have an awesome soft texture. You don't have to sit there chewing forever, but if you want u can suck not them and they won't just disintegrate or stick to the roof of you mouth. They are perfect! The only fruit snack that I have had that is in my opinion slightly better than these, is Annie's brand. However, Annie's is at least double (closer to triple) the price of these. I definitely recommend this product =)

My grandson and his friends including my clients and students prefer Ocean Spray Fruit Snacks to Welch's. I always bought Welch's until my grandson suggested Ocean Spray. Out of the mouths of babes, my 8 year old grandson was right! The kids claim Ocean Spray Fruit Snacks taste better, are easier to chew, and don't stick to their teeth. Of course I limit the amount I give them, but as an incentive or reward, the kids love them.

Forget Shan's or other mixes claiming to be your daal spice blend.  This is the best by far - I need nothing else to make a terrific tadka for red or brown lentils.  Ok, maybe a little onion & ginger fried in ghee - but that's all.  Perfect balance of flavor and heat, the chewy seeds bring a bright spark and the rest of the blend is harmonious and perfect for dressing up the dull taste of pulses.  Another note about those mixes out there - check and see how much salt is crammed into those other blends. Salt - the cheapest thing out there, diluting your value.  Ajika Lentil Curry Blend has NO salt at all - you are paying for 100% spice.  Rock on.

These are my favorite chocolate covered cherries.They are good-sized, not small. The chocolate is soft; it's a milk chocolate, but not like most milk chocolate. I normally prefer dark, but prefer these to the dark chocolate covered cherries. It has a great taste, a chocolate not like the 'cherry covered cordials' cheap chocolate. Cherry coridals have a liquid filling; these do not.It has a silky taste and texture, the chocolate melts when you eat it. If you think you might like it, I suspect you will.One note: the pricing here. These are the same item available for half the price ($5.49) at Trader Joe's - while theyr'e two for $21.00 on current pricing here (not to mention almost that much again for shipping).Very good item! Give it a try.

column9: Yummy Incredible-Edible Paring Of Chocolate and Fruit!
column10: These little round bites of DELICIOUSNESS, "Bing Cherry Dragées in Premium Chocolate - 14oz Tub - by Dilettante (2 Pack)" are amazingly addicting and I can hardly keep up with the demand to keep them in my house for any length of time. I buy mine at Trader Joe's-(a single) for $5.49 a box, (NOT AS ADVERTISED AS A (2-PACK). It seems like a lot, but they are worth it! They are great for eating straight out of the box, but they are a really nice touch in ice cream or use them as decorations on a cake. You use your imagination! Think out-side-the-box as they say! The taste of the chocolate surrounding the cherries outside the cherry is melt-in-your-mouth divine! The cherries-(dried) inside the chocolate are yummy and good for you. The best of both world's put together by wonderful human beings in Kent, Washington. I love you guys! Thank you for this amazing treat! Salute! Highly recommended! Enjoy!
Normally, I don't eat high end chocolate, but these are so good! Someone gave us a tub and after eating all of them, I needed to get more. Thanks, Amazon!!
No problems delivered on time as desribed!Kids and adultls alike all enjoyed the the special treat.  The package was more than enough for 10 adults and 13 kids!

In principle, this is a great product:  It's actual fruit, with nothing added, dried to a crisp and put in a packet that only has 85 calories.  If you're looking for light, healthy-ish snack foods that are still tasty, this is a great choice.But there are a couple of problems:1.  The packets are very narrow and long, which makes it virtually impossible to reach into them to get the fruit out, once you're past the top third or so.2.  There's a decent amount of fruit dust inside -- which, as these are berries and cherries, is red, and just waiting for a bit of added water to  stain up any fabric it lands on.Either of these in isolation is no problem, but put them together, and you've got a product that you MUST pour out, and yet a product that you CAN'T pour out.  I guess maybe if you had a bowl or something, it wouldn't be a big deal, but that sort of takes away the portable-snack nature of it, no?  As much as I liked the fruit, the inconvenience of the packaging is going to keep me from buying more.Oh, and one more caveat:  Despite the "Cherry Berry" name, this is at least 50% apple.  I suspect that apples are to dried fruit mixes what peanuts are to mixed nuts, the inexpensive and unobjectionable filler.  The apple tastes fine and all, but I wouldn't mind more cherries and berries, and fewer apples.

Weight Watchers point that is.  The bag is one point.  A great, healthy snack to incorporate into your WW diet, or any other healthy lifestyle.I haven't had a problem with crumbs and powder in the packets I've tried, no more than any other dried fruit I'd buy from Trader Joes or the Gerber ones.  It's definitely a small bag for the price, so if you're near a Trader Joes, you should really buy their dried fruits.Amazon does have a great price for this item though... I paid $1.79 for one packet at a major chain!!  That's insanity.

The Sensible Foods Cherry Berry snacks are great.  I keep them at my desk and anytime I need a little something they are perfect.  No drips or dribbles on the keyboard.  I have ordered some other selections of the dried fruit, but be mindful that there are more apple pieces than berries.  The pouches average about 2 blueberries, 6 strawberry slices and 2 cherries.

When it comes to snacking, the crunch dried snacks are the best. Each fruit has a distinctive texture and flavor. The individual pieces are flavorful so you can nibble one tiny piece of banana and actually taste banana. There is no fat so you don't have greasy fingers.  You can take the packages anywhere.  Dried blueberries taste like blueberries.  Dried cherries taste like cherries. In some of the dried fruit mixes, the general taste is "blend." With Sensible Foods crunch dried snacks, you can savor the morsels slowly, one individual flavor and one individual texture at a time or eat them fast, mingling textures and tastes depending.I keep packages on hand to satisfy midnight snack urges,  to crunch instead of chips when I eat a sandwich, to snack while I watch the tube or to grab and go.  Cherry Berry is frankly delicious.  I buy regularly to always have some on hand.  It is much tastier, more interesting to the palate, and cleaner eating than nibbling on rice cakes, popcorn or chips. The product satisfies hunger, too, which makes it a close to perfect food in my world.  The ONLY reason I did not give it a 5 is because I've gotten packages that were light on the cherries and I really like the cherries a lot.
While the taste is good, the name is quite misleading.  There are very few cherries in the mix.  It is mostly apple.

column9: Best low calorie snack in the world
column10: These fruit snacks are the best low calorie, extremely flavorful snacks in the world.  I eat the Orchard and Cherry Berry for breakfast at my desk every day.  The fruit is dried to a crunch not a gummy chew and the flavor has no aftertaste or funky smell.Overall, I love these snacks more than any other pre-packaged food.  I carry them with me on trips and eat them at my desk or in my comfy chair at home.  Try them!
Very good product to have on hand if you need a quick on-the-go snack. Good tasting and easy to eat. I keep a couple in my car to snack on if I can't stop for a meal right away.

My family and I do all we can to eat our fruits and vegetables, but it's not always easy.  But this product is so easy to eat as a snack and is so delicious, I don't even buy chips anymore!  I love this and am going to keep this product on stock in my house.  I recommend it 100%!!!

These are the perfect size and the fruit is delicious, the only drawback is that the contents are mostly apples, some only have 1-2 blueberries per package and 4-6 strawberry pieces. The apples are very good but are a little bit "sharp" if you are thinking these would good toddler snacks.

The Cherry Berry snacks from Sensible Foods are my new favorite food on the go.  I've taken them on road trips, shared them at the office, and even gave them as stocking-stuffers this year.  I find them delightfully sweet and crunchy, which is perfect for my typical snack craving.  The powder at the bottom of the bag doesn't bother me, but I can understand the frustration some folks have voiced; if you get it on your hands with any moisture at all, it can stick.  I always have little hand wipes in the car or in my purse, so it hasn't caused me any trouble.  I highly recommend this product as a healthy alternative to candy, and I'm looking forward to trying other flavors.

This is the best dried fruit I've had.  There are some big whole berries in there and it's great tasting.  Contains only fruit and nothing else. No fat or extra sugar.  And it's crunchy instead of chewy like most dried fruit.  If I had one complaint it would be once I added up the cost (no shipping cost for Prime) it comes out to $1.11 per bag.  Still, good for you snacks never come cheap.

Love, love, love this snack.  It's low in calories with no sugar added, and it is definitely satisfying.  I like to add it to 0% fat Greek yogurt and it really kicks it up a notch into a nice treat.  It also satisfies my sweet tooth.Much cheaper to purchase on Amazon than buying single packets at Vitamin World or one of those other GNC-like stores.
Easy to pack around for a serving of fruit without the unhealthy extras! We love it!
My family loves these snacks - healthy and easy "on the go" for them!  Great for the toddlers and my older kids!

I love these snack packs!  They're surprisingly satisfying, really crunchy, and have and lots of fruit variety.  For less than 100 calories, I find they REALLY satisfy my hunger pangs and help me wait till my next meal.  So easy to tuck into my bag to take with me on-the-go.  I will DEFINITELY repurchase.  I'm a big fan!

These dried fruit snacks are great for camping and hiking.  The seal is waterproof and the fruit is always crunchy.  I eat them with lunch almost everyday!  The price is a great value.3 Years later:I get these through subscribe and save and it makes them about $1 a pack (compared to over $2 in the store).  My 10 month old loves them too.  She eats the strawberries and blueberries and I eat the apples and cherries. They sell some baby food like this but you get very little dried fruit.

I haven't been able to find these locally, so we ordered a case from Amazon.  We weren't disappointed.  Our only complaint is that there could be more dried berries.  Instead, you get mostly apples which are good, but not quite as exciting.
This is a really great snack food idea.  It is all natural fruit with no sugar added and has a great crunchy texture.  I like to eat it anytime I need something extra!

Not a big "dried fruit" lover by nature, THIS has changed my thinking.  Fresh fruit flavor in nicely dried form. Not at all leathery, very light texture. No additives is a big plus! Easy to grab and go, great for snacking or taking the edge of a "sweet" craving!
CRUNCHY and great tasting. A bit pricey, but hey, you gotta treat yourself once in a while!

Think freeze dried and you have the consistency of this product. You actually re-hydrate it in your mouth. Very convenient way to have 87 calories of real fruit. The longer it is in your mouth, the more the flavors come thru. I will buy again -- I just wish there were more cherrys and less apple in the mix.

This is my favorite topping for cottage cheese each morning. Being diabetic, using a pre-measured envelope ensures that I eat the correct amount. The variety of taste and texture, as well as the quality of the fruit makes Cherry Berry a great product. The ratio of cherries to apples has improved, so those who wanted more cherries should be pleased. Enjoy!

These individual snack size bags are perfect for moms on the go.  A nutritious snack everyone can enjoy.  I saw them at the store for $1.75/bag, and these are just over $1/bag from Amazon.  No sugar added, and very tasty fruits inside. Even my picky 3-year-old loves them.  I only wish they had more strawberries in the mix.

I was pleasantly surprised by the simple goodness of these snacks. They remind me more of fruit that has been "freeze-dried" (like the ice cream at the Air and Space Museum in DC, if you are familiar) than of conventional dried fruit. They are light and flavorful with "nothing else" added to the fruit (as the ingredients state). They might take some getting used to if you are familiar with sugary (or high fructose corn syrupy) dried fruit, though. They are a great addition to organic cereal and low-fat ice cream, too. Yum!

If you haven't tried these, you must.  I have to have these and the other varieties in my home at all times.  Only around 80 calories, and 100% fruit.  Great snack at home, and great for travel snacks.
I was looking for a healthier snack since I am trying to lose weight. I keep this in my office and at home and even eat a pack for breakfast. It is great and my kids age 5 and 2 love it.
These are a great treat without the guilt.  I would prefer more cherries in the mix though.  I'm definitely going to order another box of them.
I really enjoy these as a light snack. They are only 85 calories a bag so it is easy to fit it in your diet.

I tried 3 flavors (Cherry Berry, Orchard Blend and Tropical Blend) and found the following to be true of all of them.1) Packaging is impressive with long, narrow, foil lined one-serving sized bags. However, the size of the bag is deceiving for the amount of product inside. Although they are easy to open by simply tearing off the top inch, they are not resealable - not that you would want to because the servings are so 'small'. The bag design also makes it near to impossible to reach in by hand for snacks. Even a child's hand is too large, resulting in having to eat this snack by pouring into hand or bowl.2) At the bottom of each bag is a layer of fine 'powder' residue from the dried fruits. It gets on everything and stains: esp. when wet from fingers, etc. It also makes it difficult to get the last of the snacks from the bag to your mouth, esp. if eating directly from the package,  because the powder from the bottom of the bag puffs out, up your nose and all over your mouth. Makes a mess.3) All 3 flavors that I tried had the same issue as someone mentioned in their comments before me: each flavor seems to have an over-abundance of one particular fruit. In the Cherry Berry, it is apples. In the tropical, I found it to be mangoes, and in the orchard, it was bananas, lots and lots of bananas.4) I also found some of the snack to be 'crunchy' while other pieces of fruit were sticky/mushy once in my mouth. Ex. banana slices. The combo of moosh and crunch (very little crunch) was disappointing when this is suppose to be a 'crunchy snack'. I found myself using it up in yogurt and oatmeal rather than as a snack.This is a natural snack so the first time around I didn't mind the expense. However, now that I know what to expect, I will not purchase again unless the packaging and fruit 'dust' issues could be addressed. Then it might be worth the money. Until then, I'll buy my own fresh bananas, mangoes and apples.I will admit, however, a few of these put together in a gift basket would make a nice presentation for someone who has never tried this product.

column9: Love this product...and so do the kids!
column10: This is the best dried fruit product we have tried. Sweet and crunchy, totally portable, great for toting around in your bag and a super quick and easy snack. A good choice for people trying to reduce their calories because it is portion-controlled and very satisfying, as well as delicious.

This is a good tasting snack, but I should have read the reviews more carefully.  It's called "Cherry Berry" but it should be called "Apple Cherry Berry with more Apples and some Apples on top".  The apples are fine, but I expected more berries.Also, I don't know if this is an effect of shipping or what, but there's a lot of "fruit dust" in the bottom. Be careful if you tip the package up over your mouth (which you will do since your hand doesn't fit in the narrow package) because it's easy to inhale it.

i tried this about two months ago and really loved it. i love the crunch and natural sweetness.  i also made corn chowder with their corn product. i recommend this for any one who loves healthy natural snacks.
This is a very tasty & nutritious snack!  No fat, sweet & crunchy, a great alternative to running out to the vending machine at work!

Great stuff even though the pouches are small, I'm quite satisfied with one and the quality seems to be very consistent.  Not the typical dried fruit they call it "crunch dried", more akin to freeze dried, seems to agree better with me then the typical dried bulk fruit and being portion controlled you can count calories with ease.  Something people forget when they eat bulk packed dried fruit, they tend to eat too much of it.  Also works well on cereal or oatmeal.It's also nice that Amazon offers it by the box, it's more economical then buying it piece price locally.
I always have these on hand.  They are crispy and taste great.  I wish there were more cherries and strawberries and less apples, but overall these are great.

column9: Good addition to healthy snack arsenal
column10: This is a tasty freeze-dried fruit blend. For the calories in it (84), you get a pretty good snack that'll take you a while to finish. It's a mix of apples, cherries, blueberries, and strawberries - all healthy fruits. No preservatives, fillers, etc. Maybe a bit overpriced, but convenient.

I am Celiac and it is hard to travel, particularly in airports, where it is hard to find RELIABLE gluten-free foods.  I always carry these Sensible Foods items with me; all the varieties I have tried are delicious.  I also share them with my work mates, and all love them and several have become Amazon subscribe and save members on this, as I am.  Great work, Sensible Foods!

column9: Cool idea, but I bought too much
column10: I really liked the idea of having pure fruit at my disposal at any time of the day. I didn't realize that after eating these bags, I would get a bit overwhelmed with the concentration of sugar in these bags. All natural sugar to be sure, but it is a bit overwhelming. Two years later, I still haven't finished eating the 24 packs that I purchased, but it's a lot harder for one person to eat 24 than for a family so... make sure you like this before you buy in bulk!
I think their name says it all-"Sensible Food".  It's a great snack and good for you.  My dog Chloe loves it too. :)
I order this for my office and everyone loves it. I think its a great low cal alternative to chips and such.

I found these at Publix Supermarket the first time I purchased them and then started shopping for them on-line. Amazon is cheaper than the home site for this item. This is a great product! My family is going through our first case very quickly! My little boy has a dye allergy so we struggle to find snacks that are healthy and taste good!! He loves these!!
I add this Cherry Berry and one of the other fruit packages to my tea each morning.  Delicious and healthy.
Worth every cent.  Crunchy sweet, yummy, low cal can't say enough good stuff about this one!
Great flavor and a pleasure to eat.  I find it is easy to get fruit in my diet by carrying these around with me for a healthy snack.  Only 84 calories per bag!

Good sweet crunchy snack to have on hand wherever. Purse, car, office. One (1) WW point! High Vit C (22%), low cal (84) 2 grams fiber. They also come in organic but are more expensive. Good mixed with cereal and yogurt as well as by itself. I keep buying this by the case.
I love all the Sensible foods crunch dried fruits, but I think Cherry Berry is the Best!
My 10 year old daughter loves these. They are all natural dried fruit, and a wonderful snack!!!

i love this snack! i have had a lot of other freeze-dried fruit snacks and these are the best! not only are they delicious, crunchy and light, but they are the perfect portion. some of the other brands give you too much per pack. not sensible foods! and great combo flavors. i also love the orchard blend!

Tasty, tangy.  The only drag is how crumbling the pieces can get. When you get to the bottom of the bag you can't pick up with fingers anymore too tiny. But, you can still eat by just tipping the bag straight into your mouth :-D
My teenagers eat these like crazy. They are just dried fruit with no added sugar and they are delicious!

column9: Definately a good between meal snack or add to cereal
column10: Its tough finding 100% real fruit snacks that low in calories, and these are pretty good. These work well on there own as a snack, good with cold cereal, or even tossed into oatmeal.At a bit over $1 USD per bag, I think they are priced accordingly, but wish they were about $.80 USD per bag generally.There is sometimes alot of fruit 'dust' at the bottom of the bag that obviously weight (sack is .75 OZ), where you wish there were larger pieces.  Also, the pieces range from easy to pick up indivually, to small pieces (like blueberries or 'dust') that can't easily.The bag does not have a re-seal, but they are really built to be a single snack.
Sure they're not healthy, but usually when you're looking for a sugary treat...it's for the indulgence and flavor, not health. Gushers are DELICIOUS. My favorite fruit snack!

I bought these here to put in pirate theme goodie bags (they look like jewels!). I never buy gushers so I didn't realize how much cheaper they are at the grocery store. I'm really mad at myself for spending nearly $30 for them here, when I could have spent a third of that at the local store.
Don't know if we received a bad batch, but this was truly one of the worst things I have ever tasted.  Maybe it was spoiled, I don't know, but they went down the sink.  Unbelievably bad.

First of all, I was worried about the pulp that is present in this product.  But it's not like orange juice pulp.  The little bits of aloe are actually quite juicy.  As someone who does NOT like to have floaties in anything I drink, this pulp was quite tolerable.The flavor was very interesting.  It wasn't very sweet, and the reason for that is obvious.  There is no added sugar.  The only sugar present is the stuff that naturally occurs in the mango, mangosteen, coconut, and aloe.  The result was actually quite refreshing.  But I will warn that it was very coconutty.  I could barely taste the mangosteen and mango.  It was almost like a piña colada.  Coconut is a flavor I absolutely love, so I had no problem with this at all.The one warning I have is what aloe can do to a person's digestive system if that person is not used to aloe.  I highly recommend starting off with about a quarter of a bottle a day and work your way up.  I drink this before I spend any time where I need to keep hydrated because the high potassium content helps the body retain water.  But overdoing it can lead to diarrhea, and that would conter-act the hydrating qualities.I'm editing after drinking a few bottles to give an updated impression.First of all, I've started having to strain the pulp out of the juice.  This isn'ta big deal, but after a couple of glasses, I started to develop a gag reflex due to the pulp.  It's not specific to this drink.  I do the same when I drink pulpy orange juice.  I do, however, have to drop one star because of this.  If it was pulp free, it would get the full five stars.Another thing I've noticed is that this tastes almost identical to all of the other Coco drinks made my Alo, so which one I buy in the future will be determined mostly by which one is the cheapest.And of course, the final thing I'd like to point out is that this stuff has some pretty amazing hydration qualities.  If I drink a half a bottle before excercising, the water I drink while excercising goes a lot further towards quenching my thirst.  The reason, of course, is because it contains such a large amount of potassium.  Potassium is an electrolyte, and electrolytes are needed in order for the body to absorb water that is ingested.  I used to get full on water while spending four hours in the 100 degree heat on the golf course, but a quick potassium pick-me-up before the round helps me to regulate the amount of water I need to drink while outside in that heat.  For that reason alone, the fact that it is a great natural alternative to Gatorade, I will be continuing to buy this product.

column9: Very good. Tastes like a graham cracker with figs.
column10: These taste like a combination of graham cracker, with a little cinnamon, and with fig mixed in. They are sweet, but not overly so. I put them in a ziplock bag after opening and they stayed crisp for over a week. So the fig is not so overwhelming as to make the cracker "soggy".  They are about 3 inches diameter, and are round. The nutrition information says they are about 100 calories, with about 2 gm of fat in a two cookie serving. These are a good snack for those moments when I have a sweet tooth and do satisfy.

column9: Tasty but Not as Good as Original Newtons
column10: For a `healthy' snack they are quite good.  They have a very sweet taste and bits of fruit that will remind you of the original fig newtons.  I liked the crunchy texture of the cookies which reminded me of Honey Graham crackers.Each serving of 3 has about 140 calories and contains about 2 g of fiber and 5 g of fat.  To get the fiber in there the cookies are a little dry and I had a glass of milk when eating them.  They are quite good dunked.Overall I enjoyed them and will probably buy them again.  One note I seem to have eaten them all myself as none of my children cared for them.  I suppose it is more of an adult taste.

column9: Da Better Flavor, but still I've eaten better
column10: This was the flavor most people preferred when I shared these Fruit Thins in the Office and the response was 45% YUCK, 40% GOOD, and 15% Neutral.  The Yuck group complained that the cracker was too dry, fruit tasted like cough syrup, texture was too chewy.  The Good group like that this was at least nutrious compared to similar crackers and tasted like newtons.  I fell into the neutral group and my main opinion is that it is okay, this type of cracker has been done before, some have had baked better versions and the price is quite expensive for a bag of crackers.  One of the more colorful comments is that NEWTON'S are always characterized by a soft fruit filled cake and this product just does not come close to that description hence the comfort food factor which might have made this more acceptable is lost.  Good effort, bad execution.
I have enjoyed the original fig newtons, but this new cookie was not as pleasing.  It tasted like a sweet cracker, with odd chewy fig bits, speckled throughout.  A poor imitation in my mind.
These are just okay. As cookies go, the taste is nothing special nor that unique. While they certainly are not bad, I will likely not be purchasing these in the future.

These cookies are awesome. They taste very good and they are more heathly for you than most other cookies. They are very crisp and they are made with real fruit. They come in a variety of flavors. If you like Fig Newton's then you will like these cookies.

It's a small thing, but the figs in these cookies will really stick in your teeth and I would not recommend these if you are currently wearing braces.  I really like the shortbread texture and the fact that three of them only total 140 calories, making them a great snack insert for my perpetual diet.  There is a distinctively figgy taste, which is somewhat overdone in my opinion, but the pieces of fruit themselves just get so imbedded to the point that I feel the need to brush my teeth immediately after eating.  Otherwise, of the ingredients that I can pronounce, they are made with unbleached enriched wheat flour, sugar (no wonder they taste good), whole grain wheat flour, soybean and/or palm oil, rolled oats, dried figs, raisins, honey, salt, baking soda, rice flour, and natural favor (contains cinnamon).

These little cookies are delicious! And not altogether horrible for you. They are crispy with a little bit of stickiness (in a good way) from the figs. They remind me somewhat of teddy grahams in their flavor: strong but not too artificial. I brought them to work and they were gone within the hour! Great snack for any age.Downside: They package isn't that protective, and they got a little crumbly in the mail. I saw them at Albertson's for something like 4 dollars a package? There are also other flavors, but I think the fig is probably best.Filling without being heavy or unhealthy, and healthy without being bland! What more could you ask for?

First, a couple of minor negatives with these cookies.First is the name. For years Nabisco advertised, "A cookie is just a cookie, but Newtons are fruit and cake." Why the Nabisco marketing gurus would think that it was a good idea to associate the "Newtons" name with these thin, crisp cookies is beyond me.Next is the packaging. The trend today is toward recycled-content paperboard packaging, such as the one Nabisco used for their new Ritz Crackerful Multigrain Crackers. These cookies come in a foil-lined bag with a plastic liner, neither of which can be recycled.The cookies themselves are quite good. They have a light texture similar to that of a shortbread or butter cookie. There is a nice light sweet flavor that is not overpowering. As is often the case when you use dried fruit in a cookie, the fig bits are a tad hard and chewy. I thought these go best with a beverage. Tea, coffee, soft drink, and even (according to Mrs. Boilermate), wine. We both agreed these are "adult" cookies.While we prefer the Cranberry Citrus Oat flavor by a slight margin, we will buy these, too.

My kids don't like them and I don't care for them, however I'm not really much of a cookie eater. I think these cookies are more designed for adults because they are not very sweet and are hard and brittle. If you like a hard dry cookie like the Canadian Biscuits you'll probably like Newton's Fruit Thins. They may be good for dipping in milk, tea or coffee.

column9: C is for cookie -- that's good enough for me.
column10: In the great word-association game that is cookie-eating, "Newton" conjures up immediately the image of those pillowy fruit-filled cookies, the kind that some people carefully pull in half to get to the fruit first and others just gulp down whole. Well, forget about them, because the Newton folks have something new here.These cookies, as the name implies, are flat -- really flat and think, like the chocolate wafers you use for baking or a ginger snap. Thinner than most crackers, certainly thinner than your standard cookie. So they have a crunch and a snap to them that's unusual for an cookie. It's a satisfying crunch; these are thin, but eating one feels like a real cookie. (Not to say that the thinness won't lead to eating vast quantities -- ask my wife; she demolished most of the box, even after I told her I need to eat more of them -- purely in the interests of science, of course! -- for review here.)The fruity taste comes as something of a surprise -- it's throughout the cookie, as well as baked into tiny little nubbins of fruity something-or-other. (I'm not an industrial chemist, so I'm flailing around for the right terminology.) These cookies obviously don't have the fruity softness of the pillowy Newtons, but they're fruity enough for a good taste.Actually, let's be honest here: these are *cookies.* They're sweet and crunchy and my family demolished a whole box of them in less than a weekend. There may be bad cookies out there, but these are not among them -- if you've read this far, you obviously want to know "Are these cookies good to eat?" and the answer is most definitely Yes.

column4: Wayne Klein "If at first the idea is not absu...
column10: My wife picked these up for me just around the same time that we ordered these from the Vine program. Newton Fruit Things have a nice fruit flavor to them and are lighter than regular Fig Newtons. They're a nice alternative to those and to something as simple as graham crackers.Recommended.

column9: Surprise!  Husband Likes a HEALTHY Cookie
column10: These cookies make a perfect accompaniment to a cup of green tea.Not too sweet, with an interesting infusion of flavor from the fig and raisin bits.  They're nicely crisp, with a barely perceptible oat flavor that adds an extra dimension to the taste. And despite having added fruit, the cookies manage to stay crisp and maintain their texture, even after opening the package.I like the fact that they're made with some multigrain flour and I find that 3 cookies makes a satisfying snack.I was shocked to find that not only would my husband eat these (he's a notoriously picky eater) but would actually say he LIKED them.  Awesome feat, Nabisco!These are unlike any cookie I've tasted before (and nothing at all like a fig newton, in my opinion).  Give them a try; you might be surprised to find a new cookie favorite!

More of a cross between a cracker and a cookie. I love these! They have a very distinct flavor that both my wife and I enjoy, as well as the kids. Trust me, to find a snack that everyone likes in our family is no small task! But we are very happy with the Newtons Fruit Thins Fig and Honey, and look forward to trying other flavors.

column9: Thin, crispy cookies with a bit of fruit
column10: I am a big fan of all types of cookies, including all varieties of Fig Newtons. These Fruit Thins are not exactly a thin Fig Newton, they are a thin, circular cookie with bits of fig and a honey flavor. The taste is reminiscent of the original Fig Newtons, but there is no soft, paste filling.The cookies are perfect for a light treat with a cup of tea, and the thinner size keeps them from being too sweet or filling.  I think you could compare them somewhat to a sweet biscuit instead of a full size Fig Newton. Light and crisp, my husband and I both enjoyed these cookies, and have already bought another bag.

column9: A different type of graham cracker
column10: I was pleasantly surprised when I tried these cookies. From the packaging and description, I expected a stronger fig taste. However, after my first bite, I thought, "Wow, these taste like fancy graham crackers." Aside from the typical graham cracker taste, these also had a hint of cinnamon, which went well with the overall taste. My only criticism is that, after I was done chewing the cookies, I would have small bits of fig in my mouth, as the pieces are kind of hard.Definitely worth a try, though, especially if you like graham crackers!

Ahhh research.....it needn't be reading or testing product 100% of the time.  Taste testing is a pleasure when it tastes like these thin, cookie like disks.  They are a perfect compliment to coffee, and possibly hot tea.  They do not work well with iced tea for some reason. The specific taste is hard to place...somewhere between a butter cookie, fig, and raisin.  These thins are at their best when nibbled slowly with a late morning cup of coffee - oral confection heaven.

column9: Very different than Fig Newtons, but a terrific snacking biscuit in its own related right.
column10: 'Newtons Fruit Thins', as the name of the product, evokes a pretty specific response in my head.  Fig Newtons maintained a better-than-irregular presence in our pantry when I was growing up, and that dense cake(y) exterior of the Newton wrapped around the dark and rich fig filling was (and is) a pretty distinct taste and experience amongst mass-produced cookies.  It's always interesting, I think, when an (at least somewhat) iconic brand rolls out a new derivation of its core product -- or at least that's what I imagined 'Newtons Fruit Thins' was going to be.  I was wrong, but I wasn't disappointed.Unlike the soft richness of the original Fig Newtons, these snap a bit like crackers.  They are crumbly, not flaky or otherwise too dense or tough to be difficult to bite into, but they are wholly a different textural experience than the original Newtons.  Toned down is the sweetness, although the rich and chewy (sometimes a little tough/dense against the relatively softer biscuit) bits of fig still elevate the overall flavor are still reminiscent of the original cookie.  These are, perhaps, a more mature and refined thin biscuit when compared to the classic Newton; they're light, tasty, and satisfying, while still managing to be relatively healthy when compared to similar snacks (and that's what I think this is, a snack item rather than a dessert).  Three biscuits represents 140 calories, 5g total fat (1g sat fat), 95mg of sodium, 60mg potassium, 21 total carb, 2g fiber, 7g sugar, and 2g protein.A bag of the fig and honey has impressed us enough that we've added two of the other three currently available flavor combinations to our list; the Newtons Fruit Thins Raspberry Chocolate, 10.5-Ounce (Pack of4) and Newtons Fruit Thins Blueberry Brown Sugar, 10.5-Ounce (Pack of4).  Good stuff, looking forward to trying the others, and that's the bottom line when and as it comes to this review.

column4: J. Thompson "Janet's Treasures, a little of e...
column10: Let me start off by saying, I don't normally like fig cookies. Just something about them in cookies. Love them every other way. These have such small pieces of the fig in them that you get a really good flavor from them. You can taste the honey, also. I had my husband and daughter try them also. Husband loved them! Daughter only slightly liked them. I do believe we will buy these when we get a chance. I thought they might be a little bit on the dry side but overall, they were good!

I've been a Fig Newton fan for over 30 years, and was delighted to try the new Newton Thins.  What a disappointment.  Original Newtons live in a chewy-fruity world of texture-taste sensation.  The Newton Thins are supposed to be crisp, but are more crisp-ish, while the fig is negligible and tasteless.The concept is a good one.  If this cookie had been done with cranberry or something punchier than fig in small doses it probably would have fared better.  Likewise doing a fig cookie more like the danish cookies would also have been a good concept transference.  Instead, the Newton Thin tries to be a cookie AND a Newton and it can't be both; which I guess is why the old tagline was, "it's not a cookie... it's a Newton".

column9: light and healthy, with only a single flaw
column10: I like Fig Newtons, and Newtons in general. I also like honey. So it goes without saying that I wanted to try these. Newtons are always a healthy alternative to other types of cookies and snacks, so I was hopeful these would be the same.I wasn't disappointed.These cookies are very crisp, they are flaky but not soft. They hold their shape very well, and surprisingly, even after shipping, only a few were broken in the package. There are about 30 cookies in s single 10.5 ounce package.In terms of consistency, I'm very pleased. They remind me of shortbread. Each cookie is about 2.5 inches in diameter, so they are a decent size.There are three cookies in a serving, and the serving totals 140 calories. Personally, three is a bit much, so I keep it to two. However, in a regular serving, there is 5g of fat, 2g of fiber, and only 7g of sugar. The sugar content is really low, making for a good healthy alternative.My only complaint is that the figs are a bit chewy and hard in the cookie. This may immediately turn you off from having more, since it takes a little more effort to chew than a Newton. It could also be the honey combined with the fig pieces that makes them a little tough. Also, I've come across one fig pit piece in a cookie...so you need to watch your teeth. In other words, you just need to be mindful of this while eating the cookies (and the same holds true for Newtons, too).I like these enough to buy them again in the future. They are delicious, hearty, and healthy. Other than watching for a rare pit, I highly recommend them.

column9: If you like your Newtons crispy...
column10: I brought these Newtons Fruit Thins Fig and Honey into my office to share with my colleagues during an afternoon break.The first thing we noticed is the lovely cinnamon-and-cookie smell when you open the package. These sweet mild cookies with tiny bits of fig call out for a cold glass of milk or a good cup of tea.  I prefer the older fruity-Newtons, but these are a really good alternative for crunchy cookie fans, mixed cookie plates, or those looking for a less fruity Newton that still has plenty of sweet, cinnamon, cookie goodness.

column9: Reasonable Cookie - Palm Oil is a Concern
column10: The cookies themselves are reasonably good.  They are thin, but that was the idea, wasn't it? The cookies have a nice texture.  You can taste the honey and figs.  They do go well with tea. The calorie count, 140 for three cookies, is about the same as the granola bars that I sometimes snack on.  Just don't eat the whole box at once.The ingredients are also reasonable with the exception of the use of palm oil.  As palm oil use has increased dramatically over the past ten years, commercial growers have been clearing rain forests in Indonesia and Malaysia to create palm oil plantations.  The palm oil is used in food production, as in these cookies, and in the manufacture of bio-fuels.  The result is a loss of endangered species and ironically increased carbon emission. There has been some movement to either reduce palm oil use or use only palm oil from sustainable sources.  There have even been stories of girl scouts agitating to sell only palm-oil-free cookies.Kraft is aware of the palm oil situation.  It is not clear that they are doing anything about it. This is from a July 15, 2009 Wall Street Journal article:  "Kraft spokesman Richard D. Buino said that while the company supports the RSPO's [Roundtable for Sustainable Palm Oil] efforts, "it is clear more work is needed to consolidate standards, enforce principles, verify traceability along the supply chain and ensure competitive pricing to bring certified palm oil to market. We're monitoring the RSPO process and actively engaging our suppliers to monitor their certification efforts to find viable options for sourcing sustainable palm oil." Neither Nestlé nor Kraft directly addressed purchases of Malaysia's certified palm oil."The cookies go from four to three stars from me as a consequence of the palm oil.

The cookie is pretty tasty, presumably because of the honey.  The fruit is a bit hard and bland, and definitely disappointing.  Overall, I could see that some people would really enjoy the cookies, but I did not.  Don't get me wrong: they were fine.  I would eat them if they were offered to me, without complaint.  But I don't think I will be buying these any more.  It was surprising because I definitely enjoy Fig Newtons.

I am one of those people who has a disgustingly ravenous sweet tooth. Almost any sweet treat will do but of late I have been making an effort to go for fruit over cookies. But come on, everyone deserves a real sugary snack now and again. Candy bars and pints of ice cream have been my vices in the past but the humble cookie is the one I go for when I want to feel like I'm eating a lot when I'm not really. When I saw these cookies offered on Amazon's Vine I skipped them in favor of books and went out and bought a box (to conduct my very own taste test review) because they sounded good. I'm glad I did because I love these!Newtons Fruit Thins are hardly Double Stuf Oreos as far as sweetness goes but if you enjoy the classic Fig Newton this one is like a crunchy cousin. A little bit cinnamony with a graham-crackery note of honey and little nibs of fig sprinkled through-out. If you like graham-crackers or crispy oatmeal cookies these will probably be a delight. Certainly they're not for everyone and it's a matter of personal likes but these are hardly the tasteless bits of cardboard others have suggested they are. I believe it is fair to compare them to tea biscuits, these the aren't sugar-coma inducing cookies your 8-year-old is going to demand.
