While nice in taste the fruit bits just didn't contrast well with the thin crispy cracker texture.I will probably serve the rest of these with, say, tea. When there is an expectation for a not too sweet, crispy accompaniment. But, I won't get these again otherwise.
These cookies are really more like crackers.  Thin and crunchy and very slightly sweet.  The sweetness comes from the fig, but they smell wonderfully of honey.  Great with tea.

column9: not what i expected, but good ...
column10: I was not expecting a hard cookie w/ little chewy pieces, but they are actually very tasty.  Kind of like a hard oatmeal cookie, but the fig pieces are quite small and chewy.  Great with tea or coffee.  Just remember that these are hard and thin ... there is no filling.  The fig parts are tiny chewy pieces in the hard cookie.  I am fond of these, but just want to make sure you know what you are getting.

column9: Don't go in expecting a Fig Newton, and you'll be content
column10: For some reason the incorporation of the Fig Newton product name in these didn't trigger enhanced expectations in me, even though I am a Fig Newton fan.  I looked at some of the other reviews here, and found a number of reviewers who seem bitterly disappointed that this is not some kind of thinner Fig Newton.  Just to get the idea out of the way, this is NOT a Fig Newton!What it is is a dryer, thin cookie.  I found the taste to be decent, not too sweet, and for some reason the texture is interesting, much more so than on a true Fig Newton.  There isn't a sign of the oozey filling that a Fig Newton has.  I like them fine, but they didn't rock my world.  Thanks to the hard reality of weight control and middle age, I don't allow myself to have cookies or Fig Newtons very often anymore, but when I do give myself that guilty privilege, I'll consider this product in the future.

I think that these cookies are great to go along with a cup of tea or coffee.  They are very crispy and the flavor is light, I thought they would taste like a crisp fig newton but they aren't. I don't think that they would be consider to be 'diet' food either, so if you are looking for a low sugar cookie this isn't it.  This cookie is something that I think would fit in with a sensible eating plan in that you can have 3 cookies and only consume about 140 calories. Which makes them a good indulgent snack that isn't the same old thing.

These Newton Fruit Thins in the Fig and Honey flavor are in a word Delicious!The flavor of the cookie is just sweet enough without being too sweet tasting. Thetexture is crisp without being too crunchy. In other words just right all around.

column9: Grown-up Great (and kids will love them too!)
column10: I am watching what I eat, so some kinds of cookies are off-limits.  This is a notable exception.  The ingredients read like something your Mom would make:wheat flour, enriched flour, sugar, whole grain wheat flour, soybean or palm oil, rolled oats, dried figs, raisins, honey, salt, baking soda, rice flour, soy lecithin, cinnamon.Three cookies are four Points Plus points as calculated by the WW calculator, which means you can have a few without blowing your whole day.  They're really good with coffee or tea.  There are some kinds of bread that don't taste good to me (Wheat hot-dog rolls for example) because of the wheat.  These cookies don't give away that they're made with wheat flour, and I like that.  I get to feel like I'm cheating when I'm not!Good stuff!

column9: Plenty of heft for a cracker - more like a cookie,  healthier than a Newton
column10: I was prepared to pooh pooh these and say not bad, but I was really quite impressed. A single cracker, which looks like a bog standard cracker, actually has tons of flavor, texture, and heft, and the fig and brown sugar (really raisin, don't tell anyone) flavor lingers. It smells like a graham cracker, which is no means a bad thing.I actually have some fig newtons to compare with here, so I'd note that for the serving size (30g) the Thins are 140 calories while the Newtons are 110 calories, so the thin is only in one dimension.The Newtons have 'Enriched Flour, Figs preserved with sulfur dioxide, corn syrup, high fructose corn syrup, sugar, ...' while the Thins have 'Unbleached Flour, sugar, ...'. This is a big win for the Thins for me if true.Okay, let me eat a Newton here. *HOMF* The sacrifices I make for you people. The Newtons very clearly have more 'fig' texture and fruit mass, but the mealy soft bleached wheat texture of the Newton shell has never been a plus in my book. I much prefer the crunchiness of the Thins and the way the gooey fig and raisin tastes linger - I assume because they're more dried in the Thins.Eating another Thin now. *MONCH*. Oh yeah, that really is better. Okay, stopping here for tonight.So other than the 30 extra calories per serving for the Thins I give the win entirely to the Thins. I have no problem ditching the Newtons for these - they've got more fruit, but much more extra crud crammed in as well, so even with the extra calories I'd deem the Thins healthier, or at least as healthy as mass produced food products can be. And heck, they taste better. If you can restrict yourself to eating just one, it's quite a satisfying snack for 50 calories.

column4: Prosecute Wall St. Criminals "End Corporate Rule"
column9: Not too soft, not too sweet...just right
column10: I really love these new & very different cookies.  They are crisp yet chewy, not extremely sweet like most cookies.  The dough reminds me of a cross between a digestive & a graham cracker, but very crisp & thin in comparison to either of these.  Bits of dried fruit throughout make it chewy at the same time, & quite unique.  I'm finding it very difficult to stop eating these.  I got both the fig & blueberry and they're both excellent, although I probably like the latter a wee bit better.

Expectations are important - I generally associate Newtons with a soft fruit-filled cookie, but these Newtons Fruit Thins don't match that description whatsoever. They're neither soft nor fruit-filled.That said, they ARE delicious!The Fig and Honey cookies are just the right level of crispy, with a fresh taste and just sweet without being over the top. My girlfriend said they remind her of pinwheel cookies her grandmother used to make, and I recognize that flavor too, a little zing of ginger and cinnamon and a touch of sweet honey. Tiny pieces of dried fig mixed in give the cookie a bit of texture without being chunky.And dipped in coffee? Divine! This is the ideal cookie to complement your morning cup of caffeine.The Amazon price at the time of this review is a little steep for my taste - about $27 for a bundle of four packages, meaning almost seven dollars per package. I'd pay more like four or five dollars per package as a treat for myself and my family.The name is something of an enigma - these cookies have little to do with the Newtons I know. But they are a delicious surprise, and I'm sure we'll be back for more, especially if the price comes down.The first package we got was gone in only a few hours. I'd better think about stocking up!

I must have liked these since I ate six upon opening the packet. These cookies are certainly tasty, flavored with both fig and honey. I suspect they would be delicious with cream cheese. On the other hand, as I gobbled these down, I kept wishing I were eating those delicious chewy fig newtons so I guess I'm damning them with faint praise.Additionally one serving-- that's three cookies-- has 140 calories and 45 from fat.I see from the packet that Nabisco offers other fruit thins as well.

Yum! These are a combination of all the things I like in a cookie. Texture like shortbread but a more interesting taste. (To the reviewer who complained that they are crumbly and break up in your mouth--that's what shortbread is supposed to do!) The honey is subtle, not too sweet, and the whole grains add some substance. The bits of fig and raisin are small--about the size of caraway seeds--and chewy. I was able to recognize the figs, but then, I like Fig Newtons, so I probably knew the flavor from that. Package says serving size is 3 cookies, but I found just 1 or 2 make a satisfying snack to nibble on without being too many calories or too much sodium. I'll probably buy these again.

First of all, these are nothing like the original Fig Newtons, which I think I was expecting with fig in the name.  They are a good, not too sweet cookie, kind of like a spicy shortbread in texture (not chewy).  The fruit bits are a little too tough (get stuck in your teeth), and there are other ingredients that seem too crunchy.  They are good enough that I would try the other flavors.

Got these yesterday and needless to day the bag is gone! They are the perfect mix of a shortbread cookie  with hints of figs and honey! The  figs are candied so they have a nice caramelized crunch as you eat the cookie, couldn't really taste the honey, which is cool, because I'm not a honey freak, all in all this cookie was delish and i would highly recommend it!

NABISCO NEWTONS FRUIT THINS CRISPY COOKIES comes in a 10.5 ounce package.  In side, is a clear plastic drawer that can be pulled out and pushed back in.  The drawer has two compartments.  The bag is made of foil, and it has a sturdy aluminum clasp for re-sealing.  Now, this is about what is inside. Inside, there are about 28 cookies.  I cannot be totally sure, since I already consumed a few.  The cookies are colored light brown and they have a wavey, scalloped edge.  The cookies are not soft and they are not particularly crisp.  They are in-between.  There are little flecks of dark stuff here and there, which are bits of figs and raisins.  The flavor can be characterized as "generic."  The flavor is like JUICY FRUIT CHEWING GUM.  In other words, it does not have any particular flavor.  The fruit component of these cookies is not convincing.  Using the term "Newtons" in the name of this product does not do justice to real fig newtons.  Real fig newtons, as everybody knows, is mostly fruit.  But I would guess that the quantity of fruit in these cookies is under 0.5%.  And so, what I say to the food scientists at Nabisco (Kraft Foods) is, "Nice try, food scientists, but you have not in any way improved upon the classic fig newton!  And you have not even come close to the original!"

One of the great pleasures of a Fig Newton is the wonderful chewiness of the outer cookie and the filling.  I was a bit suspect about a thin, crunchy cookie under the Newton name, but I have to admit the cookie is good.  It has a nice crunch and a balanced sweetness.  Three nice-sized cookies are only 140 calories, which is another pleasant surprise.  My only complaint is that the cookie leaves a bit of a chalky feeling in my mouth after eating it.  I can't say this will topple the original Fig Newton from its perch near the top of the cookie world, but it is a nice complement to the product line.

column9: Yummy and very different to my taste buds.....
column10: Okay...My girlfriend is the expert on ingredients etc and I'm not a dietician but I know what I like and these are thin like crackers but are moist and seem to have a healthier flavor and taste to them than cookies. I did read that they had no high fructose corn syrup so that is excellent but the serving sizes are 3 crackers so ....If you can limit your scarfage they may be somewhat healthy.  I like them and if my gal pal signs off on the ingredients I'm sure I'll pick em up from time to time at the market. I guess all I am saying is that they taste good to me.

column9: Surprisingly tasty and not too sweet.
column10: I wasn't sure what to think of these cracker/biscuit/cookie thins.  They don't really look like a cookie and I guess the name on the package is more accurate than anything I could come up with, Fruit Thins indeed.But I kinda like them.  I didn't much care for them when I got them in the mail yesterday.  I might have been too full from dinner (pulled pork with broccoli slaw and potato salad) and I was jonesing for chocolate, nothing satisfies a chocolate craving but chocolate, so these fruit thins seemed a bit bland for me.But I grabbed one to go with my coffee this morning and it went down all right, in fact the overal crunchy, lightness of the thins were the perfect counterpoint to my overly creamed and sugared coffee (I'm a coffee-with-my-cream-and-sugar coffee drinker, don't judge).  My son didn't care for them, he didn't like the little chewy bits of dried figs or the honey-vanilla taste of the cookies themselves, but I really like figs (and honey, too) so, to me, they were just about perfect.The packaging could be a little better, my thins were mostly broken when they arrived, not a huge problem, a broken cookie never hurt anyone, but if I'd wanted to share these with guests it would be nicer if most of them had arrived in one piece.  Also, they were a tad stale.  It is the rainy season here and the reifastenable bag should be a little more airtight to preserve the crunchiness (also, not a huge problem, I popped them on a plate into my toaster oven for a couple of mins to 'recrisp' them).As an added bonus the thins have 2g of fiber (3 cookies per serving) at 140 calories per serving.  Not exactly diet food (which I really hate, btw), but compared to the dark chocolate covered oreo truffle I ate with my coffee last week, these are healthy and filling.

I was really excited to try these cookies when I first saw them in the grocery store. We didn't buy them right away and when I found them offered through the Vine program I was quite pleased. Fig and Honey wouldn't have been my first flavor choice, but as I do like regular Fig Newtons, I figured I'd give them a try. How bad could they be? The answer is...very, very bad.I like cinammon but the cinammon in this cookie was both overpowering and artificial tasting. Something was just "off" and "too strong" about them. It might be whatever other "natural flavors" are in the cookie and not just the cinammon, I'm not sure, but something just didn't work and the cookie had a bad aftertaste. My 11 year old son said he thought they had a bad "before" and "middle" taste too! I can't argue with him there.The dried fruit bits were equally bothersome. They made the cookie difficult to eat as the bits were too chewy and stuck in my teeth. I don't want to have to pick fruit bits out of my teeth when I eat a cookie.All in all, this cookie was a huge disappointment.  My children wouldn't even take a second bite of the cookies and I wasn't too thrilled about eating more myself.  As a fan of fruit newtons (both fig and other flavors), I had high hopes for these cookies. If the basic cookie for all of the flavors is the same, I won't bother trying any of the other flavors.

I wasn't so sure I'd like these cookies.  Fig and honey sounded like it would taste alright, but when I opened the package, the cookies looked more like wafers or crackers instead of a cookie.  I'm not really a fan of those more healthy cookies that look like crackers, so when I opened this up, I was skeptical of trying it.  I gave one to each of my three children as well to try.  I have very picky children yet each of them wanted another one.  They were very tasty and since they have real fruit, you could surely taste that in each bite.  My pickiest daughter proclaimed, "Those cookies were really good!"These cookies also have no high fructose corn syrup in them at all and contain about 7g of sugar for 3 cookies.  They are a healthy alternative to other sweet snacks that contain undesirable ingredients.  Overall I thought this product was healthy and tasty. I liked it and so did my kids!

column4: Marilyn Meredith "Marilyn, author and avid re...
column9: A tasty cracker with a hint of fig
column10: I enjoyed this tasty cross between and cracker and a cookie. I've always loved Fig Newtons, and expected the taste to be more like one of those cookies. The one thing it didn't have was much fruit--probably a good thing for many people, but I love the taste of figs and would have liked more. The cookie itself had a great flavor and texture. My husband didn't have any trouble downing several along with a glass of milk.

column9: A Fig Version of A Graham Cracker
column10: The cookies (crackers - something) are about as round as a baseball.  They are crispy and crumbly like a graham cracker.  I shared both boxes I received with my co-workers and the comment I heard most often was that they tasted like a graham cracker. I also heard quite often, "Mmmmm, I would buy these."I thought they tasted very nice. The fig part was subtle and a great burst of flavor that complimented the cookie part.  If healthy was a taste then that is what I would describe them as. They aren't unhealthy from what I can tell but they aren't exactly low fat or low calorie.  5gs of fat. 140 calories.They really did make for a nice little snack.While I thought these were good, I did prefer the taste of the orange cranberry ones better.

column9: Better than I thought they'd be!
column10: Okay, first, you need to know that I usually don't buy cookies, we try to really limit our sweets intake and we also try to eat things that are 100% whole grain, so cookies just don't fit into that, we also shop almost exclusively in the natural/organic section.  I love regular Fig Newtons, but stopped eating them when we started eating more whole grain and no/low sugar and over all healthier.  Also please know, I do not like crunchy cookies, I like soft cookies, period.  That said, I was surprised by how much I liked these.  They are thin and relatively crispy without being dusty/messy crispy.  I definitely taste the fig but not so much any honey, nothing wrong with that.  Over all the flavor is nice and there is enough flavor, some plain cookies of this type are just like sugary cardboard, but these have flavor.  I think I prefer the flavor of the cranberry ones to these because the flavor of these is not as strong and is warmer flavor than the citrusy cranberry ones.  Now, what surprised me the most, how not-that-bad-for-you these are.  There are no preservatives which is nice.  The first ingredient is enriched flour, but they do have some whole wheat flour and whole oats in them too, the are sweetened with sugar, not HFCS, and has fructose listed near the end.  We won't buy treats or sweetened cereal where a serving has more than 9 grams of sugar, and guess what?  These only have 7 grams of sugar per serving which is three cookies.  I will not at all feel bad letting my kids eat these cookies, especially since a serving for a preschooler would be one cookie.  I also like that they bag is re-sealable.  Now, while I said I preferred the cranberry flavor that preference is not enough to make but the cranberry ones over these and the reason is that the fig ones have one more gram of fiber and one less gram of carbs per serving, that little extra is enough that I'd choose the fig over the cranberry and why these got 5 stars instead of 4 like I gave the cranberry ones.

Newton's Fruit Thins are a wonderful new addition to the Newton's family. I'm a big fan of fig and I loved their Fig and Honey cookies. They are made with whole grain and real fruit, which is a big thumbs up for me. The are not overly sweet, which also is a plus in my book. I hate when something is so sweet that you get that sick feeling after eating it. The are crispy, but not too hard.I highly recommend these crispy cookies! They're very good and everyone in the family will like them!

I didn't know what to expect from this new product in the Fruit Newtons line, but I find this Fig and Honey flavor Newtons Fruit Thin to be a very tasty cookie.It's crisp but not brittle, infused with pockets of fig and honey flavoring.  It's also not too sweet -- kids may be disappointed that they'll be denied their usual sugar rush, but adults will be pleased, and indeed you could serve these without embarrassment alongside some posh European biscuits at a tea party.Newtons Fruit Thins also don't seem to have too many chemical ingredients.  I recognize almost all the ingredients listed, and the cookies are low in saturated fat and offer zero cholesterol.So I give these a thumbs-up, and I would be interested to try the other flavors in the line.

These Fig and Honey Newtons Fruit thins are the perfect tea biscuit! Made with whole grains and real fruit, this is one biscuit I am happy to let my little one snack on.  She does not even like figs, but says, "These are by far the best cookies ever!"  The fruit thins are delicious, with a delicate fig flavor, not too sweet, and wonderfully crispy.  Just 140 calories, 7 grams of sugar, and 5 grams of fat (only 1 gram of saturated) in 3 nicely sized cookies.  And best of all...no high fructose corn syrup!  I look forward to trying the other flavors.

column4: T. Lee "God has died lots of times, but someo...
column10: These are passable thin cookies.  The packaging was sealed tight and they were fresh with a honey taste that wasn't cloying.  However there were bits baked in (I'm guessing the figs) that were a little on the tough side.  I don't see myself getting these again; I'd much rather stick to the Fig Newtons.

Having grown up on Nabisco Fig Newtons, I was eager to sample this latest Nabisco fig product. After trying these fig and honey thins, I wondered "what was the point?" Although tasty and good for dunking in coffee, they pale in comparison to fig newtons from the standpoint of taste, nutrition, and overall appeal. These thins are pleasantly sweetened with honey with specks of dried figs, but they can hardly be called "Fruit Thins" since the figs are so insignificant. I and members of my family enjoyed them with our coffee, but we all decided that we probably would never purchase another bag. We found this product too understated. We'll stick with our Fig Newtons, thank you very much.

Newtons Fruit Thins Fig and Honey, 10.5-OunceI love fig newtons and thought this would be a great, low-sugar snack food. I was surprised to find that there was only a hint of the fig newton taste. There are bits of fig in the cookie, but it is hard and not really appealing. The cookie itself is crisp and a pretty good size but the overall taste is bland to me. Also, it isn't overly sweet which is nice but I wish it tasted more like fig newtons. For the price and taste I will be looking elsewhere for alternatives to cookies and the like.

column9: Better alternative to traditional graham crackers or Teddy Grahams
column10: I found these to be a better option to comparable snacks...For the GOOD:*quite yummy...reminded me of Teddy Grahams Graham Snacks - Honey, 8 oz*Ingredient list is completely understandable...no super multi-syllabic preservatives or flavoring agents or hygrogenated oils.*sodium level is pretty good -- 95mg per serving (about half that of traditional graham crackers).Now the not so good:*figs -- it's really more fig bits.  It's great that real fruit is used but I doubt I could've ever figured out what it is based on the tiny bits.*The second ingredient is sugar:( and contains palm oil:(The thin cripsy cookies/crackers are about 2" in diameter (actually slightly smaller than the picture on the package).  And three of them (30g) = 140 calories...about the same as traditional graham crackers.Overall, I would choose these over the traditional graham crackers or the Teddy Grahams.

I'm a little torn on this review.  I think that the key question for any Vine review (which means the product was given free to review) is whether or not the person would buy it (again) with their own money.  In this case, the answer is: I might.I like these crackers/cookies a lot.  They are sweet and crumbly, akin to a Graham cracker.  The "real fruit" may be real, but it is composed of tiny gummy bits o' fig in there, very much like breakfast cereals that boast "real fruit"...I ate a large number of these and craved more.  But at the same time, I felt the same guilty feeling I feel after eating too many Chips Ahoy or Oreos... They are tasty and are pretty elegant looking--they'd be perfect for putting out at a party for a snack.

Generally speaking I find that the changes companies make on classic snacks are really more about grabbing more shelf space for the company than really producing appealing product.  The family of Oreos is a good example, with the originals being the only really tasty family member.  And as a fan of Fig Newtons, I have to say I was skeptical about these new fruit thins, but what the heck, right?Well these things are really good.  Like original Newtons, part of their appeal is that they're not icky sweet.  If anything, these new fruit thins are even less sweet than Newtons, and the sweetener is sugar, not hfcs.  You may or may not care about that.  I think it's important.  What's also important is that a deal of the sweetness, as with Newtons, comes from the fruit.While the cookie itself is made with white flour, it does boast 2g of fiber from the addition of some rolled oats in addition to the dried fruit.  The result is a crisp cookie that has a nice, fruity flavor and no nasty aftertaste.  There are three large cookies to a serving at 140 calories.  That's not a bad snack, really, when you consider how little you get in most of those 100 calorie packs of cookies.This is perhaps not the most wholesome snack you can eat, but you could do far worse, nutritionally, and unless you like the uber sweet, artificial-tasting cookies that flood the supermarket shelves, you'll probably really enjoy the new Newton fruit thins.

column4: Wandrwoman "Wise as Aphrodite, Beautiful as A...
column10: These are OK for British Tea Biscuits. The kind your Auntie Maude eats at 4pm with her cup of tea. Not too sweet. Not too much fruit. Not much taste or texture. Nothing to over stimulate or even partially stimulate the senses. Just something to eat mindlessly to curb a small appetite until dinner.I really wouldn't call these cookies, or at least not red-blooded, proud-to-be-an-American cookies. They are certainly not French or Italian or even Greek cookies, either. Newtons Fruit Thins are the wan, oat-y things you get served on a small plate in a London tea room right before the check comes. I have nothing against the UK, but other than Scottish shortbread, I can take or leave their "sweet biscuits".Now, these Newtons Fruit Thins are not particularly bad for you. In fact they have some whole grain flour added to the enriched, unbleached wheat and rice flours. There is soy lecithin for protein. The mild flavoring comes from bits of figs, raisins, honey, sugar and a tiny, tiny bit of cinnamon. Three of them are 130 calories. I got bored at two.In the classic 1963 movie comedy "Come Blow Your Horn", the aging playboy played by Frank Sinatra warns his mooching younger brother to "Stay away from my Fig Newtons!"Fig Newtons! Now that's a cookie I can get excited about!

Oh my goodness, these Newtons Fruit Thins Fig and Honey smelled so good. While the spices are the last item on the list of ingredients ("natural flavor, contains cinnamon"), the scent of homemade oatmeal cookies permeated the room.It's too bad that the cookies were disappointing.  I expected something wonderful from Nabisco's Newton line.  Oh, they weren't bad; they were comparable to generics on the supermarket shelf. They are crispy, not soft like Fig Newtons. However, note that they were dry, and the fruit bits were tough.Scent is supposed to heighten flavor, and that's probably why they tasted as good as they did.  I give them three stars.My Gentleman Caller gave them two stars out of five.I am glad that I was given an opportunity to "try before you buy" because, at their price, I'd rather save my pennies and buy something generic.  If this was my only cookie option, I might skip cookies altogether.

I really wanted to try these cookies because I love Fig Newtons. I got the package and was pleasantly surprised that the bag was resealable. The cookies come in a short tray. My bag had some broken cookies but most of them were whole. I had my husband taste them. He loved them because he could dunk them in coffee and they do not disintegrate. He loved the flavor and texture of the cookie.Since I had some cookie pieces, I decided to see if my dog would like them... he LOVED the cookies. After I gave him the pieces I had to break another 2 coolies because he kept asking for the cookies.Overall, this cookie was a huge success in my household. I will be buying them again.Serving size 3 cookies - 140 calories.

column9: a great snack, slightly British, but not "out of this world"
column10: These "cookies" or "biscuits" remind me of biscuits I eat whenever I'm in Britain.  they're thin, crispy & crumbly.  They're definitely tasty with a strong honey accent.  As for the "fig" taste, there is a mild taste of what you had in the original fig newtons, but it's not so strong that I would definitely pick out the fig.  They remind me of the kind of cookie/biscuit that you would eat with tea.  I liked them.However, my 5 & 3 year olds did not find them as enjoyable.  They found them uninteresting.  That's what I expected since the cookies look like they're intended for a mature audience.What I love about these cookies is that they're a cookie while not being the traditional calorie-loaded cookie we think of.  If I want a tasty, little light snack, I grab one or two of these and I'm good.  Pair it with some grapes and it's a decent snack for a busy mom.  They're delicious and tasty enough for that.why did i give it five stars?  Because I really like them.  Having said that, I won't rush out to buy them, which should make them a four star item.  However, four stars implies there's something wrong with the item, which there isn't.Remember the old commercials for the original fig newtons?  The children sitting with the elder people with British accents having tea?  That's what this product is.  I think they need new product packaging, though.  The box makes them look more fun than they are.  They should be in some organic food-type package that is fashionable because these cookies fit more into that category.  They seem like they would be perfect to flavors like "lavender" and "rose".Overall, give them a try.  The flavor is much lighter than the original fig newtons.  Don't expect your children to love them, though!

column9: I like the regular Fig Newtons better
column10: I was looking forward to trying these since I like Fig Newtons and love fig in general. They do have a good taste to them, but I don't like the texture of the fig pieces. They are hard and chewy (like old, stale raisins) and stick in your teeth. I don't find it enjoyable for that reason.

column9: I like them, but I'm in the minority
column10: The main reason the Newton Fruit Thins earned 3/5 instead of 4/5 is because I'm the only one who liked them out of all the people I tested them on.Let me back up. These Fruit Thins are flat, crispy cookies with a touch of fruit flavor (Being from the Fig Newton family, I expected a bit of moisture, but you'll never get confused that you're getting one of your daily fruit servings from these cookies).  Since Amazon sent me an entire package, I shared it with my 8th grade students and some adults. The students across the board tolerated the cookie, but wouldn't select it given a choice. The adults were mixed in their reviews. Some gave it a thumbs down, citing a cardboard bland taste, and others loved it as a low-calorie snack (about 50 calories per cookie.Me, I think they live up to their name--a crispy thin with a hint of fruit. If you like graham crackers, you may like these, although they aren't as flavorful. I certainly don't find the 'luscious flavor of figs, sweet raisins and honey' advertised on the package. A couple of setbacks: The fruit is so sparse--ninth on the ingredient list and behind 'folic acid' and 'palm oil'--I don't know how they can call it 'real fruit'. It is 0 carbohydrates, which is good, but it's also 0% of vitamin C, A and Calcium. You won't eat these for their nutrients.One complaint: the packaging is inferior. When I opened the bag and tried to use the retie at the top, it fell off, so I had to transfer the crisps to a plastic bag.Overall, a good choice for a snack that doesn't overfill you.

A friend of mine brought a package of these to a meeting and it was a hit. I love thinner, crispier cookies and these are full of flavor! When I brought a package of these home, my husband and kids devoured them! If you are a fan of fig newtons but also like the crispy feel of thinner cookies, try these!

column9: Taste peaks so does the price
column10: The first bite was honey sweet, then granola wave then a recall of ohoy's chocolate chip cookies without the chocolate chips. For all the healthy attire, the thins have taste. The fig tinies can get sticky. I do not like the fig crisps of Newtons but I liked this.But the price, for the new fangled fig looking packaging is unbelievable. I did rather buy dried figs from Sprouts and feel lot more healthy and righteous.

I was excited to try these and was not disappointed. I was in love after the first bite. They are light and crisp with bits of fig in them. 140 calories for three is not bad, if you are really worried about calories, have only two is 93. They are perfectly sweet and awesome!

I am sensitive to high fructose and bought a pack of these with out checking the lable. I was awake all night long after eating those.I can't believe they are still adding HFCS to these when everyone is trying to stop using this harmful ingredient.

Something new to try in the world of healthier snacks, I suppose. Kinda like a cookie combined with a cracker with little bits of fruit in them. Very thin, Wasn't really impressed by these. If there was nothing else in the house to snack on, I MIGHT have some of these, but I wouldn't go out of my way for them.
These cookies have a great crunch and terrific flavor. The fruit tastes quite fresh, and they aren't too sweet. I'd like to try the other flavors as well. I'd definitely buy them again.

I was surprised at just how much i loved these.I have always loved fig newtonsthese are even better than the fig newtons themselves and dont leave you over filled.the only criticism  i have is the figs can be hard some times-- like when you catcha popcorn kernel in your teeth. But that was infrequent and The taste supercedes this issue !!These ship well and the packaging was sealed tight.i will be buying more!

column9: Looking for Fig Newtons? Look Elsewhere. Cookie? YUM!!
column10: If you are a fan of the typical Fig Newtons (which I am most definitely NOT!), then you may expect these to be similar. They are COMPLETELY different.  More like a thin cookie with a grainy, earthy, fig taste with a tad bit of honey. REALLY yummy and crunchy.  It is on par with the typical "organic" type of cookies which are so delicious. I highly recommend them!

Newtons Fruit Thins are a cross between a cracker and a cookie.  They're rather sweet, but tasty.  Not a bad snack for those counting calories.  The figs are cut up really small, so you don't get the fig flavor like you do with a regular Fig Newton.  They've sat in the pantry for quite awhile, so not a big favorite at our house.

column9: These are nutritios as well as tasty
column10: If you have to treat yourself with something nutritios as opposed to empty calories, this is a good choice. 140 calories per 3 cookies, 45 from fat, 2g protein and 2g fiber...not bad at all...and they are super tasty.

I have to start out by saying i"m not a big fan of Fig Newtons (or any other variety of the previous Newton cookies).  However, I loved these little cookies.  I'm not a fan of the "gooeyness" of Fig Newtons or the stickiness of the fruit filling. These are crisp cookies with bits of fruit and a hint of a honey flavor.  They would be great with a cup of tea for an afternoon snack or a decadent breakfast.  They have some amount of fiber in them. So, you can tell yourself they're nutritious.

These were surprisingly delicious.  The serving size is three for about a 100 calorie count. Lots of times I want something crunchy when hunger beats its way to my stomach, these guys fit the bill perfectly and are quite filling also.

First things first, I was struck by how hard and thin these cookies are. They don't look appealing at all, but somehow got eaten REALLY fast.Not as good as the cranberry/citrus ones, and you mostly taste cookie and some random hard bit of dried fruit you can't put your finger on.I can't remember the serving size, but it's more than 2 cookies so you get a good amount of cookies for your WW points plus value.

Our household is 66% like, 33% dislike on these "cookies".They have a great crunch and the fig/honey fruit has just the right amount of chewy-ness to it. It is probably 98% crunch and 2% of the fruit chewy-ness.  They also seem to keep well (and maintain the crunch) even after the package was left open overnight.By healthy, well, it is far better than junk food and real chocolate chip cookies - it's a good "healthier" compromise when you really want a quick snack.Our household isn't unanimous on these though - so if your family likes fig newtons, then I'll they will probably like these "cookies" too.I'll be packing the lunch boxes with these...

I received these in the mail and immediately opened them.  I am a big fan of Fig Newtons (fruit and cake) and I wanted to try these immediately.I was less than enthused.  The cookie had a good taste and crunchy at first, but seemed to have a bitter aftertaste and seemed "waxy".  The aftertaste seemed to be primarily associated with the glazing of the cookie.  Not sure if this was part of the effect of the honey or not.  Anyway, I found it difficult to finish the box and would not buy these from the store.  I tried them a few more times,just to see if anything had changed, but the bad aftertaste was still present.I did not try any of the other flavors and I'm not sure if this one is still offered or not.

column9: A little bland, but good with coffee...
column10: These are one of those thin, more subtly flavored cookies that work better going with a hot beverage than on their own.I do like the regular Fig Newtons better, but these serve a different purpose, so comparing them isn't really that fair.3 stars because I feel the flavor could be improved, but all in all they're not bad.

I was a little unsure of how I would like these. I'm a big fan of the texture of Fig Newtons, and since these were thinner, crispier snacks, I didn't know if the familiar flavor would make up for the lack of the usual Newtonish softness. I was pleasantly surprised, however! They're not a replacement for Fig Newtons, but they are an interesting take on figs as overly sugared food-shaped objects. They were softer than expected, but I did like them, and the honey was a nice additional note to the flavor. Good stuff!

I think this is the best "new" cookie to come along in a very long time. Not too sweet. You can really taste the fig. I like a crisp cookie and this one is perfect. I have tried one other flavor, and I love it also. I hope these become a staple on the shelf in the cookie isle. I want to eat these for the rest of my life, like I have always had Newtons. I like this cookie so much I may never buy another kind for myself again. It would be wonderful with a little cream cheese!

I've always loved the taste of figs, but have honestly found most fig cookies to be a bit rich, in particular Fig Newtons.  That's why I was really curious to try this new variation.  I can honestly say that they have the fig flavor I'm looking for without the over-rich fig filling of the normal cookies.  They have have a bit more substance to them in terms of texture, and are more cookie-like and less short-bread in nature.
These are way too crunchy.  They do not have the best flavor. Not recommended. There are many other better cookies available.

Newtons Fruit Thins may be a bit dry for some tastes.  There is a nice contrast in texture between the chewy fruit bits and the cookie.  The fruit gives some extra substance that makes the Fruit Thins more filling and satisfying than the cookie alone would be.  The cookie portion is delicious, as well.
These are good but I think I was spoiled by the Blueberry flavor.  They are my favorite.  I like the whole line because they use better quality ingredients.These are delicious but I'd like more figs.

Newtons Fruit Thins are hard to review because my family and I ate them all so quickly! The fruit thin is a cookie with a little bits of fruit (fig) mixed in.  The cookies are crisp, but not overly sweet (they go very well with milk). We enjoyed them more than the classic fig newtons.The hint of honey is subtle and gives the cookie its sweetness.  The fruit bits give a good mix of texture between the crisp cookie and softer fruit.As far as "healthy" goes, Newtons Fruit Thins may be a step up from Chips Ahoy, but ultimately the Fruit Thins are still snack food/junk food.I suggest you buy two of them because everyone in my house enjoyed them quite a bit.  They are a perfect snack and a great choice for something a little different in your cookie treat.

I really enjoy these to fill my belly a bit without indulging in junk.  These thins are pretty large and taste great.  I think the best way to describe them would be that they have a graham cracker taste with a bit more density than a graham cracker, with small chewy bits of fig baked in.  I was expecting a more fig newton taste and they aren't like that at all but are vey good.  I will buy more to keep at my desk at work for a snack.

Before you try the Newtons Fruit Thins, please don't think "cookie" in the traditional way.  At first, I was expecting more of a 100 calorie version of a Fig Newton and I was wrong. This is more of a biscuit wafer (crunchy) with pieces of dried fig in it.  My first bite, I bit into a hard piece of fruit and OUCH. I was not expecting that.  However, the entire package was enjoyed my myself with tea.  The good news? The kids wouldn't go near them!  Ha! Gotta love that!  I am giving the Newton Fruit Thins a 3 due to the hard pieces of fig here and there. I would think that might be an issue for people with dental issues.  As for taste, I would have given them a 5 because I don't like traditional sweet cookies.

column9: Not as good as the original
column10: I rec'd these and thought they were decent enough.  It's kind of like a fig newton, except in a sweet cracker form.  I much prefer the original yummy fig newtons (although now I eat the Paul Newman ones - no HFCS).However, after having 1 or 2 I put these out for my co-workers and they ate them up!  So it's all a matter of preference I suppose.  Note that this version of the fig newton contains quite a bit more fat than the original.

Don't try these without a big glass of milk! Even the bits of fig are dry and chewy.My husband liked them, so maybe it was me, but it was like a mouthful of dry oatmeal, they have an oatmeal kind of texture/taste.I prefer soft, moist fig newtons to these. They kind of remind me of the tasteless cookies made just for toddlers, but you can't give these to babies, the fig part is too chewy and they contain honey.I never met a cookie I didn't like, until now. I gave it three stars because my husband liked them and my kids didn't spit them out and refuse to eat them, although they weren't wildly enthusiastic about them, but I just didn't like them.

Nabisco's Newtons Fruit Thins are an interesting creation, and they were nice to sample.  I like the flavor-- it's mild, not super-sweet and would actually be a great choice to have with coffee or tea.  The fig pieces are a little hard, but I suppose I'd rather them at that texture than to be super-soft.  The package has lots of servings, so one purchase should last you a while.  Based on my experience with this flavor, I'd like to try the others as well.

Newton's Fruit Thins Fig and Honey are wonderfully addicting.  This delicious, crispy cookie is filled with little bits of real fruit and made with whole grains who would have known something this healthy would be so yummy. First bite I was not to sure I would like them but quickly realized this unique and lightly sweet flavor combination was filled with delight and surprise and I could not stop eating them.  Watch out!

column9: Product Review: Newtons Fruit Thins Fig and Honey Cookies
column10: As part of the Amazon Vine Review Program, I get to review some pretty interesting items. And I'm always happy when I can snag a food item that we want to try, but not pay money for something we might not like. With food prices the way they are today, you can all understand.So I was thrilled be be able to review the new Newtons Fruit Thins Fig and Honey Cookies!The Newtons Thins line is a new line of delicious, cripsy cookies made with the goodness of real fruit and 8g of whole grains per serving. There are four choices: Fig and Honey, Blueberry and Brown Sugar, Raspberry and CHocolate and Cranberry Citrus and Oats.We all like figs, so i opted to go with the Fig and Honey, as Kiddo REALLY likes fig newtons, and with Summer around the corner, I wanted to see if these would be a good option for a summer snack!First off, I was happy that the package has a resealable (fold-over ties) top- no having to use an extra bag or container to keep the cookies fresh- yeah!Secondly, I was surprised at how large the cookies were each! Healthy cookies usually equate to smaller sizes! The cookies are crisp (as they are thin) and have bits of dried fruit instead of a fruit filling, like tradition Newtons.Even Kiddo was impressed that the cookies tasted good! Now admittedly she said she liked the traditional Newtons better, but then she's four and likes the fruit filling ooiness the best! The adults were split on which they liked better. I think it would depend on what you were in the mood for. We even considered grinding up the cookies for a crust for a cheesecake (but didn't get around to it before too many were gone). I think they would be great as a crust for cookie bars as well! Definitely recommend this for kids and adults!Disclosure / Disclaimer: I received this product for review purposes, free of charge, from the Amazon Vine Program ! No other compensation, monetary or in kind, has been received or implied for this post. Nor was I told how to post about them!Newtons Fruit Thins Fig and Honey, 10.5-Ounce (Pack of4)

If your a fan of dry cookies/crackers, then look no further. Think of these new lil snacks as a flat, dry fig newton. As far as taste is concerned.. In my opinion, not so much. The texture reminds me of a cross between a ginger snap, and a caars cracker, which is not a bad thing in itself. However when i'm eating a cookie, i'm hoping not to have to compare it to somthing else. Try em for yourself. See what u think?
We enjoyed these flavorful cookie-cracker hybrids. The fruit pieces were plentiful and chewy, the cookie was mild and sweet. A great combination.
This tastes so good especially during really cold days in winter around the holidays. It makes me feel more festive!

As with the other Earth's Best products, Chunky Orchard Fruit is a quality and wholesome food for my baby.  According to the label, the ingredients are: Organic Apples, Water, Organic Apricots, Organic Pears, Organic Bananas, Organic Dehydrated Apples, Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C).
These are just chunky enough to keep things interesting without being a choking hazard.  Definitely a great transition to 'real' fruit chunks!

I loved this food for my girls and they loved it too.  They didn't like the texture at first because they were not used to having chunks in their purees.  They quickly adjusted to a new texture and this food became a favorite.  I still give them this at 19 months when we travel.

I use jar foods when I am on the go or if I did not have time to leave the babysitter food. I made a majority of my twins food from scratch using the baby bullet, a chopper or just by mashing it. Now that my twins are 11months they have been eating table food. I was excited to see that Earth's best made Stage 3 foods.Unfortunately, this Particular Stage 3 option (Earth's Best Junior Baby Food Organic Chunky Orchard Fruit, 6-Ounce Jars) is not Stage 3 quality. It is very thin comparable to the Stage 2 food. It does have a few small tiny tiny pieces of fruit in it but nothing compared to the other stage 3 thicknesses. Seeing as my twins are used to have bigger thicker pieces of food they eat the food off the spoon so quickly.As with all Earth's best I love the quality of the food and my twins love the taste. However, I would not have purchased if I knew it would be so thin.

I love Earth's Best and I was a little weary of ordering it online. But, everything was great and just what I would expect from this brand. I do have to say that it was not as chunky as I thought it would be. My son is almost 10 months old (only has 2 bottom teeth) and he is somewhat picky about textures, so I mix it with oatmeal and he is a happy camper.

The 3rd stage has more texture than 2nd stage. In the beginning, my boy doesn't like 3rd stage that much as his variety 2nd stage Earth's best. But after a few weeks, he get used to the texture and love his 3rd stage food.
Great quality at a good price and pure yumminess!!! I ate them! It felt like eating a jar of healthy goodness.Thanks!

I have an 18 month old who only has 4 teeth. Needless to say, she still eats a lot of pureed foods. She can eat cereal, which she usually has for breakfast with fruit, however she's gotten bored with it. I got her some of these Earth's Best Oatmeals, which adds some variety to her breakfasts. She seems to like it a lot. I heat it up for 20 seconds in the microwave to make it warm oatmeal. I like the fact that this oatmeal has a lot of iron in it, which is necessary for a growing toddler!!

This is a good combo and our baby loves it, but he esp likes the chunky pasta. Stage 3 is supposed to be chunkier but we find that the pasta is the only part that is. Wish there were more veggies for him to chew.

We've had some trouble finding baby food that was thick and chunky enough for our little one. We've come across some that may as well have been soup. This is not that soup. This is a good thickness, and she seems to like the taste. No complaints at all!

I bought this for my baby (since she didn't have teeth at the time) thinking that it would be a good source of iron. Unfortunately, the ingredients did not mention that there are RAISINS in this product. The combination of apples, raisins and cinnamon is not a good idea at all. My baby actually started gagging when I put a spoonful in her mouth. When I tasted it myself, I felt like doing the same. This mixture is just too sweet because of the raisins. There is also a very strong flavor of cinnamon. I usually add some cinnamon to the food she eats so I know that she likes cinnamon if its in a normal quantity. I tried diluting the flavor in several ways, but it's no use. The cinnamon flavor was still too strong. I still have about 8 more jars to experiment with. I'm thinking I'll give it one more try by mixing apple puree with a little bit of this mixture and see if the baby will take it or not. Otherwise, it's all going in the trash. I hate wasting food but there doesn't seem to be another option.

At first my son loves it but when he tried other baby food he doesn't like this anymore . I think it's the sourness of the apricot that he's not fond of. Earths best should sell a variety so it is easier for us,moms, to feed our children. I was worried that we had to throw about six jars.
This product isn't too runny like a couple of the other Earth's Best #3 baby food.  Had good consistency and tastes very good.

My daughter loves this Spring Vegi Pasta. So I ordered a dozen Earth's Best Junior Baby Food Organic Spring Vegetable and Pasta, 6-Ounce Jars (Pack of 12) - very disappointed to have a package arrived broken leaving me a huge mass and short food supply! I ordered previously the stage 1 and stage 2 with the same brand ( forgot the seller) which arrived in perfect condition with a tight box wrapped with plastic. Another disappointment is that it's not eligible for return! A huge mass and waste of money!!

I was a little apprehensive about ordering this product. However, once tried on my twins and they love it! The all natural ingredients, organic nature, and good calorie count (120 in 4 Oz), makes it very appropriate for my kids. I wish it was less chunky but I can work with it. So far we have not been dissatisfied with any Earth's best food products.
My son LOVES this oatmeal. He is 16 months and has been eating it consistently for abt 7 months. It has a great texture and is a great transitional food for stage 3 toddler.

My granddaughter absolutely gobbles this stuff up.  This has been one of her favorite Earth's Best foods and she has only refused to eat the Chickem & Stars.  Quality of food is consistently good with Earth's Best.
This stuff  smells like oatmeal cookies. It's thick and a little chunky - my daughter loves it!  (i have also tasted it and it is quite good.)

column9: Chunky thick consistency, baby doest like the taste
column10: My daughter will eat just about any flavor from earths best, incl. Fruits, vegetables and soups. But for some reason she won't eat this one. The consistency is thicker and chunkier than the others. At first I thought it was because she wasn't ready for stage 3. But now that she is 10 months old and is used to eating thicker soups and other foods, she still refuses this one. It tastes fine to me, go figure

I have given this to both of my kids throughout their first year and it was a hit with both.  It's a nice thick texture and very filling (which means a good morning nap). Both my kids ate this for breakfast, along with a yo baby yogurt each morning and they got a very nutritious breakfast.  Love it because iy is a little thicker so it doesn't fall off the spoon before you make it to their mouth!

My son gobbles up the veg and pasta every time I give it to him. One review said it's to thick but you could always add a little water to thin it out if you need to. This is a great meal to help transition your baby into eating more table foods eventually.

My 11 month old loves this flavor!  I love it, too, since it is healthy and doesn't stain clothing! LOL.Will definitely be buying it again- it's a great deal on Amazon.com, too.  We have the Amazon Prime membership andyou can't beat the price, and I LOVE the 2 day free shipping that comes with the Prime membership!Another reviewer said that it gets thick in the fridg- EASY FIX- Just STIR IT before you give it to your baby!I always stir it when I open the jar for the first time and have never had a "too thick" problem after the jar has been in the fridge. Remember, like any food product, the liquid separates sometimes and you just have to stir the food.  No big deal.  Problem solved.  If you still have an issue with it, I would recommend adding a few drops of water or formula to the food. Then stir again.
Some of the oatmeal(or something else) seems to be too chunky and my son, who normally can eat small pieces of chicken, tends to gag a lot with it.
This really make my son's pupu happy. Everyday my son only take in half jar is enough to have soft pupu. And easy to be feed.

I love Earth's Best products (except their diapers, they are very hard and stiff and seem uncomfortable for my baby) and this isn't an exception. Baby doesn't really like it but we keep trying because babies tastes change. I only buy Earth's best babyfood and the thick consistency is much better than Gerber's stage 3 veggies.
Will not be buying this flavor again.  My 10 month old will not eat it.  It is very thick, especially after being kept in the fridge after opeing.
Very happy with my purchased. I told my sister about it and she said she'll order for herself too. I couldn't wait to use it for my cooking and definitely will order more, don't wanna run out again.

column9: My favorite balsamic cream I tried from Amazon so far
column10: I first encountered Balsamic Cream in England a few years ago. When I was in Italy March 2008, I bought Mazzetti Balsamico Cremoso at a grocery store, which was wonderful and reasonably priced. Earlier this year I bought a couple varieties on Amazon, and I just bought a few more for holiday gifts, not all of which are making the cut! Here are my personal views of the ones I bought:#1 Casa Rinaldi Crema di Balsamico Blanco (white). This is not the dark Balsamic Cream I have had before, but of all the ones I've now tasted, this is my favorite. It is the perfect balance of vinegar and sweet, the texture is thick, but the flavor is light. Wonderful! ($11.95 for 8 oz from [...])#2 De Negris Balsamico Glaze - also a great flavor, balancing vinegar and sweet, but much thinner texture. Fine for dipping bread etc. ($11/7.3 oz) ($10/13.5 oz on Amazon)#3Da Magreta Acetaia Real Crema di Aceto Balsamico di Modena (Glaze of Balsamic Vinegar of Modena): second best flavor and thicker ($23/16.9 oz)#4 Modenaceti Balsamic Gkaze: thicker, good flavor, but more grapey than the others above. (3x13.5oz for $28)I also tasted Earthy Delights, which was thick and more tangy/vinegary than the others above. I'll use what I have, but probably not buy more. $14.50/500mlFor my taste I would not again purchase Mussini Crema di Aceto Balsamico di Modeno (Glaze of Balsamic Vinegar of Modena - sweet, grapey, caramel-y" and don't know what to do with Roland Balsamic Glaze (thick, but very, very vinegary - ugh).
I love this glaze! Great on any fruit, even ice cream; delicious finish to chicken or fish. A small amount packs a lot of flavor!De Nigris Balsamic Glaze Balsamic Reduction 7.6 Fl. Oz.

This Glaze is the best!!!  Forget buying all those expensive balsamic vinegars - adding a bit of brown sugar and reducing for a nice glaze.  Just get this and save the money and the time.  Try it in ways mentioned on other reviews, the label....but then do yourself a wonderful favor and try it on some braised or grilled veges OMG!!!
Amazing.  Way less calories than salad dressing.  Use to cook with.  Love it so much !!

column9: Excellent taste and good as a salt substitute
column10: Many people need to reduce salt intake and this has been the best solution for me. Very versatile. I sometimes bring some to a restaurant and order my food unseasoned.I got turned on to basalmic glaze when Trader Joes carried their own brand which was great... but they discontinued it due to problems with the cap. And I suspect some customers like me hoarded some, reducing apparent demand for long stretches. The cap and no spill dispensing on De Nigris brand is first rate.I bought Roland and De Nigris, and one other. The Roland one comes in several quality levels, the highest of which is hard to find and expensive. I am on this site to buy more De Nigris Basalmic Glaze Reduction because it provides the best taste and the price is right in a good sized bottle.
I bought this for the first time a few months ago...I think it's delicious...can't get enough of it!
Very good glaze to dress tomatoes or fish.  Saves using the really expencive aged balsamic.Now I use this finishing glase when you have a heavy handed pour.
Yup, this stuff is amazing. I use it on just about everything and it is great.

These are some of the largest seeds I've ever seen.  They have ruined me for other brands.  The shells of these sunflower seeds are almost square in section, and they pop open like they are on a hinge.  The buffalo wing flavor is nice.  It's not melt your face off hot.  I don't know if these have any less sodium than the standard salted variety, but they don't seem to have the "cure your mouth like a country ham" effect I've experienced with the salted flavors.  You may not have experienced this effect if you eat human sized portions, but if you have a 5 oz. bag a day habbit like myself, you probably know what I'm talking about.

column9: OK, but Bacon is much better.
column10: This bag of seeds is good, but not great. I don't know if its inherent in the process of adding the Franks Red Hots Sauce flavor, but sometimes random seeds taste stale or sorta wet/bitter. I would suggest buying the Sizzling Bacon Flavor, it has both spice and flavor. Plus, most importantly, the Bacon Flavor seeds are consistently good throughout the bag. my 2c
These are the seeds to get. Generally not a big fan of Frank's Red Hot, but man does it ever compliment a good sunflower seed!

column9: Great mixed with sizzlin bacon flavor
column10: Any of the Bigs brand seeds are better than the rest no matter the flavor! I like mixing these hot sauce ones with the sizzlin bacob flavir because i dont like the hot factor just the tangy flavor. So mixing the bacon and buffalo together makes them less hot and they taste even better! Although the dill are still my favorite. I have to search every gas station and store in hopes of finding this rare brand. Spitz brand are easy to find and are okay but have too many worm holes/bad seeds. Bigs virtually has none. Awesome size, quality, taste, and flavor selection! A must have for any sunflower seed addict like myself :)

I've been buying Davids for a long time, first time I've tried BIGS and the bigs stands for big seeds.  This flavor isn't that great, I'd rather have something different.  But this brand blows away Davids in my opinion.  Davids also has a larger seed line, but I haven't seen any flavors I like on amazon.  I'll continue to buy bigs, but next time I'm getting a different flavor.

column9: Forget AA, I need bigs seeds anonymous
column10: I eat sunflower seeds all day while at work.  These are have such a crisp shell, they open with little ease and the flavor is perfect.  My mouth doesn't feel cut up or burn from the salt.  I will never eat another brand.  They really are huge.

My husband adores these seeds - especially the Buffalo Wing flavor. We had tried to find these in the stores and were thrilled when we found them for sale on Amazon. Would recommend trying to others since they're very tasty.

I have been a david seeds fan since I was a kid, I didnt think anyone could beat their seeds. Since trying Bigs seeds Buffalo wing I now have a new favorite. The seeds are a little spicy but you can eat a whole bag wihout it leaving your tongue raw.I have tried all the flavors but Buffalo wing is my favorite.  Try them you will be surprised. I am not a young kid I have 45 years of sunflower seed eating experience.

I have been a sunflower seed aficionado for quite a few years.  I was turned on to the BIGS brand a couple of years ago and tried a sampler pack when I fell in love with these seeds.  The Buffalo Wing flavor is nicely balanced - not really hot - but it does have the vinegary hot sauce flavor that you would expect.  The size and quality of the seeds themselves are great.  If you like sunflower seeds and you like buffalo wings - you can't go wrong.
The seeds are OK.  I love hot stuff and Red Hot, but they do not mix well with sunflower seeds...  They are OK, but I will likely not buy them again.

These seeds don't have near as much "buffalo wing" flavor at all to them as the giant words on the bag would make you believe. That would have been fine if the Frank's spice kicked in, but alas, I'm just left with a tiny tingle on my tongue from the "spice"... these need WAY more spicy buffalo sauce flavor if they're gonna advertise it as such.

column9: not as good as the bacon flavor
column10: Wanted something spicy, but this one tastes like pop corn flavor to me. I didn't like it at all. Now I have to figure out finish the box.

When I got these seeds, I was kind of disappointed, the main reason being that they were not hot enough for me. I put one seed in my mouth just to try them out and they tasted like regular flaver. I can really only taste the Frank's when I stick an entire handful in my mouth and its still not that spicy.I just tried this brand out because the Jalepeno Davids were out of stock but since I was so use to those, these just could match up to the level of spicyness that the Jalap's had.The seeds are, however, really big(compared to David's) and are much better quality. They are definatly better than the original flavor of David's.My team loves these seeds so I guess they cant be that bad.And the resealable bag is a nice perk .
I sent these to a GI who has given up smoking and chewing.  Sent him a whole box so he is set for a while.  He loves them.

I LOVE these seeds.  I have been a David Jalepeno fan for a long time, but found these browsing amazon and decided to give them a shot.  When I first put them in my mouth I thought "hmmm, this really needs more buffalo flavor."  However, as I continued to eat them over several days, I realized that what I was missing was just a TON of salt like David uses.  I can eat these seeds all day long without shredding my mouth with all the salt.  That always happens to me with David.  I've gotten hooked on the flavor of not only the spices but of the seed as well.  They are fairly big seeds (though not as big as David Jumbo seeds - but who wants a seed you can only get in salt flavor?), and they taste great.

I was really disappointed in the flavor of these seeds.  I didn't get any of the "tang" that goes along with the heat in Frank's sauce.  I got a little bit of heat at the end, but again, none of that trademark tang. I gave 2 stars instead of 1 because they were nicely sized, good quality seeds and I liked the fact that these were not overly salty like some seeds can be.

Sunflower seeds are great in general, and I'm a big fan of these. I generally used to buy David's Jalapeno seeds, but recently gave these a shot. I will say, these aren't as hot as the Davids, but the flavor is very good. David's tend to make my tongue hurt after eating them for a while, and these don't do that as much, which is nice. I bought a 12 pack, and they last for a really long time. Much better than a bag of chips for a snack.
These are the best sunflower seeds that I have ever had! Nice hot flavor. My personal favorite!
These are good, but a little too hot for me.  The inside of my upper lip got really sore!
These are the best. I always put a bunch in my mouth and eat one at a time. Sometimes the jolt from the mouthful is so hot I gasp but that just makes it all the better.

This are THE seeds to buy.  WARNING: once you go Bigs, you cannot go back to David's sunflower seeds!I've given up waiting for supplies to sell on amazon and went directly to their web site: [...].One good item you can order mix and match seeds in one order verses buying a case of one specific product here.

This tea has just the slightest hints of orange zest and a little spice. It reminds me of when I used to go to Seattle to my grandmother's house and we would have tea and her famous apple pie. A relaxing tea you can drink with honey or with milk and sugar. Orange Blossom honey is recommended with this refreshing tea.~TheRebeccaReview.com
Had a little trouble with the original item.  Advised Bigelow, and they immediately made a replacement.  I was extremely satisfied with the service and the purchase.

column9: The BEST customer service and great coffee!
column10: My first order of alohaislandcoffee.com was the Light Roast 100% Kona pods.  I had just bought the Bunn My Cafe machine.  The coffee tasted bitter to me, not smooth like I'd hoped.  I was ready to return the Bunn My Cafe and give up on pod coffee. I called Anita at Alohaisland and she talked with me and gave me great info on over-extraction, pod brewers, Kona, different roasts.  She asked me to hold on the Bunn one more week and she would send me a sample pack with more pods so I could decide.  She assured me that the Bunn My Cafe was not the reason I didnt like the Light Roast Kona.  Anita was correct!  After trying 4 more flavors(Choco Macadamia Nut, Dark Roast, Espresso, and Hazelnut)we loved them all!  Finally we had the rich smooth coffee that we had hoped for.  If you are not sure which flavor pods to order first, just call Alohaisland, talk with them and they will help you decide.  I have loved Dunkin Donuts coffee for years, thinking it was a light roast.  I learned that its a dark roast and thats why I didnt like the Light Roast Kona.  I highly recommend the Chocolate Macadamia Nut pods!!!

column9: kona light roast is the 'pop' version of the best coffee in the world
column10: Man, if you have never drank Kona coffee, and you have a senseo or a similar coffee pod machine, you must try these!  Sure, they are as expensive as it gets as far as coffee is concerned, but, if you really want a unique experience, and you really love coffee, you will be surprised at the subtleties of true Kona coffee.  You don't have to be a conisseur of coffee to appreciate the flavor, just a lover of the stuff.  The light roast much subtler than the dark roast, and much more enjoyable to the less than hardcore coffee nut, which makes these particular pods a great try for folks new to the Kona coffee market.  I have no idea why coffees from different regions taste so much different, and I really don't even care!  All I know is that coffee from Hawaii, especially Kona coffee, it is the best I have tasted so far, and I even think it is worth the huge amounts of cash it costs to drink it...If the cost is too much, or you don't love coffee, then leave this stuff alone.  Otherwise, you are in for a treat!

column9: Certified Organic Paradise Blend - Surf's Up Get Your Day Started
column10: I have been a longtime fan of Aloha coffee even before I tried this new line, and it is simply amazing.  The quality of Aloha Coffee is not just the best of any coffee I've ever tried, but it is truly on "another level".  This new line has a fantastic flavor and richness.  I am also very impressed by the consistency of Aloha's products -- each cup I make is 5 stars!
My 2 red-eared sliders loved the stuff, so I'd definitely recommend it if you have sliders also! Fed it to them for quite a few months, They were a little over 2 years old.

This is just wrong at this price.  This must be for 4 Bottles.  I am looking for this item in Florida, But I can purchase this item from walmart for $2.32 a 32 oz bottle.  That's 27.84 a case of 12.  I will be sure to stock up and transport it from Pennsylvania to Florida, and save myself a Huge amount.  I can't believe that price is for one bottle.  or is it...

If you're trying to find an inexpensive alternative to Lyle's Golden Syrup, this is NOT the same thing. True golden syrup is made with pure cane sugar, while this stuff is made with high fructose corn syrup. I tasted both, one after the other, and the taste of this stuff is heavy, highly processed, and not at all flavorful. I bought this to use in candy-making, but I don't have high hopes for it.

My kids enjoyed decorating the cookies. The hat and buttons are cute. They couldn't decorate much because the one tube of icing was too small. The kit needs at least two tubes, or better yet three small tubes for three cookies so three can be decorated at the same time.

So many flavors packed into one snack mix. Wouldn't think they go together but are masterfully blended.  Lightly sweetened with an unexpected zesty zip of heat that kicks the taste buds up a notch. Makes one do a double take to see just what was/is in that can.  Great bar mix, or anytime you want to wake up the taste buds. What they refer as honey roast peanuts, are actually lightly coated toffee peanuts, delicious.

column9: Description is confusing and can be deceptive
column10: Obviously the item is not a single 114 ounce bottle.  This item is for a 12 pack of 9.5 Oz bottles.  It would be nice if someone corrected this as it can be confusing.
Would have given it five stars, but the product needs to be 1 inch away from perfection for that to happen.All in all, it does what I needed it to do, and in spectacular fashion.

You can buy this product at most grocery stores for about 7 dollars per 9.8 oz container. I am giving it two stars simply because the price is too high.  The product is really good and can be used in place of sugar.

I find this to be the closest more natural sweetener to using sugar for my hot or cold beverages.  It is at least twice as sweet as sugar so one level teaspoon works for me where I might of used 2 rounded teaspoons of sugar. For people who wish to save some money on this, since it is pricy, I find that mixing this 50/50 with Splenda for baking, which is a granulated mix of sugar and Splenda, works very well and is hard to tell its not really just plain old sugar. And also keeps the one teaspoon proportion. So in one teaspoon you are only actually using 1/4 teaspoon of sugar, for anyone who is watching their sugar intake, plus that 1/4 teaspoon is the sweetness equivalent of 2 teaspoons of sugar.

column9: The best of the available versions
column10: Compared to the Bigelow, this has a better taste.  It will make an 11oz cup on the machines that support that size.

column9: Great flavor; stronger than other competitors.
column10: Other brands of chamomile tea were weak, but this brand has great flavor.  One can make larger cups of tea, which adds to the value.
I brew this tea on the smallest setting to make it strong. It is so fragrant, with a light herbal taste. I just love it.

This is the tea I first bought for my Keurig brewer and I was very happy with it and with the taste. Since then (Nov 2010) the price has doubled and that makes it a bad value. So taste is 5 stars and price is only 1 or 2 considering that I found the Twinings Chamomile tea on Amazon at a really great price. I stocked up on that and am very happy with it. Too bad the k cups are now becoming so overpriced. You have to check around the internet now for better prices than Amazon's.

column9: Good Replacement For Discontinued Gloria Jeans
column10: Gloria Jeans Chamomile was discontinued on us so we were looking for a replacement.  This is just as good!
This is very good tea as well as easy to use.  I love the taste.

Chamomile is one of my favorite herbal products.  I use it to help me relax before I go to sleep.  This particular brand of chamomile tea has a powerful (though I wouldn't say overpowering) taste.  The convenience of a k-cup makes it ideal for a quick brew before bedtime and its taste is uniquely herbal and, to a certain degree, floral.  This brand makes a very good tea and I would recommend it to anyone looking for an alternative to caffeinated teas.

I personally love Chamomile Teas especially the Chamomile Lemon.  However, I am posting this as a service to others that may not be aware of an interaction between Chamomile Tea to prescribed drugs as Chozapine or Tricyclic (antidepresants), Propranolol (treating high blood pressure), Theophylline (a Bronchodilator), Tacrine (used to treat Alzheimers) and ASPIRIN USED AS THERAPY.  Chamomile Teas contain contain coumarin which is an anticoagulant.  Warfarin (used as an anticoagulant) is derived from coumadin.Notice I say MAY interfere with these drugs as some cases have been reported from the interaction of Chamomile with these drugs.  The amount of tea one may drink while using one of these drugs has not been established.

This is my favorite tea. This is the main tea I turn to to serve guests. It is a strong herbal tea and has a good flavor for not having caffeine.Before I tried it, I had done research on the reviews for chamomile tea and this was rated pretty high, and I totally agree. THe best. You will not be dissapointed.
I tried Celestial seasons sleepy time tea and this, It's not bad it tastes good, but I actually felt relaxed with the Sleepy Time tea

column9: Timothy's Chamomile Tea for Keurig is Awful
column10: Absolutely terrible. I like chamomile, this is disgusting. Terribly bitter, and just not right. Actually, I have tried a number of Keurig teas and many of them are way bitter, or otherwise just not good. Guess tea needs to be brewed like it's supposed to be.Also, why are some of these reviews about Chai? Guess the seller uses the same item number when they run out so they don't have to create a new listing from scratch?
We bought all the other brands of Chamomile kCups, and my husband says this is the best one! Will definately buy these again
arrived in timely manner in new condition -it was a gift and the receiver has said it is very good.

column9: Not up to the hype, caused bloody stools in my puppy
column10: I purchased this food upon recommendation from my vet. They told me that they had previously used the Holistic brand but it had merged with this company & they did not have experience with Eagle Pack but that they thought it was the same. I slowly added the food to my puppy's old food over the next week and she seemed to like it just fine. Well, she started having a lot of loose stools, many of which were completely liquid and even bloody for the next couple of weeks. I decided to try another food and everything completely resolved. I have since tried a couple of puppy foods equal in quality/price/reputation with no problems. Her stools are completely better, now soft but formed (like they should be!) with no sign of blood whatsoever. She has not had any gastrointestinal problems on numerous different kinds of treats either. She has been fine on 3 puppy foods, a dozen different kinds of treats...you do the math.I have been trying to figure out what the problem may have been from the ingredient list and my concern is the "triple animal proteins" combining chicken, pork and fish meals. This is just an invitation for food intolerance because there are more potential allergens. I think the pork is the problem. I know she tolerates chicken & chicken meal fine, not sure about fish but I've seen that frequently in other foods while I have yet to find another quality food that contains pork meal. Pig does not seem akin to a domestic dog's "natural" diet anyway. If they got rid of the pork, I might consider trying it again but until then I'd recommend you try another food for your puppy. I think (hope) they are generally a good company and I do see that some people's dogs have been fine on this brand, but I'm not sure this is the safest food for baby animals. I will NOT be purchasing this again & I will be contacting my vet recommending that they no longer carry it in their store. There are so many better, safer options out there. If you care about your puppy's health and happiness, save her weeks of misery and buy something else!

column9: at least it looks like coffee
column10: The packaging is convenient.  Single paper/foil tube for one cup of coffee.I followed the simple instructions carefully and produced a 6 oz cup of hot brown liquid with almost no aroma. column9: Mmm Good - a review of Mi-Del's Ginger Snaps
column10: I am the sort of mom who likes to bake my own cookies because 1) it's fun, and 2) I like to know what goes into them. Even my extremely picky son.  The flavor is zingy with a definite bite and each cookie is only 26 calories.  One of the few store-bought treats that I have no problem handing out to the children.Pam T~

Snappy, even.  :)I'll also agree with the comment that they can be inconsistent from one bag to the next, but even when they're off, they're pretty good.As far as flavor goes, one person's spicy is another person's bland.
