For my money, it tastes similar, & certainly no worse than Better 'n Peanut Butter. It wins out over BnPB which has 100 calories per 2 T serving. But PB2 easily tastes more authentic than either of them, but PB2 does have 45 calories per 2T serving. And PB2's other drawback is that it's a hassle to mix. But if I'm not dieting, it's REAL peanut butter for me.

column9: Save your money - this stuff is gross
column10: I bought this on a whim while I was grocery shopping.  No calories, no fats and no carbs seemed too good to be true.  The ingredient list was a little scary but I thought it might be worth a shot.  Big mistake.  This stuff is nasty tasting.  To me it tasted like sickly sweet chemicals.  The healthier I eat, the more I can taste the chemicals in processed foods such as this.  If it had actually tasted anything like peanuts it might have been ok but that sickly sweet taste is just gross.  I'd rather just give up eating peanut butter altogether than try to replace it with this spread.

I saw this product and thought it would be awesome!  Peanut butter without the calories, what is not to love!?  But...then I actually tried a tiny taste.  Thank God I tried a TINY bit and was close to the sink because I spit it right out.  Can't recall many times I've ever had to seriously spit out a nasty food, but this was disgusting.  It was like a massive amount of salt and artificial sweetner.  Will NEVER buy this again or probably any other product of theirs.  Yikes...

Nothing could ave prepared me for this. The taste was horrifying! Worse thing i've ever tasted in my life. I was in shock that they'd sell it. I thought for a while maybe I had bought a bad jar. Proves I did NOT. It really baffles me... Would NEVER buy this again.

column9: Does not live up to the Walden Farms name
column10: I use many of the Walden products and they are all quite good.  The salad dressings are especially tasty.  I know what I am buying and keep my expectations at the appropriate levels; however, this product does not live up to any expectation at all.  It is terrible and tastes like chemicals.  I am a forgiving dieter when it comes to what I am willing to eat just to get "the feeling" and this just doesn't do it and in fact leaves an awful aftertaste.  Better off just taking peanut butter or any thought of it out of your diet repetoire.
Do not waste your money. This product is gross and over priced---and probably full of chemicals and such. That's all.
this tastes really really horrible and plus it looks disgusting too.Save yourself some money and do not buy this product.you will thank yourself for not getting this

I recently received a half price offer for Walden Farms, buy up to 10 of their products and get up to five free.  The Peanut Spread is one of the items I tried.  While I was not expecting anything like real peanut butter, I was hoping it would be something palatable that I could use for a sandwich or to spread on celery.  IT WAS TERRIBLE tasting nothing like peanut butter and barely tasting of anything peanut related.  The aftertaste was terrible! I tried a bit on a teaspoon and it repeated on me for hours.

I am usually pretty open and when it comes to lower caloried foods, i am willing to sacrafice taste to get that craving out of the way. But this stuff is repulsive.  I tried to even after i refridgerated it....and it didnt help..there was some sort of watery stuff in it.  I am thinking if you mix some reduced fat peanut butter in it, it may help.  I have not tried that yet..but this is really gross....I think i am going to try PB2 and see how that is.  I guess i am being too harsh considering it is zero calories..but i cant really even tollerate the taste.  :-(
Disappointed that the product did not disclose artificial flavors..not so good coming from an all natural company.
This is real yogurt in powdered form.  I use it instead of milk in muffin and biscuit recipes.  It is concentrated, so a little goes a long way

This is amazing. I do not want to pedal my bike to the grocery store in the WI snow, so decided to try this in mymorning smoothies. I was surprised at the creaminess & great taste.  Try it, you will like it!

column9: directions say that it needs guar gum
column10: Dehydration directions say that you need guar gum.  I just added the required water in order to mix it in with a recipe and it came out like water.  The guar gum is a thickener, like cornstarch.  Flavor wise, I think it tastes like sheep or goat milk...I'm not sure but I don't like it.

column9: looks like a good product but no directions.
column10: They put the SKU right over the directions on how to rehydrate. There are no directions on their website and I am stuck with a product I can't use. What good is a label if they cover it up? I can't read the ingredients or the directions. Barry Farm had plenty of room on the package for the sku, so why right over important information? Very unhappy.
The yogurt is very good.  For the soaps is very creamy and I like it. The transaction with amazon was very exceptional.

column9: Bound to be just as great
column10: I haven't had a chance to try this product just yet, but I do believe that it will work wonderfully.

I call these fummy rings because these gummy rings are fun to eat. The only reason I give them 4 stars instead of 5 is because they are tasty, but I prefer Haribo and World's Finest flavors. I've ever had. You can pop in your mouth straight from the bag or you can slip them on your fingers and eat them off.
I love mushrooms! This goes great with them. I make this & always add a lot of mushrooms. It is a good filling meal. Easy & quick to make. Good product.

column9: AS GOOD AS NATIONAL ADVERTISED BRANDS
column10: The pudding is smooth and creamy and very tasty. We eat it between snacks. And we enjoy the savings over national brands.

The pudding is fine (I have tried it before), but this order arrived in a big box and several puddings had broken open and fruit flies had discovered them. I had to throw out the entire case, so it was a waste of money for me.

This tea came in a brown, foil lined, resealable bag and had a proper green color to the tightly rolled balls of tea.It makes a very nice cup of gunpowder tea and I would buy it again.I especially liked that it was organic, since I have read that testing on various non-organic green teas had shown contamination.

We have many family recipes that call for Brandy extract.  In recent years, we substituted Brandy extract for other ingredients only to be disappointed with the results.  This year, we spent the money and got the real deal.  The Natural Flavor Blend was a game changer and restored our family's Christmas cookie recipes.  I would highly recommend.

This pasta has good taste and holds it's shape. Satisfies your hungry without feeling blouted. My family hasn't notice the change in flavor. Cost about 50% less than my local grocery stores; makes eating gluten free cost effective.

column9: 2000 packets of EQUAL = a top value
column10: Unlike other offerings that are for "Equal" and apparently are misleading this is exactly as described along with being the best price!
We use this product all the time. It was just as described in the listing. It arrived quickly and with no problems. I would definitely  purchase this item again. Great price also.

I was tired of having to buy boxes of 100 packets of Equal; then I found this.  1,000 packets for less than $20?  It might look like they will last forever, but I know they won't.  Shipping was fast and free.

column4: Gregory J. Casteel "Dr. Gregory J. Casteel"
column9: It's a big box full of Equal packets
column10: What more is there to say?  If you use Equal-brand artificial sweetener in the little blue packets, and you use enough of it to warrant buying it in bulk, then this is exactly what you're looking for.  It's just a big cardboard box filled with loose packets of Equal.  Nothing more; nothing less.  And it's actually Equal-brand sweetener, not some generic off-brand.  Supposedly there are 2,000 packets in the box; but, to be honest, I've never actually gone to the trouble of counting them all to make sure.  But, suffice it to say, there are lots and lots of them.  In fact, there are enough packets of Equal in the box to last me for about six months before I have to reorder; and I use a dozen or more packets of Equal every day.  (I've been using Equal in my coffee for as long as I can remember; so it's the only sweetener that tastes right to me.  And I drink a couple of pots of coffee per day on average.  So I use a lot of Equal.)  Anyway, if you're looking to buy a couple thousand packets of Equal, you've come to the right place.

column9: Just what my sweet tooth needs
column10: Fast delivery, a box full of Equal packets, arrived intact. My wife thinks I'm a little nuts, but I like my coffee sweet, and I never run out of Equal.

LITTLE TO SAY HERE.  THE PRODUCT SPEAKS FOR ITSELF.  I PREFER THIS OVER THE PINK PACKAGE STUFF.  NO AFTERTASTE FOR ME.  TRAVELS WELL IN ZIP LOCK BAG.  CAME LOOSE IN THE BOX....I THOUGHT IT WOULD HAVE BEEN IN A PLASTIC BAG FIRST.

column9: Equal sugar substitute in the  blue packet
column10: It's the only sweetner I use for my coffee and cereals. There is no aftertaste nor any metallic taste on your tongue at all. It's also wonderful to use in iced tea...it doesn't need to melt like sugar does to sweeten the beverage. We've even used it to boost the sweetness in our strawberry dacqueries using fresh strawberries or to make lemonade.
Very nice price for 2000 packs of equals, cannot complain, package was great, they expire in 3 years so I'll probably be finishing them in a year.

Not much to say here.  The barley is as advertised.  The shipping was slower than I expected, especially since the state of origin isn't all that far from my home, but the price was better than I could find anywhere else.This is hulled barley, which has the bran intact, unlike pearl barley.  It takes longer to cook, but it also keeps better and that is what I want in a grain.  Also, of course, having the bran intact means having the bran to eat, which is more fiber in our diets.  I have cooked this whole in a stew, and it was the same as pearl barley in appearance.  I cracked it in a Corona mill and it then cooked up like rice in a soup.When we poured it into the storage bucket, the grain appeared clean.  There was no dirt or foreign plant material.

This barley is totally free of any inedible hulls. It cooks easily in a steamer set to 75 minutes and left to sit for an additional 30 after that. Once cooked it stores nicely in the refrigerator without losing it's flavor or texture. I find the texture to comfortably chewy with a faint nutlike taste similar to brown rice. The grains of barley do tend to be sticky so you're not going to get a one grain at the time Minute Rice experience, a good thing in my estimation.

Huge Bag of a very nutty, chewy and wholesome barley. Once I saw the bag I knew I was in for the long haul but it is no problem for it keeps well as long as you follow the storage guidelines. I immediately, upon receiving it, made a batch and was aware that cooking times required would have to be longer than the supermarket version. I mostly use it for soups of all kinds and also as an alternative to lentils, beans, garbanzos, etc. There is a recipe in the old country where you would cook them as you might cook most legumes until they are plumped and ready to go. Then you would add the required mix of onions or shallots or green onions, tomatoes if desired (can or finely chopped fresh) garlic, plenty of herbs and personal choice spices to add flavor to the mix. Then you would fried bananas and eggs and put one over medium egg on top and a couple of slices of bananas on the side, all this accompanied by brown rice or white rice. The healthy nature of Barley makes it ideal for regular involvement in the kitchen and even though 25 Lbs is a lot of barley, it is a great food. Prior to buying it I went and did some research on Barley and the results were nothing short of outstanding. Some people even use it to replace rice and I don't see why not, for they have almost the same texture. Anyways, once cooked on a seafood chowder I was glad I made this purchase for Great River Organic Milling, Organic Whole Grains Hulled Barley, 25-Pound Package is a much better bargain and a much better quality than barley found at most stores. 4 Plus Stars for sure!
This is hulled barley and not pearled barley.Nutritionally hulled is better for you.This is a great product at a great price.

column4: E. Wenck "Spicy food is best food."
column9: Awesome buy at a great price!
column10: I was very pleased by this purchase.  I ordered this as well as other grains from Great River for use in my porridge which is healthy, cheap and tasty.  I have cooked them up in my rice steamer as well as stove top and they come out with great texture as well as flavor.  I would buy them more frequently if they didn't last so long.  (Review used for each grain as I am equally impressed with each)

This barley tastes great and it is so filling! The day this bag of barley arrived, I made a huge pot of bean-and-barley soup with a lot of mushrooms in it. I love the taste of mushrooms with barley. This grain has a wonderful, full-bodied, nutty flavor, and a terrific, chewy texture.I must admit that 25 pounds is a whole lot of barley. I've had trouble in the past with whole, organic grains without preservatives becoming filled with bugs, even when I stored them in a glass container in a cool pantry. To prevent that this time I immediately broke it down into 2-pound packages and froze them. That will definitely prevent any potential bug problems.

This product requires a bit of processing to unlock the flavor. Boil 1 cup to 4 cups water for 60 minutes, low heat. Then place in electric blender until uniform. If you like hot oat bran cereal, you'll also like this. It has a slight corn flavor. It is also good unblended, whole, in soups and rice dishes, but requires a lot of chewing. The unblended product is very chewy. Very very high fiber. 25 lbs of barley will keep me regular for quite a long time. I highly recommend this product for the person who needs bulk fiber.  UPDATE 6/26/2012: I tried the barley in the bulk bin at W-F Company and found that I am allergic to it. W-F barley is brown, whereas Great River barley is pale. It is also hulled, which is very healthy. I must reiterate that I like this barley a lot...mellow flavor, and I'm not allergic to it.

This barley was exactly what I expected - hulled barley ready for use without need of rinsing.  It's a whole grain, great for barley water, grinding into flour, making soups, or as a more-nutritious rice substitute.  It may take me some time to use all of this order, but I will be buying more in the future.An important note for those who want to malt or grow barley - this product will NOT sprout, so it is NOT what you're looking for.  Unlike other grains, barley is somewhat fragile and will not sprout once the hull is removed.  "Hulled barley" has had the hull removed, so it will not sprout/grow.  This is an excellent whole grain for consumption; buy it for that purpose!

Well packaged organic hulled barleys. This type of barley is much more nutritious than pearl barleys. However, I originally bought this item thinking that it was barley flours. So getting your barley types straight prior to ordering would be a good idea.

column9: Look and taste like pearl barley! Disappointed!
column10: The shipping speed was excellent.  Package was received within 3 days of ordering.  However, when I opened the package I was disappointed as the barley definitely looks like pearl barley instead of hulled barley which is what I ordered.  I thought I would give it a try anyway and soaked 4 cups of barley for less than 2 hours before cooking it in the pot.  It took less than 30 minutes before it became soft and sticky.  I waited until the barley was cooler to taste it and it taste just like the pearl barley that I bought in the supermarket.  Certainly didn't have any aroma or chewy texture like I read in the review here.  Did I receive the wrong package????
When I received this package, the sewing thread has been loosen/torn. Big question for the freshness of this product. No return slip attached to this product.

i mix this with brown rice and usually soak it overnight and cook it in a rice cooker. it has a very sweet aroma and it is so chewy i love it. my neighbor loves it. so if you are looking for an altanative to white rice,this is a reallt good one and it has tons of fiber,8 grams of fiber in 1/4 cup i hear. so it's good for you.

It is not what I expected. Seems that germ was semi removed and bran is gone.Grains are very small, size of the pearled barley and looks like it is semi pearled. Pearled barley is considered not whole grain and I did not want to buy that. I do flake my own oats and barley. Both seeds are similar in size and flakes beautifully. This barley almost becomes flour when I use my flaker. I guess I will have to use barley from Whole Foods, barley I purchase there has outer shell and germ.Planning to return this item.Shipping took very long. Amazon packed in the incredible size box and third of the box was empty. Likely will not do such purchases on Amazon.Contacted seller for prices on other grains, but did not get my answers, or at least so far.Disapointed.

Patek's is my favorite curry paste--no MSG and simple ingredients. For a great, easy meal on an evening when you are too tired to make a curry from scratch, saute some onions, throw in a can of tomatoes, some water, and a few tablespoons of Patek's Mild Curry Paste, and then you can take it wherever you like it--meat, tofu, veggies--as your fancy strikes you.Now this paste may say "mild," but there is still enough spice to make your mouth tingle pleasantly--just enough. When I serve Patek's mild, I take out some chicken or whatever before serving to my four-year-old--I don't think she could handle the "mild" spice level. Mom and Dad love it, though.The downside is that one little jar does not go a long way. If you use the paste in the concentration that it calls for (and I recommend doing so, for an authentic Indian taste), you will get two or three dinners out of it. But for flavor and ease of use and sheer delight, you cannot beat Patek's. The guests you serve it to will be amazed--and you can hide your little jar in the refrig and bask in all that glory.Amazon's cost is high for this item, at $5, but if convenience is important to you, then that's a consideration--having a powerful culinary secret delivered to your door might make the extra buck or two worth it. If you have time and are near an Asian/Indian foods store, then expect to pay $3 if you are lucky, or around $4 in most places. Stock up, because unopened, these last forever.

I tried this curry paste after I found it recommended in Pressure Perfect by Lorna Sass, a cookbook with recipes for pressure cookers.  Well, the first thing that I made with it was curry chicken.  It became an instant family favorite.  Since then, I have tried it in other dishes and I was never disappointed.  The flavor is rich and intense without being overpowering.  I have also used it in Hot and we like it too, but it would not be good for people who are not used to heat.  I find the paste to be much better than any powders that I have tried and it gives a more authentic flavor.

column9: Easy Indian food in a few minutes & Not too spicy!
column10: Yummy, yummy!This curry paste is now my favorite.  It is easy to use, store, and best of all it is delicious!  Pataks Curry is very mild....not super spicy like many others.  My husband likes flavor and a little spice so this is his favorite as well.  I can use the one jar for about 4 meals which is a great deal.I have found that is it so simple to make a "stir-fry"  with a protein like tofu, chicken or even salmon and then add veggies such as carrots, or potatoes.  There are many combinations and just about any typical veggie taste great in this sauce (love cauliflower).  I think it is best kept simple with 2 or 3 ingredients.This sauce is great for an easy meal with guests, throw the rice in the steamer, make the curry stir-fry, and add another side dish and you are set.  Our friends love it!Pataks also makes other great sauces but this is my favorite to keep on hand at all times.

column9: I use this all the time
column10: This curry paste is great for putting flavor into something simple. I throw a can of diced tomatoes in the crock pot along with some chopped onion and garlic, a few tablespoons of the paste, a little broth and whatever meat I have on hand. Chicken, beef, lamb, it doesn't matter. I come home to a wonderful aroma and after steaming some rice I have a meal that tastes like I've been working on it all day.It is very mild but flavorful. In fact, a friend who absolutely hates spicey food loved this. I actually like spicey food and sometimes mix one tablespoon of the hot along with two tablespoons of the mild. Just depends on my mood and who I'm cooking for.

This curry paste is delicious.  I sauteed some onions and green bell peppers.  Added a half can of spagetti sauce (next time I'll try stewed tomatoes), half cup of water and about 3 teaspoons of the paste.  I let simmer for a few minutes, then added salmon, covered and let simmer for 15 minutes.  I served over a mix of hot brown rice and peas.  This was my first attempt at cooking with curry paste and I absolutely loved it.  Spicy and delicious.

This is the best product I have tried for curry paste, unless you want to make your own. The flavor is nice and not so overwhelmingly spicy. You actually taste the flavor of your food. A little goes a long way, so don't over do it. This is the only brand I buy for Thai recipes.
$4.99 - when i can buy it in the local store for $2.79?? I don't think so.

I'm a big fan of authentic indian food, aficionado almost, but this is a far cry from anything I have ever tasted from that region, which makes sense because Patak's is NOT from India, but rather imported from the fish & chip capitol of the world... UK.  I have tried a variety of sauces, including the chutney from Patak and they all share a similar, unfortunate attribute : They all taste of vinegar, ketchup, more vinegar and more ketchup.  I am truly surprised that nobody has mentioned this abomination.  It was as if somebody poured salad dressing over my chicken, dumped out half a bottle of ketchup on top of it, soaked it overnight in a bag of vinegar, and then crapped over it with a can of manwich.  This company should be out of business.If you want to try the most authentic indian food in a jar that I've found, try Tiger Tiger.

column9: Good product - good price - good taste
column10: I was looking for a quick alternative to making Sujata's curry paste from scratch (as per Beth Hensperger's "Not Your Mother's Slow Cooker Recipes for Two). This is it, for now.  Taste-wise it's a close second, however, it's way more convenient. You'll be rubbing it on long before you even find your mortar and pestle, or finish conducting your spice inventory. Shipping was the usual quick and efficient AMAZonING way.

I have used Patak's Curry Paste (mild) for years. I mix it in rice, stir frys, vegetables, and I love the taste of the paste. It has just the perfect blend of spices to add pizzaz for those who love curry.
this paste is authentic, giving you the buzz of an indian curry wihout burning your taste buds.  delicious!

This is my personal favorite tea. The floral scent is terrific and I love it for the aromatherapy effects. This is the only Jasmine tea that I've found that tastes like it smells. Other Jasmine teas I've tried smell nice, but disappoint when you take a sip. This tea delivers and the presentation is beautiful the way the blossoms fill up the sachets when brewed.

Jasmine tea has been one of my favorites for decades, and I've probably tried every brand. There's just something about the flowery fragrance of jasmine steaming your face as you sip that makes break time special.Harney & Son's Dragon Pearl Jasmine tea comes in a pretty metal tin, and the 20 attractive tea bags make the process of steeping the tea a pleasant ritual.  Pour hot water over the bag, and watch the little pearls unfurl into petals.  Wait for that first hint of jasmine scent to waft up to your nose. The flavor of the tea is just like the scent - light and flowery.  I like mine without sweetening, but a teaspoon of apple blossom honey would compliment the tea perfectly.This is a very nice tea, and one I savor often.

A few years ago, my mom and sister went to china, and the best thing they were able to bring back was a tin of chinese dragon pearl jasmine tea; or just plain "Jasmine tea" as it was called there. I loved it right away, and bribed my sister $20 for the last bit of tea before it ran out. after a long, fustrating search, I found this tea here on amazon, and decided to give it a try. I'm really glad I did, because this tea is an almost EXACT duplicate of what they brought back, except this time the tea came in fancy silky packets, and the writing on the tin was in english, not mandarin.it's got the same delicate aroma, and is the perfect cup of tea after dinner, or just to relax and unwind. If you've never tried this type of tea, you should, even my non tea drinking friends LOVE this tea, and always ask for it when they come over.
This tea is great if you like jasmine tea. Has a great aroma and flavor. One of my favorites thus far.
Great tea and darling tin can it comes in. The tea is smooth and does not have a strange aftertaste like those other cheaper brands. Pleased with it although it's a little pricey.
Harney & Sons make delightful products and this is no exception.  The Jasmine tea is delicate and light, with a marvelous aroma of the flower.  The sachets are a must.  Try this.
This tea is absolutely delicious. Very fragrant not too strong and not too weak - just perfect. I'd give it more stars if I could.

Intersting tea. I wasnt sure what they meant by "pearls" but when I received the tea, and put it in the water, the leaves are shaped like little pearls and they fill out and turn into whole leaves in the water. Kinda cool, I like that. This is NOT like Hedleys Jasmin green tea, no Jasmin green tea is. I dont know what it is about that brand, but they are out of business now, it was the most exceptional green tea Ive ever tasted, its like sipping jasmin perfume.However this tea, comes in second, I guess.But its not worth how expesive it is, not worth the money
I really enjoy this tea, so don't get me wrong.  But I found a jasmine tea at the local oriental grocery that is just as good at 1/10th of the price.
ive never has this type befor and liked it. the smell and taste were good. loved watching the balls unwind. was pleased with the quality and price.
I love these pretty little tea bags!  so yummy and the jasmine just soothes your soul.  I love this tea and so happy to show it off when my friends come over!  great great.

There is a reason why this is ranked the highest on Steepster and that's because it is the best Jasmine tea you'll ever put in your mouth.  It's ranked much higher than the other famously rated jasmine tea on Amazon but I won't name it.  I've shopped Harney for 2 years and they are wonderful!

column9: This the tea that started it all for us
column10: The only tea we now drink (pretty much) is Harney and Sons.  This was our first Harney and Sons purchase.  It's excellent and still probably my favorite tea by them.  Check out their "wedding tea" which is also very good.
I first tried this tea at an upscale bridal boutique in Los Angeles and have been hooked ever since; so good!

column9: Lovely, Fragrant, Tea, Very Pleasing to all the senses
column10: I really love this Jasmine Tea !!! The price it can't be beat!!! Beautiful triangular tea bags, that are see-thru, truly a presentation to the eye as well to the taste and smell. The tin is very pretty too, and keeps the tea fresh and is lovely to leave on the counter or on a shelf. You won't be disappointed and its very hard these days to find a real good Jasmine tea that doesn't involve green tea!!! Love it will never be without again..

column9: Tangerine are great; watermelon are better!
column10: These are DELICIOUS! They remind me a lot of Wonka Jaw Breakers as far as taste, but they are soft and powdery instead of hard. I prefer them over conventional candy and while they are obviously a bit more expensive they are worth every penny and you don't get that nasty sugar rush then crash that you get with conventional candies. Enjoy!! They're great!

I got these because they were super cheap at the local Big Lots.  After trying a 4 pack, I went back for more.This is not quite a carbonated coffee.  The color is lighter colored than coffee, which is a tip off that it's coffee flavored rather than actual coffee.  It tastes like coffee, but mildly sweet and mellow.  The carbonation is the novelty, and it works well.About two thirds of my friends who tried this liked it.  One compared it to bottled Starbucks frappuccino (Java Pop is not heavy like frappuccino).  It is a sweet coffee flavored novelty, and I can see the similarities.  Friends who like one seem to like the other, even though the beverages are very different.This would be a good option for a novelty drink at a party where guests like coffee.

The first time I tried Espresso flavored Java Pop I was hooked. It's a great way to enjoy a wholesome refreshing cold pop-like beverage with a hint of coffee flavor for people like me who love coffee. There is a flavor for all tastes...try it you will like it!

I've tried all the different flavors of bars that Fiber One offers and these are definitely my favorite. The caramel flavor is light and sweet and the fiber in these bars (a whopping 9g!) makes them a very filling snack or a quick meal on the go! I typically enjoy these in the afternoon to carry me through between lunch and dinner but have eaten them for breakfast on occasion as well and they keep me satisfied until lunch. Fiber is one of the hardest things for me to get enough of (25-35g is recommended daily) and these bars definitely help! Some people have reported digestive upset when eating these but I've never had a problem with them. I highly recommend this product!

column9: Quite Pleasant alternative to Flax-meal but has a brief learning curve.  We're sold!
column10: Updated 9/7/12: The product being sold as White Chia Seed by Nutiva "CHIA seed" is a new variety of Salvia Hispanica seed selected by growers to produce only white seeds.  It is just as good for you as the nurtitional powerhouse  that is marketed as "Black Chia" which has become a common offering as a health food as well as the seeds that grow furry looking Chia pets!.  White Chia Seeds come from the the same species of plant, just a different cultivar.  The Protein, oil and fatty acid profiles are basically the same  as any black Chia grown in the same climate.  there is no appreciable difference.  The white or light color of these seeds make them easier to incorporate into smoothies and porridges when you add them to water to form the filling and nutritious gel that is described on the back of the package.  I don't mind the Gel form and find it helpful and filling when added to a banana-berry smoothie with only a little bit of agave syrup for sweetener.  The gel holds up well and I don't get that unpleasant bitter taste I associate with flax-seed or Flax meal.  So I'm already thrilled with the White Chia as a substitute for Flax & will be using the 15% Subscribe & Save option to make this an even better buy for my family in the future.Where I see this being even more useful is lightly dry-toasted and added to salads or atop cold cereal and we've had some success with that.  My husband has also been adding the toasted White Chia to a snack mix he makes of grated bittersweet chocolate, All-Bran cereal and a variety of Chex cereals for what he calls his "sweet snack" of the day.  Since it's a dry mixture with just a little bit of Cinnamon and allspice added, it doesn't gel up once it's toasted and it adds more fiber to an already better snack choice.  The other possible benefit is that when using the gel as a thickener insteadof wheat flour Rue, you can feed the suaces and gravies to Celiac patients since there is no Gluten in Salvia Hspanica seeds.  Another Win/Win!I was quite curious about the so-called "White Chia"  and it took me some extra research to finally peg the source as being this new cultivar and not a similar but different species because Nutiva doesn't list the species on the label as do other sellers of White Chia.  In the process I learned a great deal about just how healthy this product is!  Nutritionally speaking, it's main benefits seem to be from the soluble plant-based fiber and the small amounts of protein and Omega-3 you get with each recommended serving of 1 Tbsp.  I would suggest starting slowly before you increase your daily intake any higher becuase you will have an increase in bowel frequency , volume (larger) and texture (softer) the more of this you eat.  For most of us, this is a desired outcome and why we choose to add a supplement like Chia or Flax to our diets but for people with Irritable Bowel Syndrome, Diverticulitis or other Bowel disorders, please discuss this with either your Gastroenterologist or regular Primary Care Physician before adding to your diet.  You might have some sudden changes that you can't predict.  For healthy people, just take it slowly until you find the correct amount to keep you regular, and also provide that feeling of stomach fullness that the Chia Gel can provide.Even if you have chronic health problems, don't turn away from Chia Seeds out of fear!  There are good books and resources that can guide you if you wish to try and work this into a healthy eating plan.  For example, many diabetics use Chia Gel to help them feel full.  This book, Diabetes Without Drugs: The 5-Step Program to Control Blood Sugar Naturally and Prevent Diabetes Complications, has a good recipe for a filling Almond bread using Chia seeds of either color.  Another good book about Chia seeds and their possible benefits is Chia: Rediscovering a Forgotten Crop of the Aztecs.  Remember, however, to always clear the addition of a new fiber source with your doctor , in the event that fiber has been a problem for you in the past.  Also, Diabetics should always test-drive new foods by checking their blood sugar before and after consuming itthe new food, at the intervals your educator recommends or what you have come to know is your impact time. The Calories per serving are 60 with calories from fat coming in at 20, sugars 0 but total Carbs at 5 grams.  I would treat this as both a source of fat and fiber and adjust accordingly.Our overall experience with this has been great and I will update this after we have been consuming this regularly for a few more months.  The cost is comperable to Flaxmeal and yet the product is gentler on the digestive system and has no bad fatertaste.  We love it!  It's been a good experience and one we might not have chosen over our Flaxmeal from thelocal Trader Joe's had it not been for the ease of ordering via Amazon.  I hope Nutiva expands their offerings thru Amazon.Now that we've been using White Chia for a while, we have stopped using the strong tasting flax meal completely and now use White Chia in its place.  We're very happy with the products ease of use and  the many foods to which it can be easily added for extra nutritional benefits.  We love it  and we're sold on it!

Chia seeds (Salvia columbaria) have been a staple food in my vegan kitchen for many, many years, but I had never before tried white chia seeds, so I was quite excited to be able to sample Nutiva Organic White Chia Seeds, 14-Ounce, 2-Count Pouches through the Amazon Vine.  I am utterly delighted with this product!Just as an interesting aside, the genus name of "Salvia" for chia is derived from the Latin "salvere,"  meaning "to save."  The Mayan word "chiabaan" from which chia gets its common name means "strengthening."  So you can understand how these tiny seeds get their reputation for packing an astonishing nutritional punch.  Chia seeds are rich in omega-3 fatty acids and have long been considered an energy tonic.  The native peoples of the Americas have used chia since ancient times for endurance and also to treat constipation.There is apparently no difference in nutrition between black or white chia seeds but the lighter colored white chia seeds are preferable in recipes where the food presentation is enhanced by their more neutral coloring.Having gone raw vegan some years back, chia seeds are very popular with me (as are flax seeds) for substituting the grains in my dehydrated raw crackers, breads and sweet treats.  I use chia seeds as I use flax seeds, or in combination with flax seeds, for the same mucilaginous effect of being "sticky" enough to hold together when dehydrated, making a very reasonable and tasty facsimile of  a cracker, bread or sweet treat.Chia seeds, especially these Nutiva Organic White Chia Seeds, 14-Ounce, 2-Count Pouches, make a wonderful pudding that reminds me of tapioca pudding.  I also sprinkle 2 tablespoons of chia seeds over my sprouted buckwheat cereal and the thickening effect of the chia when I add liquid transforms my cereal into a very appealing, very nourishing porridge.  For added nutrition in my smoothies I also add 2 tablespoons of chia seeds.I am very pleased with Nutiva Organic White Chia Seeds, 14-Ounce, 2-Count Pouches and look forward to devising more creative culinary applications for this delicious, certified organic product of Mexico in my raw vegan kitchen.  Of course chia seeds are not confined to the raw or vegetarian kitchens alone.  Every diet should include these mightily nourishing, antioxidant and fiber rich seeds.  The ancient Aztec and Mayan peoples revered these seeds... and perhaps we modern people should too!

I wanted to try these for the great benefits I have read about. As a vegetarian, I don't get my Omega-3's from any fish source, so I normally depend on Flax seeds. I have read that Chia seeds contain an even higher amount of Omega-3. . I mix 2 tablespoons with a small glass of orange juice and drink it down. You have to drink it quickly, because they absorbe the liquid quickly, and become very thick in no time. I love the idea of this happening in my intestines, and the benefit there was definitely obvious, so as a fiber source, I also highly recommend them. I even tried them as an egg substitute, something I had also read was possible, and in banana bread, they worked out just fine. I love that they are ready to use, Flax seeds have to be ground, so Chia seeds are really perfect to take on trips.I will definitely continue to buy and use these.

column9: Low Carber In Love With Chia
column10: I've been a low-carber for a long time and we're always looking for ways to extend our recipes. These chia seeds have been fantastic for adding nutrients to our smoothies and we've even made a nice  tapioca substitute with nothing more than these seeds stirred into cream with a little stevia & left to sit in the fridge for about an hour. We've made gravy by adding chia seeds to the pan drippings with a little cream and using the immersion blender. Also used them to thicken up the sauce for Beef Stroganoff. These are very versatile and since they're all fiber, they're basically a 0 carb food!

Chia seeds are high in omega-3's, protein, fiber and antioxidants and are easy to add to foods and smoothies, very similar to flax seed. The white chia is definitely less noticeable in foods; the dark chia has a nutty quality. There are some websites that claim white chia is superior to black chia, but they are actually very similar in terms of composition. If you eat them dry, they are slightly crunchy. Adding water makes a gel - so it's a good way to add omegas and fiber to a smoothie for a small calorie tradeoff. I've also used them in chocolate chip oatmeal cookies to add nutritional value for no change in taste or texture.The bag is easy to reseal and is a sturdy bag. It is a little awkward to store in the cabinet because it is wider at the bottom.While chia are purported to be a superfood, I haven't sprouted a good aura, found myself fighting crime, or run any marathons since trying these, but will be purchasing it again. It's an easy, quick, painless nutritional boost to add to my foods.

For those who associate Chia with the green-haired, clay pets, this is something very different - FOOD!  Chia seeds are small and nutty.  They are quite tasty and equally important, packed with nutrition.  High in omega-3 fatty acids, protein, fiber, and anti-oxidants, chia seeds are great for you.  Unlike larger seeds, which need to be ground the extract their nutrition (otherwise known as the what goes in, what comes out effect), chia seeds can be added to any food.  They are quite versatile, and can be put in breads, muffins, oatmeal, smoothies, yogurt, you name.However, what is unusual about Chia seeds is the texture when added to any liquid (juice, yogurt, etc.  The seeds have an outer later that swells into a chewy gelatinous globule in about 10-15 minutes.  It adds quite a unique and fun mouthfeel to these foods.Chia seeds have many uses, and you will have fun exploring all the different ways to use them in cooking.

I've been using the Nutiva Organic Chia Seeds as part of my daily routine for the last 4 months and I've been happy with the results. Much like peanuts, Chia Seeds helps decrease your food intake and make you feel more full. I create a gel by adding a couple tablespoons to a 12 oz glass of warm water and refrigerate after stirring the contents twice within 15 minutes. I add a couple teaspoons of the gel to my morning oatmeal and to yogurt in the evenings. They give you a bit more energy and I notice I don't have to hit the caffeine like I had in the past. And they're full of fiber and Omega-3's which are both essential for your health. I definitely feel better since taking them. I have lost some weight, have increased my good cholesterol count, lowered my blood pressure, and feel more alert during the day. I highly recommend this product to anyone because they do improve your overall health and they're WAY cheaper here on Amazon than at the local GNC.

column9: Good addition to smoothies - does help with energy for endurance sports
column10: I first heard about chia seeds when reading the book "Born to Run," which (among other things) told how the Tarahumara Indians - with their great super distance runners - relied on the seed for sustained energy.  I read more more about these tiny seeds, and was struck by what a decent source of omega-3 fatty acids (the "good" fats in foods such as salmon), fiber, and even protein.  I tried some by basically tossing them into a blender as part of yogurt/milk/berry smoothies, and they mixed in well, though the black chia seeds ended up leaving a lot of small specks in smoothies, while making them  a bit thicker.Anyway, it was nice to try these white seeds out in that they mix in well with smoothies, without giving them a gritty appearance.  I do think the claims associated with chia seeds have some truth in terms  of helping with energy -- I do a fair number of races (10 miles and over) and find it is good to drink a smoothie with a tablespoon or or chia seeds a couple of hours before the race.  It may be the fiber and the fact that the seeds soak up liquid (presumably after being consumed) but adding them to a smoothie before a race really does increase energy over the course of the race, I assume by slowing digestion and release of sugar.As far as this product is concerned, I do like the light color of these seeds and believe the packaging is very good here - bags are a not too large and seal easily.Product and packaging come highly recommended - 5 stars!

column9: Boost Your Health with Super Food Chia Seeds
column10: I started changing over my eating habits by adding one new Paleo recipe a week and one new health food every two weeks. I started by adding Magnesium Citrate since I was magnesium deficient. Just by taking the recommended daily allowance I felt my body respond with new energy, my insomnia disappeared, and there is no sluggishness when I go to the bathroom.I started drinking smoothies for breakfast - deep chocolate whey protein powder, bananas and almond or soy milk.  I wanted to add more Omega-3 and fiber to my diet. Adding Nutiva chia seeds to meals is a quick and easy nutritional boost.You can find recipes on the Nutiva package and on their web site. Here are a few recipes to get you started:WAYS TO EAT CHIA SEEDS:- Lightly roast 2-3 teaspoons to put in soups, stews, salads, nut butters, tartar sauce, marinades, salad dressings or mayo- Grind 2 teaspoons to add to bread and muffin mixes- Create a gel (1 tablespoon to eight ounces of water let sit for 15 minutes) that can be added (2-3 teaspoons) to juice and smoothies. The gel lasts in the fridge for up to two weeksIMPORTANT REMINDERS:- Most people will think of the Chia Pet, but those seeds are not food grade and should not be eaten.- Make sure that the chia seeds you eat are organic and pesticide free. White or black, the seeds have the same nutritional value.- These chia seeds hold up to ten times their weight in water and help clear toxins from your body. It is very important that you drink your eight glasses of water a day. If not, you will look like you are retaining water.- Chia seeds also lower blood pressure and help to control your blood sugar level. If you are on medication for high blood pressure or diabetes, be sure to talk to your doctor before taking these seeds daily. Then monitor your pressure and progress each day.- Bestselling author and skin doctor Nicholas Perricone, MD says "Chia delivers more Omega-3 than flax or fish, satisfying skin's craving for moisture. Omega-3 is the world's most perfect anti-inflammatory featuring DHA and EPA."I encourage everyone to give these organic chia seeds a try. I will be ordering them on a regular basis.

Nutiva's Organic White Chia Seeds are a fantastic, nutritious food you can add to most anything. The seeds are mostly tasteless so they won't adversely affect the food or drink they've been added to. This is my first experience with chia seeds and I could not be happier. Looking to find an egg replacement for recipes, and having had mixed results with flax seed which sometimes alters the taste, I set out to try the chia in as many different recipes as possible. The recipes ranged from cookies to muffins and cupcakes, breads to pancakes, and they've all turned out terrific; the seeds worked just as well as eggs and I feel better about it. In place of 1 egg, 1 tablespoon of chia seed with 2-3 tablespoons of water, soaked for 15-20 minutes, worked out best in my baking experience. They are also great in homemade granola bars, tossed into both cold and hot cereals, and in smoothies or juices. The versatility of the "superfood" the Aztecs and Mayans revered is amazing. The nutritional benefits, which are many, of chia seeds can be found by an internet search, but a some of them include: omega-3 fatty acids, fiber, protein, essential minerals, and rare antioxidants.  I'm sold and I highly recommend Nutiva Organic White Chia Seeds, 14-Ounce, 2-Count Pouches without reservation. You can be sure I'll always have this stocked in my pantry.

column9: A little goes a very long way.
column10: This was my first "taste" of chia seeds.  I've read that the sprouts are tasty and very nutritous, but I've not tried that, yet.Actually, Chia seeds have no discernible taste.  Unlike flax, they are not grainy or gritty, but a bit softer, which I see as a good thing.I mix them in oatmeal, add to smoothies, mix into granola (or into baked granola bars) and mix into Larabar-type concoctions.Because they are softer than flax, they integrate nicely and don't reuire grinding, which is a time saver.The color (white) is especially nice because you don't "see" them mixed with other ingredients (read: your kids won't be suspicious).If you're currently using flax or dark-colored chia, I highly recommend giving these a try.

column9: Worked well as an egg replacer in my gluten free baked goods.
column10: I decided to give Nutiva Chia Seeds a try when they were offered to me by Amazon Vine to review.First, I used them in my smoothies.  I normally use ground flax seed, but was pleased to find that these chia seeds have over twice the amount of omega 3 fatty acids in them than flax seed.  I ground them in my coffee grinder, resulting in a creamier smoothie.  I'm not supposed to eat small seeds due to a recent diverticulitis attack, and eating them ground has not bothered me. It also seemed to me that they were milder in taste than the flax seeds I had been using.Next, I decided to try it as an egg replacer in my gluten free baked goods.  Performance-wise, I could not tell the difference between chia and flax seed.  Because of the added nutrition, I will continue to use chia in baking, alone or mixed with ground flax.  I recently read a blog post that chia seed could also cut out the need for guar gum and xanthan gum in gluten free baked goods.  I'm going to try that next and see if I can adjust some of my recipes.  I'd rather not have to use the gums because they're expensive and they also bother a lot of people.  I'll post the results of my "experiments" and let you know how it goes!Update:  I decided to go ahead and try the chia without grinding.  I've been eating them that way for a couple of months now and haven't had any problems with diverticulitis. My favorite recipe is to fill a pint jar with Silk or SoDelicious coconut milk, add a packet of Stevita Supreme, a teaspoon of real vanilla extract (Tone's is GF)and add three tablespoons of whole chia seeds.  Mix well and set in the fridge for 1/2 hour.  Remove and stir well again.  Return to fridge for a few hours or overnight. Stir again before eating.  Tastes just like tapioca pudding to me!

column9: Nothing I'd crave, but not bad
column10: These little seeds are supposedly very nutritious, so eating them has a reward besides the taste or how filling they are.  They actually taste okay; not as tasty as sunflower seeds, but not bad and they are easy to add to a lot of things.  I found that I was slightly allergic to them and everytime I ate them, my sinuses would start draining like crazy and I'd begin coughing, so they aren't something I'll be continuing to eat.  But for most people, that wouldn't be a problem. You can even use them to grow sprouts if you'd prefer something more veggie-like.  Those who grow the sprouts say that they make tiny little sprouts, but good to eat.  I grew a "chia pet" years ago, but don't remember what the sprouts looked like.  I do remember that they sprouted easily, so that shouldn't be a problem for would-be sprout-growers.

Before I saw this product here on Amazon, if anyone mentioned "chia" I would think of those chia pets where you applied the seeds, watered and grew "hair" on your "pet".I can't BELIEVE what an easy way this is to add goodness to your diet! You literally can mix this with anything. I've had it in yogurt, in soup, pudding, oatmeal, smoothies, etc, etc. It makes me feel good to know that I'm doing something that can benefit my health.I have added this to my drop biscuit recipe and to banana bread. Both were extra moist and with both I was able to cut back the amount of butter/margarine in the recipes and the flavor didn't really change at all which I think is a good thing.I am a perpetual dieter and one thing I did notice for myself was that when adding this to various foods, I did seem to feel full longer than if I didn't add it. Also, my husband has type II diabetes and this is hasn't spiked his blood sugar because it's got protein and fiber and fiber acts like "brakes" for sugar/carbs so they absorb more slowly into the bloodstream and you don't get the blood sugar spikes or at the very least, it doesn't spike so high. So far, despite the holiday season and his "cheating" on his diabetic diet, his blood sugar numbers are actually better than this time last year - I'm not giving all the credit for that to this product but I think it's probably helping at least a bit.I just don't see a downside to this product. It's organic, easy to use and according to what I've read, it's good for you. I will continue to experiment with this and will absolutely be buying it again.

I had visions of "Chia Pets" when ordering these, but based on reported nutritional value, we got some anyway.While there is little taste - particularly in smoothies for example, the texture does exactly what the product packaging says it will do - thicken up fairly rapidly.I don't know what else can be said about this product, other than it is a particularly great smoothie ingredient.  There are other possible uses, and they seem very reasonable now that we've actually used the chia seeds, we just happen to prefer to use it with smoothies.The one negative is the price - nearly $10.00 per pound seems a bit steep, even for organic seeds.  Still, a little goes a long way.

column9: Adds a nice texture to oatmeal
column10: Chia Seeds are kind of weird.  You can put them in ANYTHING.When I opened the bag, my husband immediately tried them in all sorts of things, and has continued to experiment throughout.  Dry?  Gets stuck in your teeth.  He drinks them in chocolate milk when he gets home from a bike ride.  My daughter tried them in apple juice ("They're kind of like frogs eggs, Mom.").  One of my coworkers mixes them with water and then substitutes half the oil in certain baking recipes.For myself, I like them in oatmeal.  I add 2 tablespoons to my regular preparation, and a little extra water.  They give the oatmeal a little more texture.I have not noticed any appreciable health effects, and the chia seeds in oatmeal don't seem to make the fullness effect last any longer than if it was plain, but they're kind of cool.I like having weird grains and things in my pantry. If you're the kind of person who doesn't shy away from things like quinoa and jicama, then chia seeds are for you.

I have been wanting to try chia seeds since I read that they were a great source of energy and protein for pre-workout meals. They are also a Mayan superfood containing protein, anti-oxidants, and fiber. Well, I wasn't disappointed. These things taste great and gave me a quick energy boost. You can add them to salads, soups, smoothies, or any liquid. Mixing Chia seeds with water will make a quick energizing paste, that is great for a quick snack or an early morning, or pre-workout meal.They don't really have a strong flavor, but they absorb the flavor of the food they are mixed with creating a healthy, rich tasting treat. These seeds are great in smoothies or juices. I added some to a peach tea and it was a delicious energizing snack, instead of just a drink. All of the fiber made me feel full, without feeling stuffed. They are also supposed to be an aid to digestion and cleansing.The quality of these white chia seeds is exceptional. They are amazing little round seeds that plump up when soaked in water. They are easy to eat and are full of health benefits. The dried seeds are smooth and round and would also be great for making silk eye pillows, but then we wouldn't be getting the amazing health benefits.

Like many other people, I used to associate Chia seeds with the terracotta Chia pets.  The first time I heard of these seeds being consumed as a health food was in Dr. Oz's show. Nutiva white Chia seeds are USDA organic approved and come in a resealable pouch. If you are like me and don't intend to eat more than a teaspoon of seeds a day, then the Nutiva's 14 oz. bag will last you for a while.Chia seeds can be added to almost any dish because the seeds taste quite neutral although when my mother boiled them in water, I thought they had a very slightly "fish oil" flavor.  I usually mix the tiny seeds in my oatmeal or sprinkle them on the peanut butter spread on my sandwich. Sometimes, I eat them by themselves with a bit of sugar.  I simply soaked them in warm water for about 10 minutes until they start to acquire a gel consistency.  My mother took to these seeds from the very first day.  She liked the smoothness of the gel, which makes for easy swallowing, and thought it would be great as a thick soup if we threw in some beef and chopped Chinese green onions.  That gave me the idea that Chia seeds could be good for elderly people who have trouble chewing. But then, I read that older adults who take blood thinners and/or medication to control their hypertension should not eat the seeds in great quantities because the combination of the medication and the seeds might increase the risk of bleeding and/or might cause a sudden drop in blood pressure.But eating Chia seeds in moderation brings many benefits for most people. Chia seeds are a great source of antioxidants, calcium, protein, boron, and Omega 3-fatty acids; and I like the fact that Nutiva's seeds are organic which means I'm not consuming harmful chemicals along with the seeds.  I haven't been eating Chia seeds long enough to attest to their weight loss and endurance qualities, but they're nutritious and are an easy ingredient to use so I'm happy to incorporate them in my diet.

column9: Extra nutrition for a vegan diet (or any diet!)
column10: Being vegan, I look for quality nutrition from pretty interesting sources.  I blend smoothies very often (thanks to the book Green for Life for giving me many recipes to play with).  Usually I blend up greens, bananas, strawberries, and add flax oil, hemp protein, and nutritional yeast.  Adding a tablespoon of these seeds adds quite a nice dose of nutrition.Most seeds and nuts are high on fat, and these are no exception (50% fat by volume).  But for most diets the pros outweigh the amount of fat.  Plus, a little healthy fat is necessary in a balanced diet.They taste great.  Very mild.  They are great for baking, topping oatmeal or cereal, putting in a cup of almond milk, adding to smoothies (of course), or just eating raw.  You can also soak them in water for a bit to make a nice paste (which is a good way to use it in baking recipes also).The packaging is nice.  There is not a ton of wasted space, the seeds fill the entire bag.  They are USDA organic.I highly recommend them as a source of alternative nutrition, especially for vegetarians and vegans, but for anyone really.

I had never experienced Chia seeds so when I got a chance to sample them, I took it. What fun! They are small crunchy seeds with a pleasant, nutty, grain taste. I experimented with mixing them with various liquids to make chia pudding. The texture reminds me a lot of tapioca pudding. There are 60 calories in a tablespoon, but you can mix this with 8 oz. of water, make the pudding, which keeps up to two weeks in the fridge and add it to jelly and jam to reduce the calories from sugar and boost the nutritional value. I have found a new favorite supper food.

Chia seeds are considered a "Superfood," which means that they contain a very high density of nutrients. Chia provides you with complete protein, ALL essential amino acids, as well as essential vitamins and trace minerals. A great antioxidant source, chia provides high levels of chlorogenic acid, caffeic acid, and flavanol glycosides. These are all polyphenols that maintain proper function of bodily organs and tissues and that protect against cancer and cardiovascular disease through the removal of damaging free radicals. Chia is a phenomenal whole food for any diet.I'd purchased chia seeds in the past and they normally came as a mixture of light and dark seeds. I figured I would try these white chia seeds in order to see if there was any difference in taste and/or nutritional value. White chia seeds appear to have slightly less fat than the standard chia mixture (3g to 4.5g). Other values are essentially the same, such dietary fiber, carbs and protein, but white chia has more potassium at 60mg per serving. I was not able to decipher any distinguishable difference in taste between these white chia seeds and the darker ones I'd had in the past.I usually add these seeds to oatmeal, but other options include smoothies, yogurt or even baked goods. What I have yet to try is soaking the seeds in water, which creates a "gel" that can essentially be added to any recipe.

I received two pouches of Nutiva Organic White Chia seeds to test and review, and it is my first experience with Chia (ingesting that is; have made Chia pets before, lol). First off, I do like the way the seeds are packaged--the pouches are made of very tough material and the resealable zip-lock on top really does work easily and consistantly. It stands up nicely because the bottom of the pouch is wider. I find it easy to store in my fridge. The second thing I noticed is that the seeds are nice and clean looking. I have read some reviews about other Chia seeds and some have disappointed because of debris in the package. Not so with this product; the pack is full of clean, uniform small white seeds with darker centers. The proof they say, is in the pudding, but so far I have not made pudding, but have been drinking it straight mixed in a large glass of water. I am following the recommendation of mixing two Tablespoons with water, letting it set for a few minutes and drinking it down. The mixture does quickly become gelationous, but is tolerable to drink. However, I don't advise letting it sit for more than about 10 minutes because it continues to gel until the texture becomes, for me, too hard to swallow. I do believe it contributes to a sense of fullness, and I think the fiber has been helping with regularity. So far I have not lost any weight. I also think that my blood sugar is more stabilized because I do not feel hungry for a long time (by which I don't mean empty, but rather weak and shakey). My energy level has been decent. It has not cured my lupus, as I am still running a low grade fever. I will continue to use this product and update my progress. There is lots of good information in some of the other reviews, as well as recipe ideas, so I am going to try some of those, too.Good luck, and I hope it helps you, too!

Finally, I have found a nutritious superfood that doesn't have an overpowering taste. In fact, it expertly blends with whatever you add it to, making it a wise purchase for anyone who wants the flexibility of adding a healthy "boost" to diverse foods.I love this for sneaking in extra nutrition for the kids.  Even my pickiest eater can't tell when I stir it into her soup since the color of these white chia seeds is a pale beige and the grain isn't really gritty.  It turns into a type of gel after being soaked in liquid for 5-10 minutes. This makes it a valuable ingredient in my pantry, because it's so easy to add to any menu.From the back of this pouch, I learned that chia seeds were regarded by the ancient Aztec and Mayan people as vital nourishment. In one tablespoon, these raw, organic white chia seeds contain 3 grams of Omega-3 fats, with the same amount of protein, 60 mg potassium, and 5 grams each of total carbs and dietary fiber. Calcium content per tablespoon is 8%, Iron 6% and Magnesium 10%, respectively.I really feel that I stumbled upon a pleasant surprise with this product.  At last, I can stop buying supplements for my kids that they continually complain about, regarding taste.I can now just add a sprinkle of practically untraceable nutrition to their food daily, with the confidence that their minds and bodies are being fed in an amazing way.

Many claims are made regarding the health benefits of these 1 mm (0.039 inches) seeds from central and southern Mexico and Guatemala. A 52 year-old Indian won the 100 mile run in California in 19 hours and 37 minutes. He said he was able to complete the run with such high speed because he ate Chia seeds before and during the race. The seeds are said to be gluten free, the highest source of omega-3, contains minerals, phosphorous, manganese, calcium, potassium, sodium, fatty acids, and they keep the body hydrated because they absorb a large amount of water. It is also said that the seeds can last 4 or 5 years, even unrefrigerated.The seeds can be eaten raw. They can be placed in water or fruit juices, left for 15 minutes until they become gelatinous and then drunk; the seeds, however, are not dissolved in the liquid. (The name Chia means oily, probably referring to how the seeds becomes gelatinous.) They can also be placed raw on top of fruits or cereals, or baked in cakes, breads, or biscuits. I tried them in the drinks and on top of fruits and I liked them. I put a heaping tablespoon in each. They added a slight grainy taste, which I think added to the flavor.

It is what it is but I've noticed some differences between the white and the black.  I don't know if it's psychological but I swear the white ones fluff up more in water and there is less crunch in the final bite.  For those who are experienced in Chia seeds will know exactly what crunch I'm talking about.  I would say it's 99.9% white.

Recently discovered chia seeds for increased energy, suppressed appetite and health benefits on YouTube.  This is my 2nd purchase, my first was a black chia seed product here on Amazon.  Although there is no difference in the color as far as taste, I do like using the WHITE seeds (this purchase) better because it is easier to "hide" in oatmeal, smoothies, scrambled eggs for my teens.  I felt this was a great price for the 2 bags.

These work well in recipes where you want to "sneak" in some chia so no one the the family can see it!  Another plus, they are not manufactured with peanut.I use them to sprinkle on oatmeal, cereal, salads, spaghetti, even on pizza.  Easy way to get some healthy fats added without a ton of calories.They also work well in cookies, just be sure and not cook over 350.

I've purchased chia seeds before (black) and they came with a sample of the white variety.  I don't think it makes a difference, but I did like using the white ones better.  I was just about finished with the black kind when this was offered.  I don't use them like many people.  I just mix a tablespoon of these and some ground flax in a little water every morning and drink it.  Not a very pleasant experience.  Not much taste, but the slurry feels terrible.  They get stuck between your teeth no matter how I try to swallow without chewing.  Chia seeds want to stick to everything once you wet them.  Cleaning glasses, bowls, etc after using them takes extra work.  I have not soaked them overnight and added to smoothies or anything, so maybe that minimizes the mess a bit.Having said all that, I will use them as a thickening agent in soups.  Smart people out there can probably use them countless ways.  I swallow them for their protein content and to promote a healthy digestive tract.  I definitely like the fact that they are organic.  And to me, the white ones are just more appealing.  Nutiva provides high quality ingredients.

What I really like about this product is that it's so easy to just use a little bit in foods that you were going to eat anyway. I've been putting ground flax seeds in my oatmeal for a while and this can very nicely fulfill a similar purpose. It's actually a little more convenient than flax, because you need to worry about whether flax seeds are ground while this can just go right in. They're basically just a really easy way to add some extra nutrition without making any big changes to the taste of something that you were going to eat anyway.I found the packaging of these particular seeds to be very nicely done and convenient to use. I really have no complaints at all about the product. The particular package I've been using was given to me for the purpose of trying out and reviewing it, but I will likely purchase more in the future.

I have been using black chia seeds for a while now. I add them to my food for the nutritional value. Chia seeds are high in Omega-3, protein and fiber. There really is not much difference between black chia seeds and white chia seeds (besides the color).I use chia seeds now instead of flax seeds because they don't alter the food as much as the ground flax seeds do. I like that chia seeds can be used whole. They don't need to be ground to release their nutritional benefits. You can add chia seeds to almost anything you eat. They can even be added to foods that are baked or cooked. They add no flavor.The one thing I don't like about chia seeds, especially black chia seeds, is that they can get stuck in your teeth. Not a pretty site.Chia seeds do not need to be refrigerated. These chia seeds are a product of Mexico and they are labeled USDA organic.

column9: Healthy Goodness--Superfood We Should All Include
column10: I've been eating chia seeds for years, ever since I read the book Born To Run.  They are a traditional food of the Tarahumara Native Americans of Mexico and help keep them satisfied when they run long distances.  They are a powerhouse of nutrition and can keep you going for a long time.  I put them in my homemade granola when I make a big batch every two weeks and occasionlly I make a somewhat traditional chia drink.  I mix a tablespoon or two into a glass of water with some lemon or lime juice and a little sugar or other sweetener and leave it to sit for a few minutes, to make a gel.  It's a bit weird, but they don't affect the flavor.  They produce a mucilagenous gel that actually has a very interesting mouth feel.These chia seeds resemble other chia seeds that I have purchased over the years.  I can't see any difference in taste.  They appear to be fresh and the packaging is sturdy.  Chia is a source for a lot of different vitamins and minerals and even some omega-threes.  We can all stand to have more raw nuts and seeds in our diets, given how nutritious they are, so I like to add these whenever I think about it.  A good product.  I'd buy again.

The health benefits of chia seed has been widely reported.  For example, like flax seed, they contain omega-3 fatty acids,and unlike flax, there's no need to grind them to break the outer coat.  (It's also said the form of omega-3 found in both flax and chia isn't as valuable as that found in fish oil, but you may not car if you're a vegetarian, and for that matter, it doesn't have to be the best possible form of the nutrient for it to be worth eating.) Chia is also a good source of soluble fiber, which is known to promote digestive health and lower cholesterol, like the fiber in oatmeal, apples, and psyllium (the last of which, the main ingredient in Metamucil, isn't the kind of thing most people enjoy consuming.) Mixed with water, chia turns into a gel, but you don't have to mix it with water to receive the benefits--it will turn into a gel in your digestive tract regardless of how you eat it.I use them in smoothies, in yoghurt, in baked goods, and sprinkled on salads. They don't have much flavor, but then again, they also don't get in the way of the flavor what you're eating them with.  A simple way to boost your intake of soluble fiber and omega-3.  This particular brand is organic, which I appreciate.  Otherwise, chia is chia.

I don't like the hydrated (gooey) chia seeds, but dry (on cereal) they have a bit of chewiness, like smaller kiwi fruit seeds and I prefer them to flax seeds. In hot drinks, some tend to stick to the cup (not a good thing!)I can't verify the health benefits, though I think that by absorbing liquids in my stomach they may decrease my appetite and thereby my weight (which is a very good thing for the vast number of us who are overweight!).I haven't noticed more energy and am unlikely to morph into a Tarahumara long-distance runner. They must not eat them dry, and those who do need to ensure drinking plenty of liquids.

column9: This vegan loves her some Chia
column10: I've been vegan for a few years, and have been on the Chia bandwagon for about 18 months.  (In fact, last year I gave a bag to each of my sibs & cousins for xmas, which met with mixed reviews...)  Chia seeds are easy to sprinkle on or in almost anything (and don't have to be ground like flax seeds do), they are high in fiber and rich in omega-3's, and they are said to reduce both blood pressure and blood sugar.  They are 20% protein, and also high in iron, potassium, magnesium, and more.  They are said to be a 'superfood' of the Aztecs and Mayans because of the long-term sustained energy they provide.Chia seeds have a faint nutty taste that most people - even my teenagers and their friends - like.  I put a few teaspoons in my smoothies, in my baking, and in my tofu scrambles.  I also like to toast them up with sesame seeds and poppy seeds and use the mixture (in a shaker) as a garnish or condiment at the table.  Yum!This was my first experience with white Chia seeds.  I can discern no difference between the white and the (more common) black Chia seeds.  Both have a slight thickening response.  Both can be sprinkled on or in anything.  Both have only the very faintest flavor.  And by my reading both have the same nutritional benefits.  I guess white is better if you are trying to trick little kids into eating something healthy in their oatmeal or eggs.  The white are a little more expensive - I'm not sure why.BOTTOM LINE:  Try Chia seeds- you don't need to be a vegan to appreciate the amazing nutritional benefits.  If white seeds are more appetizing to you, these will be great.  Enjoy!

column9: A Different Choice for this Family
column10: I will admit, we are not the key market group for this product.  Stops at the health food stores are rare in our household.  We aren't vegan or vegetarian as many people who have reviewed seem to be, but we are always looking at ways to add nutrition and health to our diets.  I found a recipe for a pudding with the chia seeds and started from there.  It was delicious.  Very similar to tapioca.  My kids LOVED it.  We also tried it to thicken smoothies..also tasty.I'm still finding new uses for these chia seeds as I am a novice at this.  I also have not tried any other brands, so I can't compare this to similar products.  I can say that everything I have tried it with, has worked and was tasty.

I selected these white chia seeds from the Vine program because I was curious to find out whether they were different than the black chia seeds.  My husband and I added chia seeds to our diet about a year ago after reading about their health benefits. When not making smoothies, we simply soak them in water for 30 minutes or more and then squeeze some fresh lime into the glass, along with a little sweetener (such as agave nectar).  The white seeds are more "attractive" and disappear into foods more easily due to their color.  They also seem to be slightly smaller and less gritty than the black ones.  For anyone who would like to try chia seeds for the first time, I'd recommend these.  However, because they are significantly more expensive than the black ones (that I buy in bulk on Amazon), I probably won't purchase the white ones again.

Let me preface this review by saying that I have a lot of texture issues with food. And the chia seed in liquid looks and feels like frog eggs. So I was hesitant to try these. But having done so, I'm a fan. Yes, they are kinda slimy, but we're not talking okra levels of slime, and even I was able to swallow them. I actually like them better mixed in with other things (smoothies, baked goods) than taken as a beverage. I find them to have no discernible taste.But the reason I'm a fan is for the health benefits, namely the fiber boost. It is a most excellent replacement for psyllium, not only because of the higher fiber content (the chia seeds have 5.5. g of fiber per tablespoon, while the psyllium has 3 grams per tablespoon). The chia seeds also provide other nutrients that psyllium doesn't have, such as protein and small amounts of certain vitamins. If you're not used to a fiber-rich food, start using the chia in small amounts and work up to the full recommended serving size. I'm pretty pleased that this particular brand is organic, too. I will be buying these when my current supply runs out.

I've been wanting to try chia seeds for a while after hearing they're high in omega-3's, tryptophan, fiber and antioxidants. So far I've found them to be a great addition to my diet and easy to add to all sorts of foods. They're very small; much smaller than sesame seeds, a little crunchy if eaten dry and don't have a distinct flavor, which makes them perfect for adding to any kind of food, juices or recipes for extra nutrition without changing the flavor of things. When they're soaked in water or any liquid, they take on a gel-like consistency. I like mixing them into shakes, smoothies or sprinkling them on cereal and salads for added crunch. They're also good on yogurt and can be added to muffins and other baked goods. The two 14 oz. bags are a nice size and will last a while depending on how you use them. Great product! I'll definitely be a repeat buyer.

I admit... I picked these from the Vine list entirely because of curiosity.  Chia seeds?  What the heck are those?I'll let the prospective customer do the research on the details, but all I figure you need to know is that they are tiny seeds that are extremely nutritious with many different purposes.Mainly so far I have been using them as an egg substitute and a little something to throw into soups, yogurt, whatever is cooking that wouldn't be opposed to some seeds.  They have no strong taste, but add some great texture and apparently amazing nutrition.  As an egg substitute? This is the only one I have tried that WORKS.I'm searching for new ways to use them, but even in my so-far limited experience I am highly impressed.

I love making smoothies and although I don't eat healthy all the time, I try to find ways to add healthy items into my diet.  I was afraid that these would be gritty or seedy (you know, like raspberry seeds) in a smoothie, but they weren't.  They blended in well.  They add fiber and Omega-3 by just throwing a spoonful into your drink or cereal.

column4: J. Nachison "long-time SF and history lover"
column9: Nutiva Organic White Chia Seeds are versatile and easy to use
column10: This was there first time I tried this product.  After seeing an episode of "Chopped" on the Food Network I was intrigued.  What fun!  So far I have sprinkled the seeds on peanut butter and jelly sandwiches, and bagels and cream cheese. I have added them to sweet potato fries, stir fries and salads. I have soaked them and added them to cooked oatmeal.  I plan on adding them to my meatballs.  I will definitely continue to use them.  I also found many suggestions on line by googling "Chia Seed Recipes."  I would  recommend this product to anyone who strives to eat a healthy diet.

Chia seeds are one of the most nutritious things on earth. But they can be difficult to incorporate into the typical person's diet. Try this trick: add a couple tablespoons of Chia seeds to a health smoothy. After blending let it sit for a half hour or so in the refrigerator. The ground Chia seeds will thicken and add a pleasing, slightly jell-like consistency.
