It won't change the taste but will add tons of essential fats, minerals and vitamins.These white chia seeds seem to blend slightly better than the normal black or brown ones. 100% recommended to anybody concerned with increasing the nutritional profile of the food they eat.

These have a nice, mild flavor, and the texture, when cooked with other foods, blends right in, in fact my kids haven't even been able to tell I've been adding these to scrambled eggs and casseroles.It's an excellent, sneaky way to get extra fiber and vitamins into your family, even the pickiest eater didn't notice.I think it adds to the recipes and makes them taste better, even if no one else has realized there's an extra ingredient.I'm a big fan of "stealth health," I've been known to tell my kids that bits of fruit in a muffin was actually bits of candy, so this has worked out really well for me.It only takes a little bit, one tablespoon in a single serving adds 20% of the daily allowance of fiber, 3g of protein, 6% iron, 8% calcium and 10% magnesium. That's pretty nutrient-dense.Pretty soon I'll 'fess up that I've been adding chia seeds to our scrambled eggs, buffalo chicken rice, tuna mac, and other dishes, and I'll point out that no one can say they don't like them, because they never even noticed it was there.Stealth health, you gotta do what you can to get healthy foods into your kids!

These are light, crunchy little chia seeds. They are mild in flavor and texture. When you soak them in some water, they turn into Chia 'tapioca', which means they have a bit of a jelly coating. This makes it very hard for me to eat strait, but added to smoothies and other such products they are very edible indeed! Chia is a superfood. It has all your essential amino acids, and lots of protein and fiber. If you are looking to add chia to your diet, this is a good starting point.

I have to say this is a much harder item to review than I thought it would be.  I couldn't find another chia product locally for comparison, for one thing, and I've never eaten chia before, only watered it on a "chia pet".  But as I'm in the midst of a major overhaul of my diet, it seemed an appropriate food product to try.I will admit I didn't not try the cereal recipe on the back of the package, mostly because it requires additional Nutiva products that I don't have on hand.  Given the slightly crunchy texture even after soaking, I also didn't add it to my nutritional shakes.  Instead, I added the seeds to my fresh-cooked rolled oats/ground flax seed/random fresh fruit daily breakfast.The seeds come out of the package nice and white and consistent in size and shape, which makes it an appealing add-on.  Instructions call for the seeds to be soaked in warm water for 10 minutes prior to consumption, so I experimented with pre-soaking and various cooking times in the microwave with and without the pre-soak.  The best bet seemed to be to add the raw seeds to the raw oats and raw ground flax, add a bit more water than normal as the seeds tend to soak it up, then nuke for 3 minutes on 50% in a 1000 kw (that's a very small) microwave.  That left a bit of crunch all around while still making the seeds soft enough to eat and digest.The fiber level makes this a great dietary addition, especially for those just starting a high-fiber cholesterol-lowering regimen.  It's not as high as ground flax seed, which can be a plus if you tend to be sensitive to changes in fiber intake.  The combination of a tablespoon of Chia and a tablespoon of flax (that's about half the usual amount of flax) with 1/3 cup of thick-cut rolled oats was really nice both in texture and flavor.  The Chia is a tad sweeter than the nutty flavor of the flax.Quality control on the product appears to be excellent and the zip-lock package is good enough, though it lost its zip pretty quickly.  I didn't find any artifacts of the processing in the package, which is always a plus and not always a given.  I'm going to continue to use this product, and I can honestly recommend it to my fellow cholesterol-battlers as a tasty fiber option.

column4: Shawn Kovacich "Author and Creator of numerou...
column9: Really Glad I Tried Them Out
column10: I first heard about Chia seeds from a co-worker and the first thing I though of what the Chia Pet. But the more I researched them, the better they sounded. Full of Omega 3 fatty acids, protein, fiber, and oil, these are the better than flax seeds, which you have to grind to get to the nutrients. They also hold a lot of water, which I was hoping would help me with hydration.The seeds are so small that you can add them to oatmeal, muffins, etc and not notice them. I really like the Chia jello. If you soak one tablespoon of seeds in water, they make a gel. I've drank the jello in mixed plan water and added it to tea or juice. I did find that if you put them in a mixture of grape juice and water they don't soak up much liquid.I noticed that if you drink this plain, I felt a little dehydrated. So I drank more water then felt bloated. I've learned you don't need much more than a tablespoon mixed in water. Any more and it gets overwhelming. What I like to do is drink my jello after eating breakfast. I stay full longer. It's been helping me by controlling my hunger for my dieting.The only drawbacks I've noticed is that they don't really help me with the hydration. They don't soak up as much water in a grape juice water mixture. And they cost about $11 for a 14-ounce bag. I find that a bit pricey but on the other hand, you are just using about one tablespoon a day, which comes out to about 28 days use out of one bag.In the end, I'm glad that I heard about Chia seeds and got to try them from the Vine Program. This is one thing that I'm going to be sure that I keep in stock.Shawn KovacichAuthor and Creator of numerous books and DVD's.

column9: Easy to enjoy with no interruption to lifestyle.
column10: Although I don't eat much meat, I'm not a vegetarian.  I do enjoy chicken many ways, and the occasional beef entry.  My problem with food is carbohydrates and cravings that follow.  I have found adding this chia seeds do my diet effortless, and beneficial.  It certainly has many healthy factors to them being high in protein, antioxidants and a natural way to add fiber.  But they are perfect for help with losing weight and controlling appetite.  I added these to most everything, and not changed much about what I eat, and I have lost over 5 pounds, and have not finished one 14 oz bag.  I have added them to all cereals and oatmeal, muffin mixes, yogurt, pasta, even coated chicken with egg white and used the seeds as breading and baked... great!  You find you don't eat as much, and enjoy food more.  Very filling.  If you simply used them in cereal and oatmeal, it's a very beneficial way to start your day.  A great price. Especially using the subscription method.

column9: The almighty chia, but in a color that's easier to hide
column10: So, I recently read the book Born to Run and was intrigued by the almost-magical properties that were attributed to this superfood, the chia seed. Even before reading that book I had some tucked away in my pantry because I had heard they were good for me, but that really caused me to start incorporating them into more of our meals.Chia seeds are loaded with omega's and protein and all kinds of good stuff. I've been using them any place that I would use flax seed, or flax seed meal: sprinkled on oatmeal, a couple tablespoons in a breakfast smoothie, or mixed in with homemade granola bars for added nutritional benefits. You can even use them as an egg substitute when you're baking by mixing 1/4 cup of water with 1 tsp ground chia seeds (just grind them in a coffee grinder). I am a huge fan of tapioca pudding and you can use these seeds to make a faux tapioca by soaking some of them in coconut milk and then mixing in some frozen blueberries and a little stevia to sweeten. SO good. If you google 'ways to use chia seeds' you will find dozens of ideas.This particular brand of chia seeds is well-priced and excellent quality. I love this 'white' version of the chia seeds because they are easier to hide in my kids' food! They aren't actually white, more of a light gray-taupe, but certainly less conspicuous than traditional black chia seeds.I will definitely buy these again, although I think my two-bag supply from my last order will probably last me a while. Give them a try!

column4: Jessica R. Westberg "A Catholic with a sense ...
column9: A Good Item for any Kitchen to have
column10: Up front, I must confess, I am not a vegan, a vegetarian or a raw-food enthusiast. I did want to try these out and see if the claims stack up to reality. While I am still undecided as to the claims of more energy, I do find these little seeds to be a useful kitchen staple. I have been putting a few teaspoons in with my Chobani yogurt every day, which lends a nice, nutty texture to the yogurt. I also made a great, delicious bread with the Chia seeds, which was easy and fun to make. The only quibble I have is that the seeds, after soaking in liquid, have a strange texture to them, which takes some getting used to.These little seeds go a long way, I'm about half-way through the first bag, and I've been eating some every day! Even if you are not a vegan or vegetarian, I think these seeds are a good staple for any cook to have in their kitchen. The bread recipe that I made with the Chia seeds is at vegweb dot com.

These seeds have a really mild taste. They don't taste like anything, really. I've sprinkled them on cereal and in yogurts, but I really prefer making my own chia fresca.  The seeds are very small and have the crunchy texture of raspberry seeds, which I don't like, so I find it easier to soak them and drink them. For a really quick chia fresca, you can simply soak a tablespoon of the seeds in a mixture of juice and water for fifteen minutes or even overnight. Just stir or shake them up a few times to reduce clumping. The seeds get very soft and soak up a lot of liquid, which reminds me of pulpy juice. I find that a lot easier to get them down, but you may prefer eating them dry! I haven't tried baking with them yet, but it seems like they would work better than flaxseed (my main go-to) as an egg replacer.

column9: Healthy, versatile, easy to add to diet
column10: I'm already a fan of the Nutiva brand because of their extra-virgin coconut oil, which I've found to be a high-quality product. This chia-seed product is no less impressive, and I really like the packaging: recloseable bag plus a base that stands up on the countertop while you scoop it.Stirring a tablespoon of the seeds into oatmeal or a beverage of your choice (I tried cranberry-pomegranate juice) and allowing it to sit for a minute or two allows the seeds to soften and release their mucilaginous coating. I did not notice any alteration in taste of the juice or oatmeal when stirring in chia. They are pretty tasteless so you can put them into anything. They are divine sprinkled over just-out-of-the-oven cheese toast because they help add to that delicious crunch that perfectly made cheese toast has.Chia seeds have numerous health benefits, including having a higher level of omega-3 fatty acids than flax seeds while storing for long periods of time without going rancid like flax seeds do. Just google "chia health benefits" online and you'll find reams of information.These are the same type of seed that is used with Chia Pets. I've never had a Chia Pet, which grows chia-seed "hair," but there are good directions online for growing chia year-round as a microgreen using sprouting and wheatgrass-growing techniques. I'm interested in this use of Nutiva's chia seeds so we can get a little more fresh greens into us, but I haven't tried it yet. There are plenty of seeds in these two pouches to grow a lot of chia greens!Try them. You'll like them.

Is it my imagination, or do I feel slightly more peppy since introducing these powerhouse seeds into my diet more than two weeks ago? Chia is a good source of Omega 3, and maybe I hadn't been getting much of that fatty acid which is essential for metabolism, prior to eating these chia seeds.I've eaten them by the spoonful, added them to tapioca pudding and chili, and sprinkled them on top of a baked apple. I substuted them for half of the butter in the crumb topping of an apple pie (this actually worked). I sprinkled them on oatmeal (my favorite way of eating them).What I like best about Nutiva Organic Chia Seed is that it's a whole, natural food. The seeds are not overprocessed -- they're a seed, harvested from a plant. They provide nourishment. They're easier to digest than flaxseed.One Tablespoon (12g) of chia seeds delivers:Fiber 5gProtein 3 gOmega 3MagnesiumCalciumIronCalories 60Fat Calories 25I think I will buy this product after my supply is gone, and make it a regular part of my diet.

I've been wanting to try chia seems for a while. I like that you do not need to grind them before consuming like flax seeds. I also liked that these are white and not really visible in your white flour baked goods. The pouch is resealable and a good size, easy to handle. I have never tried chia seeds before, so really have nothing to compare to. But I have no complains against this particular brand.

Ever since ordering these chia seeds, my breakfast has consisted of 2-3 tablespoons of seeds, 1 tablespoon of coconut sugar, and 6-8 ounces of coconut milk. Delicious! Just soak the seeds for 10 minutes or so, stirring every few minutes and you basically get something very similar to tapioca pudding, but with nearly 10 grams of protein and fiber. Plus it's delicious. My two-year old calls it ice cream :-)Stored propertly, these seeds will be good for at least 2 years, though there's no chance they'll even last through the end of 2011 at this rate.For a tasty dessert, try soaking the chia seeds in So Delicious Chocolate Coconut milk.Highly recommended.

column9: All I can say is YUM.
column10: I LOVE chia seeds.  They are a powerhouse of nutrition and you can add them to so many things.  I love to put them in yogurt. They dont add a lot of distracting flavors (like flax for example) but they add a crunch that is wonderful.  But I will eat these for a snack by themselves sometimes because they take the edge off of hunger and keep me satiated for a really long time.

I love Chia seeds! They are so good for you. I like to put them in my oatmeal in the morning for an extra omega three boost plus they add some extra fiber which is a plus! I have used the black chia seeds in the past but these are easy to slip in the grandson's oatmeal with out him knowing. :o) I have used them in muffins in place of poppy seeds and they work just fine.

My husband eats oatmeal and fruit every morning at work. He took a bag of the Nutiva Organic White Chia Seeds to work and puts 2 tsp. in his cereal every morning. He says it thickens his oatmeal just right. He loves it because he knows it is even more healthy with the seeds added.The first thing he did when he opened the package was take out some seeds and before I could stop him, he ate them! Big mistake! Lol He said they tasted terrible. He won't make that mistake again. However they are great used in cooking. We are pleased with this product very much.

I'd read the stories about mountain trekkers who survived long days and grueling climbs on a handful of chia seeds, and I'd read about the nutritional value of chia.  Frankly, I was skeptical, but willing to try it to see for myself.  I'm no longer a skeptic.I stirred my two tablespoons of chia into fresh-squeezed juices of apple and pomegranate, rather than simply dropping it into water.  It was delightful, and although I had not blended it into a smoothy, the seeds were so small that they did not have any taste I could notice.The juice was good, the seeds not much of anything except creating a kind of gel, so why did I become a fan?  Something in this mundane drink really resonated with my body chemistry.  My energy level exploded -- even more the second than the first day.  Wow!Will it work as well for you?  I cannot say, but if you think your body needs a boost, I'd give it a try before I used the expensive energy drink.  I'm surely glad I did.FIVE STARS!

column9: Healthy But Limited Usage For Me
column10: These tiny seeds really pack it in: Omega 3 fatty acid, protein, fiber, and rare antioxidants. But for me, there aren't enough ways to use them that I like.The most popular use for these seems to be to mix the seeds with water and make a gel. I'm not a fan of gelatinous textures so this has no allure for me. It also seems they would do the same for anything they were mixed into. They are also too small to eat from the bag, as they get stuck in my teeth. While I am glad I had the chance to try them, I won't be purchasing them.So why the five-star rating? The seeds are everything they claim to be. Just because I don't like them doesn't mean this is a bad product, and they don't deserve to be down-rated for that.

column9: OMG, the yummiest all time new, favorite, healthy treat. Check this recipe!
column10: I have tried chia seeds before, but not quite sure what to do them. I never really knew what to do with them other than soaking in water and waiting for them grow on my Chia Pet, LMOA!!!I haverecently tried Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna, 15-Ounce (Pack of 2) and then found this GREAT recipe with Chia seeds with the Manna. (BTW, the Coconut Manna is a delicious, nutritious "whole-food" that is completely yummy too!) Here is my own rendition of this great breakfast treat:Take 1 cup of POM juice(Pomegranate Juice 6 X 16 Ounce Case)and mix in 2 Tablespoon Chia and Hemp Seeds. Put it in a nice, toasty warm place (like your oven at 100 degrees or even better a food dehydrator). Put your jar of Manna in the toasty place at the same time. Leave them in there for 30 minutes - 2 hours. Stir-up you Manna and nuts, and then add a tablespoon of the best honey you can find. Add 1 tablespoon of Manna and enjoy this wonderful, healthy breakfast treat. (Make sure to stir your Manna well to mix in the oil and the coconut powder.) You can add in a chopped banana to enhance the experience.

column9: Just as good as the "black" chia seeds I eat
column10: About six months ago I got turned on to adding chia seeds to my oatmeal and have been using the Navitas Naturals Chia Seeds Aztec Superfood, 16 Ounce Pouch.Chia seeds have no taste to me so they can be added to oatmeal, drinks, etc. without alterating the flavor of the food.  I use mine in oatmeal only.  They expand when added to liquid and become gelatinous.I tried these white chia seeds from Nutiva and they are no different in their taste, texture, or expansion ability compared to the ones I use now.  They are really not white, instead they are a pale sandy color with some brown ones thrown in.  This makes it easier to disguise in foods because the color is lighter.  The only difference besides the color between these "white" chia seeds and the black ones I eat periodically is the nutrition.According to the package, a serving size is one tablespoon at 60 calories with 25 from fat for these white chia seeds.  Calcium is 8%, Magnesium 10% and Iron 6% with 3 grams of protein, 5 grams of fiber and 2.5 grams of Omega 3s.  However, according to the package on the Navitas black chia seeds I also eat, a serving size is two tablespoons at 70 calories, 40 from fat. Calcium is 10% and Vitiman C is 4% with 3 grams of protein and 6 grams of fiber but the package dosn't make any claims about the quantity of Omega 3s.To me, these chia seeds are as excellent as the Navitas Naturals Chia Seeds Aztec Superfood, 16 Ounce Pouch although these white chia seeds are easier to disguise in food. I would definitely purchase either product and would base my future purchases on its use and price.

column9: Love my CHIA....works perfectly in smoothies and salad dressing... so pleased with the product
column10: UPDATE 6/6/12 : I have now been using this product for 6 months. I find it to be superior to other chia products I have purchased in the past.. AND PROMINENTLY LABELED........NON GMO ...HURRAY.... I love that....will be repurchasing this product for sure.

Like all raw chia seeds they do swell and stick when wet which makes a gel that can be added to recipes. They are relatively high in calories making them good for a high energy snack.

column9: Love as a topping for yogurt
column10: Adding them to yogurt added a little texture and crunch (and nutrition)  to it.  Also good when soaked and added to recipes.  Will buy them again.

I like Chis seeds because of the nutritional value.  I hadn't tried the white before.  These are good, but to me they aren't too different from the regular ones.  I can't tell the difference.  These are good, though.

This is the stuff that superman eats to get his super powers (just kidding)... but seriously, this is a great product and Nutiva has fashionably packaged it, seperating the white seeds into a reclosable bag, so that you can use them for baking, smoothies, puddings, or just by themselves. Chia is a great source of calcium, protein, healthy omega fats, fiber and iron, among other nutrients.The Nutiva white chia seeds are raw, certified organic which is a plus.If you are looking for a high quality, delicious chia seed brand, you can't go wrong with Nutiva Organic White Chia seeds.I was very pleased with this product.

I had never tried cooking with chia seeds before.  They work well as a thickening agent for vegan recipes, especially for sauces.  You can use them in any meal in which you might use wheat germ, to add a similar crunch or grittiness.  They are not especially low-calorie, however!

Love this!  I have used it for cereal and oatmeal so far, and I am going to try it in a lot more things.  I love that you don't need a lot to get the health benefits - only 1 Tbsp!  I can sneak it in without my kids' knowing!

column9: Use Chia seeds as a secret dieting weapon! Great nutritional asset. Easy to use. Sprinkle on cereals, oatmeal, etc.
column10: These are very nice little seeds and a great source of antioxidants and fiber. Add them to your baking, sprinkle on cereals, put them in your blender as an addition to a healthy smoothie. Great nutritional source. These chia seeds are very  easy to use!In the smoothies, they add a nice texture & subtle, nutty flavor. Nice!  Healthy & tastes good, too!.These seeds add a nice extra crunch to your salads. They take up the dressing and taste nice. Try toasting the seeds for extra flavour and crispiness in salads. Added nutrition can be tasty & interesting, not a punishment.  Can sprinkle these on in place of croutons.A good weight loss supplement as well.

Until few days ago, I hadnt heard of chia seeds and now I see that this product from Aztecs is better than the best like salmon for omega 3 fatty acids. Well its hard to know if all of that is true, we have to take the experts word for it. As a product, I first tried a tbsp of it in a glass of cold water. Let it absorb some water. I gulped some water down and hey they are harmless. If the thought of letting gelly stuff go down your throat sounds difficult, go on take a bite, you will find that it is much like a skinny sesame seed. Even if it acts like a placebo, our body will self induce the goodness we think we are feeding it. I will try to make a chia pet and also have the seeds in my oatmeal and report more observations.

I read all of the good stuff associated with Chia Seed. My husband and I have been determined to eat healthier, and go organic when possible. We are succeeding in our endeavors, and thought that this product would fit right into our new lifestyle. I have attempted to get this seed into things that we eat regularly. It just does not work for me. I cannot get past the slime and mouth feel. For those of you who are able to, I think that is wonderful, but I am going to pass on any further use of it.

I happened upon King Mints in a small specialty shop and fell in love with them.  They are just the right mix of mint and sweet.  I really prefer them over any other roll mints. I have tried dozens of these packets of snacks over the past 3 years.  Various flavors from various lots.  Some of them a while back tasted fine.  Lately, all I get are ones with a bitter, rancid taste.  Especially on the Friends variety.  Does "all natural" mean "High in THC"?What is up with that sharp nasty taste?  These things aren't expired. My kids won't even eat them anymore.  Its like they are all rancid or something.
They taste great and I like that they have good ingredients and no trans-fat and no corn syrup.  We will continue purchasing this item and other Annie's Homegrown snacks.

I wanted to try these as a slightly healthier alternative to Teddy Grahams.  These are organic and have a few less ingredients.FLAVOR:With three flavors of "bunnies" you get a medley that is kind of nice.  However, only the chocolate ones have enough flavor to even compare to a Teddy Graham.  The chocolate chip has a very, very mild chocolate flavor, but isn't too bad.  The honey flavor is pretty bland.  Honey Teddy Grahams have more flavor, so I'd choose them over plain honey bunnies.TEXTURE:These bunnies get stale very fast.  Seal them up well, or you'll have bad tasting bunnies.  Fresh, they're crispy and crunchy and a great size for on-the-go snacking or sitting at your computer with a cup of coffee and these little cookies.OVERALL OPINIONI do like the organic factor.  However, they're generally a little more money than their competing Teddies, and I like Teddy flavor better.  It's up to you and your taste buds, but I would at least recommend trying the bunnies.  I buy them when they're on sale for cheaper than Teddies.

column9: Not just for kids......these are tasty!
column10: Ok, I have to say, the packaging did draw me in... I mean, how could the little hippy bunny flashing you a peace sign steer you wrong?  So I picked up the box...organic, I like that, 8 grams of sugar, I can live with that, no trans or saturated fats, 20% calcium, 2 grams of fiber, and I can have 28 little cookies (a combo of chocolate, honey & chocolate chip) for 130 calories.  So, the bunnies and I went home together....These are my favorite little cookies when I want something sweet but don't want to obliterate all the good eating that I did all day.  Yeah, they are a cookie, but I felt good that I could eat organic and that there were no additives or preservatives.  I like to keep mine in the fridge where they stay nice and cold and crunchy and just wait for me to pair it with a glass of milk.Great snack for the little ones as well as those of us who are young at heart!
I bought these for a friend of mind for her birthday because she loves these and cannot find them everywhere.  Everyone should try these they are wonderful and healthier then others

These are FABULOUS.  I was introduced to them by a friend and I can't wait to try all the different varieties.  These go for $2.99 at Earth Fare, so they're not that expensive, especially for how much is in the box!  I know 7.5 ounces doesn't sound like that much, but I emptied the entire box into a ziploc bag, and I've been snacking on them for the past 3 days and I still haven't made a dent!  Although, I don't have kids and I won't share with my husband, so that could be why :-)  Seriously, give these a try - you will NOT be disappointed.

First of all, they taste great.  That's what matters most to kids.  I like them too!  Bunny Grahams are also made with all sorts of organic ingredients and no hydrogenated oils, no high fructose corn syrup, and no artificial colors.  Compare the label to the Bear shaped grahams treats and you'll see quite a difference.  Another great product from Annie's.

My children love these.  It's a shame that organic foods (well, all foods really) keep rising in price.  I can't afford to keep buying organic foods as I'd like to.  If you can afford them, these are a nice treat.

In my ongoing effort to provide healthy snacks to the children in my son's class (he goes to a public elementary school), I try various organic finger foods. These are a better deal than in the grocery stores.  They're great little graham cracker type cookies.
We like the fact that there is no real junk in these.  the kids love them for a snack.  We are glad that we can get them from Amazon at a reasonable price.

I am a fan of this brand, but was extremely disappointed when I tried the Bunny Graham Friends. I noticed immediately upon opening the brand new box that there was a strange odor. These bunny shaped graham snacks are really good. They are made from whole grain, are all natural, and are a good source of calcium - 20% RDA per serving. All three flavors in this pack, the honey, chocolate and chocolate chip, are delicious.

These Bunny Grahams taste terrible. I really hoped my kids would love them because they are organic, but I couldn't even eat them. We threw them all away. column9: Good, more of a meal than most TB Entrees

Item shipped fast. Taste delicious. This is the second that I bought Graroto here. Highly recommend this to those love Brazil chocolates.

column9: I hate mayo--if it isn't Dukes
column10: I don't like mayonnaise--or I thought I didn't. Other than a mere dab on a hardboiled egg, I have no use for the white, fluffy, oily stuff. I couldn't even bring myself to use it as a hair-repair pack on the recommendation of my hair stylist (you put it on like conditioner, wait an hour and wash it off. Avoid picnics, boiled potatoes, eggs and tomato sandwiches in the meantime.)But it turns out I actually really like mayonnaise as long as it's Dukes. This mayo is made from (they say) the same recipe as Mrs. Eugenia Duke created in 1917. This mayo has eggs, oil and vinegar but...no sugar. If you look at classical mayonnaise recipes, there is never sugar. Sugar is not a great addition to mayonnaise. Curry powder, paprika, mustard, tarragon are good additions. Sugar is not. When I took a test spoon of this mayo, having run out of my squeeze bottle of a national brand, I was amazed. First, this is what mayo tasted like when I was a kid, and second, this was actually so good I could eat it alone, which is damn dangerous as I don't need to be scooping mayo up with a teaspoon as an addition to my diet.The taste is tangy and somewhat perhaps more sour than you are used to. It works well on tomato sandwiches, deviled eggs, potato salad and anything requiring mayonnaise. I happen to like it as a small dab on a hardboiled egg, then sprinkled with curry for a quick breakfast.The squeeze bottle is nice until you get to the end, then it's a bit hard to get all of it to squirt out, so a knife is needed to get the rest. If this bothers you, use the plastic jars. But watch out for dipping in those dangerous spoons for a taste. This is a recipe for diet disaster.

I searched my whole city for a sugar free mayo because I didn't want to take the time to make my own.  I'm a type 2 diabetic trying my hardest to avoid sugar and every mayo in the store has sugar in it, as do 98% of all foods even meat! (one wonders why????) and then thinks no wonder our nation has an epidemic of obesity and diabetes. I was told that Duke's mayo was sugar free so I looked for it every where.  I finally found it at my World Market. I didn't care what it cost I wanted it. I must say it's delicious! I had heard about Duke's and I wondered how it could be so different. Let me tell you it is. As one other reviewer said, it's like the mayo we used to have years ago. But, everything tasted better in the 50's and 60's before hormones and antibiotics and genetic engineering of foods but I digress. I just wish I could get it locally in bigger jars. I use it for so many things as I make my own salad dressings, dips, appetizers, deviled eggs and an ingredient in baked goods. It's so versatile. If you want a good mayo with taste and flavor that's sugar free buy Duke's. You'll wonder why you ever bought another brand.

Shipping for this item came to over $24.  There was no way for me to check shipping cost before ordering, so if I had to do it again, I'd throw the money in my gas tank, drive a couple of states over, and buy it myself instead... especially when the delivery estimate for that outrageous shipping price is 1-3 weeks.Duke's is my all time favorite mayo, but not at 30 cents per ounce.

Ordered from Martha and have been very pleased with the bush. It came bare root in March just as it was beginning to bud out. Didn't do so hot here in Maryland in March. The buds died. However, the bush began growing again in April and flowered this year. Two of the flowers have since turned into pomegranates about the size of apricots. I don't know if they'll ripen or not by October (when it starts getting cold) but I was amazed it set fruit so soon. I've heard from professionals that pomegranates do not fair well in humidity (we have a ton). This bush seems to be an exception! We'll see.

column9: Bob's Red Mill Bulgur Red Wheat
column10: This is not only good for you, but it is great tasting and only takes a few minutes to cook.  I've used it in dishes as a rice substitude and it works great.

column9: Floored by the incredible price; love the freshness
column10: Seeing as how I use this as a ground beef stretcher (you can't tell the difference, really!) the price is a pleasant surprise.  The product itself is top-notch.  I've tried many different brands and Bob's Red Mill has the best texture and flavor by far.Here's how I use the product.  I put 1/2 cup of bulgur in a glass measuring cup and pour hot water on it to make it to the 1 1/4 cup mark.  I let it sit for about 10-15 minutes, then use it as a supplement to loose ground beef recipes such as taco filling or spaghetti.  Voila!  Not only are you eating healthier, you're saving money too.  As you cook, the bulgur will blend with the other ingredients and soak up additional sauce and flavors.By the way, I have tried using bulgur without meat as a meat substitute, and I found it just fine as a taco filler.  Bulgur really doesn't have much of a flavor though, so it should be used with strong accompanying ingredients.  In any case, you'll find that it is a great addition to your kitchen: easy to prepare and healthy to eat.
Great for tabouleh and made cracked wheat bread with it the other day.I hesitated about the volume I had to buy, but am using it often enough that it will not be a problem. An excellent product.

Trying to become a vegetarian and eventually a full vegan. Heart disease runs in the family and not interested in taking the statin drugs. One of the challenges is replacing one of my favorites - hamburgers and French fries. Making baked French fries that tasted like fried with the right spices was easy. Making vegie burgers that taste good has been a challenge. Bought several Amazon books on vegie burgers and this was an ingredient in many. This was another Bob's Red Mill product sourced via Amazon Prime, and as usual Bob's Red Mill stuff is of the highest quality.
I ordered these after reading about them on the Hungry Girl Web Site.  Both my husband and myself are enjoying the crunch and great flavor.  Will definitely order more.

column9: Deceptive!! Not what you think they are...
column10: I purchased these because they came up in the "organic" search on Amazon.  When I received them and read the ingredients, they use regular apples and organic cinnamon! Their product is crispy initially (I don't eat a bag at a time so they are stored in a zip-lock bag) but looses the crispiness within two days. NOW, the really bad part!! If an apple is not organic, it's been exposed to pesticides and other chemicals right?  The Funky Monkey Apple Crisps are made with the skin of the apple, frequently, with pieces that are skin only. GUESS WHERE ARE THE PESTICIDES ARE??? I am VERY disappointed in this product, there are certainly healthier options on the market. Organic buyer beware of what you feed your family!

These taste great and I really like the crunch they have. I expected them to be chewy so the crunchy texture was a nice surprise.My only complaint is the tiny package size as it's more a snack for a really small child and not an adult. The tiny package size is why I gave them 4 stars out of five.
these should really be called apple skins. all that was in any bag we tried were the dried apple peels. not appetizing, not tasty, just dry apple leftovers, that would be fed to a farm animal.

These have an excellent apple-cinamon flavor.  They are sweet and make a great crunchy-sweet but healthy snack for the kids.  The single packets are nice and easy to keep in the car/bag for "emergency" hunger sittuations.Some of the thicker pieces are VERY hard, and difficult for my 4 and 6 year old to bite through.  I wish they came with a few more in the pouch, but over all I would recomend as a healthy snack with a great flavor!

These are good. I like these almost as much the club crackers I love. They have a nice crunch & smooth flavor with the olive oil & sea salt. Great combination! I often put tuna or chicken on these. I also like them with spaghetti. And alot of other dishes. Or just by themselves. Fantastic cracker. Love them.
I don't know if it's the variety or a problem with the batch I got, but sprouting is only sporadic- I have a freshlife automatic sprouter and generally I get great results, but not with these.
These are the best!!  I buy these every year for a friend's diabetic husband and he just loves them!!!  Most sugar free is not worth eating, but he swears by these.  Give them a try!!
Not what I expected I didn't realize it was sugar free It did have good taste I thought IT was extremly hard

I was fooled by the pacakaging.  The box cover looks like they are fairly big pieces of cake with pineapple filling.  They're not.  They're cookies about 1.5 inches in length and 1/4 of an inch thick.The cookie is very tasty, a little crumbly though.  It taste kind of like cheesecake with a chewy strip (and I mean strip) of  filling (something else the package deceived me on).  They are actually reminiscent of those cookies with the bit of fruit in the center like Knotts Berry Farm's shortbread cookies.  The difference is the cookie is more buttery and instead of being in the middle of a flat cookie, it's a filling.  While you can taste the butter, in no way does it taste like pineapple.  I double checked with someonelse and they didn't get a hint of pineapple either.  The filling is secondary really especially since there's so little of it.They definitely weren't what I was expecting, but they're very good.  Since they're individually wrapped, they're easily transportable.edit 1 wk later: The filling isn't a strip in each cookie nor are all of them crumbly.  Either the manufacturing is inconsistent or my box had then end of one batch and the beginning of another.
I should've "listened" to the other reviews, and not buy this. This brand is tasteless; not fresh at all. Amazon should take this product off. What a waste of $!

column9: different brand shipped to me !!!! becareful !
column10: ordered these cakes, its a different brand from the photo description on this listing ! I'm not sure if they will do anything about this. We'll see and keep this review updated

column9: A Must Have for Perfect Gravy
column10: If you are like me and cannot abide by powdered or jar gravy, then this is what you must have!!!  THIS IS REAL GENUINE TURKEY STOCK!! I have used this product for a few years.  I usually add it and some water or broth (this is concentrated and like a gel) to the drippings I already have just to make the gravy I already have go much further, I can double or triple - I mean, everyone loves gravy and leftovers, too!  I have added small amounts when I am making turkey or chicken soups and it would probably work well in stuffing for the extra turkey flavor.  I also have the beef and ham since my family loves, loves, loves gravies.

column9: Quick and easy substitute for turkey stock
column10: I like this product. I use it when making Thanksgiving Gravy. What I typically do is add a couple tablespoons to store bought chicken stock while it's on the stove. I let it simmer along with my turkey neck, gizzards, onion celery and carrots. It helps to give the stock more of a turkey flavor as opposed to the chicken. The only drawback is that it is very salty!

It is what we have been looking for to use at Thanksgiving and other times when we have turkey but not quite enough gravy.  Gravy packets are too expensive and have a bunch of additives.  The Turkey base gives us the flavor we want and is just great.

Recipes for turkey gravy and leftovers often call for chicken base.  But chicken is NOT turkey!  This turkey base delivers an accurate flavor and is is excellent in gravies, soups and casseroles. Unfortunately it is not often available in grocery stores.

One star off for lying: get a clue folks: autolyzed yeast, hydrolyzed vegetable compound, are just other names for MSG.That said, this stuff is very useful. A handmade stock is not always needed. This stuff reconstitutes quickly.

I love passion fruit juice and this is a very good product. Each bottle makes about a gallon. It is low in sugar and low on glycemic index. Has a lot of potassium and is a natural relaxer. Makes great cocktails too if it isn't relaxing enough for you straight up! Fast delivery and great product!

I ordered this for review (provided by company) and thought it's shampoo, it's not a miracle.It's not a miracle product but it out performed my regular shampoo and I would say it worked as well as the product I bought at the saloon.It smells nice--not overwhelming.It suds well in hard water.My hair isn't heavy or greasy.I'll purchase more when I run out of it.

I've used this product several times now and it's leaving a weird texture in my hair. You don't need very much, and it's got a nice creamy consistency, but when you use it and dry your hair it's like a film is left behind. I didn't feel like this was a good product.

This shampoo lathers up really well, rinses easily, and left my hair feeling nice, shiny and clean.  My hair is curly and has sometimes frizzes in humid weather, but so far, all okay.My hair is colored treated so I will update review after several washings, but so far, I like what I see and feel.>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>As of today (May 28) still using this product and it keeps my color bright, my hair is not frizzy and I would recommend this shampoo.

I have highlighted hair but I don't consider it damaged.  I've tried this shampoo for 3 days and I like it.  The fragrance is wonderful.  The shampoo has a similar texture and slip to Matrix Sleek shampoo, which I like to use during warm, humid weather for de-frizzing.  I didn't notice any unnecessary weight on my hair, which sometimes happens with shampoos that claim to be for damaged hair.  I would buy this shampoo.

I think this shampoo is really good. I like the smell and the way it leaves my hair feeling. I spend a lot of time outside and have my hair colored often and I don't always use conditioner with this brand of shampoo. I sometimes put some on the ends, but that's been about it. Now if Amazon could just get the packing down....

Shampoos are tricky for my hair.  It's a bit more coarse, and has a bit of a curl to it, but after using this shampoo for a short time I've found that my hair has more shine and is easier to style than with my previous shampoo which I paid more for.I do color my hair, but I can't really comment on how well it protects against fading since my color was a bit faded prior to using this shampoo, but if the product lives up to this claim like it does the others than I am sure it will do an admiral job.For the price I LOVE this shampoo.  I love the way it smells (not to fruity or flowery, just a nice scent) I love that my scalp is less irritated, and I like my hair more while using it (something that is hard to do).  My only wish was that it was sulfate free, but at this price I think I will be switching to this shampoo from now on!

If you have color treated your hair and/or your scalp needs more moisture, then this shampoo is for you.  Your hair will feel fresher, shinier and will have more slide and glide when you style it.  It is very gentle and does not leave your hair feeling rough or traumatized when you wash it.  The product lives up to its claim of nourishing your scalp as it is power packed with vitamins and other natural products.  It also has a very pleasant aroma.

Ok this stuff does magic i have been struggling for a hair product that would help my nasty hair and i have finally found it!! And for people that are to lazy to go to a drug store and purchase this so they can have a full bottle come on really why would you purchase this from the internet really people!! I got mine personally at wal mart and didn't have any accidents with it!! the smell is great i don't understand peoples opinion that is to strong of a smell me personally i love when i greet people with huggs n they complimant the smell on my hair :) grow up people!! Nothing in life is perfect!!

I am really impressed with the new line of shampoos and conditioners from Clear Scalp.  This shampoo leaves my hair feeling clean and wonderfully soft.  It doesn't weigh my hair down or increase the number of tangles. It has a pleasant faint apple scent and you don't need to use very much to get a nice lather.  I have tried many different shampoos, including expensive salon brands, on my color treated long fine hair, and this is one of the best ones I have tried.  Combined with the Damage & Color Repair conditioner, this left my hair feeling soft and healthy.  I really recommend this shampoo for anyone with color treated hair.

I like my regular shampoo better.  I didn't see anything special this shampoo did, no glowing or silkiness.  I guess it is just okay.  I wouldn't buy it.  Soybean product in shampoo?  I don't like the idea of soybeans in my shampoo.  Maybe that's why the hair didn't glow or was silky.  This shampoo might be good for some, but not for me.  Oh, it's usable if you don't have anything else, but I wouldn't buy it.  It could have gotten 3 stars, but the soybeans brought it down to one.

I tried this shampoo (paired with the strength conditioner) for about a week and I had to get rid of it.  Here is why:1. It is meant to make your scalp healthy, yet it gave me an itchy, flaky scalp.2. The smell is so fake perfumy.  It smells like really cheap shampoo.3. I thought perhaps it would be a more environmentally/animal-friendly version of their company (Unilever) kindof like how L'Oreal has the line Everpure, and sadly, it isn't.  According to the website (clearhair.com) It uses stearic acid (from cows) and it doesn't have a no-animal testing policy.  It is hard to call the product "Clear" when it has so many icky ingredients.Big thumbs down.

This is a good shampoo with a pleasant, apple-y scent. I don't think a shampoo that claims to be for "color repair" should contain sodium laureth sulfate -- I'd rather have less lather and have my color last longer. That said, the lather is generous, and the shampoo left my hair feeling clean and not stripped of moisture.I ordered three shampoo/conditioner products from Amazon, and all three leaked during shipping. They were wrapped in plastic, so it wasn't a huge mess, but it would be nice if Amazon could find a way to ship shampoo without it leaking.I don't think this shampoo is anything special, and probably not worth paying extra for.

column4: Cathe Fein Olson "Avid reader and writer"
column10: I cannot review how well this shampoo works on the hair as it arrived in the mail with all of the shampoo leaked into the mailing envelope. I will say that if you are sensitive to products with strong fragrances like I am, this is not a good choice. It is heavily scented. I also don't recommend ordering this product through the mail as the pop top popped open and there was not packaging or shrink wrap to secure it shut.

I love the scent of this product. That's the good news. The only good news.But in my old age, I have developed a horrible itchy reaction to certain hair products, namely WEN, which gave me an awful rash on my hairline (front and back) as well as my entire neck. So when I saw this product, I thought it would be a relief now that my itchy WEN rash is finally (after SIX months of healing) a thing of the past.Sad to say that I was wrong. I used Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty conditioner and shampoo  three times in a row and guess what happened?  Yup. Same sort of irritation and itching in all of the same places.There must be a very specific ingredient the makers of hair products are including in their respective cleansers and conditioners because the fact that this has happened AGAIN literally has me scratching my head in disbelief.Again, this shampoo (and its companion conditioner) has a lovely scent - but I will not spend my waking and sleeping hours scratching myself like a cat with fleas.  If you have any sensitivity to hair products, avoid this one.Boo. So goes this product the way of WEN. In the trash.

After finally caving into the commercials and all the rave reviews I finally caved in and bought this shampoo and conditioner, the one labeled Damage and Color Repair, it's been a month now and I just finished the bottles and I'm not at all impressed, in fact I'm disappointed and almost angry. I have fine dry hair that I color once a month, now this shampoo, wow, it strips the color right out of my hair because of all the sulfates in it. I've NEVER seen a shampoo do this to my hair before. Because of this my color faded terribly and I had to recolor my hair. The shampoo also dried my already dry hair out even MORE and caused more shedding.Problem two, the conditioner, I felt like I couldn't rinse it out, I didn't use a lot, maybe a tiny little dime sized and still when I dried my hair it felt like there was still a weird sticky film in my hair that weighed my hair down, leaving my hair with no life, no shine, nothing.2 stars for it being pleasant smelling and having a good bottle design.

column4: Reader2008 "I write honest reviews; if you do...
column9: My beautician asked me why my hair was shedding so much! I ended up with a bald spot!
column10: My review below is very detailed, but if you are having issues with your hair because of this shampoo your FIRST step is to get it out of your hair.  Wash your hair with a moisturizing shampoo, follow with a moisturizing conditioner, and then use Apple Cider Vinegar or another vinegar to strip this shampoo and reminents out of your hair.  THEN do a hot oil treatment.  After the hot oil treatment wash and condition again and your hair should stop shedding.=============================My review:I don't know if this shampoo is damaging my hair, but I noticed that I can just touch my hair after using this shampoo and it sheds. My hair sheds a lot anyway so I definitely would not use a shampoo that causes it to shed even more. The shampoo smells good and is creamy.From reading the other reviews, apparently YOU HAVE TO USE the conditioner or you will mess up your hair.  I would NEVER use a shampoo that strips the hair just so you can use a special conditioner to re-soften it.UPdate: I am downgrading to a ONE (1*).  I have NEVER had a bald spot in my life.  It has been 3 weeks now and my hair feels like straw (in spite of several deep conditionings at home and the salon).  Today, I look in the mirror and I now have a bald spot (IN THE FRONT OF MY HEAD) from all the breakage and shedding.  It is CLEAR this shampoo has a protein in it which is a NO-NO for damaged hair UNLESS you use a certain type of conditioner to bring back the softness.Once I discovered the bald spot, I began to panic and I went and bought the CLEAR conditioner trying to get the dryness to leave and it still didn't leave.  I am sitting here now with my regular conditioner trying to get the softness back.  I am afraid it will not come back and I will have to wait for my hair to grow out.  This shampoo is HORRIBLE.Update #2: This is all I had to do to stop my hair from falling out.  I had to do a clarifier.  First, I used a mixture of baking soda and water.  This soften the hair immediately, but the shedding didn't stop so I slept in a plastic cap with an oil [I used mustard oil, but any oil likely will do]).  I woke up this morning and the hair was definitely in better condition.  I then went to my refrigerator and used Apple Cidar Vinegar, more oil, and my Creme of Nature Shampoo and Conditioner.  The hair is FINALLY back to its original condition (except for the bald spot).

column9: Very good shampoo if you can handle the strong synthetic fragrance
column10: Fragrance: EXTREMELY strong, synthetic smelling fragrance.  I used the product once to give a fair review and the scent made me ill.  If you aren't sensitive to strong and/or synthetic scents it's probably going to just smell like shampoo to you.Cleaning:  Cleaned hair very well, lathered richly, rinsed easily.Conditioning:  I normally use a conditioner but did not need to after using this shampoo.  Huge bonus points for that.Safe for color treated hair:  The product contains sodium laureth sulfate which is considered to be easier on colored hair than many of the other sulfates.  In an ideal world there would be an affordable, sulfate-free, effective shampoo--but we don't live in that world--yet.Overall:  This is a good product but I will continue my search for a color safe shampoo that has no sulfates and actually cleans your hair and leaves it in a somewhat manageable condition.

I have dyed my hair for years and am always trying different shampoos. My hair is straight and on the fine side and I wash it every day. I liked this shampoo. It lathers well (even in our hard water) and left my hair feeling nice. I didn't need any conditioner and it didn't dry out my hair or weigh it down.I think it has a strong scent - not totally unpleasant, but if you're sensitive to scents, it may bother you.I do wish Amazon didn't ship this in a padded envelope. Somehow the shampoo bottle opened and while the bottle was wrapped in plastic, I lost about 1/3 of the shampoo. Shipping this in a box would have prevented this problem.

column9: I had an allergic reaction to this shampoo
column10: I purchased this shampoo about 2 weeks ago, and used it for the first time last weekend.  After using it in the shower, I noticed that my forehead and temples were blotchy red, clearly an allergic reaction.  I put cortisone on the blotches and took two benadryl tablets and the blotches subsided after a few hours.  In order to determine whether or not it was indeed this shampoo that caused the reaction (and not some other product or a random food allergy), I used the shampoo in the shower again this morning.  While I was rinsing it, my face and neck began to itch, and when I got out of the shower and looked in the mirror, the blotchiness had returned.I don't usually have particularly sensitive skin, but do have various allergies in my immediate family - two brothers are allergic to latex, one of my sons is peanut-allergic, and another son is allergic to cats and dogs.  I checked the label of the product, and noticed that it contained almond oil and soy, which is not a problem for me, but might be a problem for someone allergic to those foods (yes, I know you don't EAT the shampoo, but sometimes people with food allergies react to it when it comes into contact with their skin).I called the 800 number on the bottle to report the allergic reaction, and they were very nice about it - a representative took my info, and another person called me back a few hours later.  They asked me to return the unused product and they are going to send me a refund and coupons for alternate products.I am giving this product 3 stars based on the fact that my hair looked clean after use, and the customer service people were pleasant.  Obviously I'm not going to purchase it again though.

First of all, this review is for the shampoo only (the colored/damaged hair version). I purchased this because I read an article in a magazine that said that normal shampoos/shampooing doesn't clear the hair follicles of dead skin cells and sebum, clogging them and making it more challenging for hair to grown long and strong. I have long, naturally curly blonde hair that I color dark brown and straighten daily. It is about 6 inches past my clavicle, and I have been trying to grow it past my breasts, ala Kim Kardashian, for what seems like years. I had beautiful long hair as a teen, but since being in my adult years, just can't seem to get past this length where it ends right around my underarms.I have been using this shampoo for a little over a week (probably around 10 days) and can honestly say I am VERY impressed. I am someone who has always believed that shampoo doesn't really matter in comparison to a good, rich conditioner. Well, I was wrong. I massage this shampoo into my roots in a circular motion with my fingertips, being sure to reach all of my scalps, and taking around 2-3 minutes to do my whole head before rinsing. I am using my usual conditioner (Tresseme Soft and Silky), which I always use. My hair feels incredibly soft and shiny, and actually appears to be stronger as I don't have as many stray hairs all over my bathroom after styling. My root area has more volume than usual and my hair just feels cleaner overall than normal.The next test is to see if it starts to accelerate in growth, which will probably not be visible for a little while. Meanwhile, I am going to switch to the Clear conditioner too once my Treseme is gone. This will be the first shampoo that I ever re-purchase out of loyalty. As for the scent, it is fine...not too floral or strong. It really just has that typical "clean shampoo" smell. My boyfriend likes it, which is great because he only seems to like very clean scents. However, if you are particularly sensitive to heavy scents, you may want to steer clear of this as it is definitely perfumed.Another nice thing I noted is that Sodium Lauryl Sulfate is listed fairly towards the end of the ingredient list, unlike most shampoos that list it right after water (like the V05 I usually use).Overall, I am happy with this product and will continue to use it. I am also going to monitor my hair growth to see if this will help my healing my scalp.**update**I finished my bottle today, roughly 30 days after I wrote this review and noticed that my hair does seem longer by about an inch. Obviously I cant be 100% sure since I didn't measure it before starting to use this shampoo, but if I noticed it that alone is a big deal as my hair grows very slowly. I will definitely re-purchase!

column9: Can't be used on it's own! Buy the conditioner, too!
column10: The first time I used the shampoo, my hair felt like it was made out of straw. It literally stripped my hair of all moisture. Reading the bottle, it requires the conditioner to make it a complete package. At first I didn't want to try the two because I was worried it would make my hair worse, but finally I gave in and selected the conditioner as well. I'm very happy that I did! Using the shampoo and conditioner exclusively, I have to say my hair is definitely shinier, softer and healthier than before. I love the pleasing scent of the shampoo and conditioner. Neither are overwhelming. I don't know that I will switch to this shampoo and conditioner exclusively when I run out, but the price and free shipping (with Amazon Prime) certainly makes it appealing. I awarded it three stars because it requires both the shampoo and conditioner to get great results. I like more freedom in selecting my hair care products.

column9: Not as appealing as their Ultra Shea shampoo...
column10: I ordered this to alternate with the Clear Ultra Shea shampoo, which, for a sulfate containing shampoo, I actually like. This Damage and Color Repair version has a very strong frangrance in comparison with the Ultra Shea, and for an alleged restorative shampoo, seems pretty drying to my color treated hair. This requires extra time with a conditioner, which is not the case with the Ultra Shea. The product was not a home run for me, and I will likely not purchase it in the future.

I received this item free for review.  I've got shoulder-length curly, frizzy hair.  Color is put on my roots every 3-4 weeks.  When I ordered this, I just hoped for the best regarding healthier hair.  The temps and humidity have been brutal this summer and I have seen some days since using this where my hair wasn't as frizzy.  Is that due to the shampoo and/or the conditioner?  Hard to determine.  Yesterday it was pretty frizzy again.Been using the product for about 2 weeks now.  Something I did notice a couple of days ago, was that there wasn't as much hair on the floor of the shower as I've been seeing for the past couple of years.  Wow, I wasn't expecting that.  It makes sense since this product is supposed to make your scalp healthier.  But slowing down hair loss is not listed as a selling point.The shampoo itself has a silky feel and a light pleasant scent and my hair feels good when getting out of the shower.  Both the shampoo and conditioner can be stood with the opening down, making it quicker to dispense.Two things I need to mention.  The first is that the item came well-wrapped in plastic, and it's a good thing it was.  There was some leakage during shipment.  Not a lot, but it would have messed up everything else in the box.  Probably better to purchase this from a brick and mortar store to avoid possible loss of product.The second is that in order to see a list of ingredients, you are told to pull up part of the label.  What???  Can you see doing this in a store?  Would you purchase one that already had part of the label pulled back?  I think a redesign is in order.On the whole I'm happy with using the product.Amending my review.  I've been using the product for over a month and I'm torn as to what I think of it.  I am definitely experiencing a lot less hair loss since using it, which is a HUGE plus.  However, my hair doesn't look and feel nearly as good and the color is being stripped out of it with each washing.  I think I'm going to have to stop using it.  I've downgraded the rating from a 4 to a 3.

Ironically, my scalp was dry and flakey...no clue why...just as the advertisements for this product started to appear.  Huh...well, decided give it a shot...other dry scalp shampoos, don't have companion conditioners and quite frankly are good tools if you want to remove hair coloring from your hair!  Nothing strips it like dandruff shampoos!  But this not only in two shampoos, relieved my itchy dry scalp, it left my hair nice...and has been much gentler on my OTC hair color.  I like the scent.  With the shampoo...a little goes a long way.  Nice rich suds that rinse easily.  I use both the shampoo and conditioner.  Will continue to do so.

The Good Stuff:The container is nice, dispenses well. The color is pale lavender. Whatever.The product itself is very creamy and light and has a whitish color before you apply it to your hair. It then lathers very well, especially in soft water. I had a 2-day dirty head so this worked very well on my hair and cleansed it without stripping it or making it feel dry.I dried and styled my hair like always yet it was more manageable than normal and did not have any frizz or "stick out" hairs. I liked that part.Here's the Bad Stuff:Woah, that is some flowery, perfume-y, strong scent! I rinsed my hair extremely well (hoping most of that scent would leave) and it still smelled VERY strong, after towel and blow drying it. This might be OK for some ladies, but this particular guy does not appreciate smelling like he just wallowed in the perfume display at Nordstrom.As well, there seems to be a slight residue after a few hours, especially the next morning. (And I had to throw my pillowcase in the laundry, it smelled just as strong.)All in all, not a bad product for your hair per se, but it's one that consumers should probably not buy unless they love smelling like a giant room freshening wick.+4 stars for what it did to my hair, -1 star for what it did to my nose.

column9: Five Star Container For An Average Shampoo...
column10: "Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Damage & Color Repair Nourishing Shampoo" is an average shampoo packaged in a 5-star container.  The shampoo is lightly scented; the fragrance is very pleasant.  A tablespoon of the shampoo does a nice job of cleaning one's hair.However, while "Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Damage & Color Repair Nourishing Shampoo" is labeled as specifically formulated for hair that has been "color refreshed," it strips the color from hair much more than other similar products.  The suds, following shampooing, are very tinted by my semi-permanent hair color.  If I shampoo daily as is my custom, I foresee this shampoo "stripping" the color and revealing the grays in two weeks or less.  As I only recolor every four weeks, this is not acceptable."Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Damage & Color Repair Nourishing Shampoo" is packaged in a uniquely shaped container.  It fits nicely in one's hand; is easy to hold, even with wet hands; and is easy to control with respect to dispensing the shampoo.  I plan on saving the container and refilling when the "Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Damage & Color Repair Nourishing Shampoo" is gone."Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Damage & Color Repair Nourishing Shampoo" is an average shampoo in a 5-star container.  If you recolor more frequently than I do or use permanent color, you will find the product performs adequately.  Overall, it rates only 3 stars.

So a little background. My hair started turning gray early and I have to color it every 6 weeks. All that color has changed my scalp and hair texture. My scalp is now oily. I don't wash it for 3 or 4 days and I look like I put cooking oil in it. But the ends feel like straw. I went and bought Shampoo and Conditioner from a salon and figured I would need to buy the expensive stuff from now on. I saw this and was instantly interested because it talked about healing the scalp where all the problems come from. After using almost a whole bottle of this I feel like I can give it a thorough review. I have discovered you don't need as much, it covers and lathers well with a quarter size.I love the smell! Very light sweet and refreshing. My hair is not as oily as before and I don't have the straw feeling in the ends when I use the conditioner too. I am impressed and that is not an easy thing to do when it comes to hair care.

but nothing to jump up and down about.  As the other reviewers stated, it smells very nicely.  Interestingly enough, the scent does not fade in my hair.  At different times, when I swished my head, I caught whiffs of it.  It would not be a problem but it competed with my cologne in a horrible way.It cleans as promised but as someone who colors their hair, sulfates in a shampoo are not good and will wash your color out after a few washings.I gave it to my niece who doesn't color her hair and likes fruity scents.

column9: One of the worst I have ever used
column10: I typically purchase Aveeno shampoo and conditioner, but saw a commercial for Clear and decided to give it a try. What a horrible mistake!  I used the Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Damage and Color repair Shampoo and Conditioner together. I have shoulder length, thin, straight hair which I color every few months and blow dry every day.  The damage and color repair seemed like the best fit for me.The smell during use was okay, but it leaves a terrible chemical cloud around my head all day and even left the same smell on my pillow. This is not a fragrance it left-- it's chemicals.  My scalp started burning not long after use and it left my hair dry, dull, and frizzy.I cannot remember the last time I used such a terrible beauty product and cannot wait to wash this out of my hair!*The only redeeming quality of this product was the bottle design.  I do really like the way it opens and closes.

I hd ordered the men's dandruff shampoo in this same brand.  It worked super well so I decided to try this one for my thin ageing hair.  When I use conditioner it just plasters my hair down because it's so thin.  This shampoo works great.  My hair is clean but not stripped.  No conditioner is needed.  Shiney and straight it has never looked better.  I highly recommend this shampoo.

I like having 3-4 different shampoo and conditioners on the go,  so when I was offered this on Amazon vine,  even though I didn't know the brand,  I thought,  what the hey,  and ordered it.  I received a shampoo and conditioner that were the same brand but not identical titles. One thing I didn't like straight away was that it wasn't blatantly clear which was the shampoo and which was the conditioner,  I like to know without squinting at the bottles.I used the shampoo and my hair felt heavy and dull and greasy.  It was a weirdly humid day so I thought I would give it another chance,  and this time used it without the same brand conditioner,  but it still gave me limp hair,  and certainly  my hair was not shinier or did the color come out more...  It actually made my hair look sad and I won't use it again.

I decided to try this shampoo as I regularly hi-light my hair.  To start, I'm a little skeptical over any shampoo that claims to be for damaged or color treated hair but isn't sulfate-free.  Regardless.... I like my shampoo to lather and I have found that when I actually use sulfate-free shampoo I don't notice any difference in the life of my hi-lights, and I end up wasting it because I keep trying to get it to lather by putting more and more in my hair (to no avail).Regarding this shampoo - I liked it and I'll buy it again.  The shampoo has a pleasant smell - it's not too strong as others have noted.  And once you rinse it out, it's about the same as any other shampoo.  I almost wish it had a stronger smell as I enjoy the smell of clean/fresh hair.  It didn't do anything mind-blowing-ly awesome to my hair, but it was nice.  A rich lather, a pleasant smell, and I will note - blow drying my hair was fast and less frizzy than normal.  I've noticed with the use of some other shampoos claiming to be for damaged hair, it takes me longer to blow dry my hair, which in turn, causes it to get frizzier.  Not with this shampoo - blow drying was fast, and for the most part, my hair has remained pretty flat all day (and I live in South Florida - so I know a thing or two about humidity).Overall, a good product that I would use again and recommend.  I can't give it 5 stars, simply for the fact that it claims to be for color-treated/damaged hair, yet contains sulfates.

I ordered this product because my hair is extremely damaged from hair coloring, and have been looking for a shampoo for color treated hair that didn't have a conditioner in it. My hair is extremely fine and thin, and conditioner weighs it down horribly. I also assumed that a new shampoo for color treated hair would be sulfate free, since sulfates are supposed to strip color from treated hair. The name 'Clear' carries connotations of purity to my mind.Sadly, the shampoo is not sulfate free- it's the second item on the list. So while it might be making my hair feel and look better temporarily, it's not going to help the color stay in. Which means more color damage as I have to frequently recolor... Also, the shampoo contains silicons. Now, silicons are much, much better for thin hair than oils are, but it's still a conditioner that can weigh thin, fine hair down.I've been using the shampoo daily for just over a week now. I can say that my hair is shinier after washing and drying, and a little easier to comb tangles out of. But the silicon does weigh my hair down a bit - not nearly as much as other shampoos for color treated hair do! - and I've noticed it collecting dust. I use a white comb, so I can readily see if there is dirt in my hair at the end of the day. Of course, I work in a very dusty/dirty atmosphere a lot of days, so YMMV.My decision in the end? This is a decent shampoo, and will probably use it a couple of times a week. But I want something without any conditioner/silicon for the rest of the time. Someone who has thicker hair will probably love this shampoo! I had my husband try it (his hair isn't damaged, or as limp as mine) and he thought it was really nice.Just one thing- I was a little confused when something named 'Clear' came out of the bottle as a creamy, opaque liquid. I rechecked the bottle to make sure I hadn't accidentally gotten conditioner!

column9: Works with my Hard Well Water + Highlighted Hair
column10: I have long hair that is fine in texture and lots of it. I have my hair foil-wrapped (highlighted) about every 6-7 weeks or so. I live in a rural area and have somewhat hard well water.I don't really have any problems with my scalp like dandruff but because I have sort of hard well water, sometimes when I use certain moisturizing shampoos, due to all the "gunk" in them, they'll cause my scalp to itch and very occasionally will cause bumps like they are "plugging up" my folicles or something. In addition, after a few uses, some moisturizing shampoos leave my hair limp and lifeless.I can usually tell within a couple of uses or so whether or not the shampoo is going to work for me. I'm happy to say this shampoo works for me. After a few uses, my scalp felt fine - no itching or bumps - and my hair was soft without being weighed down.Also, I love the bottle this shampoo comes in. You might not be able to tell my the picture but rather than being a round bottle, it's quite oval shaped and to dispense the shampoo, you press down on one end of the top and it clicks down raising up the opposite edge that has the hole in it where the shampoo will come out.The oval shape makes this bottle much easier to keep ahold of than some of the bigger round bottles. One of the times I was using this shampoo, I didn't get quite enough shampoo to totally cover my hair and had to dispense more and even though my hands were soapy, I was able to grab the bottle with one hand, click it open, turn it upside down and dispense more shampoo into the palm of my opposite hand and then close the bottle up again and replace it on my shower shelf. All of that one handed and with soapy hands and I didn't drop it and it never felt like it was too slippery to keep ahold of.The shampoo itself is a creamy light pink color and fairly thick. Make sure your hair is extremely wet when applying so you can disperse it more easily through your hair.The only downside to this shampoo is the scent. To me it was a cross between ever-so-slightly chemically and sort of like the smell in the vitamin aisle of a healthfood store. It's wasn't absolutely hideous but just not my favorite and thankfully it dissipated quite a bit after my hair was dried and styled.I give this 4.75 stars. I like this enough that I would buy more in the future.Sincere THANKS to Amazon and the manufacturer/distributor who gave me the opportunity to give this product a try.

I loved (LOVED!) the Clear conditioner and had very high hopes for the shampoo. Perhaps too high. Because while I'm happy to report that it left my hair and scalp feeling fresh and clean -- which is, after all, what a shampoo is supposed to do -- it didn't leave my hair exponentially softer, the way Clear conditioner did.

I gave this to a woman in my life who is a lifelong salon shampoo and conditioner user and she said she really noticed a difference in the texture of her hair afterwords. The split ends were helped considerably. Being an older woman who has had her her colored many many times this was a shampoo that was surprisingly helpful despite its price. What was most noticeable to me was that her hair seemed to have more sheen than before using the product. Now I myself can't say I've used it, but for a woman that's had many hair treatments she has a pretty good estimation of how well these types of products work. I'd recommend at least sampling if you have damage from color treatments.

I got this item to see if it works even better with the Clear conditioner. I couldn't tell that much difference, but I really like both products and they make my hair very soft with a good smell. Again, I have curly hair which I color so when I find a new product that works well, it's a good day! I just wish all the hair products weren't so expensive. I recommend this product because if it works well on my hair, chances are it will on yours.

Well this shampoo is great.  First, it smells really nice without being overly perfumed.  Second, it lathers very well in my very thick hair.  Third, it cleans my very oily hair without overdrying.  Lastly, it leaves my hair looking very silky.  I have noticed a slight improvement in my dermatitis so that is an added benefit.  I got this bottle for free but I will buy one when it runs out.  And lest you wonder why I knocked off a star...it is because I am not a big fan of the spout and shape of the bottle.  It is a little akward to open and squeeze.

This shampoo does the job. It lathers well, smells pleasant, and seems to work fine. After lathering, the shampoo rinses out well and my hair feels squeaky clean. You don't have to use much shampoo...a little goes a long way. I really can't find any superlative things to say about it, it does the job without any problems. I will say that I have an issue with telling which is the shampoo and which is the conditioner because the bottles are almost identical and I always forget which is which.I can't really tell if there is a benefit to using this on my colored hair or not. Everything seems fine with this shampoo, nothing stands out as being wonderful or awful. I did not have any leakage like other reviewers have reported with the shipping of this product. The cost is reasonable, that might be the best thing about this product.

There is a bit of a problem with these shampoo bottles that only really applies for shipping; the new pop top. I actually like the way the bottle opens during use - it's a vast improvement over smaller flip tops that are difficult to open with wet hands or those horrid little spout type bottles. Unfortunately, they don't ship well and arrived as a big mess. Fortunately, Amazon wrapped these in plastic which contained most of the mess but still about 1/4 of the bottle was gone.Now, aside from that, I'm not a big fan of the fragrance which seems quite strong...however, my better half loves the smell of this entire line of products. As for the function, with summer in Florida and very long hair, I have sun damage especially near the ends and this does seem to help keep the friz and breakage down. Hair is smooth although perhaps just a bit heavier feeling than I'd normally like.All in all, a nice product but open pop tops - despite the convenience when in use - leave something to be desired during extended shipping.

column9: Has a nice scent to it
column10: This product left my hair soft and shiny without being too limp or greasy looking. It has a really nice smell to it as well. It also helps with dandruff, so if you have hard water, then this would be a great product for your hair. I like this product, I would definitely buy it. I would next like to try the matching conditioner.
