This shampoo has a nice scent and leaves my hair feeling very soft and smooth.I didn't find the scent to be too strong at all. The price is comparable to other brands so I will probable buy this again (although I don't recommend buying through the mail).

column9: Not as good as the CLEAR conditioner
column10: I love the CLEAR Conditioner and even though I received a bottle of it for review, I'll keep buying it.  The difference in my hair is amazing and though I complained that I'm getting weird little tangles at my hairline, it dawned on me that that's because the product is so good.  Duh!So, since I'd used the CLEAR conditioner with my regular shampoo and getting fabulous results, I was expecting great things from the CLEAR shampoo.  Alas, I've been using for about a month now and have come to the reluctant conclusion that it's merely average.  It smells wonderful and gets my hair clean, but it's not making any more difference in my hair than just using the conditioner.If you like your grooming products in matched sets, then by all means purchase away, but there's really no need.  It's possible to get the CLEAR results from the conditioner alone.

The Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Damage & Color Repair Nourishing Shampoo smells absolutely incredible!  That's what makes it 2 stars and not lower.  I have used this shampoo about 5 or 6 times and even tried different conditioners with it.  However, each time, I had trouble combing the conditioner through my hair.  Also, my scalp itched slightly after using it.  I've used one of Clear's conditioners before, and it didn't get me an itchy scalp, so there must be a different ingredient in this shampoo that my body does not like.  Once again, the smell of the shampoo is absolutely incredible -- very clean, fresh, and great; but it doesn't make up for the tangly hair and bothered scalp.

Let me share the positive first.This is a fine shampoo. I can't say I saw anything very special about it's shampooing ability, all the promised scalp and hair benefit, but I saw no negatives either. Just does a nice jobI think it has a pleasant smell, not too strong in my opinion.And it has a nice consistency, although the lavender color is a little strange and unnecessary.But back to that container.In use it is nice, wide, easy to use tilt top.But once again (I reviewed a different variety of this brand before) the bottle leaked in transit.Certainly a problem if you plan to buy it online. This time the top was wrapped in plastic, but it still came partially open and leaked. I guess the same factors that make it easy to use in a wet shower make it too easy to open in an Amazon box in shipping.

Okay, so I'll be the first to admit that I'm not super picky about the kind of Shampoo I use. I've been using K-PAK by Joico, but was running low. So when I saw this in the vine program I ordered it. I like the scent, and it doesn't seem to dry out my hair or scalp, so all's good.

This shampoo lathers thick and rich.  A relatively small amount made a huge amount of lather.  It's quite creamy, and it left my hair feeling quite nice and soft, not stripped.  My hair is long and thick, with a tendency towards dry ends.  This shampoo worked very well on it, and it smells fine.  The scent is not very strong, and not offensive.  The scent is not amazing, but certainly satisfactory.
nice shampoo. does a nice job in repairing and nourishing the hair.  I found it very easy on my hair. Lathered well, and rinsed out well--leaving no residual on my hair. Nice smell as well.

column9: Is it really any different than other shampoo?
column10: I was unsure what to make of this new hair care line.  All of the basic ingredients are the same as my other shampoos for color-treated hair.  Also, my understanding of basic health science regarding healthy hair & scalp left me skeptical that the Clear shampoo or conditioner would be much different than any other.Many people rely on hair care products to give them healthy hair, but forget that the food you eat and the shampooing technique used are far more important.  To properly shampoo hair, use the pads of your fingers, stimulate the scalp in rows of circular motions, for at least 30 seconds.  This increases nutrient-rich bloodflow to the scalp to encourage healthy hair growth, as well as adequately exfoliate the scalp.----------------Despite my initial misgivings that this line was all hype, I still gave both the shampoo and conditioner a try.The shampoo lathered up better than the other shampoo I had been using, so I ended up needing less of it.It rinsed away smoothly, leaving my hair feeling strong.  My other shampoo left my hair feeling a bit rough and tangled, and I had always thought this was just how colored hair felt.I see sunflower, soybean, almond & coconut oils, as well as aloe vera, further down on the Clear ingredient list.  While my other shampoo contains some fruit extracts and grape seed oil, it does not contain the soothing ingredients found in the Clear product.  I do think this must be part of the difference between the two that I've experienced.I don't have fragrance sensitivities, but I don't like when it is overwhelming.  I found the fragrance to be pleasant, to me it smells like apples.The lid design presses open with a lever-like motion, which is much easier to operate with wet hands than a flip-open cap.The assymetrical design of the bottle is interesting to look at, but is a huge pain when the wider part is put away facing down (such as when the contents are running low).  I use an over-the-shower-head wire rack for my products, and the awkward shape of this lid kept getting stuck under and around other bottles when I would try to pull it out, pulling other products out with it.----------------Keep in mind that shampoo is more for the scalp area of the hair, while conditioner is for the ends.  This works well for this product line's image when it comes to the shampoos, but not for the conditioners.  I also tried the Damage & Color Repair Conditioner, and the directions instruct the user to massage it into the scalp.  This is awful, resulting in greasy hair.  So be warned, if you use the conditioner as well, just use it like regular conditioner, combed through the ends of your hair, and keep it away from your scalp.  When used this way, it is nice conditioner.----------------Overall, I was pleased with the results of using the Clear shampoo and conditioner.  My hair looks nice, seems less stressed, more shiny, and styles well.

Since I color my hair, fading between treatments can become an issue, especially in the summer when I'm outside more often. I was excited about trying this product because I hoped it would slow the fading process. Unfortunately, that didn't happen. It could be that I'm looking for a miracle since probably the only thing that would keep hair well conditioned and glossy is to stick with one's natural color. On the plus side, the shampoo is pretty, pink, creamy, and scented (like strawberries).

column9: A Good Value, but Not Good for Color Preservation
column10: The Clear Scalp Damage & Color Repair shampoo is a reasonably good product: it has helped to minimize split ends during use. However, after spending a small fortune on coloring, I'm loathe to use this product: it contains sodium laureth sulfate, which can fade color more rapidly than shampoos without it.The fragrance is almost like a citrus, but a bit too cloying for my preference. The scent doesn't really linger after washing, though, which is good.The major drawback is actually a functional design. The bottle's closure and cap doesn't avoid inadvertent opening and leaking. The product arrived, having opened during shipment, and had spilled all over the inside of the shipping box. This meant a loss of about 1/4-1/3 of the shampoo; had there been other items in the box, they would've been destroyed. A similar issue was encountered when packing it in luggage for a trip.

column9: Smells great, but my hair didn't feel clean
column10: Perhaps I have really odd hair texture, but unlike others who have reviewed here, my hair didn't feel clean after using the shampoo. I have very fine, straight as a board hair, that has been colored with a semi-permanent color to hide the grey. It can get dry, but not overly so. I liked the smell of the shampoo., and it lathered up nicely. But after I rinsed, my hair felt greasy, as if I hadn't used shampoo at all. My scalp also felt itchy afterward. Unfortunately I think I'm going to have to keep looking for a shampoo that works for me.

column4: K. Hernandez "DailyReadz - One Great Book Eve...
column10: My hair is dry and damaged from years of coloring and blow-drying, and this shampoo makes it feel soft and silky. And it smells so great, and leaves my hair smelling good for hours afterwards. I love it!!!

column9: Shampoo and conditioner work well together.
column10: I had seen the commercial for the Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Therapy.  I was intrigued by the idea of a shampoo and conditioner working from the scalp and its claim to restore the scalp's natural moisture balance.  I had never seen a product focused on the nourishing of the scalp which makes more sense than all the shampoos and conditioners of the past that are supposed to work on the ends of your hair.  The past products focused more on the prevention of split ends or ending fizzy hair.  I color my hair every 6 to 8 weeks, so I always purchase a color-safe shampoo and conditioner.  I also liked that has vitamins and nutrients including vitamins B5, C & E, sunflower, almond, soybean, coconut oils and aloe vera.The bottles arrived wrapped in plastic bubble wrap and did have a small amount of leakage on the shampoo bottle but the conditioner bottle was okay.  I have used both the shampoo and conditioner for over a week and I like the products very much.  The shampoo has a lovely lavender color and a light scent.  I didn't find the scent overpowering.  I like that it takes a dime size amount to get a good lather.  The conditioner also works well with a small amount in your palm.  Most conditioners I use require quite a bit to work through my entire head of hair.  I think the conditioner is very easy to work through my hair without a lot of pulling and snagging.  It feels good and it doesn't leave a heavy, greasy film on my hair.  It rinses very clean.  Overall, I like the products.  Often in the past, most store bought shampoos begin to break my head and scalp out and neither of these products have done that.  I like that both shampoo and conditioner are designed to be set in such a way that the conditioner and shampoo bottles can be set flat so that the product is always draining down towards the opening.  I would recommend both of these products.

I found this shampoo good for every-day use. It's gentle but cleans thoroughly. I tried it with its companion product, Clear Scalp Hair Beauty Damage and Color Repair Nourishing Conditioner (how's that for a long name?) and found they work well together. The shampoo is a little less effective at adding body than some other shampoos, and overall I like the conditioner better than the shampoo. But I have very fine, curly hair that's temperamental, so another person might not have the same experience. All in all, I'd say this product is worth a try.

Many times , I'm skeptical , I'm mean it's shampoo. How revolutionary can it be ? WRONG ! I truly felt a difference after finishing the bottle (which really lasted a long time). I don't use hair coloring , but years of styling products (mostly gel) have damaged my hair.Clear scalp and hair beauty was a refreshing addition to my morning ritual.

column9: If this were Facebook I'd click "Like"
column10: I'm getting up there in years so my hair is turning into that wiry gray state.  I've started coloring which after the first few days out of the salon has turned me into porcupine head.  I've never thought much of shampoos & have usually just grabbed what's on sale.  Clear Scalp & Hair Therapy has turned me into a believer.  Just the smallest dab on the palm works into a frothy treatment.  I love the aroma (but remember, just a dab).  My hair is soft and cooperative for the first time in years.Unfortunately, as other reviewers have mentioned, the top loosened during shipping and some leakage did occur.  All in all, though, I'm very pleased with this product and would recommend.

My hair is short, regularly coloured and I use shampoo and conditioners specificly for coloured hair.The first time I used this I didn't use a conditioner and towel dried my hair, to be able to see the effectiveness of this product.Works up into good lather (we have very hard water) and rinses quickly.After being towelled dry, my hair felt clean with no residue and with a light lift in volume.This was impressive given the heat and humidity of Texas in the summer.Smells nice, very light scent but use a small amount as a little goes a long way.A clean light fragrance after dry, feels clean and light with no residue, a good product.

I used both the shampoo and matching conditioner, they made my hair feel clean and soft. I had no problem combing through it and there was no residue feeling left on my hair after I rinsed it out. It also smells great. I will definitely buy this product again in the future. Try them both, they work well together.

column9: Badly designed bottle, OK shampoo for UNcolored hair
column10: The bottle for this shampoo has an opening that you lever up when you want to put shampoo on your hair.  The problem is that it also levers up easily during shipping, meaning the bottle is covered with shampoo when it arrives.  Amazon did wrap the bottle in a plastic bag to limit the damage, but the manufacturer should really design a bottle that doesn't leak, or at least seal the top with plastic tape.Clear Scalp & Hair Therapy has a strong, lingering fruity scent. Whether you like it will be a matter of taste. I color my hair, and I was hoping that a "damage and color repair" shampoo would do a good job of preserving color. I can't speak to the damage repair part, but it's not a very good color preserving shampoo. I would recommend it for someone with average, uncolored hair.

I was curious to try this after seeing a commercial about it. I am pleased with it overall - I have thick, wavy, hair down to the middle of my back with a fair amount gray up around my face. The smell is very pleasant, and my hair doesn't feel stripped after I've used it. I also don't have to use as much as I would with many shampoos. I don't wash my hair every day (more like every 3-4), so it's hard to tell about any improvement in breakage, but I do think there is a little bit. Overall, especially combined with the conditioner, I like it.

I have color treated hair and after several weeks using this shampoo I can say that it doesn't fade my hair color. I like the creamy consistency (rather than clear liquid) without leaving a greasy residue. Hair feels clean and light after washing without being too dry or dull. It also suds up well and I end up using much less than I normally do with a similar Pantene product. The drawback is that I don't detect any added benefit from the nutrium 10. I've used other salon quality shampoo that gives me thicker, more supple hair. This one doesn't - so only 4 stars.

column9: Move over Nexxus, this is just as good, if not better
column10: I am really picky about my shampoos/conditioners, and was SO dubious when Amazon sent me this item to review.I have colored, fine hair, which frizzes easily and breaks often.  It grows very slowly and any harsh shampoos/conditioners will either break my hair or weigh it down and make it look dirty and lifeless.Amazon sent me this item (Clear Scalp and Hair Beauty Damage and Color Repair Nourishing Shampoo) and the corresponding shampoo (Clear Scalp and Hair Beauty Damage and Color Repair Nourishing Conditioner).I usually use the Nexxus damaged hair products that are found at Costco.  It is expensive, even at Costco.  But it didn't weigh my hair down nor cause breakage.This shampoo and conditioner smells GREAT.  I usually don't notice the scents, unless they are gross or medicinal, because my sense of smell is limited.  But this one smells really great, like fruity flowers.I use it basically like everyone--shampoo, rinse, condition, let sit for a minute and rinse.Here is where it's different:  When I comb out my hair, which is longer than shoulder length, it doesn't pull, tangle, or (on the other end of the spectrum) feel greasy or heavy.  It combs out sleekly (is that a word?) and as my hair dries naturally, it's not frizzy or lifeless--it shows off my natural curls.  If I dry it with the blowdryer, it doesn't frizz at all.  I can flat iron it, and maybe because it really allows the hair to curl naturally, it takes a bit more work to get that curl out, but it looks GREAT.I have been using it for a month now, and my hair dresser actually noticed a difference in my hair. She said that it grew more than usual (she's been doing my hair for 3 years now, every 6 weeks).  I believe that because my hair doesn't break or frizz, my hair really is "growing" faster because it's not breaking off.I didn't think that any line could replace my Nexxus, but this has.  It took me a long time to find the Nexxus--with my sensitive hair that breaks so easily...  And it saves me money, too, which is a great thing, especially in this economy.

Let me say right up front that I haven't noticed any real change in my hair.  It hasn't been thicker or had less breakage or any of those things, but I still love this CLEAR Shampoo because of the thickness of the suds.For years I've been a Pantene user but I'm switching!Unlike other shampoos that suds up but tend to run if not washed away quickly, CLEAR is thick and doesn't run.  I actually scrub my hair and then leave it up while I finish showering then rinse.  And it just feels so good.As I said, though, even with my newfound shampoo love, I can't speak to it's "special affects," because I haven't noticed any difference in my own hair.My hair is clean and shampooing feels good - that's enough for me!

My unmanageable mane of hair currently falls to the middle of my back.  It's very fine, tangles easily and tends to confound many shampoos.  Given the amount of hair, I am used to having to use a lot of product just to work up a lather.  I've occasionally used some higher end brands and given up simply because I'm pouring out too much  at once trying to work up a lather.  It's hardly worth the price if I'm use a quarter of the bottle at a time.  Cheaper shampoos tend to fall into two categories, gloppy or watery enough to run out of my hand.  I've tended to use them because of price, but it's a quick suds and wash with the objective to get my hair rinsed as quickly as possible.This shampoo is neither gloppy nor too watery.  I can pop up the spout and use just about a quarter sized amount of shampoo to lather up the entire mass of hair.  It lathers quickly, with a pleasant texture and smell and rinses out without the feeling I've either dried my hair out  or left a stick residue.  My hair is noticeably more manageable, especially when I have to brush it out and detangle it (which is a chore).  I'm able to get it combed and ready for my day in about half the time it takes with cheaper shampoos. While I don't like this shampoo quite as much as the Shea shampoo, it's a wonderful go-to for my color weary hair that doesn't cost my grocery budget to buy.  As with all products, if you have sensitive skin, it's probably worthwhile to be cautious with anything not designed for sensitive skin.  I haven't had any problems with it, and my skin appears to be less dried out than usual after showers--which is a plus.^_^ Shanshad

column9: Terrific product for color treated hair!
column10: This shampoo is very good for your hair.  I have a scalp problem, plus I color my hair and this is a great product.  I use it with the conditioner and it leaves my hair very silky in spite of washing it often.  It is a pink creamy texture and the scent is terrific because it is not overpowering just a nice soft clean smell.  You will love it!

I have used ths shampoo for a month or so. This bottle was the first i recieved from amazon but not the first i used. I'm very happy with it. It has a pleasant but not overpowering scent, lathers up quickly and rinses out easily. My hair when dry doesn't look weighed down the way it does with some other shampoos. It was shipped tightly wrapped in plastic and while there was a little leakage into the wrap it was completely contained and easily rinsed off from the bottle so it didn't concern me.

My husband and I tried this product along with the corresponding conditioner. His hair is dry, thinning, and brittle, very curly but not color treated. Mine is normal, slightly wavy, with good body, and salon colored.He likes this product for the moisturizing effect. We have tried just about every product we can find but his hair continues to be fragile.  This is the first product that he said actually makes a difference. His hair is softer and breaks less after only 2 weeks.For my color treated hair, it's made no positive difference. I don't like the texture feel of the hair when wet, and my color has faded twice as fast as it does using John Frieda shampoo for red hair.We'll probably keep buying this product for my husband's brittle hair, but I've stopped using it on mine.

I was surprised by how much I loved this shampoo. It is, after all, just shampoo. That said, the lather is very rich and the smell is fantastic. Has a hint of a berry smell. My hair always feels great after use. I am switching my brand!

This is my first time using this shampoo and I was very happy with it.  The product is smooth, has a wonderfully pleasant aroma --not too strong-- and lathers up well.  My hair felt soft and shiny, and after using nearly the entire bottle I haven't experienced any build-up or other strange after-effects.  I did not use it with the conditioner, so I don't know what their combined effect would be, but I would recommend the shampoo and will likely use it again.

I ordered both the Clear Scalp Shampoo and the Conditioner for Damage and Color Repair since I regularly color my dark hair and like to use products that help sustain the color. I typically buy sulfate-free since those seem to work best, and was a little bit surprised that this formula contained sulfates. However, I didn't notice any negative difference in my color after using it for a just few weeks.The shampoo did seem to be a thorough cleanser,leaving my hair "squeaky clean" and once I added the conditioner it left my hair soft and silky as I stepped out of the shower. I found the scent clean and pleasant and it doesn't linger at all after rinsing.Once blow-dried, it did seem that the shampoo might have been a bit of a stronger cleanser than I am used to since my hair was slightly fluffier than usual. It could also be that the conditioner was not as deep conditioning as I have found with other products made for color-treated or damaged hair. I should note that I have relatively "normal-dry" wavy hair and this might be a bit more ideal for those who have "oily-normal" hair.I would recommend this combo to anyone looking for a super clean head of hair with body, but not to anyone who tends to have dry hair to begin with since it may be a bit too harsh. I also wonder about long term use on color treated hair with a product that contains sulfates, since I prefer those without. They performed pretty well, so I did give the shampoo/conditioner 4 stars, but it could have had 5 if it were sulfate-free.

For the shampoo: This smells really nice and my hair is shiny and soft. As for is it is helping me damaged scalp? I don't think anyone would really be able to tell. I trust the scientific formula the smart guys put in it that it will actually make my scalp healthier. I do really like the scent and how soft and feathery my hair is after using this repeatedly. I also got the conditioner with it and use them together.

column9: Wonderful scent, buffered lather, didn't strip my hair
column10: If you were a child of the 80's you will feel a definite sense of deja vu with this product! The smell and feel of it reminded me instantly of PermaSoft. The next closest smell would be Pert Plus. It's the same manufacturer as Pert Plus so that makes sense.This shampoo did a great job of removing hairstyling product buildup without stripping my hair, and I didn't have to shampoo twice to achieve that. I tested it on 3-day-old gross hair, and one wash removed all the buildup and gunk! I used it without a follow up conditioner and my hair was not frizzy, dry, or flyaway like it normally would be with what I consider a 'drugstore product'. It was very soft and had soft waves, no frizz.I normally only use a few certain salon brands on my hair because I have it colored and I use a flatiron a lot (lots of damage potential there!); I would consider this brand of shampoo to be an acceptable substitute and not worry too much that it's stripping my color in the meantime.I would buy this.

I was a bit skeptical about this item.  But the shampoo smells great and works well.  It puts a lot of hydration in my hair, especially at the ends, which always seem to be dry and splitting.  I haven't tried it with its corresponding conditioner, but I feel that would even be better and I am happy with using only the shampoo then my usual conditioner.

The shampoo is opaque, with a slightly pinkish color. It is very smooth and comes out of the bottle easily.  Note the bottle opens at the top, whereas that of the conditioner opens at the bottom. Also the bottle is skinny, so it looks to hold more than its 12.9 fluid ounces or 381 milliliters.  It did not irritate my scalp and was smooth to apply.  If you have really filthy, greasy hair then Dawn Ultra Dishwashing Liquid, Original Scent, Blue,  24 Ounce (Pack of 2) would provide a stronger degreasing effect, but it could make the hair dry.  So the shampoo has to be rubbed in for a while to remove dirt well. Then the hair has to be rinsed to remove the bubbles and other shampoo ingredients.I tried it twice - the first time I did not use conditioner.  The second time, after I used the shampoo I used CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY Volumizing Root Boost Nourishing Conditioner, 12.7 Fluid Ounce.  The shampoo was so creamy that I thought it might be possible to avoid using conditioner - the results were OK - my hair was not frizzy. However, with the conditioner it became quite shiny and silky.I am not commenting on the toxicity or lack of toxicity of the ingredients.  I am giving an ingredient list so readers can find what is in the product.  The ingredients in common with CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY Volumizing Root Boost Nourishing Conditioner, 12.7 Fluid Ounce are:Aloe Barbadensis Leaf ExtractAscorbic AcidDimethiconolDMDM HydantoinFragranceGlycerinGlycine Soja (Soybean) OilHelianthus Annus (Sunflower) Seed OilHydrogenated Coconut OilLysine HCIMethychloroisothiaszolinoneMethylisothiaszolinoneNiacinamidePanthenolPrunus Amygdalus Dulcis (Sweet Almond) OilRed 33 (CL 17200)Sodium ChlorideTEA-dodecylbenzenesulfonateTocopheryl AcetateWaterZinc PyrithioneZinc SulphateThe ingredients in the shampoo and not in the conditioner are:Bismuth Oxychloride (Cl 77163)CarbomerCitric AcidCocomidopropyl BetaineDimethiconeGuar Hydroxypeopyltrimonium ChlorideMica (Cl 77019)Poloxamer 407Sodium IsethionateSodium Laureth SulfateSodium Lauroyl IsethionateStearic AcidTallow AcidTitanium Dioxide (CL 77891)Xanthan GumIngredients in the conditioner and not in the shampoo are:Behentrimonium ChlorideCetearyl Alcohol - emulsifier, foaming agentCyclopentasiloxane - silicone to stop hair breakingDimethylamineDipropylene  GlycolLactic AcidPEG-150 DistearateStearamidopropylI may have missed some ingredients in common as some ingredients have multiple names and shampoo labeling tends to be inconsistent.As you can see there are multiple chemicals. The shampoo claims it has 10 vitamins and nutrients.I prefer shampoos with simpler ingredient lists.  Despite various nut and seed oils, this is really a chemical-based shampoo.  However, the shampoo works well and provides a high quality wash. It does what it claims to do - repairs damage. With 4 coloring agents at least (that make the shampoo the same hue as the bottle), I assume it "repairs color" - whatever that means!I wish the ingredients weren't hidden under the label - as it was they came off with the label and I had to scan them from behind then reflect them in Adobe Photoshop CS4 - Old Version to read them.

I have naturally light colored hair...aka grey/white...lol but wanted totry this to see if it would help soften it a bit more cause lets face it,grey hair has a mind of its own!  I liked this, my hair felt very cleanand a nice scent.  I also liked the shape of the bottle, most people couldcare less about that, I have small and arthritic hands, so appreciate abottle I can grip and hold without dropping it.  It was also used by myhusband, well...he says its shampoo...lol  I liked this and also triedthe matching conditioner and reviewed that product too.

I live in a dry climate with hard water and colored hair and that equals dry skin and dry hair. I'm skeptical about hair product claims because I have found that products vary only slightly - if at all - from the cheapest products to the most expensive. But Clear Scalp and Hair is distinctly different. After about a week of use I actually could tell that my scalp was less dry - I didn't have flakes and  it didn't feel tight after a hot shower. My hair is prone to oiliness, and I didn't experience excessive oiliness with this product, nor did it weigh my hair down. It also smells great, which is a bonus.Overall, I'd say I have found my new shampoo - it works great.

column9: A great shampoo for color treated hair
column10: This shampoo foams up very well and doesn't fade your color.  Leaves your hair soft and shiny and rinses out well leaving no residue.  All in all, just what a shampoo for color-treated hair should be.

column9: Finally a shampoo that improves hair
column10: After watching commercials I wanted to give this a try and I was so happy I did. Best shampoo/conditioner I have used In my life and i have really damaged color highlited hair!!!! This actually makes your hair silky soft and the smell lasts in your hair the whole day. The conditioner works better than my neutrogena deep conditioner by far

column9: Has worked well on my hair
column10: I have been having my hair highlighted for years, so I am always looking for products that care-take long-colored hair.  At the same time, I have oily hair and need to wash it daily.  This product has been surprisingly good.The shampoo itself has a nice consistency and a pleasant fragrance that, in my opinion, does not overpower.  It lathers well, and my scalp has had no issues with either dryness or oiliness.  In addition, my color has looked better - something that friends/colleagues have remarked on since I began using this.I like to switch off my shampoos, and I could definitely see keeping this in the rotation.

column9: Great shampoo; hair has more shine!
column10: I have been using the CLEAR Damage & Color Repair shampoo with the CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY Damage & Color Repair Nourishing Conditioner, 12.7 Fluid Ounce for two weeks now. While I don't know if my hair is stronger, I can definitely see a difference in the shine. Also, my color hasn't visibly faded while using it. But what I love most about this shampoo is the scent. I can't really pin it down--it's maybe slightly fruity?--but it reminds me of the Matrix Biolage shampoo I used to buy simply because I loved the scent. Since this is a fraction of the Biolage price, I think I'll stick with CLEAR!

First of all I want to say that I also had a problem with my shampoo bottle breaking and getting everywhere during shipping. In my case, it was UPS's fault since the package actually had foot prints on it and looked beat up. Amazon was quick to reship me a new bottle that arrived fine. If you have this issue, Amazon is willing to fix it for you.On to the shampoo..I normally alternate between Herbal Essences, Pantene Pro-V and Aussie. I have straight, thick, long, highlighted hair. I was a little disappointed to see that this shampoo has Sodium Laureth Sulfate in it. Sodium Laureth Sulfate is known for being bad for colored hair, so I am not sure why it is in this "Color Repair" shampoo.The shampoo itself is thick and creamy and has a slightly pink color. It has a really nice almost floral scent. It lathers well and you don't have to use a ton of it. Honestly, it feels like Pantene Pro-V. It leaves your hair feeling clean, soft and healthy. However, I don't think it does anything to repair your color. The Sodium Laureth Sulfate may even harm it. My hair is not damaged, so I can not attest to that part of the shampoo claim.Overall, I do like the shampoo and will buy it in the future, but only if it is on sale.

column4: Valerie J. Wood "Author and Sports Journalist"
column10: I'm always careful about products for my color treated "naturally blonde" hair. This shampoo is thick and creamy, goes on smoothly, has a fresh and very pleasant scent and does a very nice job. My hair is silky and smooth after use, and I've noticed it doesn't get so flyaway in humid weather. This goes great with the matching conditioner, of course. Highly recommend.

column9: Very Thick ... Helped Flakiness on Scalp
column10: I tend to have a flaky and dry scalp. I occasionally use dandruff shampoos and they help somewhat. When I saw this new shampoo, I thought I'd give it a go. I'd prefer to use a "regular" shampoo than a special one so it seemed worth a try.The CLEAR shampoo is very thick. It lathers up quite nicely and stays on your head rather than dripping down. It seemed thicker than any other shampoo I tried -- more like a conditioner than a shampoo. After using it for a week or so, I'd have to say that my scalp felt less itchy and dry. I didn't notice any significant other changes -- my hair wasn't shinier or easier to manage but I did think it help clear up my scalp issues somewhat.The smell is subtle and not too strong.I would use this shampoo again.

I've been using this shampoo exclusively for a couple of weeks and will continue using it.  The scent is difficult to pin down: it's a light scent and reminds me of the smell of shampoo at my hairdresser's but it doesn't really smell like anything (mint, fruit, spice).  It has pleasant lather and leaves my hair manageable.  I'm not sure that using this will keep my color from fading more rapidly than it does, but it's not a bad shampoo.I have fairly thick wavy hair and live in a humid climate--so I appreciate the fact that my hair does not frizz much with this product.The only problem I had was with the delivery of the shampoo. Although it was wrapped in plastic, the cap was not secured and about 1/3 of the bottle emptied into the shipping envelope.  I don't think I'd ever order shampoo in the mail after that experience.

I find it odd that a color safe shampoo would contain sulfates. Beware if you are trying to avoid them, especially if you have any kind of keratin treatment.The shampoo lathers well, and smells nice. I didn't see a noticable difference in my scalp being less dry, though. It is an okay product, but I don't see myself using it again.

I have wavy hair which I wear blow dried and flat ironed. It has a tendency to be dry, and it is very prone to frizziness.I have tried a lot of products (of various costs) to try to make my hair shiny, straight, and non-frizzy.I received this shampoo, and the accompanying conditioner a couple of weeks ago, and have been using them exclusively, without using any additional products.The shampoo is packaged in a very usable bottle, it is easy to get the shampoo out, even with hands that are wet and slippery.The shampoo is very sudsy, and has almost no odor. Even though there are lots of suds, they rinse out very easily. My hair feels clean and soft after shampooing.I have not used the shampoo without the conditioner, so the comments are for both products used together.After towel drying my hair, it is relatively easy to comb through, although there are some small tangles. After blow drying my hair is really soft and nice, and the flat iron straightens it very well.I have noticed, though, that my hair has a tendency to be somewhat fly-away with this product, so I will try to use a leave-in product as well.Since I live in Florida, humidity is a big problem, and I do not find this product to help with frizziness.All in all I really like this shampoo, and I would give it 5 stars if I lived in a less humid area.

i gave this to the wife for her to use.  after a couple of applications she said that it did help her hair and was repairing the split ends.  she said wouldn't know about the color repair since her hair is turning silver anyway.  looking at her hair it seemed to me that it seemed fluffier and the color was a little bit bolder-but hey what does a man know.

column9: Not as great as I hoped.
column10: I am a big fan of Suave and since this product is made by the same company, I jumped at the chance to try something new from them. I have to say my review may be tainted by the way the product came to me. First, when the package arrived, it was leaking. The bottle was inside a plastic bag which must have been made to seal in any leakage. I don't know if it was broken or the button on top somehow got pushed, but half of the bottle of shampoo was out. Once I cut off the wrapping and threw away the spoils, the bottle seemed okay. I put it in my shower, eager to try it the next morning.The shampoo itself is okay. It smells and feels like the "color seal" shampoo you get in a hair-dye box for after rinsing. I'm not found of that sort of smell everyday, but it's not unpleasant. After using the shampoo for a couple of days, my hair felt limp and oily compared to using Suave shampoo and conditioner (I like to use Mango Mandarin, Citrus Smoothie, or Apple). For someone who's hair is usually light, healthy, and shiny, I did not like the effect this shampoo gave to my hair. For someone who tends to have dry scalp, it might help you. I stopped using it after a week.After a few uses, the bottle started leaking from the (almost) invisible seam holding the lid on. I don't know if I got a messed up bottle or if this is how they all are. I would not buy this again.

column9: Doesn't live up to the hype
column10: I am a die hard salon product user, usually Aveda Color Conserve Shampoo, 8.5-Ounce Bottle or Bumble and Bumble Gentle Shampoo, 8-Ounce Bottle as I color my hair every 6 weeks at the salon. So a product really has to be good to get my approval. Clear falls short.It will clean your hair, but the quality here is very much more grocery store - you get what you pay for. Its claims to give one a healthier scalp are unfounded, in my opinion, as there was no decrease in scalp dryness over weeks of use. For a truly healthy scalp, try Nioxin Cleanser, System 2 (Fine/Noticeably Thinning ), 33.8 Ounce and pair it with Nioxin Scalp Therapy, System 3 (Fine/Treated/Normal to Thin-Looking), 33.8 Ounce.The scent of Clear lingers all day, but it does this by being overpowering. Hair is not nourished, feeling dry and fly away after use.

I gave my wife the new "CLEAR Scalp and Hair Therapy shampoo and conditioner for damage and color repair" for her birthday.  She is picky about her hair products and has trained me to purchase only those for color treated hair, though she rarely admits to having color added.  I've learned my lesson, about her pickiness, when buying shampoo and conditioner, but I dared to try something new.Whew! Did I ever score with CLEAR!  She told me "the bottle shapes are so cute, and the open/close mechanism was very secure," something she doesn't always find on her regular brands.  She also said she doesn't need to use as big a portion to clean as she has before, making it very economical.  She said the suds felt thick, smooth, and it had a nice mild scent.After just a couple days of use, and especially after a full week of daily use, she thought her hair was indeed shinier thatn before, had much better texture, and seemed smooth, manageable, and extremely soft.  Usually in the humidity of warm weather she has the "frizzies."  When the CLEAR runs out, she asked me to get her more.  Boy, do I now have little gifts for future occasions--the jackpot of suprise gift-giving!

column9: good, but wait a few days to get used to it
column10: This shampoo has a nice light fragrance and lathers quickly and efficiently (even in pretty hard water). My hair is color-treated and on the dry and thick side. The first time I used this product, my hair felt more dry, but after a few shampoos, I find that it leaves my hair feeling comparatively clean and soft. It is definitely best applied with the companion conditioner (clear scalp and hair beauty damage and color repair nourishing conditioner). A good choice for the price.

I have very fine, long and thin hair that I color to hide the gray.  I also live in the northern part of the country and during the colder months my hair is SO dry it is like straw.  I tried the Clear Scalp conditioner, and really liked it, so I broke down to try the Clear Scalp shampoo.  I got this one because my hair is colored and so dry that I would call it a bit damaged.  I tried this shampoo with the conditioner and didn't need to add any leave in conditioner after my shower - this stuff just really cleaned my hair and conditioned it so well that I just blow dried it and was good to go.  I am very happy with this product, and I love the smell.  I would recommend this and buy it again.

I've been using both the shampoo and conditioner for a few days now. It has a nice long lasting fragrance. My hair feels clean and soft. I reitterate SOFT. I go the salon on a regular basis to have my hair colored. I use shampoo/conditioner for color treated hair and some have left my hair feeling dry. Not the case with Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty. It really left my hair feeling soft through out the day.Another bonus: for people like me, who need eye glasses to read and have a hard time deciphering which bottle is the shampoo and which is the conditioner, the shape of both bottles is not only very helpful but is also very clever. Both bottles have a flat spot and you push down for the spot to open and dispense shampoo or conditioner. The shampoo sits up right with the spot on the top and the conditioner sits with the spot on the bottom. No problem with trying to figure out which bottle is the shampoo or conditioner.I liked this product and will be purchasing more.

For the last 12 years I have colored my hair religiously every 3 months. For the last 11 years I spent countless dollars on salon products and finally decided that their has to be other products that work as well if not better. I am surprised I liked this shampoo as much as I did because I have been using sulfate free however I did assume that since this was "Clear" it was also sulfate free however it is the second ingredient on the list. Lathers well, great scent, and leaves my hair soft and silky. Color is very vibrant however I will alternate after this bottle finishes back to my sulfate free and then back to this just to change it up.

column9: bottle design not good, liked what was left of the shampoo
column10: I actually bought this shampoo at the supermarket.  The reason I give it 3 stars is the bottle lid design.  It is WAY too easy for the top to open in a bag, box or whatever.  The checkout person bagged this shampoo by itself which was a godsend because the top tipped open and half the contents were in the bag.  I would expect many more negative comments like this one unless they change their lid design or tape off the top so it can't tip to the open position.  I liked the scent of the shampoo (on the strong side) and thought it cleaned well, left my hair full bodied and my scalp moisturized.  I agree with another poster about the SLS.  I primarily use WEN or Loreal Creme (LOVE IT) and my bleached hair looks wonderful after being severely damaged due to bleaching and nutritional problems.  Clear did not give me the luminosity and shine or define my color hair the way the creme poo does.  I will only use whats left on occassion when I want a fluffier style.

column9: Goodbye Garnier Fructus, Hello Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty!
column10: I have thick shoulder-length hair that every 3 - 4 months my salonist either colors or highlights (and chops away some of the thickness so I don't look like a wooly mammoth).  For this reason, I switched from using my usual brand, Fructis Sleek and Shine fortifying Shampoo By Garnier for Unisex Shampoo, 13 Ounce, to this brand.PLEASE NOTE: This was used in conjunction with CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY Damage & Color Repair Nourishing Conditioner, 12.7 Fluid Ounce.I rather liked the packaging.  It is a little similar to the Clear Conditioner, but fortunately, I have sharp eyes.  The shampoo itself had a nice, light pleasant smell, and a good consistency (neither too thick, nor too thin and watery).I started out with about a palm-sized amount of shampoo--what normally would have been just enough with my regular brand.  I quickly found out that this was too much for the Clear shampoo.  It lathers quite nicely and also rinses out quite easily.But the end results were what stunned me.  My hair was delightfully soft and smooth!  After flat-ironing my hair, my hair was sleek and flat in a way that I could only rarely get from my usual hair products.  But the best part was when a coworker approached me and asked if I had recently gone in to have my hair cut and colored.  I told him, no, my last appointment was a month ago!I am now a convert; I'm saying goodbye to Garnier Fructus, and hello to Clear and better hair!Brought to you by:*C.S. Light*

I can't say enough good things about the Clear Scalp & Hair line. The product delivers exactly what it claims to do...beautiful, clean hair. The shampoo is creamy and silky with a very rich lather. It rinses well without a filmy residue left behind. The scent is light and pleasing and not overpowering like some leading shampoos on the market. The only negative thing I can say about this product is that I wish it came in a bigger size! Definitely worth the money!

For a product that is supposed to nourish damaged and colored hair, I was surprised that the second ingredient is sodium laurel sulfate, a harsh, cheap ingredient to help foaming/lather. I haven't been a vegetarian for over a decade, but I still make a lot of vegetarian meals.  Better Than Bouillon (BTB) is one of my go-to ingredients for adding flavor to vegetable soup and stock, and also less expected dishes like pasta, or braised veggies and even stir-fry sauces.  Though shelf-stable when you buy it, the BTB needs to be refrigerated once open.  I keep mine in the door of the fridge for easy access, and can fit three or four varieties of BTB in the shelf where eggs are meant to be stored.  Though it takes up space in the fridge, it gives me lots more room in my pantry and freezer, since I'm no longer storing boxes, cans or jars of broth.I also like the flexibility to use the amount I need for a specific recipe.  I wouldn't always open a huge box of broth if I only wanted a splash of it to loosen a stew, for example, but I can easily use a 1/2 tsp of BTB in water and dilute my gravies without diluting their flavor as well.  You'd be surprised how many places you can ramp up flavor with this product.  I often use it in place of salt as well, particularly in saucy dishes where it blends easily.  The sodium content is comparable to other bouillon I've seen, but the flavor seems richer, so less is required overall.I'm not a nutritionist but I feel like I should comment on the reviews which blast BTB for adding MSG; as far as I can tell from my research, they don't add MSG.  Now, not *adding* MSG is not the same as not *having* any MSG, which is I think what confuses and frustrates some people.  MSG is a naturally occurring compound in some foods, but can also be isolated and added into foods where it doesn't naturally occur.  BTB *does* contain ingredients that have natural MSG in them, therefore it has some natural MSG as well, but is stating the truth when they say they don't use MSG as an additive.For what it's worth, completely avoiding MSG in a typical American diet can be quite a challenge.  I've gotten really horrid migraines for a long time and spent years cutting out all kinds of different foods, including MSG, to try to decrease the frequency of my headaches.  For me, MSG can make pain worse, but doesn't cause it to occur altogether.  My husband, being a thoughtful man, has made soups for me using BTB when I've been knocked out due to a migraine, and with the quantities we use in our cooking, I haven't had any problems.  Of course, your experience may differ.Overall, I highly recommend Better Than Bouillon's Vegetable Base.  It's an excellent way to add flavor to dishes, easy to use and undeniably better for you than most traditional bouillon cubes.

column9: Superior Touch, Please advise if there is ANY MSG in your product
column10: I have been using the Better Than Bouillon Vegetable Base for years.  I was in the process of ordering additional jars, when I read Ms Hill's comment, from December, 2008. The articles indicate there are over 40 food ingredients besides "monosodium glutamate" that contain processed free glutamic acid (MSG). It appears that autolyzed yeast extract and maltodextrin are two of those food ingredients.  In addition, "NO MSG ADDED" does not mean that there is NO MSG in the product. If MSG is "processed into" a product as opposed to being "poured into" a product (just a matter of a different processing method), then a company can declare "NO MSG ADDED"  or "NO ADDED MSG", even though the product contains MSG.Therefore, before I make an additional purchase,  I am asking Superior Touch --- Please advise if your Better Than Bouillon products actually contain any MSG.

column9: all right by me--with a minor cautionary note or two
column10: Kellogg's Corn Pops breakfast cereal in these 1.5 ounce cups boasts a delicious and flavorful taste. It contains no cholesterol, no fat and it is low in calories. The delicious taste and the nutritional value that it does have make this better for you or your kids than skipping breakfast. It is low in carbohydrates, too. It stays crunchy in milk; and I enjoy the strong corn taste. Milk enhances the excellent flavor of the cereal. It is also certified kosher if that's important to you.Unfortunately, some disappointments exist. The cereal is only average in terms of vitamin content, reaching at the very best 30% of your recommended daily intake of niacin, vitamins B6 and B12, riboflavin, thiamin and folic acid. It delivers somewhat less than average value in the vitamin department. Corn Pops in these 1.5 ounce cups cannot be considered a substitute for a morning vitamin if you need one. Therefore I will take off one star to make this a four star review.Kellogg's Corn Pops cereal does contain partially hydrogenated vegetable oil and this can convert in your body to trans fat. Be careful!One more caveat: this product contains traces of soybeans and it is made with wheat. Ask your doctor before eating this cereal if you are unsure if your body can tolerate these ingredients. In addition, consult your doctor about your diet from time to time.Overall, these 1.5 ounce cups of Kellogg's Corn Pops truly are very useful for people on the go or kids who want an after school snack that's not too bad for them. The cereal does have some basic nutritional value. Nevertheless, Kellogg's Corn Pops cereal cannot be a substitute for a daily vitamin.
